genres.name: Portraits
genres.blurb: Faces from long ago that still seem to look back at you.

genres.name: Seas & Ships
genres.blurb: Storms, sailors, harbors and endless waves.

genres.name: Faith & Scripture
genres.blurb: Stories from the Bible and sacred traditions.

genres.name: Still Life & Animals
genres.blurb: Flowers, fruit, horses, hounds and more.

genres.name: Dreams & Big Ideas
genres.blurb: Symbols, feelings and wild new ways of seeing.

collections.name: Art for Kids
collections.blurb: The 100 most fun paintings for young explorers: animals, fairy tales, circuses, storms and wonders.
collections.intro: Welcome, young explorers! These 100 paintings are picked for you: tigers in thunderstorms, mermaids, a giant wave, 42 cats and a spinning top. Each one has a little challenge — can you find what the painter hid?

collections.name: Jewish Artists
collections.blurb: Paintings by Jewish artists across Europe and beyond, from Amsterdam to Montmartre to Jerusalem.
collections.intro: These painters came from Jewish families in Germany, the Netherlands, Poland, Russia, France, Italy and beyond. Some painted Jewish life and history; many painted whatever they loved — fishermen, gardens, city streets and friends. Together, they show how much Jewish artists helped shape modern art.

collections.name: Canada
collections.blurb: From Tom Thomson's wild north to Krieghoff's snowy Quebec: Canada's most important early paintings.
collections.intro: Canada's art begins with explorers and Indigenous portraits, grows through the snowy villages of Quebec and ends with the Group of Seven's wild north. Here are the paintings that taught Canadians to see their own land. Some paintings show Indigenous peoples as artists of the time saw them, so it's worth asking whose story is being told.

collections.name: Norway
collections.blurb: Fjords, Vikings, trolls and Munch: the great paintings of Norway.
collections.intro: Norway's painters gave the world dramatic fjords and misty mountains, the Vikings of the sagas, cozy farmhouse lights and the famously haunting art of Edvard Munch. Many of these artists also worked in Denmark and Germany, where Norwegian painters often trained.

collections.name: United States
collections.blurb: Great American paintings: wild landscapes, sea storms, Revolutionary heroes and the artists who made America look like itself.
collections.intro: From the Hudson River School's glowing wilderness to Winslow Homer's stormy seas, from Revolutionary War heroes to Mary Cassatt's quiet rooms, these are the great American paintings from the nation's first 150 years.

collections.name: France
collections.blurb: Impressionists, revolutionaries and the heart of modern art.
collections.intro: France gave us Impressionism, Romanticism and many of history's best-known paintings.

collections.name: Italy
collections.blurb: Italian painters of the last 300 years, from Venice to Milan.
collections.intro: Italy's art after the Renaissance kept going: romantic lovers, sunlit Alpine peaks and shimmering portraits.

collections.name: Spain
collections.blurb: Goya, Sorolla and the painters of Spain.
collections.intro: From Goya's court portraits and dark visions to Sorolla's dazzling beaches.

collections.name: Netherlands
collections.blurb: Van Gogh, the Hague School and Dutch painters.
collections.intro: The land of windmills, canals and Van Gogh's swirling skies.

collections.name: Germany
collections.blurb: Romantic mountains, expressive colors and German painters.
collections.intro: Germany's painters gave us misty Romantic mountains, wild Expressionist colors and dreamlike modern art.

collections.name: United Kingdom
collections.blurb: Turner's storms, Pre-Raphaelite fairy tales and England's great portraits.
collections.intro: British painters loved storms, fairy tales, portraits and the English countryside.

collections.name: Russia
collections.blurb: Giant historical canvases, forests and snowy landscapes from Russia.
collections.intro: Russian painters made huge, emotional pictures of history, forests, rivers and the lives of ordinary people.

collections.name: Poland
collections.blurb: Poland's proud history in paint.
collections.intro: Polish painters kept their country's history alive in huge canvases, countryside scenes and portraits.

collections.name: Sweden
collections.blurb: Midsummer dances, cozy homes and Nordic light.
collections.intro: Sweden's painters made sparkling summer pictures, family homes full of sunlight and scenes from Norse legends.

collections.name: Denmark
collections.blurb: The Danish Golden Age and the artists of Skagen.
collections.intro: Quiet Copenhagen rooms, sunny beaches at Skagen and some of the calmest paintings ever made.

collections.name: Finland
collections.blurb: Finnish heroes, forests and the Kalevala.
collections.intro: Finnish painters turned their national legends and lakeside forests into glowing pictures.

collections.name: Austria
collections.blurb: Vienna's golden age of painting.
collections.intro: Austrian art sparkled in turn-of-the-century Vienna with gold leaf, bold lines and dreamy patterns.

collections.name: Belgium
collections.blurb: Masks, Symbolists and Belgian painters.
collections.intro: Belgium's painters gave us carnival masks, mysterious Symbolist dreams and sunlit gardens.

collections.name: Japan
collections.blurb: Woodblock prints, folding screens and the painters of Japan.
collections.intro: Japan's artists gave the world The Great Wave, golden folding screens, puppies, cats and ghosts. This collection includes woodblock prints as well as paintings, since prints were one of Japan's great art forms.

collections.name: China
collections.blurb: Imperial court paintings from the Qing dynasty.
collections.intro: Huge scrolls, emperors on horseback and bustling cities from the court of the Qing emperors.

collections.name: Middle East
collections.blurb: Painters from Turkey and Iran.
collections.intro: Ottoman and Persian painters who studied European techniques and painted their own world: palaces, courtyards and quiet moments.

collections.name: Mexico
collections.blurb: Volcano landscapes and folk traditions from Mexico.
collections.intro: Mexican painters celebrated their volcanoes, valleys and traditions like the Day of the Dead.

collections.name: Australia
collections.blurb: Sunburnt landscapes, sheepshearers and the Heidelberg School.
collections.intro: Australian painters like Tom Roberts and Arthur Streeton painted the golden bush and the working people of the outback.

collections.name: Abstract Art
collections.blurb: Pictures that don't show things, but color, shape and feeling: Kandinsky, Mondrian, Klee, Hilma af Klint and many more.
collections.intro: Abstract art is painting without a picture of something. Instead of a person, tree or boat, you get colors, lines and shapes that make you feel something, like music you can see. A few artists in the early 1900s, in Munich, Moscow, Paris and Stockholm, realized that paint didn't have to copy the world. This collection takes you from the painters who were nearly there, through the pioneers, to playful corners like Klee's cats and fish and Schwitters's collages made from trash. Try asking: what does this sound like? What would it feel like to step inside?

sections.title: How it began: roads to abstraction
sections.blurb: Long before anyone painted a pure shape, some artists were already letting color, light and feeling take over from the subject. These are the stepping stones.

sections.title: Color and feeling: Kandinsky and the Blue Rider
sections.blurb: Wassily Kandinsky believed colors work like music: yellow is a trumpet, blue is a cello. He and his friends in Munich, the Blue Rider group, painted feelings, sounds and dreams instead of things.

sections.title: Squares, grids and straight lines
sections.blurb: What happens if you throw away everything except shape and color? Malevich painted a black square, Mondrian a grid of red, yellow and blue, and Russian artists built whole imaginary worlds out of lines and planes.

sections.title: Circles, spirals and rainbows of light
sections.blurb: Hilma af Klint painted glowing spirals and flowers years before anyone else dared, and Robert Delaunay made color itself the subject, circling and dancing across the canvas.

sections.title: Paul Klee: playful lines and secret worlds
sections.blurb: Paul Klee said that drawing is like taking a line for a walk. His pictures are full of tiny jokes: cats and birds, twittering machines, fish that glow, houses that spin.

sections.title: Cubism and Futurism: breaking the world into pieces
sections.blurb: Cubists showed an object from many sides at once. The Futurists added speed: cyclists, soccer players and racing cars smeared across the canvas.

sections.title: Cut, paste and build: collage
sections.blurb: Kurt Schwitters glued tickets, scraps and bits of rubbish onto his pictures and called the result Merz. It was a new way to make art from whatever was lying around.

collections.name: Impressionism
collections.blurb: Quick brushstrokes, sparkling light and everyday moments: the painters who stopped trying to hide their brushwork.
collections.intro: In the 1860s and 70s a group of Paris painters left their studios and painted outside, catching the light of a single moment. Critics laughed and named them after one of Monet's paintings, Impression, Sunrise. Look for dabs of color that blend only when you step back.

collections.name: Post-Impressionism
collections.blurb: Van Gogh's swirls, Cézanne's apples, Gauguin's flat color: artists who took Impressionism somewhere new.
collections.intro: After Impressionism, painters wanted to say more than just how a moment looked. Van Gogh turned feelings into thick swirling brushstrokes, Cézanne built pictures from solid shapes, Seurat used tiny dots and Gauguin used flat, bold color.

collections.name: Romanticism
collections.blurb: Wild storms, misty mountains and big feelings: nature and imagination in charge.
collections.intro: Romantic painters believed feelings mattered more than rules. They painted shipwrecks, thunderstorms, haunted ruins and lonely figures staring at huge landscapes, to make you feel how small and amazed a person can be.

collections.name: Realism
collections.blurb: Real people, real work, real life: painters who showed the world as it is.
collections.intro: Realist painters decided that farmers, stone breakers and city crowds were as worthy of a big painting as kings and gods. They painted what they saw, with no prettying-up.

collections.name: Neoclassicism & Academic Art
collections.blurb: Heroes in togas, perfect poses and Greek and Roman stories: clear, balanced and carefully painted.
collections.intro: In the late 1700s and 1800s artists copied the order and calm of ancient Greece and Rome. This collection covers Neoclassicism and the polished academic painters who followed, famous for smooth finish and big stories from history and myth.

collections.name: Pre-Raphaelites & Victorian Dreams
collections.blurb: Knights, maidens, mermaids and jewel-bright colors: dreamy Victorian storytelling.
collections.intro: In 1848 a group of young English painters, the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood, wanted to paint with the honest detail and bright color of art before Raphael. They filled pictures with legends, poems and gorgeous flowers. Later painters carried on the dream.

collections.name: Symbolism & Art Nouveau
collections.blurb: Dreams, moods and mysteries: artists who painted ideas and feelings you can't quite name.
collections.intro: Symbolist and Art Nouveau artists painted dreams, myths and moods, and swirled flowing lines through posters, jewelry and buildings. Look for gold, mysterious faces and curving, plant-like shapes.

collections.name: Expressionism & Fauvism: Wild Color
collections.blurb: Paint it how it feels: wild color, bold lines and strong emotion.
collections.intro: Expressionist and Fauvist painters used color and shape to show feelings. Matisse and the Fauves, called wild beasts by a critic, painted in bright, flat color. In Germany and Austria, Expressionists turned anxiety, joy and energy into paint.

collections.name: Hudson River School & American Landscape
collections.blurb: Glowing mountains, waterfalls and endless skies: the great American landscape painters.
collections.intro: In the 1800s painters of the Hudson River School showed America as a wild, glowing paradise, with huge skies, peaks and rivers. They traveled far to sketch the real places, then made giant pictures that made people proud of their land.

collections.name: Ukiyo-e: Japanese Woodblock Prints
collections.blurb: Great waves, rainy bridges and kabuki stars: Japan's woodblock prints that stunned Europe.
collections.intro: Ukiyo-e means pictures of the floating world. Artists drew a design, carvers cut it into wooden blocks and printers pressed the colors one at a time, making cheap prints for everyone. They inspired Monet and Van Gogh.

collections.name: Rococo & Eighteenth-Century Elegance
collections.blurb: Pastel elegance, flirty swings and fancy portraits: art of the 1700s.
collections.intro: The 1700s loved lightness: pink and blue colors, curling frills, picnics, portraits and glittering views of Venice. Look for playful details and fancy clothes.

collections.name: Renaissance Masters
collections.blurb: Leonardo, Raphael, Botticelli, Van Eyck, Dürer: the artists who brought back the beauty of the ancient world and learned to paint space, light and real people.
collections.intro: Around 1400 painters and sculptors in Florence began to study nature, the human body and the rules of perspective, so that pictures looked like windows into the real world. Leonardo, Michelangelo and Raphael became legends, while in Flanders Jan van Eyck's oil paint caught every glint of a jewel. Look for calm triangles of figures, soft landscapes and faces full of feeling.

collections.name: Baroque: Light, Drama & Motion
collections.blurb: Spotlights, storms of motion and big emotions: Caravaggio, Rubens, Velázquez and Artemisia Gentileschi.
collections.intro: Baroque painters of the 1600s wanted to make you feel something. They used deep shadow and spotlights, twisting bodies and swirling clouds, and they painted saints and heroes as real, sweaty, passionate people. Look for the single beam of light, the diagonal lines and the moment right before something happens.

collections.name: Dutch Golden Age
collections.blurb: Rembrandt, Vermeer and Frans Hals: when the Netherlands was rich and painted its own homes, ships, tulips and faces.
collections.intro: In the 1600s the Dutch Republic was one of the richest places on Earth, and ordinary merchants bought pictures for their homes. Painters turned to portraits, quiet rooms, stormy seas, ice-skating villages and still lifes of cheese and oysters. Look for window light, tiny details and clever hidden symbols.

Q448189.bio: Jacek Malczewski was born in Radom, Poland, and became a leading Symbolist painter. He studied in Kraków and Paris and often painted himself in dreamlike scenes full of Polish folklore and history. He lived in Kraków, where he later taught. He died there in 1929.

Q320980.bio: Lucas van Leyden was a Dutch painter and printmaker born in Leiden in 1494. He began making prints as a child and became one of the best engravers of his time. He died in 1533.

Q466639.bio: Olga Boznańska was born in Kraków, Poland, and studied in Munich and Paris, where she lived for much of her life. She became one of the most important Polish painters, with a soft, gray-toned style, and she painted many portraits. She was widely admired in Paris. She died there in 1940.

Q1390614.bio: Eero Järnefelt was born in Vyborg and became a leading Finnish painter of rural life and landscapes. He studied in Saint Petersburg and Paris. His family included the composer Jean Sibelius, who was his brother-in-law. He died in Helsinki in 1937.

Q5582.bio: Vincent van Gogh was born in a small village in the Netherlands and worked as a teacher and art dealer before becoming a painter at age 27. He lived in the Netherlands, Belgium, Paris, and finally the sunny south of France, where his colors grew brighter and bolder. He painted more than 800 paintings in about a decade, yet sold almost none while alive. After his death at 37, his brother's family helped make him one of the most loved artists in history.

Q353014.bio: Peter Nicolai Arbo was a Norwegian painter born in 1831 who studied in Düsseldorf and Munich. He painted Norse myth and Viking history, making them familiar to Norwegians. His 'Wild Hunt of Odin' is his most famous painting. He died in Christiania in 1892.

Q436803.bio: Hanna Hirsch-Pauli was born in Stockholm in 1864 and was a leading Swedish woman painter. She studied in Stockholm and Paris and was a friend of many Nordic painters. She is best known for her warm family scenes. She died in 1940.

Q2555178.bio: Nicolas Mignard was a French painter born in Troyes in 1606. He worked for many years in Avignon, where he was nicknamed Mignard of Avignon, and then moved to Paris to paint for the royal court. He was the older brother of the painter Pierre Mignard and died in Paris in 1668.

Q3290532.bio: John Steuart Curry was born on a farm in Kansas and became one of the main painters of the Regionalist movement, which celebrated the American Midwest. He painted farm life, storms and big moments from history. He also painted murals for the Kansas State Capitol. He died in Wisconsin in 1946.

Q1357759.bio: Lambert Sustris was a painter born in Amsterdam around 1515 who moved to Italy and worked in Venice and Padua. He painted portraits, myths and big landscapes in the style of Titian, whom he worked with. He died in 1584.

Q4129638.bio: Oscar Wergeland was born in Christiania in 1844 and became a Norwegian painter of history. His huge painting of the Norwegian constitution of 1814 is one of Norway's best-known pictures. He died in 1910.

Q171344.bio: William Hogarth was born in London and became one of Britain's best-known painters and engravers. He made funny, sharp pictures about the follies of society, often in sets of prints that tell a story. He also championed the rights of artists. He died in London in 1764.

Q701669.bio: Hans Gude was born in Christiania (Oslo), Norway, and spent much of his career in Germany. He was a star of Norwegian landscape painting, depicting mountains, fjords and coasts. He taught in Düsseldorf and Berlin and trained many painters. He died in Berlin in 1903.

Q5664.bio: Fra Angelico was an Italian painter born around 1390 who was a Dominican friar. His gentle, glowing paintings of saints and angels in the convent of San Marco in Florence are among the loveliest of the early Renaissance. He died in Rome in 1455.

Q766362.bio: William Etty was born in York, England, and spent his life training to paint like the Old Masters. He is best known for his rich colors and glowing skin tones. He worked in London but retired to his hometown of York. He died there in 1849.

Q4974655.bio: Sofie Ribbing was born in Sweden and became a painter and teacher who lived in Sweden, Denmark, and Norway. She studied in Copenhagen and was known for scenes of children and family life. She was one of the notable Scandinavian women painters of her era. She died in 1894.

Q333323.bio: Pietro da Cortona was an Italian painter and architect born in the town of Cortona in 1596. He lived in Rome and became one of the leading artists of the Baroque, painting giant ceilings such as the one at the Palazzo Barberini. He died in Rome in 1669.

Q958052.bio: Konstantin Savitsky was born in Taganrog, Russia, and studied at the Imperial Academy of Arts in Saint Petersburg. He was a member of the Peredvizhniki, or 'Wanderers,' a group who took realistic art to ordinary people around Russia. He was known for paintings of people and animals. He died in 1905 in Penza.

Q215773.bio: Oscar Bluemner was a German-born American painter, born in Prenzlau in 1867. An architect by training, he moved to the United States in 1892 and made paintings of the New Jersey landscape in strong flat colors, especially red. He died in Braintree, Massachusetts, in 1938.

Q548914.bio: Philipp Veit was born in Berlin and became a painter in the Nazarene movement, a group who admired the art of medieval and Renaissance Germany and Italy. He lived in Rome, Frankfurt and Mainz. He was also a museum director. He died in Mainz in 1877.

Q203643.bio: James McNeill Whistler was born in Lowell, Massachusetts, in the United States, and spent his childhood partly in Russia. He moved to Europe as a young man and lived in Paris and London, where he became one of the most famous (and sharp-tongued) artists in the world. He titled paintings like pieces of music, such as 'Nocturne' and 'Arrangement.' He died in London in 1903.

Q175130.bio: Alfred Sisley was born in Paris to English parents and was one of the key Impressionist painters. He painted quiet landscapes along the Seine River and in small villages near Paris. He lived most of his life in France but remained a British citizen. He died in Moret-sur-Loing in 1899.

Q1398809.bio: Fausto Zonaro was an Italian painter born in Masi, near Padua, in 1854. He moved to Constantinople in 1891 and became court painter to the Ottoman sultan Abdul Hamid II, painting scenes of the city and its history. He returned to Italy and died in Sanremo in 1929.

Q1627994.bio: Horatio Walker was born in Listowel, Ontario, and became a famous painter of rural Quebec. He lived much of the year on Île d'Orléans near Quebec City and painted farmers and animals in a soft, glowing light. His paintings sold well in the United States. He died in Quebec in 1938.

Q468632.bio: Mattia Preti was an Italian painter born in 1613 in Calabria, nicknamed the Calabrian Knight. He worked in Rome, Naples and Malta with dramatic light and big, strong figures. He died in Valletta, Malta, in 1699.

Q2596759.bio: Kitty Kielland was born in Stavanger, Norway, and was one of the first Norwegian women to become a leading landscape painter. She lived in Germany and France for many years. Her atmospheric pictures of Norwegian summer light are admired today. She died in 1914.

Q5423992.bio: Felix Octavius Carr Darley was an American illustrator born in Philadelphia in 1822. He illustrated books by Washington Irving and Charles Dickens and made many pictures of the Civil War. He died in Claymont, Delaware, in 1888.

Q77132.bio: Albert Bierstadt was born in Germany and raised in Massachusetts. He traveled west with survey expeditions and painted vast landscapes of the Rocky Mountains and Yosemite. His work was admired by huge crowds in the East. He lived in New York and died there in 1902.

x-giovanni-villani-nuova-cronica.bio: The Nuova Cronica was written by Giovanni Villani, a Florentine merchant and historian born around 1276, who died in the Black Death in Florence in 1348. The surviving manuscripts of his chronicle were illustrated by artists whose names are not known.

Q2273503.bio: Niccolò Antonio Colantonio was a painter from Naples, born around 1420. He was influenced by Flemish painters and taught Antonello da Messina. He died in about 1460.

x-peter-of-eboli.bio: Peter of Eboli was an Italian poet who lived in the south of Italy and Sicily around 1196. He wrote a long poem about the emperor Henry VI and illustrated it with lively colored drawings, including scenes of the capture and ransom of Richard the Lionheart.

Q250194.bio: Anselm Feuerbach was a German painter born in Speyer in 1829. He studied in Düsseldorf, Munich and Paris and lived for many years in Italy, where he painted calm scenes from classical antiquity. He died in Venice in 1880.

Q183221.bio: Jean-Antoine Watteau was a French painter born in Valenciennes in 1684. He invented the fête galante, a dreamy picture of elegant people in silk costumes having a party or flirting in a park, and he also loved painting actors and clowns from the theater. He died young, at 36, in 1721.

Q7799.bio: Bramantino was an Italian painter and architect born in Milan in about 1465. His pictures have smooth, geometric shapes and pale, cool colors. He died in 1536.

Q312616.bio: Petrus Christus was a Flemish painter, born around 1410 in Baarle. He lived in Bruges and followed in the footsteps of Jan van Eyck, with calm, clear pictures. He died in 1475.

Q740396.bio: Václav Brožík was a Czech painter born in Trhová Kamenice in 1851. He studied in Prague, Dresden and Munich, and moved to Paris, where he painted big scenes from Czech and European history. He died in Paris in 1901.

Q25710346.bio: Jacques Laumosnier was a French painter born in Paris in 1669, who worked as a painter of history and portraits. He died in Paris in 1744.

Q236038.bio: Sofonisba Anguissola was an Italian painter born in Cremona in 1532. She was one of the first women artists to become famous across Europe, and worked as a court painter for the king of Spain. She lived to the age of about 93 and died in Palermo in 1625.

Q1778899.bio: Asta Nørregaard was born in Christiania (now Oslo) and was one of Norway's first professional women painters. She studied in Munich and Paris and painted portraits, including one of Edvard Munch. She was an important supporter of other artists. She died in 1933.

Q151803.bio: Piet Mondrian was born in the Netherlands and started out painting windmills and trees. He lived in Amsterdam, Paris, London and finally New York City. Over time he simplified his art into straight black lines and blocks of red, yellow and blue. He died in New York in 1944, and his style inspired architects and designers worldwide.

Q182664.bio: Giovanni Antonio Canal, known as Canaletto, was born in Venice and painted its canals, palaces, and festivals with great precision. His views were popular with wealthy British visitors on their tours of Italy, and he lived in London for several years. His paintings are still the way many people picture Venice. He died in Venice in 1768.

Q346952.bio: Jan Gossaert was a Flemish painter born around 1478. He traveled to Italy and brought Renaissance ideas back to Flanders and the Netherlands, where he painted myths and portraits. He died in 1532.

Q285423.bio: Sebastiano del Piombo was an Italian painter born in Venice around 1485. He moved to Rome and became a friend of Michelangelo, painting powerful portraits that mixed Venetian color with Roman grandeur. He died in Rome in 1547.

Q1827276.bio: Lionel Royer was a French painter born in Château-du-Loir in 1852. He studied in Paris and painted large pictures of French history and legend, which were popular in the years after France's defeat in the war of 1870. He died in Neuilly-sur-Seine in 1926.

Q445891.bio: Frits Thaulow was born in Christiania (Oslo) and became a leading Norwegian Impressionist, known for painting water in rivers, streams and mills. He lived in France and Denmark, as well as in Norway. He died in 1906.

Q21995307.bio: Sidney Simon was an American painter and sculptor born in Pittsburgh in 1917. He was a combat artist for the US Army in World War II and painted the Japanese surrender in Tokyo Bay. He died in 1997.

Q5075054.bio: Charles Alexander Smith was a Canadian painter born in Galt, Ontario, in 1864. He painted historical scenes and portraits. He later lived in London, England, where he died in 1915. His painting of the 'Assembly of the Six Counties' recorded an important event in Quebec history.

Q1854159.bio: The Master of Saint Giles was a French painter whose name is not known, active in Paris around 1500. He is named after a famous altarpiece showing the Mass of Saint Giles, now in the National Gallery in London, and he painted richly detailed religious scenes.

Q18325079.bio: Léon Sabatier was a French painter and lithographer born in Paris in 1800. He traveled widely, made views of cities and landscapes and recorded the burning of Paris in 1871. He died in Paris in 1887.

Q8017370.bio: William Ranney was an American painter born in Middletown, Connecticut, in 1813. He fought in the Texas Revolution as a young man and painted scenes of the American West and of the Revolutionary War. He lived in New Jersey and died in West Hoboken in 1857.

Q1383101.bio: François-Auguste Biard was a French painter born in Lyon in 1799. He traveled widely to Lapland and Brazil, painted exotic scenes and political pictures, including one about the abolition of slavery in 1848. He died in Fontainebleau in 1882.

Q314548.bio: Gerard van Honthorst was a Dutch painter born in Utrecht in 1592. He went to Rome and learned from Caravaggio's use of light, and became known for night scenes lit by a single candle. He died in 1656.

Q964791.bio: Paul Émile Chabas was born in Nantes, France, and became a popular painter in Paris. He is best known for dreamy paintings of young people by lakes and meadows in soft light. His work was admired by the public in the early 1900s. He died in Paris in 1937.

Q5432.bio: Francisco Goya was born in a small village in Spain and became the court painter to the Spanish kings in Madrid. After an illness left him deaf in his forties, his art grew darker and more personal. He witnessed war and cruelty and made powerful pictures about it. He spent his last years in Bordeaux, France, and is seen as a bridge between old masters and modern art.

Q472073.bio: Alesso Baldovinetti was a Florentine painter, born in 1425. He painted fresh, bright pictures with careful landscapes and also worked in mosaic and stained glass. He died in 1499.

Q266415.bio: Isidor Kaufmann was born in Arad, then part of Hungary, to a Jewish family and trained in Vienna. He is best known for his warm, realistic portraits of Jewish people and religious scenes in Eastern Europe. He lived and worked in Vienna for much of his life. He died there in 1921.

Q204138.bio: Viktor Vasnetsov was born in a village in northern Russia, the son of a priest. He lived in Moscow, and became known for painting scenes from Russian folk tales and legends, with warriors, witches and firebirds. He also designed churches and theater sets. He died in Moscow in 1926.

Q2695615.bio: Thorolf Holmboe was a Norwegian painter born in 1866 who painted landscapes and winter scenes. He studied in Norway and in Paris. He lived most of his life in and around Christiania (now Oslo). He died in 1935.

Q33981.bio: August Macke was a German painter born in Meschede in 1887. He lived in Bonn and Munich and was a member of the Blue Rider group, painting happy scenes of parks and shop windows in bright colors. He was killed in World War I in France in 1914 at the age of 27.

Q3514329.bio: Takeuchi Seihō was born in Kyoto and became one of the leading painters of Japan in the early 1900s. He studied Western painting during trips to Europe and mixed it with Japanese styles. He is known for animals, such as his famous 'Tabby Cat'. He died in 1942.

Q297838.bio: Jusepe de Ribera was a Spanish painter, born in 1591, who spent most of his life in Naples. His dramatic pictures of saints, philosophers and beggars use strong light and dark. He died in Naples in 1652.

Q180932.bio: François Boucher was born in Paris and became the favorite painter of Madame de Pompadour, the French king's companion. He lived in Paris and was the leading figure in the Rococo style, with its pastel colors and playful, romantic scenes. He painted, designed tapestries and decorated palaces. He died in Paris in 1770.

Q1763678.bio: Henry Holiday was born in London and was a painter, designer and stained-glass artist. He was influenced by the Pre-Raphaelites. He also illustrated Lewis Carroll's poem 'The Hunting of the Snark'. He died in London in 1927.

Q939968.di: Royal Monastery of San Lorenzo de El Escorial
Q939968.bio: Francisco Rizi was a Spanish painter, born in Madrid in 1614. He painted religious pictures, festivals and ceilings at the court of Spain. He died in 1685.

Q2090815.bio: Jean Leon Gerome Ferris was an American painter born in Philadelphia in 1863. He painted a series of scenes of American history, from the Pilgrims to the Revolution, and his pictures were published in many schoolbooks. He died in Philadelphia in 1930.

Q296.bio: Claude Monet was born in Paris but grew up on the coast of Normandy, where he learned to paint outdoors. He was a leader of Impressionism, and he lived in places like Argenteuil and, for his last 43 years, Giverny, where he built a famous garden with a pond of water lilies. He painted the same scenes again and again at different times of day to capture changing light. He kept painting until he was 86, even as his eyesight faded.

Q215100.bio: Mikhail Vrubel was born in Omsk, Siberia, and studied in Saint Petersburg. He lived in Russia and Ukraine, creating glittering, mosaic-like paintings and designs for theaters. He is best known for paintings of the Demon, a moody figure from a Russian poem. He lost his sight in later life and died in Saint Petersburg in 1910.

Q8453.bio: Giovanni Battista Cima da Conegliano was a Venetian painter, born around 1459. He painted peaceful altarpieces with bright, clear landscapes of his home hills. He died in 1517.

Q1528580.bio: Giuseppe Pellizza da Volpedo was born in Volpedo, in northern Italy, and lived there much of his life. He painted in the style of dots and fine brushstrokes of pointillism. His masterpiece 'The Fourth Estate' shows workers marching for their rights. He died in 1907 at age 39.

Q271470.bio: Oda Krohg was born in Oslo and was a painter who became a leading figure of the Norwegian bohemian circle. She studied in Paris and Germany. She was married to the painter Christian Krohg. She died in Oslo in 1935.

Q450490.bio: Bernt Notke was a German painter and sculptor born in the Baltic region around 1440. He worked in Lübeck, Tallinn and Stockholm, and made big works for churches, including the Danse Macabre in Tallinn. He died in Lübeck in 1509.

Q11996965.bio: Ragnhild Keyser was a Norwegian painter born in Oslo in 1889, who studied in Norway and Paris. She painted still lifes and landscapes with a quiet, careful style. She died in Oslo in 1943.

Q336747.bio: François Clouet was a French painter born in Tours around 1510. He was the court painter to several kings of France, and he painted neat, careful portraits and miniatures. He died in Paris in 1572.

Q150679.bio: Anthony van Dyck was a Flemish painter born in Antwerp in 1599. He was Rubens's most gifted assistant, traveled to Italy, and in 1632 moved to London as court painter to King Charles I, where he set the style for English portraits. He died in London in 1641 at the age of 42.

Q363968.bio: Fritz von Dardel was a Swedish artist born in Neuchâtel, Switzerland, in 1817. He moved to Stockholm and became a court painter, also known for lively cartoons and sketches of events of his day. He died in Stockholm in 1901.

Q6800323.bio: McClelland Barclay was an American illustrator born in St. Louis in 1891. He became famous for his magazine and poster art, then joined the US Navy as an artist in World War II. He disappeared at sea in 1943 when his ship was sunk.

Q61064.bio: Wassily Kandinsky was born in Moscow and trained as a lawyer before becoming a painter at age 30. He lived in Russia, Germany and later France. He is considered one of the first artists to paint truly abstract works, using color and shape like music. He died in Neuilly-sur-Seine, near Paris, in 1944.

Q353008.bio: Alexei Savrasov was born in Moscow and taught at the Moscow School of Painting. His painting 'The Rooks Have Returned' is often seen as the start of the Russian landscape tradition. He painted ordinary rural scenes with deep feeling. He died in Moscow in 1897.

Q1700176.bio: John Gast was a painter and lithographer born in Berlin, Germany, who worked in Brooklyn, New York. He is known for his 1872 painting 'American Progress', which became a symbol of westward expansion. He died in Brooklyn in 1896.

Q379300.bio: Giovanni Segantini was born in Arco, in the Alps, and became a leading Italian painter of mountain scenes. He lived in the Swiss Alps, painting glowing, detailed landscapes and shepherds. He died at the age of 41 on a mountain peak, in 1899.

Q17169.bio: Giovanni Bellini was a Venetian painter, born in Venice around 1430 into a family of painters. He was the teacher of Giorgione and Titian and led Venetian painting into the High Renaissance with his glowing colors and quiet, thoughtful Madonnas. He worked in Venice all his life and died there in 1516.

Q7781952.bio: Theodore Poulakis was a Greek painter born on Crete in 1622, who moved to the island of Corfu. He painted religious pictures in a mix of Greek and Italian styles. He died in 1692.

Q296265.bio: Filippino Lippi was a Florentine painter born in Prato in 1457. He was the son of the painter Filippo Lippi and trained with Botticelli, and is known for graceful, elegant figures. He died in Florence in 1504.

Q1567177.bio: Michele Gordigiani was an Italian painter born in Florence in 1835. He became a popular portrait painter, painting the English poet Robert Browning and Italian politicians such as Cavour. He lived in Florence and died there in 1909.

Q33477.bio: Eugène Delacroix was born near Paris and became the leading painter of the Romantic movement in France. He lived mostly in Paris, but a trip to Morocco in 1832 filled his sketchbooks with bright colors and scenes that inspired him for life. He believed color and emotion mattered more than perfect outlines. Later artists like Monet and Van Gogh studied his work closely.

Q214062.bio: Joseph Wright of Derby was born in Derby, England, and spent nearly his whole life there. He was famous for painting scenes lit by a single candle or lamp, often showing scientific experiments. His friends included inventors and scientists of the Industrial Revolution. He's often called the first painter to capture the spirit of the Age of Science.

Q253446.bio: Anna Ancher was born in Skagen, Denmark, the daughter of an innkeeper. She became one of the greatest painters of the Skagen artists' colony, known for her use of light, and for her portraits and interiors. She married the painter Michael Ancher and lived her whole life in Skagen. She died there in 1935.

Q43270.bio: Pieter Bruegel the Elder was a Flemish painter born near Breda in about 1525. He lived in Antwerp and Brussels and became famous for crowded paintings of village life, proverbs and landscapes. He died in Brussels in 1569.

Q56660294.bio: Eugène Hamel was born in Quebec City and became a Canadian painter and a portrait artist. He painted people of Wendake and other communities, as well as religious paintings. He lived most of his life in Quebec. He died in 1932.

Q63596.bio: Carl Gustaf Hellqvist was born in Sweden in 1851 and studied in Stockholm and Munich. He painted large history paintings full of drama. He died young, in Munich, at 39.

Q2559361.bio: Jean-François Pierre Peyron was a French painter born in Aix-en-Provence in 1744. He won the Prix de Rome, worked in Rome and became an important early Neoclassical history painter and later a director of the Gobelins tapestry works. He died in Paris in 1814.

Q436726.bio: Ary Scheffer was a French painter born in Dordrecht in the Netherlands in 1795. He moved to Paris as a young man and became a popular Romantic painter of literary and religious scenes, also teaching drawing to the royal family. He died in Argenteuil in 1858.

Q817668.bio: Benjamin Robert Haydon was an English painter born in Plymouth in 1786. He wanted to be a great painter of history, made huge pictures and also lively group portraits, but was always in debt. He lived in London and died there in 1846.

Q375926.bio: Rembrandt Peale was an American painter born in Bucks County, Pennsylvania, in 1778, the son of the painter Charles Willson Peale. He painted portraits of Thomas Jefferson and George Washington, and lived in Philadelphia, where he died in 1860.

Q367895.bio: Adriaen van Stalbemt was a Flemish painter born in Antwerp in 1580. He painted landscapes and scenes of collectors' rooms. He died in Antwerp in 1662.

x-unknown-photographer.bio: The photographer who made this picture is not known. Press photographers and news agencies of the early 1900s often did not record the names of the people who took their photographs.

Q604107.bio: Wilhelm von Kaulbach was a German painter born in Arolsen in 1805. He worked in Munich, where he became head of the art academy and painted huge murals of history and legend for the king of Bavaria. He died in Munich in 1874.

Q185850.bio: C. R. W. Nevinson was an English painter born in London in 1889. He painted the war in the dynamic style of Futurism and was an official war artist in World War I. He lived in London and died in Hampstead in 1946.

Q368546.bio: Domenico Veneziano was an Italian painter, born in Venice around 1410. He worked in Florence, and his paintings are known for their clear, pale and sunny colors. He died in 1461.

Q559559.bio: Fernand Khnopff was born in Belgium and became one of the leading Symbolist painters. He lived in Brussels and designed his own house. His quiet, mysterious pictures often show dreamlike women. He died in Brussels in 1921.

Q2975556.bio: Clarence Gagnon was born in Montreal and studied in Paris. He is best known for his bright, colorful paintings of Quebec villages in winter, and also for illustrating the novel 'Maria Chapdelaine'. He lived part of his life in France and part in Quebec. He died in Montreal in 1942.

Q130531.bio: Hieronymus Bosch was a Dutch painter, born in the town of 's-Hertogenbosch around 1450. He lived there all his life and painted strange, crowded visions of heaven, hell and human foolishness filled with monsters and tiny details. He died in 's-Hertogenbosch in 1516.

Q17325127.n: Master of the Battle of Anghiari
Q17325127.bio: The Master of the Battle of Anghiari is the name given to an unknown Italian painter active in Florence around 1470. He is named after a painted chest panel of the Battle of Anghiari, and made colorful painted wooden chests that were given at weddings.

Q4027439.bio: Harald Slott-Møller was born in Denmark, near Copenhagen, and was a painter and designer. He is known for dreamy Symbolist pictures and portraits. He lived in Copenhagen and was married to the painter Agnes Slott-Møller. He died in 1937.

Q212593.bio: Hendrick Avercamp was a Dutch painter born in Amsterdam in 1585. He was deaf and could not speak, and became famous for his crowded winter scenes of people skating and playing on ice. He died in Kampen in 1634.

Q263080.bio: Hugo Simberg was born in Hamina, Finland, and studied art in Helsinki and Paris. He lived mainly in Finland and painted strange, gentle scenes full of angels, devils, and skeletons, often with a wink of humor. His work blends Finnish folk tales with Symbolism. He died in 1917 at age 43.

Q315102.bio: Alexander Roslin was born in Malmö, Sweden, and became a leading portrait painter at the French court. He lived in Paris, where he painted queens, kings and the leading minds of the day. His specialty was the shimmer of silks and satins. He died in Paris in 1793.

Q13489405.bio: Andrew Carrick Gow was an English painter born in London in 1848. He painted battles and scenes from English history and became a member and later Keeper of the Royal Academy. He died in London in 1920.

Q2757568.bio: Thomas Pollock Anshutz was a painter and teacher born in Kentucky and active in Philadelphia. He taught at the Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts, where his students included Robert Henri and Charles Demuth. He died in 1912.

Q311082.bio: Pisanello was an Italian painter and medal maker, born in about 1395. He painted elegant, detailed pictures of knights, ladies and animals for noble courts, and he invented the portrait medal. He died in about 1455.

Q1273537.bio: Ephraim Moses Lilien was born in Drohobych, in the region of Galicia, then part of Austria, and grew up in a Jewish family. He studied art in Kraków and Munich, and later lived in Berlin. He was an early artist of the Zionist movement and illustrated books with beautiful Art Nouveau designs. He died in Germany in 1925.

Q334200.bio: Christian Krohg was born near Christiania (now Oslo) and was a painter, writer and a leader of the Realist movement in Norway. He studied in Germany and France and painted fishermen, poor people and the sea. He supported social change and caused controversy with his novel and paintings. He died in Oslo in 1925.

Q2408093.bio: Charles-Nicolas Cochin was a French engraver and draftsman born in Paris in 1715. He was an official artist for Louis XV and the keeper of drawings at the Louvre, and he drew the frontispiece of the Encyclopédie. He died in Paris in 1790.

Q274298.bio: Edouard Louis Dubufe was born in Paris to a family of painters. He painted portraits and historical scenes for the French court and nobility. He was a successful society painter in the era of Napoleon III. He died in 1883.

Q151152.bio: Juan Gris was a Spanish painter born in Madrid in 1887. He moved to Paris in 1906, became a friend of Picasso and one of the leading Cubists, painting clear and colorful still lifes. He died in Paris in 1927 at the age of 40.

Q1291901.bio: Tom Roberts was born in England and moved to Australia as a teenager. He was one of the leaders of the Heidelberg School, and he painted some of the most famous pictures of Australian life, including 'Shearing the Rams'. He died in 1931.

Q203371.bio: Georges de La Tour was a French painter born in 1593 in Lorraine. He is known for quiet night scenes lit by a single candle, with smooth, simple shapes. He died in 1652, and was almost forgotten until the 1900s.

x-grigory-shukaev.bio: Grigory Shukaev was a Russian painter of the 1800s who made a picture of the Siege of Sevastopol in 1856, soon after the end of the Crimean War. Not much is known about his life.

Q318393.bio: Vasily Polenov was born in Saint Petersburg, Russia, and became a leading landscape painter and teacher. He traveled in Europe and the Middle East. He built an estate on the Oka River that is now a museum. He died in 1927.

Q1554716.bio: Gunnar Berg was a Norwegian painter born in 1863 in the Lofoten region, known for his scenes of fjords and northern Norway. He studied in Germany. He died young, at 29, in Berlin in 1893.

Q335927.bio: Gerrit Dou was a Dutch painter born in Leiden in 1613. He was Rembrandt's first student, and became famous for tiny, polished pictures with glowing candlelight and very fine detail. He died in 1675.

Q525092.bio: Erik Werenskiold was born in Kongsvinger, Norway, and was one of the leading Norwegian painters of his generation. He is famous for his realistic scenes of Norwegian life and for illustrating Norwegian folk tales with Theodor Kittelsen. He also painted portraits of famous Norwegians. He died in Oslo in 1938.

Q11680193.bio: Benet Mercadé was a Spanish painter born in La Bisbal d'Empordà in Catalonia in 1821. He worked in Rome, where he joined the Nazarene group of painters, and later in Barcelona, where he became a respected teacher. He died in Barcelona in 1897.

Q164735.bio: Johan Christian Dahl was born in Bergen, Norway, and became known as the father of Norwegian landscape painting. He lived most of his life in Dresden, Germany, where he was a friend of Caspar David Friedrich. He painted clouds, mountains and fjords with great realism. He died in Dresden in 1857.

Q762949.bio: August Malmström was born in Sweden and became a painter of Nordic legends, fairy tales and landscapes. He studied in Stockholm and Düsseldorf. He later directed the Swedish National Museum's art school. He died in Stockholm in 1901.

Q9342.bio: Palma Vecchio was a Venetian painter, born near Bergamo in about 1480. He painted rich portraits of women with golden hair and warm skin and tones. He died in 1528.

Q1415196.bio: Jean-Jacques Scherrer was a French painter born in Lutterbach in Alsace in 1855. He worked in Paris, painting historical and patriotic pictures, especially of Joan of Arc, at a time when she was a national symbol after the war of 1870. He died in Paris in 1916.

Q17627030.bio: Robert Herdman was a Scottish painter born in Rattray in Perthshire in 1829. He lived in Edinburgh and painted scenes from Scottish history and everyday life, and became a leading member of the Royal Scottish Academy. He died in Edinburgh in 1888.

Q242121.bio: Alexandra Exter was a Ukrainian-born Russian artist, born in Białystok in 1882. She knew the Cubists in Paris, taught in Kyiv and Moscow, and designed colorful scenery and costumes for theaters. She moved to France in 1924 and died near Paris in 1949.

Q365068.bio: P. S. Krøyer was born in Stavanger, Norway, and grew up in Copenhagen, Denmark. He was the central figure of the Skagen Painters, an artist colony in northern Denmark. His paintings capture the beautiful blue light of summer evenings by the sea. He died in Skagen in 1909.

Q483992.bio: William-Adolphe Bouguereau was born in La Rochelle, on France's Atlantic coast, and studied in Paris and Rome. He became the most celebrated painter of the French Academy, famous for smooth, glowing figures from myths and everyday life. He taught thousands of students. When Impressionism rose, he fell from fashion, but his technical skill is again widely admired.

Q2926650.bio: Bruno Bobak was a Canadian painter born in Poland in 1923. He grew up in Canada and served as an official Canadian war artist in World War II, then taught art in Fredericton, New Brunswick, where he lived until his death in 2012.

Q176694.bio: Antonis Mor was a Dutch painter born in Utrecht in about 1517. He became the court portrait painter to the Habsburgs and painted Philip II of Spain and Queen Mary I of England, working in Brussels, Madrid and London. He died in Antwerp in about 1577.

Q1441399.bio: Francis Bicknell Carpenter was an American painter born in Homer, New York, in 1830. He lived for six months at the White House in 1864 to paint Abraham Lincoln and his cabinet, and he died in New York City in 1900.

Q3568797.bio: Will Longstaff was an Australian painter born in Ballarat in 1879. He served in World War I and then painted memorials to the missing, including Menin Gate at Midnight, which toured Australia and Britain. He died in Littlehampton, England, in 1953.

Q4215366.bio: James Wilson Carmichael was an English painter born in Newcastle upon Tyne in 1799. He started as a sailor and became a well-known painter of ships, sea battles and harbor scenes, and moved to London. He died in Scarborough in 1868.

Q1658589.bio: Ilya Chashnik was a Russian artist born in Ludza, now in Latvia, in 1902. He was a student of Kazimir Malevich and worked in the Suprematist group in Vitebsk and Petrograd, painting geometric shapes and designing porcelain. He died in 1929 at the age of 26.

Q434575.bio: Arthur Hughes was born in London and was an English painter linked to the Pre-Raphaelites. He is best known for glowing, romantic scenes of young lovers and medieval stories. He worked in London and in the countryside, and he also illustrated children's books. He died in 1915.

Q34661.bio: Gustav Klimt was born near Vienna, Austria, the son of a gold engraver, which may be why gold glitters in so many of his paintings. He lived his entire life in and around Vienna and co-founded the Vienna Secession, a group of artists who broke from tradition. He painted beautiful portraits, murals, and landscapes. He died in 1918 at age 55 after a stroke.

Q727637.bio: Wojciech Kossak was a Polish painter born in Paris in 1856 who lived in Kraków. He painted battle scenes, horses and moments from Poland's history, as part of a family of artists. He died in Kraków in 1942.

Q37140565.bio: Julian O. Davidson was an American marine painter born in Cumberland, Maryland, in 1853. He lived in New York, painting sea scenes and naval battles of the Civil War for popular prints. He died in 1894.

Q263025.bio: Harriet Backer was born in Holmestrand, Norway, and became one of the country's greatest painters. She studied in Munich and Paris and became famous for her glowing pictures of rooms and churches. She also ran a painting school that trained many young artists. She died in Oslo in 1932.

Q2832922.bio: Alex Colville was a Canadian painter born in Toronto in 1920. He was an official Canadian war artist in World War II, painting the Netherlands and the liberation of Bergen-Belsen, and later became famous for calm, mysterious pictures. He lived in Nova Scotia and died in Wolfville in 2013.

Q538350.bio: Maarten van Heemskerck was a Dutch painter born in the village of Heemskerk in 1498. He lived in Haarlem but traveled to Rome from 1532 to 1536, where he drew the ancient ruins, and these drawings are now an important record of Renaissance Rome. He died in Haarlem in 1574.

Q44054.bio: Franz Marc was born in Munich, Germany, and loved painting animals as a symbol of purity. He co-founded the Blue Rider group with Wassily Kandinsky, and he used bold colors like blue and yellow to express feelings. He lived in Bavaria. He died in World War I in 1916 at age 36.

Q69708.bio: Charles de Steuben was a German-born French painter born in Bauerbach in 1788. He moved to Paris as a child and became a leading painter of dramatic history pictures, including many for the palace of Versailles. He died in Paris in 1856.

Q1278282.bio: Eastman Johnson was an American painter born in Lovell, Maine, in 1824. He studied in Düsseldorf and The Hague, lived in New York and painted warm scenes of American life, including pictures related to the Civil War. He died in New York City in 1906.

Q2059687.bio: Paul Fürst was a German engraver and publisher born in Nuremberg in 1608. He made popular prints, including the famous image of a plague doctor in a beaked mask, and lived in Nuremberg until he died in 1666.

Q762.bio: Leonardo da Vinci was an Italian painter, inventor and scientist, born in 1452. He painted the Mona Lisa and The Last Supper, and filled thousands of notebook pages with drawings of flying machines, anatomy, water and plants. He died in France in 1519.

Q550302.bio: Nicolas de Largillière was a French painter, born in Paris in 1656. He trained in Antwerp and London, and became one of the most successful portrait painters of his time, painting rich dresses and sparkling jewelry. He died in 1746.

Q316731.bio: Federico Barocci was an Italian painter born in Urbino in 1535. He painted soft, warm, sweet pictures of the Holy Family with pink and blue colors and loving faces. He died in 1612.

Q1795226.bio: Walenty Wańkowicz was born in a village in what is now Belarus and studied in Vilnius. He became a Polish painter famous for portraits of poets, including Adam Mickiewicz. He lived in Saint Petersburg and in Paris. He died in Paris in 1842.

Q11478804.bio: Kawamura Kiyoo was a Japanese painter born in Edo in 1852. He studied Western-style painting in Italy and helped bring oil painting to Japan. He painted historical scenes and legends. He died in 1934.

Q2775516.bio: James Wilson Morrice was born in Montreal and spent most of his life in Paris, where he became a friend of Matisse. He painted quiet landscapes and city scenes in bright, simple colors, and also traveled to North Africa and the Caribbean. He is regarded as Canada's first modern painter. He died in Tunis in 1924.

Q203828.bio: Gustave Moreau was born in Paris and became a leading Symbolist painter. He painted glittering scenes from myth and the Bible, with fantastic detail. He later taught at the École des Beaux-Arts, where Matisse was a student. His Paris house is now a museum.

Q7173913.bio: Peter F. Rothermel was an American painter born in Nescopeck, Pennsylvania, in 1812. He worked in Philadelphia, where he painted huge canvases of historical subjects, including the Battle of Gettysburg for the state of Pennsylvania. He died in Linfield, Pennsylvania, in 1895.

Q273115.bio: Anna Bilińska-Bohdanowicz was born in Ukraine, then part of the Russian Empire, to a Polish family and studied in Saint Petersburg, Munich and Paris. She lived in Warsaw and was one of the first Polish women to win international acclaim as a painter. She painted portraits and scenes in a modern style. She died young, in 1893, at age 39.

Q680528.bio: Joseph Légaré was born in Quebec City and was one of the first painters in Canada to paint landscapes and historical events. He collected European paintings and taught himself by copying them. He was also a politician and a businessman. He died in 1855.

Q110228.bio: Vasily Surikov was born in Krasnoyarsk, in Siberia, and moved to Moscow and Saint Petersburg. He painted huge history scenes of Russia's past with crowds of vivid individuals. His paintings are among Russia's most loved. He died in Moscow in 1916.

Q142398.bio: Francesco Rosselli was an engraver, painter and map maker born in Florence in about 1445. He is best known for his early views and maps of cities, including a view of Naples. He died in 1513.

Q979541.bio: Martinus Rørbye was born in Drammen, Norway, and moved to Denmark as a child. He was a leading painter of the Danish Golden Age and traveled to Italy, Greece, and Turkey. He painted precise scenes of streets, interiors and windows. He died in Copenhagen in 1848.

Q3174641.bio: Jean-Simon Berthélemy was a French painter born in Laon in 1743. He worked in Paris, where he painted large history pictures for the royal court and, later, for the Revolution and Napoleon. He died in Paris in 1811.

Q347220.bio: Fujishima Takeji was born in Kagoshima, Japan, and became one of the first Japanese painters to master Western oil painting. He studied in Paris and Rome. He later taught art in Tokyo. He died in Tokyo in 1943.

Q2856626.bio: Antoine Plamondon was born near Quebec City and studied painting in Paris in the 1830s. He became one of the most important portrait painters in Quebec, painting priests, nuns and political leaders. He taught many younger artists. He died in 1895.

Q5827.bio: Pietro Perugino was an Italian painter, born near Perugia in about 1448. He painted calm, sweet figures in wide, airy landscapes, and he taught Raphael. He died in 1523.

Q3196514.bio: Suzuki Kiitsu was born in Edo (Tokyo) and studied under Sakai Hōitsu. He painted flowers, plants and scenes of nature in the Rinpa style, with bold colors and graceful shapes. He is admired for his modern-looking designs. He died in 1858.

Q64633.bio: George Peter Alexander Healy was born in Boston and became a portrait painter who worked in Paris, Rome, Chicago and Washington. He painted American presidents and the kings and queens of Europe. He lived long in Europe before settling in Chicago. He died there in 1894.

Q553259.bio: Marsden Hartley was an American painter born in Lewiston, Maine, in 1877. He traveled to Paris and Berlin, where he made bold abstract paintings of flags, symbols and military insignia, and later returned to paint his native Maine. He died in Ellsworth, Maine, in 1943.

Q18289401.bio: Eugène Romain Thirion was a French painter born in Paris in 1839. He painted religious and historical scenes and portraits, and is best known for his poetic picture of Joan of Arc. He lived in Paris and died there in 1910.

Q902649.bio: David Klöcker Ehrenstrahl was a painter born in Hamburg in 1628. He became the royal painter of Sweden and painted portraits and big allegories for the court. He died in Stockholm in 1698.

x-johannes-vingboons.bio: Johannes Vingboons was a Dutch mapmaker and painter born in Amsterdam around 1616. He drew maps and views of the world for the Dutch West India Company, including early views of New Amsterdam, now New York. He lived in Amsterdam and died there around 1670.

Q1346539.bio: Lars Hertervig was born on an island near Stavanger, Norway, and studied in Düsseldorf. He struggled with mental illness, was often poor, and was little understood in his lifetime. His glowing, dreamy landscapes are now seen as among the finest in Norwegian art. He died in Stavanger in 1902.

Q2090482.bio: Alfred Jacob Miller was an American painter born in Baltimore in 1810. In 1837 he traveled west to the Rocky Mountains and made the first paintings of the fur trade and Native American life there. He lived in Baltimore and died there in 1874.

Q336908.bio: Meindert Hobbema was a Dutch landscape painter, born in Amsterdam in 1638. He is best known for peaceful pictures of country roads, watermills and trees. He died in 1709.

Q142420.bio: Edmund Blair Leighton was born in London and became famous for painting romantic scenes from the Middle Ages and the Regency period. He studied at the Royal Academy and lived in London. His paintings of knights and ladies are widely reproduced. He died in 1922.

x-stepan-mukharsky.bio: Stepan Mukharsky was a Russian artist who made posters for the Soviet government during and after the Russian Civil War. His bright, cartoon-like posters were made to explain the revolution to people who could not read.

x-nasa.bio: NASA, the National Aeronautics and Space Administration, was created in 1958 and organized the American space program, including the Mercury, Gemini and Apollo missions. Its photographs, made by employees of the US government, belong to the public.

Q94297287.bio: Jacques Bertaux was a French painter born in Harcy in the 1740s. He worked in Paris, and is best remembered for a vivid painting of the storming of the Tuileries Palace on August 10, 1792, which he made while the events were fresh.

Q727060.bio: Victor Meirelles was born in Florianópolis, Brazil, and studied in Rio de Janeiro and Europe. He painted large pictures of the history of Brazil, such as 'The First Mass in Brazil'. He died in Rio de Janeiro in 1903.

Q2149073.bio: Victor Honoré Janssens was a Flemish painter born in Brussels in 1658. He painted historical, mythological and religious pictures for churches and nobles in Brussels, where he lived and worked until he died in 1736.

Q192488.bio: Paolo Uccello was a Florentine painter born in about 1397. He was so crazy about the new science of perspective that he filled his pictures with lances, broken spears and tiled floors that line up to a point. He died in 1475.

Q380704.bio: Bartholomeus van der Helst was a Dutch painter born in Haarlem in 1613. He moved to Amsterdam, where he became one of the most successful portrait painters of his time, rivaling Rembrandt. He died in Amsterdam in 1670.

Q504949.bio: Giovanni Battista Moroni was an Italian painter, born around 1520 near Bergamo. He painted honest, quiet portraits of ordinary and noble people. He died in 1578.

Q5233531.bio: David Fairrington was an American artist born in 1940 who served as a member of the US Army's Vietnam combat art team in 1968. His paintings of soldiers, helicopters and Vietnamese people are in the US Army art collection.

Q169311.bio: Johann Friedrich Overbeck was born in Lübeck, Germany, and moved to Rome, where he led the Nazarenes, a group of artists inspired by medieval and early Renaissance painting. He lived in a former monastery with his friends. He stayed in Rome the rest of his life and died there in 1869.

Q561205.bio: Raphael was an Italian painter born in Urbino in 1483. He worked in Florence and then in Rome, where he painted the Vatican's famous rooms, and with Leonardo and Michelangelo he is counted among the three giants of the High Renaissance. He died in Rome in 1520 at the age of only 37.

Q13422424.bio: Fredrik Borgen was a Norwegian landscape painter born in 1852, known for paintings of winter scenes and evening light. He studied in Germany. He died in Christiania in 1907.

Q355213.bio: Gabriel Metsu was a Dutch painter born in Leiden in 1629. He painted quiet pictures of people reading and writing letters and shopping, in neat houses. He died in Amsterdam in 1667.

Q833333.bio: Jakob Bogdani was a painter born in Prešov, in modern Slovakia, in 1658. He moved to England and was famous for his colorful pictures of birds and fruit. He died in 1724.

Q3106117.bio: Lawren Harris was born in Brantford, Ontario, and was a founding member of the Group of Seven. He became known for his bold, simple paintings of Lake Superior, the Rocky Mountains and the Arctic. His work shaped the idea of the Canadian landscape. He died in Vancouver in 1970.

Q449519.bio: Richard Dadd was born in Chatham, England, and became a talented painter before he fell seriously ill in his twenties. He spent the rest of his life in hospitals, where he kept painting amazing, tiny, detailed fairy pictures. He lived in Bethlem and then Broadmoor Hospital. He died in 1886.

Q1661665.bio: John Vanderlyn was born in Kingston, New York, and studied art in Paris. He was one of the first American painters to be trained in Europe, and painted large panoramas and history pictures. He painted 'Landing of Columbus' for the U.S. Capitol. He died in Kingston in 1852.

Q130777.bio: Kazimir Malevich was born near Kyiv, in what is now Ukraine, to a family of Polish origin. He lived in Moscow and Saint Petersburg and founded Suprematism, an art of pure shapes and colors. He also taught, wrote, and designed. After the Russian government turned against modern art, he was forced to return to simple realist styles before his death in 1935.

Q213163.bio: Élisabeth Louise Vigée Le Brun was born in Paris, the daughter of a painter, and became a famous portraitist at only 20. She painted Queen Marie Antoinette and fled France during the Revolution, working in Italy, Austria, Russia and England. She was one of the most successful women artists in history. She died in Paris in 1842.

Q1543513.bio: Eugène Lenepveu was a French painter born in Angers in 1819. He won the Prix de Rome, directed the French Academy in Rome for several years, and painted a famous series of scenes from the life of Joan of Arc in the Panthéon in Paris. He died in Paris in 1898.

x-english-school-formerly-attributed-to-.n: English School (formerly attributed to George Gower)
x-english-school-formerly-attributed-to-.bio: The Armada Portrait was painted by an unknown English artist in 1588. It was once thought to be by George Gower, Queen Elizabeth's Serjeant-Painter, but experts now believe it came from a workshop of several painters, and it exists in a few versions.

Q702272.bio: Johann Zoffany was born in Frankfurt, Germany, and moved to London. He painted 'conversation pieces' — groups of people in rooms and gardens — as well as theatrical scenes. He traveled to Italy and India, and became a favorite of the British royal family. He died in London in 1810.

Q45006.bio: Franz von Stuck was born in Bavaria, Germany, and became a celebrated painter and teacher in Munich. He was a founding member of the Munich Secession and painted mysterious and powerful symbolic pictures. Kandinsky and Klee were among his students. He lived in a grand villa in Munich, which is now a museum.

Q452733.bio: Amaldus Nielsen was a Norwegian landscape painter who painted the wild mountains and fjords of Norway. He studied in Düsseldorf and Munich. He lived to the age of 94 and died in Oslo in 1932.

Q193064.bio: Ivan Shishkin was born in the town of Yelabuga, in Russia, and became the great poet of the Russian forest. He lived in Saint Petersburg and traveled into the countryside to sketch trees in incredible detail. His pine and birch forests are among the most loved Russian paintings. He worked up until the day he died at his easel in 1898.

Q7751.bio: Giuseppe Arcimboldo was an Italian painter, born in Milan in 1527. He is famous for portraits made of fruit, vegetables, flowers, fish and books, which work as faces when you look from far away. He worked for the Habsburg emperors in Vienna and Prague and died in 1593.

Q123098.bio: Angelica Kauffman was born in Chur, Switzerland, and was a child prodigy who traveled across Europe as a teen artist. She lived in Italy and London, where she became a founding member of the Royal Academy of Arts. She painted portraits and scenes from myth and history. She died in Rome in 1807.

Q2837691.bio: Aaron Allan Edson was born in Quebec and became a Canadian landscape painter who painted the forests and mountains of the east. He lived in Montreal and worked in Quebec and New England. His quiet, glowing landscapes were very popular. He died in 1888.

Q3034741.bio: Domenico Induno was an Italian painter born in Milan in 1815, the older brother of Gerolamo Induno. He painted scenes of everyday life and portraits of Risorgimento heroes. He lived in Milan and died there in 1878.

Q594345.bio: Samuel Hirszenberg was born in Łódź, Poland, to a Jewish family and studied in Kraków, Munich and Paris. His large paintings show the suffering and hopes of Jewish people in Eastern Europe. In 1907 he moved to Jerusalem to teach at the new Bezalel art school. He died there the next year.

Q237726.bio: Rosalba Carriera was a Venetian painter born in 1675, who was famous for portraits in soft pastel chalk. She was welcomed in Paris, Vienna and Venice, and she was one of the first women to be admitted to the French Academy. She died in 1757.

Q712821.bio: Nicolas Froment was a French painter born in Uzès in about 1430. He worked in Avignon and for King René of Anjou, and painted lifelike portraits and altarpieces. He died in about 1484.

Q161145.bio: Horace Vernet was a French painter born in Paris in 1789. He painted many battles of Napoleon and the French army, and lived in Rome and Paris, where he died in 1863.

x-illustrator-b-h.bio: This print was made by an illustrator who signed it with the initials B&H. Prints like this appeared in magazines and books to show readers far away what the West looked like.

Q207758.bio: Ivan Kramskoi was born in Ostrogozhsk, Russia, and worked in Saint Petersburg. He was a leader of the Wanderers, artists who rebelled against stuffy academic rules. He painted deeply felt portraits of writers, scholars and ordinary people. He also wrote and taught about art, and he inspired a generation of Russian painters.

Q3786446.bio: Homer Watson was born in Doon, Ontario, near what is now Kitchener, and taught himself to paint. He became known for his dramatic pictures of fields, skies and rivers, and was admired by Oscar Wilde. He is considered a pioneer of Canadian landscape painting. He died in Kitchener in 1936.

Q6682.bio: Gustave Doré was a French artist born in Strasbourg in 1832. He became the most famous book illustrator of his time, drawing scenes for the Bible, Dante's Inferno, Don Quixote and fairy tales. He lived in Paris and died there in 1883.

Q3680885.bio: Francis William Edmonds was an American painter born in Hudson, New York, in 1806. He was a banker who painted in his spare time, making charming scenes of everyday life. He lived in New York and died in Bronxville in 1863.

Q235903.bio: Evelyn De Morgan was born in London and studied at the Slade School of Art. She was a Pre-Raphaelite painter who painted glowing allegories about peace, war and the spirit. She lived in London and Florence and was also a pacifist and a supporter of women's rights. She died in 1919.

Q3123472.bio: Martin Johnson Heade was born in Pennsylvania and traveled widely. He is famous for his misty salt marshes, stormy skies, and his paintings of hummingbirds and orchids in Brazil. He settled in Florida late in life. He died in St. Augustine in 1904.

Q1936604.bio: Reinier Nooms, also called Zeeman, was a Dutch painter and etcher born in Amsterdam around 1623. He had been a sailor, and he made detailed pictures of ships, harbors and sea battles. He died in Amsterdam in 1664.

Q76824158.bio: Guadalupe Carpio was a Mexican painter born in Xalapa in 1828, and one of the first women to study at the Academy of San Carlos in Mexico City. She painted portraits and scenes of daily life. She died in 1892.

Q29032736.bio: Elisabeth Sinding was a Norwegian painter born in 1846, and one of the earlier women painters in her country. She painted landscapes and portraits. She lived in Oslo until her death in 1930.

Q718020.bio: Hans Heyerdahl was born in Norway, to a family of Norwegian-Swedish roots, and studied in Copenhagen, Munich and Paris. He painted portraits and religious paintings with a clear, quiet realism. He became one of the leading Norwegian painters of his generation. He died in Oslo in 1913.

Q921230.bio: Johan Thomas Lundbye was a Danish painter born in Kalundborg in 1818. He painted fields, animals and old monuments of the Danish countryside. He died young, at 29, in 1848, during the first Schleswig War.

Q313498.bio: Benjamin West was born near Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, and moved to Europe in his twenties. He settled in London, where he became the history painter to King George III and later President of the Royal Academy. He taught many American painters. He died in London in 1820.

Q380706.bio: Vilhelm Hammershøi was born in Copenhagen and became famous for his quiet, gray pictures of empty rooms and of his wife Ida. His soft colors and calm mood are unforgettable. He lived and worked in Copenhagen all his life. He died in 1916.

Q209615.bio: Francisco de Zurbarán was a Spanish painter born in 1598. He painted monks, saints and still lifes with strong light and deep shadows, and a calm, simple look. He died in Madrid in 1664.

Q578067.bio: Hendrick Cornelisz Vroom was a Dutch painter born in Haarlem in 1562. He is often called the father of Dutch marine painting, and made pictures of ships and sea battles for admirals and the government. He lived in Haarlem and died there in 1640.

Q8459.bio: Giorgione was a Venetian painter born around 1478, who died very young, around 1510. He painted dreamy landscapes and moody portraits, and only a handful of his works survive. His soft style helped shape the work of his friend Titian.

Q1284465.bio: Charles Conder was born in England and raised in Australia. He became a member of the Heidelberg School at a young age. He later moved to Paris and London and painted silk fans and delicate landscapes. He died in London in 1909.

Q514628.bio: Russell Lee was an American photographer born in Ottawa, Illinois, in 1903. He worked for the Farm Security Administration, took thousands of pictures of rural life in the 1930s and 1940s, and later taught photography in Texas. He died in Austin in 1986.

Q506483.bio: Sebastiano Ricci was an Italian painter, born in Belluno in 1659. He painted bright, airy pictures and traveled to London and Paris to decorate palaces. He died in Venice in 1734.

Q2286906.bio: Joseph-Siffred Duplessis was a French painter born in Carpentras in 1725. He became one of the best portrait painters in Paris, painting Louis XVI and the American Benjamin Franklin, and he was the curator of the royal paintings at Versailles. He died there in 1802.

Q1391078.bio: John Frederick Lewis was an English painter born in London in 1805. He traveled to Spain and the Middle East, lived in Cairo from 1841 to 1851, and became famous for detailed scenes of Eastern life. He died in Walton-on-Thames in 1876.

x-unknown-artist.bio: The artist of this work is not known. Many early portraits, prints and manuscripts were made by artists whose names were never recorded or have since been lost.

Q1009816.bio: Gerhard Munthe was a Norwegian painter and designer, born in 1849. He was a leader in reviving Norwegian folk art and illustrated Norse sagas. His bright, decorative style influenced Norwegian design. He died in Lysaker in 1929.

x-john-of-kastav.bio: John of Kastav, in Croatian Ivan iz Kastva, was a painter from the town of Kastav in what is now Croatia, active in the late 1400s. In 1490 he painted the Dance of Death wall painting in the church of Hrastovlje in Slovenia, and very little else is known of his life.

Q16228969.bio: Xu Yang was a court painter in China in the 1700s, born in Suzhou. He painted big, detailed scrolls recording life in the city and the Qianlong Emperor's travels. His pictures are treasured as history. He lived and worked in the Qing court.

Q209050.bio: Jan Brueghel the Elder was a Flemish painter born in Brussels in 1568, the son of the famous Pieter Bruegel the Elder. He lived in Antwerp, was a friend and partner of Rubens, and became known as 'Velvet' Brueghel for his soft, delicate paintings of landscapes and flowers. He died in Antwerp in 1625.

Q356777.bio: Dosso Dossi was an Italian painter born around 1480, who worked for the dukes of Ferrara. His pictures are full of magic, mystery and bright colors. He died in 1542.

Q1805696.bio: Sébastien Leclerc was a French engraver born in Metz in 1637. He worked in Paris for Louis XIV, making many prints of the king's science and military projects. He died in Paris in 1714.

Q390904.bio: Luc-Olivier Merson was a French painter born in Paris in 1846. He won the Prix de Rome in 1869 with his picture of the runner of Marathon, then taught at the École des Beaux-Arts and also designed banknotes and stamps. He lived and worked in Paris until he died in 1920.

x-works-progress-administration-poster-a.bio: This poster was made by an artist working for the Works Progress Administration, a New Deal program that hired thousands of artists in the 1930s to make posters, murals and prints for the public.

Q652305.bio: Johann Moritz Rugendas was a German painter born in Augsburg in 1802. He traveled and lived in Brazil, Mexico and Chile, producing many sketches of landscapes, daily life and the lives of enslaved people. He died in Weilheim an der Teck in 1858.

Q40599.bio: Édouard Manet was born into a wealthy Parisian family and lived in Paris all his life. He painted modern city life — cafés, bars, and picnics — in a bold, flat style that scandalized critics. He never officially joined the Impressionists, but he inspired them, and they admired him as a leader. He died in 1883 at age 51.

Q2116186.bio: Albert Eckhout was a Dutch painter born in about 1610. He was sent to Brazil in 1637 by a Dutch governor, and he painted the people, plants and animals he saw there in great detail. He died in 1666.

Q5944348.bio: José María Obregón was born in Mexico City and studied at the Academy of San Carlos. He painted historical scenes, including 'The Discovery of Pulque', and was a leading artist in his country. He died in 1902.

Q711770.bio: Dirck van Delen was a Dutch painter born in Heusden in 1605. He specialized in imaginary views of church and palace interiors, and lived for most of his life in Arnemuiden and Middelburg in Zeeland. He died in Middelburg in 1671.

Q123071.bio: Arnold Böcklin was born in Basel, Switzerland, and spent long periods in Italy and Germany. He painted dreamy scenes full of myths, strange creatures and mysterious islands. He is best known for 'Isle of the Dead'. He died near Florence in 1901.

Q1065418.bio: Charles Marion Russell was an American painter born in St. Louis in 1864. He moved to Montana as a teenager, worked as a cowboy and lived among the Blackfeet, then became the most famous painter of the Old West. He lived in Great Falls, where he died in 1926.

Q3290536.bio: Margaretha Haverman was a Dutch painter born in Breda in 1693, who painted flower pictures. She moved to Paris and was admitted to the French Academy in 1722, but was soon accused of fraud and left. She died in about 1723.

Q155158.bio: Kurt Schwitters was a German artist born in Hanover in 1887. He made collages and sculptures from scraps and trash that he called Merz, and also wrote poems and designed his own Merz Building. He left Germany when the Nazis came to power, lived in Norway and then in England, and died in Ambleside in 1948.
