Q372277.bio: Alexey Bogolyubov was a Russian painter born in 1824 in the Novgorod region. He painted seas and ships, served as a painter for the Russian navy, and lived for many years in Paris, where he died in 1896.

Q821537.bio: Karl Friedrich Lessing was a German painter born in Breslau in 1808. He worked in Düsseldorf, where he painted dramatic scenes from the Reformation and medieval history, and later directed the art gallery in Karlsruhe. He died in Karlsruhe in 1880.

Q15520500.bio: Thomas Davies was a British army officer and artist born in Shooter's Hill, near London, in 1737. He served in Canada and the American colonies and made watercolors of what he saw, which are some of the earliest views of North America. He died in Blackheath in 1812.

x-florentine-painter.bio: This picture was painted by an unknown Florentine artist, shortly after the events it shows, in the 1490s. Many Florentine workshops made pictures for sale, and artists did not always sign them.

Q1606486.bio: Henry Bacon was an American painter born in Haverhill, Massachusetts, in 1839. He fought in the Civil War, then lived in Paris for most of his life, painting scenes from American history and Egypt. He died in Cairo in 1912.

Q167220.bio: Cornelis Cort was a Dutch engraver born in Hoorn in 1533. He moved to Venice and then Rome, where he made prints after famous paintings by Titian, Raphael and others, spreading their compositions across Europe. He died in Rome around 1575.

Q8511.bio: Lorenzo di Credi was a Florentine painter born in 1459. He worked with Leonardo da Vinci in the workshop of Andrea del Verrocchio, and painted smooth, polished pictures. He died in 1537.

Q1342328.bio: Michiel Sweerts was a Flemish painter born in Brussels in 1618. He worked in Rome, where he painted busy city scenes, and later in Brussels and Amsterdam, before joining a missionary journey to Asia. He died in Goa, India, in 1664.

Q1963206.bio: William Frederick Yeames was an English painter born in Taganrog, Russia, in 1835, where his father was British consul. He moved to London and painted historical pictures, becoming a member of the Royal Academy. He died in Teignmouth in 1918.

Q984242.bio: Louis-Maurice Boutet de Monvel was a French artist born in Orléans in 1850. He became famous as an illustrator of children's books, including a beautiful book about Joan of Arc in 1896, and also painted portraits in Paris, where he died in 1913.

Q2048640.bio: Alonzo Chappel was an American painter and engraver born in New York City in 1828. He made hundreds of portraits and historical scenes of American history for books and prints. He lived and worked in New York and died in 1887.

x-henri-ambrosius-pacx.bio: Henri Ambrosius Pacx was a painter who made a picture of Prince Maurice of Orange at the Battle of Nieuwpoort in the 1800s, long after the battle itself. Very little is known about his life.

Q983492.bio: Mårten Eskil Winge was born in Stockholm and became a leading Swedish history painter. He studied in Düsseldorf and Paris and painted subjects from Norse mythology. He died in Enköping in 1896.

Q771658.bio: Juan Bautista Martínez del Mazo was a Spanish painter born in around 1611. He was the son-in-law and assistant of Diego Velázquez and became the court painter to King Philip IV after Velázquez's death. He died in Madrid in 1667.

Q381728.bio: George Stubbs was born in Liverpool, England, and taught himself to paint. He studied horse anatomy by dissecting horses and published a famous book about it. He became Britain's finest painter of horses and other animals. He died in London in 1806.

x-british-school.bio: This painting is by an unknown English artist working in the 1540s. Many English paintings of the time were made by artists whose names have not survived, and later experts label them with the name 'British School' or 'English School'.

Q380726.bio: Reza Abbasi was a Persian painter, born in about 1565. He worked at the court of Shah Abbas the Great in Isfahan, and painted elegant figures in graceful lines. He died in 1635.

Q380052.bio: Mariano Fortuny Marsal was born in Reus, Spain, and became one of the best-known Spanish painters of the 1800s. He traveled to Morocco and painted bright, detailed scenes. He lived in Rome and Madrid, and died young in Rome in 1874, at age 36.

Q159606.bio: John Everett Millais was born in Southampton, England, and was a child prodigy who entered the Royal Academy at 11. He co-founded the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood, a group that painted with bright color and fine detail. Later he became a famous society painter and was made a baronet, the first artist to receive that honor. He ended his life as President of the Royal Academy in London.

Q3340395.bio: Nicolas-Guy Brenet was a French painter born in Paris in 1728. He studied in Rome and became a history painter, painting scenes from ancient and national history for the French royal court. He died in Paris in 1792.

Q3286980.bio: Robert Gibb was a Scottish painter born in Edinburgh in 1845. He painted battles and military scenes, became the Painter and Limner to the Queen in Scotland and was Keeper of the National Gallery of Scotland. He died in Edinburgh in 1932.

Q213612.bio: Jacob van Ruisdael was a Dutch landscape painter born in Haarlem in 1628. He painted windmills, forests, waterfalls and giant stormy skies, and his work inspired later painters like John Constable. He died in 1682.

Q312617.bio: Rosso Fiorentino was a Florentine painter born in 1494 with wild red hair. He painted jagged, strange and colorful pictures, and went to France to decorate the palace at Fontainebleau for King Francis I. He died there in 1540.

Q561783.bio: Pedro Berruguete was a Spanish painter, born around 1450, who worked in Spain and Italy. He brought Italian Renaissance ideas to Spanish painting and died in 1504.

Q1494309.bio: Alphonse de Neuville was a French painter born in Saint-Omer in 1835. He became known for realistic scenes of the Franco-Prussian War, in which he had served, and for illustrating books. He lived in Paris and died there in 1885.

Q528460.bio: Jozef Israëls was born into a Jewish family in Groningen, in the Netherlands, and became the leader of the Hague School of painters. He is famous for his tender pictures of fisherfolk and poor families in the dunes. He lived in Amsterdam and The Hague, and spent many summers in the fishing village of Zandvoort. He died in 1911.

Q388523.bio: Peter von Hess was a German painter born in Düsseldorf in 1792. He worked in Munich and became the leading battle painter of Bavaria, painting scenes of the Napoleonic wars and the Greek War of Independence. He died in Munich in 1871.

Q11705308.bio: William Brymner was born in Scotland and raised in Canada. He studied in Paris and became an influential teacher at the Art Association of Montreal, where he taught many of the country's best-known painters. His own paintings show women and children in warm, soft light. He died in 1925.

Q128534.bio: Fredrik Kolstø was a Norwegian painter born in 1860 in the region of Haugesund and studied in Paris. He painted historical and landscape pictures. He lived in Trondheim for part of his life. He died in 1945.

Q3048418.bio: Edvard Isto was born in northern Finland and became a painter who studied in Helsinki and Paris. He is best known for 'The Attack,' which became a symbol of Finnish resistance. He died in Helsinki in 1905, at the age of 40.

Q265665.bio: Pierre Auguste Cot was born in the south of France and became a popular painter in Paris. He studied with Bouguereau and painted romantic and mythological subjects. His paintings were very popular in America. He died in 1883.

Q1659496.bio: Kamal-ol-Molk was born in Kashan, Iran, in 1848 and became the court painter of the Qajar kings. He studied European painting and painted portraits and scenes of daily life with great realism. He later founded an art school in Tehran. He died in Nishapur in 1940.

Q5592.bio: Michelangelo was born in Caprese, Italy, in 1475 and worked in Florence and Rome. He was a sculptor, painter and architect who made the statue of David and painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel. He died in Rome in 1564, almost 89 years old.

Q155626.bio: John Singer Sargent was born in Florence, Italy, to American parents and grew up traveling around Europe. He trained in Paris, then worked mostly in London, becoming the most sought-after portrait painter of his day. He painted with dazzling, confident brushwork and also made lovely watercolors on trips to Venice and the Alps. During World War I he painted soldiers at the front. He died in London in 1925.

Q160422.bio: Theo van Doesburg was a Dutch artist born in Utrecht in 1883. In 1917 he founded the magazine De Stijl with Piet Mondrian and others, promoting art made of straight lines and primary colors, and he also designed buildings and stained glass. He lived in the Netherlands, France and Germany and died in Davos, Switzerland, in 1931.

Q719668.bio: Hasegawa Tōhaku was a Japanese painter born in 1539. He painted giant folding screens and sliding doors for temples and warlords, and is best known for his misty ink painting of pine trees. He died in 1610.

Q319843.bio: Ford Madox Brown was born in Calais, France, to English parents and trained in Belgium before settling in London. He was a close friend of the Pre-Raphaelites, though he never formally joined them. He painted history, literature and scenes of modern working life, including the famous 'Work'. He died in London in 1893.

Q314275.bio: Quinten Metsys was a painter from Leuven, who worked in Antwerp. He made realistic scenes of everyday life, from moneylenders to funny old women, and helped make Antwerp a great art center. He died in 1530.

Q97603495.bio: Henry Brueckner was a painter who worked in the United States in the 1800s. He painted historical scenes, such as the marriage of Pocahontas, for patrons in the New World.

x-ronald-a-wilson.bio: Ronald A. Wilson was an American artist who served as a combat artist with the US Army in Vietnam in 1967. His moody, colorful paintings of night operations and helicopters are in the US Army art collection.

Q7031.bio: Luca Signorelli was an Italian painter born in Cortona around 1450. He painted powerful, muscular bodies, and his frescoes of the end of the world in Orvieto Cathedral impressed Michelangelo. He died in 1523.

Q328369.bio: Edwin Landseer was born in London and showed an extraordinary talent for drawing animals as a child. He became Queen Victoria's favorite animal painter, and he created the bronze lions at the base of Nelson's Column in Trafalgar Square. He painted dogs, horses, and stags with great warmth. He died in London in 1873.

Q3526663.bio: Théophile Hamel was born near Quebec City and studied in Europe in the 1840s. He became one of the most important portrait painters in Canada, painting political leaders and church figures. He lived in Quebec City. He died there in 1870.

Q214957.bio: Thomas Nast was an American cartoonist born in Landau, Germany, in 1840. He moved to New York as a child and became famous in Harper's Weekly for his political cartoons, and is credited with creating the Republican elephant and the modern Santa Claus. He died in Ecuador in 1902, where he served as US consul.

x-remigio-legat.bio: Remigio Legat was an Italian painter of the 1800s who painted scenes from the Risorgimento, the movement that united Italy. His picture of the Battle of Calatafimi was painted in 1860, soon after Garibaldi's victory.

Q938058.bio: Jean Germain Drouais was a French painter born in Paris in 1763. He was a favorite pupil of Jacques-Louis David, won the Prix de Rome at 21, and became one of the most promising artists of his generation, but he died of smallpox in Rome in 1788 at the age of 24.

Q918605.bio: Herbert James Draper was born in London and studied at the Royal Academy. He painted scenes from Greek and Roman myth with glowing color and graceful figures. His 'The Lament for Icarus' is his best-known work. He died in London in 1920.

Q965809.bio: Frederick McCubbin was born in Melbourne and became a leading painter of the Heidelberg School. He painted the Australian bush and the pioneers with great feeling. He taught at the National Gallery school. He died in Melbourne in 1917.

Q369263.bio: John Trumbull was born in Lebanon, Connecticut, and served as an officer in the American Revolution. Afterwards he studied painting in London with Benjamin West. He is best known for paintings of key events in the Revolution, such as the signing of the Declaration of Independence. He died in New York City in 1843.

x-attributed-to-robert-peake-the-elder.bio: Robert Peake the Elder was an English painter born around 1551 who worked in London. He was the Serjeant-Painter to King James I and painted portraits of the court, including the royal family, in a bright, detailed style. He died in London in 1619.

Q720035.bio: Nicolaas Pieneman was born in Amersfoort, in the Netherlands, and became a portrait and history painter in Amsterdam. He painted royalty, battle scenes and a famous picture of the arrest of the Javanese prince Diponegoro. He died in Amsterdam in 1860.

Q207929.bio: Jacopo Pontormo was an Italian painter born in the village of Pontorme near Empoli in 1494. He worked in Florence for the Medici and became a leading Mannerist, known for his elegant, twisting figures and bright, unusual colors. He died in Florence in 1557.

Q2132490.bio: Loyset Liédet was a manuscript painter born in Hesdin around 1420. He worked for the Dukes of Burgundy in Bruges, painting large histories and chronicles in miniature for their libraries. He died in Bruges in 1479.

Q205148.bio: Filippo Lippi was a Florentine painter born in 1406, who was a Carmelite friar for much of his life. He painted tender Madonnas with real, lovely faces, and his son Filippino also became a painter. He died in Spoleto in 1469.

Q1606630.bio: Henry Courtney Selous was an English painter and illustrator born in Deptford in 1803. He painted big historical pictures and illustrated books, including a famous painting of the opening of the Great Exhibition in 1851. He died in Devon in 1890.

x-anonymous-illuminator-french-chronicle.bio: This picture comes from a medieval French royal chronicle, painted by an illuminator whose name was not recorded. Manuscripts like this were made by workshops of artists in the 1300s and 1400s for kings and nobles.

Q164961.bio: Adolph von Menzel was born in Breslau (now Wrocław, Poland) and lived most of his life in Berlin. He was Germany's greatest realist painter and an amazing draftsman. He painted history scenes, factories and daily life. He was a very short man who worked until his death in 1905.

x-anonymous-artist.bio: This work was made by an artist whose name was not recorded. Many historical paintings and prints, especially from the time of the events themselves, were made by anonymous artists.

Q5580.bio: Albrecht Dürer was a German artist born in Nuremberg in 1471. He was a painter, but he is most famous for his woodcuts and engravings, which made him known across Europe, and for traveling to Italy to learn from Renaissance artists. He lived mostly in Nuremberg and died there in 1528.

Q469379.bio: Francesco Melzi was an Italian painter born in Milan in 1492. He was Leonardo da Vinci's student and companion, and inherited his drawings and notebooks when Leonardo died. Melzi died in 1570.

Q183245.bio: George Frederic Watts was born in London and trained as a sculptor and painter. He painted portraits of the great and the good, as well as symbolic works on big themes like Hope and Love. In his later years he lived in the English village of Compton, where his gallery still stands. He died in 1904.

Q919806.bio: Juan Sánchez Cotán was a Spanish painter born in 1560. He painted still lifes of vegetables and fruit that seem to hang in a dark window, and later became a monk. He died in Granada in 1627.

Q718975.bio: François-André Vincent was a French painter born in Paris in 1746. He won the Prix de Rome, studied in Italy and became a leading history painter in the Neoclassical style, a rival of Jacques-Louis David. He taught at the art academy in Paris and died there in 1816.

x-currier-and-ives.bio: Currier and Ives was a famous American printmaking firm based in New York, founded by Nathaniel Currier and James Ives, which published cheap hand-colored lithographs from 1857 to 1907. They sold millions of prints of news events, landscapes and everyday life.

x-anonymous-kurz-allison.bio: Kurz and Allison was an American printing firm in Chicago that made colorful lithographs of famous battles and historical scenes in the 1880s and 1890s. Their prints brought the Civil War and the American West into many homes.

Q314889.bio: Pieter de Hooch was a Dutch painter born in Rotterdam in 1629. He painted peaceful scenes of Dutch homes and courtyards, with careful perspective and bright sunlight. He died in Amsterdam in 1683.

Q47551.bio: Titian was an Italian painter born in Pieve di Cadore around 1490. He worked in Venice and became the most famous painter in Europe, painting portraits for the Emperor Charles V and King Philip II of Spain with rich color and loose brushwork. He lived to a great age and died in Venice in 1576.

Q160141.bio: Chaïm Soutine was born into a poor Jewish family in a small village in what is now Belarus. He moved to Paris in 1913, where he lived and painted in a crowded artists' colony and became close friends with Modigliani. His wild, twisting paintings of waiters, pastry cooks and landscapes made him famous. He died in Paris in 1943, during the German occupation.

Q127171.bio: Jean-Honoré Fragonard was born in Grasse, in the south of France, and moved to Paris as a boy. He studied in Italy and became a star of the Rococo style, painting playful, romantic scenes for the nobility. After the French Revolution, his style fell out of fashion, and he spent his last years nearly forgotten in Paris. Today we again admire his speed and charm.

Q876701.bio: Ludwig Thiersch was a German painter born in Munich in 1825. He lived mostly in Munich and painted religious and historical pictures, spending some time in Greece, which inspired his scenes of the ancient world. He died in Munich in 1909.

Q290812.bio: Stefan Lochner was a German painter born in about 1410, who worked in Cologne. His sweet, gold-and-jewel-bright pictures, like the Madonna of the Rose Bower, made him the most famous painter of Cologne. He died in 1451.

Q322582.bio: Paul Delaroche was born in Paris and became one of France's most popular painters of dramatic history scenes. He worked and taught in Paris, where he trained many future artists. His paintings often show famous tragedies, such as the death of royalty. He died in Paris in 1856.

Q7325393.bio: Richard Edward Miller was born in St. Louis, Missouri, and studied in Paris. He joined the American art colony at Giverny, near Monet's home, and painted bright Impressionist scenes of women in sunlit rooms. He later lived in Provincetown, Massachusetts. He died in 1943.

x-paul-revere.bio: Paul Revere was born in Boston in 1735 and became a silversmith, engraver and patriot. He is best known for his midnight ride in April 1775 to warn colonists that British soldiers were coming. He made the engraving of the Boston Massacre, and died in Boston in 1818.

Q39931.bio: Pierre-Auguste Renoir was born in Limoges, France, and started his working life painting designs on porcelain. In Paris he became a founding Impressionist, famous for glowing scenes of friends, dancing, and sunshine. Later in life he lived in the warm south of France, and he kept painting even when arthritis twisted his hands, with a brush strapped to his fingers. He left thousands of cheerful paintings.

Q259594.bio: Lyubov Popova was a Russian painter and designer born near Moscow in 1889. She studied in Paris, became a leader of the avant-garde in Moscow, and designed theater sets and fabrics for the new Soviet state. She died of scarlet fever in Moscow in 1924 at the age of 35.

Q13604459.bio: José María Jara was a Mexican painter born in 1866 who studied at the Academy of San Carlos in Mexico City. He painted scenes of Mexican life, with a special interest in customs and traditions. He died in 1939.

Q41513.bio: William Blake was born in London and lived there nearly his entire life. He was a poet, painter and printmaker who claimed to see angels and visions, and he created magical books mixing words and pictures. Few people understood him while he lived, and he was poor. Today he's honored as one of the greatest imaginations in British art and literature.

x-leonardo-da-vinci.bio: Leonardo da Vinci was born in the village of Vinci, near Florence, in 1452. He painted the Mona Lisa and the Last Supper, but he was also a scientist, engineer and inventor who filled notebooks with ideas for flying machines and anatomy. He worked in Florence, Milan, Rome and France, where he died in 1519.

Q217128.bio: Valentin Serov was born in Saint Petersburg, Russia, to a musical family. He studied under Repin and became Russia's most sought-after portrait painter, painting writers, musicians, and even the tsar. He lived mostly in Moscow. His portraits are admired for being fresh, sunny and natural.

Q2582642.bio: James Pollard was an English painter born in London in 1792. He specialized in lively pictures of stagecoaches, inns and early railways, and he lived in London, where he died in 1867.

Q211356.bio: Isaac Levitan was born in Lithuania to a Jewish family and grew up in Moscow, where he studied painting. He became one of Russia's greatest landscape painters, known for his poetic scenes of rivers, forests and quiet villages. He often painted along the Volga River. He died in Moscow in 1900, at age 39. Levitan was born into a poor Jewish family in Lithuania, and he rose to become one of the most beloved painters in Russia.

Q540219.bio: Pedro Américo was a Brazilian painter born in 1843 in Paraíba. He studied in Paris and painted huge history pictures, including 'Independence or Death!' He also wrote books and was a politician. He died in Florence, Italy, in 1905.

Q8537.bio: Bernardino Luini was an Italian painter, born near Lake Maggiore around 1480. He worked in Milan, where he was influenced by Leonardo da Vinci, and painted sweet and gentle religious scenes. He died in 1532.

Q707729.bio: Jean-François de Troy was a French painter born in Paris in 1679. He painted elegant scenes of high society, with silk dresses and flirting couples, and worked in Rome, where he directed the French Academy. He died there in 1752.

Q1056977.bio: Cesare da Sesto was an Italian painter born around 1477 near Milan. He studied the work of Leonardo da Vinci, whose soft shading and gentle faces he copied, and later worked in Rome and southern Italy. He died in 1523.

Q82445.bio: Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec was born into a noble family in Albi, France, but broken bones in childhood stunted his growth. He moved to Montmartre in Paris and painted the dancers, singers and cabaret stars of the Moulin Rouge. His bold posters helped invent modern advertising art. He died at 36, at his mother's château in southwestern France.

Q7422343.bio: Sarah Goodridge was born in Templeton, Massachusetts, and taught herself to paint miniature portraits. She worked in Boston, where she was a well-known painter of tiny portraits on ivory. She painted the great statesmen of her day, including Daniel Webster and Gilbert Stuart. She never married and ran her own successful art business.

Q737635.bio: Childe Hassam was born near Boston and became a leading American Impressionist. He painted the streets and parks of New York, and a famous series of flag paintings. He also painted on the coast of Maine and at Appledore Island. He died in East Hampton, New York, in 1935.

Q290407.bio: Gentile Bellini was an Italian painter born in Venice around 1429, the older brother of the painter Giovanni Bellini. He worked for the government of Venice and in 1479 was sent to Constantinople to paint the sultan Mehmed II. He returned to Venice and died there in 1507.

Q333380.bio: Gerard David was a Dutch painter born in about 1460. He worked in Bruges and became the city's top painter after Hans Memling died. He died in 1523.

Q181568.bio: Ivan Aivazovsky was born in Feodosia, a port town on the Crimean coast of the Black Sea. He became one of the greatest painters of the sea, producing about 6,000 works in his career. He traveled widely in Europe and served as a Russian navy painter. He lived most of his life in Feodosia, where he built a studio and art gallery for his hometown.

Q780102.bio: Wyndham Lewis was a painter and writer, born in 1882 on a yacht off the coast of Nova Scotia. He lived mostly in London, where he led Vorticism, a British avant-garde movement, and served as an artillery officer and official war artist in World War I. He died in London in 1957.

Q506000.bio: Paul Kane was born in Ireland and grew up in Toronto. Between 1845 and 1848 he made a long journey across Canada to the Pacific, sketching Indigenous peoples and landscapes. He then painted a series of large pictures from his sketches. He died in Toronto in 1871.

Q334001.bio: Thomas Cole was born in England and moved to the United States as a teenager, settling near the Hudson River in New York. He founded the Hudson River School, a group of artists who painted America's wild landscapes. His paintings often carried messages about nature and civilization. He died in Catskill, New York, in 1848.

Q316016.bio: John Singleton Copley was born in Boston and became America's finest portrait painter before the Revolution. He painted merchants and patriots, like Paul Revere. In 1774 he moved to England as war loomed, and spent the rest of his life in London. He died there in 1815.

x-benjamin-moran.bio: Benjamin Moran was the artist who designed the cover of the official program for the Woman Suffrage Procession in Washington on March 3, 1913, showing a woman on a white horse in front of the Capitol.

Q326548.bio: Pieter Aertsen was a Dutch painter born in Amsterdam in 1508. He painted huge market scenes with mountains of food in the front, and tiny Bible scenes in the back. He died in 1575.

Q3382963.bio: Pierre-Denis Martin was a French painter born in Paris in 1663. He painted battle scenes, including some for the Russian court in the 1720s, and spent his life in Paris, where he died in 1742.

x-league-of-women-voters.bio: The League of Women Voters was founded in 1920 by suffragist Carrie Chapman Catt, as women across the United States won the right to vote. The organization still teaches people about voting and publishes posters and guides.

Q54454217.bio: Frederick Thwaites Bush was an English artist born in Market Harborough in 1887. He made lithographs of scenes of the front, including Vimy Ridge, during World War I. He died in Greenwich in 1985.

Q512648.bio: Reinier Vinkeles was a Dutch engraver and draftsman born in Amsterdam in 1741. He made prints of history and portraits, including scenes of the French Revolution for Dutch audiences. He lived in Amsterdam and died there in 1816.

Q43136084.bio: Richard Rummell was an English-born American painter, born in 1848. He painted watercolor views of American college campuses and other buildings, and lived and worked in New York. He died in 1924.

Q570172.bio: Gaspar de Crayer was a Flemish painter born in Antwerp in 1584 who worked in Brussels and Ghent. He painted altarpieces and portraits in the Baroque style and was a respected rival of Rubens. He died in Ghent in 1669.

Q5571.bio: Andrea del Sarto was a Florentine painter born in 1486. He was called the faultless painter, because of his smooth, harmonious pictures. He died in Florence in 1530.

Q37974034.bio: John Ward Dunsmore was an American painter born in Ohio in 1856. He studied in Paris and became known for paintings of events of the American Revolution, which were used in schoolbooks. He died in 1945.

Q1240575.bio: Itō Jakuchū was born in Kyoto, Japan, the son of a vegetable seller. He ran the family shop for years before devoting himself to painting, and kept chickens in his garden so he could study them. His colorful and detailed pictures of birds, plants and animals are among the most beloved in Japan. He died in 1800.

Q3127237.bio: Harada Naojirō was born in Edo (now Tokyo) and studied painting in Germany. He was one of the first Japanese artists to learn Western oil painting abroad, and he painted some of Japan's early oil paintings. He died in 1899.

Q5598.bio: Rembrandt van Rijn was born in Leiden in 1606 and moved to Amsterdam in 1631, where he became the most famous painter in Holland. He painted portraits, Bible stories and over eighty self-portraits, and went bankrupt later in life. He died in Amsterdam in 1669.

Q215251.bio: Hugo van der Goes was a Flemish painter born in Ghent around 1440. His large, emotional altarpieces were admired by Italian artists, and later in life he joined a monastery. He died in 1482.

Q215073.bio: Moritz Daniel Oppenheim was born in Hanau, Germany, to a Jewish family and trained in Munich, Paris and Rome. He lived mostly in Frankfurt, where he became a favorite painter of the Rothschild family. He is best known for warm pictures of traditional Jewish family life. He died in Frankfurt in 1882.

Q4562720.bio: Gustav Lærum was a Norwegian painter born in 1870, who painted portraits and landscapes. He studied in Norway and Paris. He worked in Oslo. He died in 1938.

Q35548.bio: Paul Cézanne was born in Aix-en-Provence in southern France and lived there for much of his life, painting its hills, orchards, and the mountain Sainte-Victoire. He studied with the Impressionists in Paris, but then went his own way, building forms from blocks of color. He is often called the father of modern art, and both Picasso and Matisse praised him. He died in 1906 after catching a chill while painting outside.

Q214074.bio: Claude Lorrain was a French painter born in Chamagne in 1600. He moved to Rome as a young man and spent his life there painting glowing landscapes and harbors in golden light, which influenced painters for centuries, including Turner. He died in Rome in 1682.

Q355406.bio: Paulus Potter was a Dutch painter, born in 1625. He painted animals such as cows, horses and bulls, in a very true-to-life way, and died young, aged 28, in Amsterdam in 1654.

Q773855.bio: Alfred Stevens was born in Brussels and settled in Paris, where he became a leading painter of elegant women in fashionable rooms. He was a friend of Manet and Degas. He died in Paris in 1906.

Q134150.bio: Marie Spartali Stillman was born in London to a Greek family and became one of the few women to be a respected Pre-Raphaelite painter. She studied with Ford Madox Brown. She modeled for other artists, too. She lived in London and Italy and died in 1927.

Q369776.bio: David Roberts was a Scottish painter born in Stockbridge, Edinburgh, in 1796. He started as a theater scene painter, traveled through Egypt and the Holy Land, and made famous views of ancient monuments. He lived in London and died there in 1864.

Q1555416.bio: Gustaf Cederström was born in Stockholm in 1845 and was a Swedish painter known for dramatic history paintings. He studied in Düsseldorf and Paris. He later became director of the Royal Academy of Fine Arts. He died in 1933.

Q78893573.bio: Antonio Cotti was an Italian painter born in Craveggia, in northern Italy, in 1840. He painted historical and literary scenes in a polished style, including a famous picture of the poet Dante in Verona. He died in 1929.

Q958927.bio: Aleksander Gierymski was born in Warsaw, Poland, and studied in Germany and Italy. He painted moonlit city scenes, with great honesty about everyday life. He lived in Warsaw and later in Rome, where he spent his last years. He died in 1901.

Q102272.bio: Jan van Eyck was a Flemish painter born around 1390 who worked for the Duke of Burgundy and lived in Bruges until he died in 1441. He was a master of oil paint, using thin glowing layers to paint jewels, fabric and reflections in amazing detail. His Arnolfini Portrait and the Ghent Altarpiece are among the most famous pictures of the 1400s.

Q455133.bio: George Catlin was born in Pennsylvania and trained as a lawyer before becoming a painter. In the 1830s he traveled across the American West to paint portraits of Native Americans and their lives. He hoped to preserve a record of cultures he feared would disappear. He died in New Jersey in 1872.

Q366212.bio: Frederic Edwin Church was born in Hartford, Connecticut, and studied with Thomas Cole. He traveled to South America, the Arctic and the Middle East, painting giant landscapes full of wonder. He became one of the most famous artists in the United States. He built a Persian-style mansion called Olana on the Hudson River.

Q2627916.bio: Ulpiano Checa was a Spanish painter born in Colmenar de Oreja in 1860. He moved to Paris, where he became famous for dynamic pictures of chariots, horses and battles, and later lived in France. He died in an automobile accident in Dax, France, in 1916.

Q664680.bio: Alexander von Kotzebue was a Russian painter born in Königsberg in 1815, the son of the famous German dramatist. He became a battle painter for the Russian tsars and later lived in Munich. He died in Munich in 1889.

Q2573180.bio: George Henry Boughton was a painter born in Norwich, England, in 1833, who was brought up in Albany, New York, and then lived in London. He painted gentle scenes of the Pilgrims and of early America and became a member of the Royal Academy. He died in London in 1905.

Q347139.bio: Jean-Baptiste Greuze was born in Tournus, France, and moved to Paris, where he became famous for sentimental paintings of family life and young girls with moral messages. He was admired by the philosopher Diderot. His popularity faded after the French Revolution. He died in Paris in 1805.

x-nasa-apollo-17-crew.bio: The Blue Marble was taken by the crew of Apollo 17, Eugene Cernan, Ronald Evans and Harrison Schmitt, on their way to the Moon in December 1972. It was the last Apollo flight to the Moon.

Q44032.bio: Egon Schiele was born in Tulln, Austria, and studied art in Vienna as a teenager. He was inspired by Gustav Klimt and developed a raw, angular and expressive drawing style. He lived in Vienna and in smaller Austrian towns. He died of the Spanish flu in 1918 at just 28, three days after his wife.

Q1066580.bio: Charles de La Fosse was a French painter born in Paris in 1636. He studied in Italy and became known for big, colorful decorations in the churches and palaces of Louis XIV, including the dome of Les Invalides in Paris. He died in Paris in 1716.

Q18125545.bio: Hervey Smythe was a British army officer born in 1734. He served under General Wolfe at Quebec in 1759 and made drawings of the campaign, then served as an adviser on military matters. He died in 1811.

Q452321.bio: Emanuel Leutze was born in Schwäbisch Gmünd, Germany, and moved to the United States as a child. He later studied in Düsseldorf, Germany, and lived there for years while painting American history scenes. He returned to the U.S. in 1859 and worked in Washington, D.C. His painting of Washington crossing the Delaware became a national icon.

Q172911.bio: Ilya Repin was born in a small town in Ukraine, then part of the Russian Empire. He trained in Saint Petersburg and traveled to Paris before becoming Russia's most celebrated realist painter. He lived much of his later life in a country house near the Finnish border, now a museum. His huge paintings of people, history, and ordinary life made him a national treasure.

Q8009345.bio: William Franklin Draper was an American painter born in Hopedale, Massachusetts, in 1912. He was a combat artist for the US Navy in World War II and later a portrait painter in California. He died in 2003.

Q432826.bio: Saturnino Herrán was born in Aguascalientes, Mexico, in 1887, and moved to Mexico City to study art. He painted Mexican workers, Indigenous people and traditions in a bold, strong style. He helped inspire later Mexican muralists. He died in 1918 at only 31.

Q10319762.bio: Laureys a Castro was a marine painter born in Antwerp around 1644 who later moved to England. He painted sea battles and ships, and he is known as one of the Flemish artists who brought the Dutch style of sea painting to Britain. He died in England around 1700.

Q213973.bio: Johann Heinrich Wilhelm Tischbein was born in Haina, Germany, to a family of painters. He lived in Rome and Naples and became a friend of the poet Goethe. He painted portraits and scenes from mythology. He died in Eutin, Germany, in 1829.

Q2370524.bio: Vasily Timm was a Russian painter and illustrator born in Riga in 1820. He worked in Saint Petersburg, painted historical scenes and published an illustrated magazine, and later lived in Germany. He died in Berlin in 1895.

Q723863.bio: Lluís Dalmau was a painter from Valencia, born around 1429, who went to Flanders in 1431 and learned the style of Jan van Eyck. He brought that style to Spain. He died in about 1461.

Q6171629.bio: Severin Segelcke was a Norwegian painter born in Christiania in 1867. He painted landscapes and portraits and lived part of his life in Norway's countryside. He died in 1940.

Q240526.bio: Lawrence Alma-Tadema was born in a village in the Netherlands and settled in London, England, in 1870. He became famous for sunny paintings of ancient Rome and Greece, filled with marble, flowers, and sea views. He was knighted and extremely popular during his lifetime. He died in Wiesbaden, Germany, in 1912.

Q7300143.bio: Rea Irvin was an American artist born in San Francisco in 1881. He drew magazine covers and cartoons, and designed the first cover of The New Yorker in 1925, featuring the dandy Eustace Tilley. He lived in New York and died in the Virgin Islands in 1972.

Q381458.bio: Christen Købke was born in Copenhagen and was a leading painter of the Danish Golden Age. He painted views of the city, the shore and portraits of friends with a light, delicate touch. He died in 1848, at 37.

Q3659111.bio: Carlo Bossoli was an Italian-Swiss painter born near Lugano in 1815. He worked in Odessa and then Turin, where he painted detailed pictures of the battles and events of the Italian wars of independence. He died in Turin in 1884.

Q833224.bio: Juan Carreño de Miranda was a Spanish painter, born in 1614. He became the court painter to Charles II of Spain and was known for portraits and religious paintings in the style of Velázquez. He died in Madrid in 1685.

Q7345286.bio: Robert Harris was born in Wales and raised in Prince Edward Island. He studied in London and Paris and became one of Canada's leading portrait painters, and the president of the Royal Canadian Academy. He is best known for his painting of the Fathers of Confederation. He died in Montreal in 1919.

Q1516217.bio: Isidor Popper was a German lithographer and cartoonist born in Hildesheim in 1816. He worked in Hamburg, where he made satirical prints, including some about the revolution of 1848. He died in Hamburg in 1884.

Q217715.bio: Caspar Netscher was a Dutch painter born in 1635 in Heidelberg, Germany. He became famous for small portraits and indoor scenes with beautiful, shiny silks and satins. He died in The Hague in 1684.

Q443199.bio: Isaak Brodsky was a Russian painter born in 1884 in what is now Ukraine. He trained in Odessa, Saint Petersburg and Italy, and after the revolution became a leading Soviet painter, known for his portraits of Lenin. He died in Leningrad in 1939.

Q432266.n: Willem van de Velde the Younger
Q432266.bio: Willem van de Velde the Younger was a Dutch painter born in Leiden in 1633. He painted ships and sea battles in great detail and moved to England in 1672 to work for King Charles II. He died in Greenwich in 1707.

Q3370554.bio: Paul Balze was born in Rome to French parents and became a painter and student of Ingres. He lived and worked mostly in Paris, and was known for careful, classical work. He also copied works of the old masters. He died in Paris in 1884.

Q104884.bio: Caspar David Friedrich was born in the Baltic port of Greifswald, Germany, and later settled in Dresden. He painted quiet, mysterious landscapes of mountains, fog, ruins, and seashores, often with a tiny figure seen from behind. He believed nature was a way of feeling something divine. He became a hero of German Romanticism, though he was nearly forgotten for decades before being rediscovered.

Q6238971.bio: John Henry Walker was an Irish-born illustrator, born in County Antrim in 1831, who moved to Canada. He lived in Montreal, where he drew historical and city scenes for books and newspapers, and he died there in 1899.

Q2958767.bio: Charles Comfort was a Canadian painter born in Edinburgh, Scotland, in 1900. He grew up in Winnipeg, served as an official war artist in World War II and later became the director of the National Gallery of Canada. He died in Ottawa in 1994.

Q207447.bio: Jean-Baptiste-Siméon Chardin was born in Paris, the son of a cabinet-maker. He became one of the greatest painters of still lifes and quiet scenes of everyday life in 1700s France. He worked slowly and carefully with a soft touch. He spent his entire life in Paris.

Q728712.bio: Mór Than was a Hungarian painter born in 1828 in Bečej, then part of Hungary. He studied in Vienna, joined the Hungarian national cause of 1848 and later painted many scenes of Hungarian history. He died in Trieste in 1899.

Q457976.bio: Nikolai Ge was born in Voronezh, Russia, and studied in Saint Petersburg and Italy. He painted powerful scenes from history and religion with dramatic light and strong emotion. Later in life he lived on a farm in Ukraine. He died in 1894.

Q405444.bio: Maruyama Ōkyo was born into a farming family near Kyoto and became one of the most important Japanese painters of the 1700s. He taught himself to paint from nature and was famous for his realistic animals and plants. He founded the Maruyama school. He died in Kyoto in 1795.

x-dorothea-lange.bio: Dorothea Lange was an American photographer born in Hoboken, New Jersey, in 1895. She moved to San Francisco, and during the Great Depression worked for the government photographing the lives of poor farm families, creating the famous Migrant Mother. She died in San Francisco in 1965.

x-nasa-photograph-by-william-anders.bio: William Anders, born in Hong Kong in 1933, was an American astronaut who flew on Apollo 8, the first mission to orbit the Moon, in December 1968. His photograph Earthrise, taken on that flight, became one of the most famous images of the 1900s. He died in 2024.

Q515879.bio: Alexey Venetsianov was a Russian painter born in Moscow in 1780. He is considered the founder of Russian paintings of peasant life, and started a school at his country estate. He died in 1847 in an accident when his horse bolted.

Q443136.bio: Maurycy Gottlieb was born in Drohobych, in Galicia, to a Jewish family and studied art in Kraków, Vienna and Munich. He was a student of the great painter Jan Matejko and painted striking pictures of Jewish life and history. He died in Kraków in 1879 at only 22. His few works are treasured today.

Q927350.bio: Jacopo de' Barbari was an Italian painter and printmaker, born in Venice around 1460. He made a huge, famous bird's-eye view of Venice, then worked in Germany and the Netherlands. He died in about 1516.

Q15407085.bio: Louis Bombled was a French painter and illustrator born in Chantilly in 1862. He specialized in military subjects and painted battle scenes for books and magazines. He died in Pierrefonds in 1927.

Q433434.bio: Anne-Louis Girodet was born in Montargis, France, and studied under Jacques-Louis David. He became a leader of French Romanticism with dreamy, mysterious paintings. He lived in Rome and Paris. He died in Paris in 1824.

Q3695965.bio: Robert Walter Weir was an American painter born in New Rochelle, New York, in 1803. He taught drawing for more than forty years at the military academy at West Point and painted the Embarkation of the Pilgrims in the US Capitol. He died in New York City in 1889.

Q6308657.bio: Julien Binford was an American painter born in Powhatan County, Virginia, in 1908. He painted for the US Army Air Forces in World War II and later taught art at Mary Washington College in Fredericksburg, Virginia. He died in 1997.

Q360888.bio: Geertgen tot Sint Jans was a Dutch painter who was born in Leiden around 1460 and lived in a monastery in Haarlem, where his name means Little Gerard of the Brothers of Saint John. He died young, in his late twenties, around 1490.

Q313275.bio: Boris Kustodiev was a Russian painter born in Astrakhan in 1878. He lived in Saint Petersburg and painted colorful scenes of Russian merchants and festivals, and after the revolution made pictures of it despite being paralyzed and working from a wheelchair. He died in 1927.

Q37693.bio: Paul Gauguin was born in Paris and spent part of childhood in Peru. He worked as a stockbroker before turning to painting full-time. He lived in Brittany, in Arles with Van Gogh, and then in Tahiti and the Marquesas Islands in the South Pacific, seeking a simpler life. His flat, vivid colors influenced Picasso and Matisse.

Q211763.bio: William Holman Hunt was born in London and, with Millais and Rossetti, founded the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood in 1848. He traveled to the Middle East to paint biblical scenes with realistic backgrounds. His most famous painting is 'The Light of the World'. He died in London in 1910.

Q1371063.bio: Timothy H. O'Sullivan was an American photographer born in Ireland or New York around 1840. He photographed the Civil War, including the dead at Gettysburg, and later made photographs of the American West. He died in New York in 1882.

Q112894782.bio: Yosef Zvi Geiger was a painter from Safed, in the Holy Land under Ottoman rule. He painted religious scenes and local life in a simple, heartfelt style. He lived and worked in Safed, a town famous for Jewish study. He is remembered as one of the earliest painters from the land of Israel.

Q346808.bio: Gerard ter Borch was a Dutch painter born in Zwolle in 1617. He traveled widely, including to Münster where he painted the signing of the treaty of 1648, and was famous for quiet indoor scenes with beautifully painted satin dresses. He lived in Deventer and died there in 1681.

Q5594.bio: Antonello da Messina was a painter from Sicily, born around 1430. He learned the new oil paint technique from Flemish painters, and is famous for portraits with sharp eyes and lively expressions. He died in Messina in 1479.

Q118810.bio: Marie-Guillemine Benoist was born in Paris and studied with Vigée Le Brun and Jacques-Louis David. She was one of the leading women painters of her time and exhibited at the Paris Salon. Her 'Portrait of Madeleine' is one of the most celebrated works of the French Revolution era. She died in Paris in 1826.

Q3897020.bio: Pasquale Cati was an Italian painter born in Jesi in about 1550. He worked in Rome, where he painted frescoes and altarpieces for churches in the style of the Catholic Counter-Reformation. He died there in 1620.

Q2880664.bio: Baldassare Verazzi was an Italian painter born in Caprezzo in 1819. He lived in Milan and painted historical pictures related to the Italian struggle for independence, including the Five Days of Milan. He died in Lesa in 1886.

Q2159499.bio: Roberto Ferruzzi was born in what is now Croatia and lived in Italy, mostly in Venice and nearby. He painted people and village scenes. His painting 'Madonnina' made him a celebrity when it won a prize in 1897. He died in 1934.

Q369366.bio: Matthew Paris was an English monk and chronicler born around 1200. He lived at the abbey of St Albans, where he wrote and illustrated long histories of England and the world, with lively drawings of battles and kings. He died at St Albans in 1259.

Q922483.bio: William Orpen was born near Dublin, Ireland, and became a leading portrait painter in London. He served as an official war artist in World War I and painted the Paris Peace Conference. He died in London in 1931.

Q154349.bio: Odilon Redon was born in Bordeaux, France, and spent most of his life in Paris. He began with strange, dreamlike black-and-white drawings, then later painted flowers and myths in luminous color. His art was admired by Symbolists and later by the Surrealists. He died in Paris in 1916.

Q561916.bio: Henry Raeburn was born in Stockbridge, near Edinburgh, Scotland, and became Scotland's best-known portrait painter. He painted writers, lawyers and clan chiefs with a lively, confident brush. He was knighted in 1822. He lived and worked in Edinburgh until his death in 1823.

Q2545507.bio: George Washington Lambert was born in Saint Petersburg to American parents and moved to Australia as a child. He became a famous portrait painter and an official war artist at Gallipoli and in the Middle East. He died in 1930.

Q155575.bio: Martin Schongauer was a German painter and engraver born in Colmar around 1440. His detailed prints were copied across Europe, and the young Albrecht Dürer wanted to meet him. He died in Breisach in 1491.

Q32859679.bio: Manuel Ocaranza was born in Uruapan, Mexico, in 1841 and studied at the Academy of San Carlos in Mexico City. He painted romantic scenes and portraits and was one of the best Mexican painters of his time. He died young, at 41, in 1882.

Q200798.bio: Utagawa Hiroshige was born in Edo (Tokyo) and became one of Japan's greatest print artists. He is known for his landscapes, such as the Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō and One Hundred Famous Views of Edo. Van Gogh and Monet admired his work. He died in 1858.

Q106851.bio: Hans Memling was born in Germany in about 1435 and became the most successful painter in Bruges, in what is now Belgium. His calm, sweet and beautifully detailed religious pictures and portraits were bought by rich merchants and bankers from all over Europe. He died in Bruges in 1494.

Q739176.bio: Eilif Peterssen was born in Christiania and studied in Munich, Paris and Italy. He painted historical scenes, portraits and landscapes, and helped bring the Realist style to Norway. He lived in Oslo and in Lysaker. He died in 1928.

Q3424670.bio: Ole Peter Hansen Balling was born in Christiania and moved to the United States in 1856. He fought in the American Civil War and painted portraits of President Lincoln, Ulysses S. Grant and other leaders. He later returned to Norway. He died in 1906.

Q324288.bio: Jan van Huchtenburgh was a Dutch painter born in Haarlem in 1646. He specialized in battle scenes and made paintings for Prince Eugene of Savoy and King William III. He lived in Amsterdam and died there in 1733.

Q148475.bio: Jean-Baptiste Camille Corot was born in Paris and spent much of his life painting the French countryside and trips to Italy. His silvery, misty landscapes influenced Impressionist painters such as Monet and Pissarro. He was known as a kind and generous man. He died in Paris in 1875.

Q1361950.bio: Pietro Rotari was an Italian painter born in Verona in 1707. He painted portraits and charming scenes of young women, worked in Vienna and Dresden, and in 1756 moved to Saint Petersburg to paint at the court of Empress Elizabeth. He died there in 1762.

Q318640.bio: Antonio del Pollaiuolo was a Florentine artist born in 1429, who was a painter, goldsmith and sculptor. He studied the human body in action, and was one of the first to examine dead bodies to learn how muscles work. He died in Rome in 1498.

Q550401.bio: Govert Flinck was a Dutch painter, born in Kleve in 1615. He was a student of Rembrandt, and later became a popular portrait painter in Amsterdam. He died in 1660.

Q1345289.bio: Giovanni Battista Salvi, called Sassoferrato after his home town, was an Italian painter born in 1609. He painted many sweet, smooth pictures of Mary, with deep blue robes, in a style that looked back to Raphael. He died in Rome in 1685.

Q187850.bio: Mathew Brady was an American photographer born in New York State in 1822. He ran studios in New York and Washington, photographed presidents, and organized teams of photographers who recorded the Civil War. He died in New York City in 1896.

Q18507975.bio: Carl Frithjof Smith was born in Christiania (Oslo) in 1859 and trained in Germany, where he lived in Weimar for much of his life. He painted quiet scenes of family life and portraits. He died in Weimar in 1917.

Q3187562.bio: Juan Antonio de Ribera was a Spanish painter born in Madrid in 1779. He studied in Paris under Jacques-Louis David and became a leading Neoclassical painter, later working for King Ferdinand VII of Spain. He died in Madrid in 1860.

Q8010746.bio: William Halsall was an English-born American painter, born in Kirkdale near Liverpool in 1841. He moved to Boston and painted ships and the sea, including the Mayflower, and had a studio in the city. He died in Winthrop, Massachusetts, in 1919.

x-nasa-photograph-by-david-scott.bio: David Scott, born in 1932 in Texas, was an American astronaut who flew to the Moon as commander of Apollo 15 in 1971. He took photographs of his crewmate James Irwin on the surface and the lunar rover.

Q194402.bio: Joshua Reynolds was born in Plympton, England, and became the first president of the Royal Academy of Arts in London. He was the most famous portrait painter of Britain in the 1700s, and he painted kings, writers, and children. He gave important lectures about art and was knighted. He died in London in 1792.

Q577974.bio: Johannes Cornelisz Verspronck was a Dutch painter born in Haarlem in 1601. He painted fine portraits, especially of children and women in elegant clothing. He died in 1662.

Q214666.bio: Léon Bakst was born in Grodno, then part of the Russian Empire, to a Jewish family. He became a star of the Ballets Russes in Paris, designing the vivid costumes and sets that astonished audiences. He also painted portraits and illustrated books. He died in France in 1924.

Q689388.bio: Franz Anton Maulbertsch was an Austrian painter born in Langenargen on Lake Constance in 1724. He lived in Vienna and became the greatest painter of the Austrian Rococo, famous for his colorful ceiling paintings in churches and palaces. He died in Vienna in 1796.

Q585323.bio: Franz von Lenbach was a German painter born in Schrobenhausen in 1836. He became the most fashionable portrait painter in Munich and was famous for his many portraits of Otto von Bismarck and of the pope and emperors. He died in Munich in 1904.

Q374744.bio: Kanō Naizen was a Japanese painter born in 1570 who belonged to the Kanō school, the main painting school of the Japanese military rulers. He lived in Kyoto and is known for his colorful folding screens of the Portuguese traders who arrived in Japan. He died in Kyoto in 1616.

Q1161631.bio: Daniel Maclise was an Irish painter born in Cork in 1806. He moved to London, where he painted big scenes from history and literature, including huge murals in the Houses of Parliament, and was close friends with Charles Dickens. He died in Chelsea in 1870.

Q14198216.bio: Philippe de Mazerolles was an illuminator who worked in Bruges in the 1400s, painting books for Burgundian nobles. He was admired for his lively pictures in chronicles and books of hours.

Q3182324.bio: John Quidor was born in New Jersey and worked in New York City. He made humorous, wild illustrations of stories by Washington Irving, such as 'Rip Van Winkle' and 'Sleepy Hollow'. He was not widely known in his lifetime. He died in Jersey City in 1881.

Q1355256.bio: Eugène Lami was a French painter and lithographer born in Paris in 1800. He painted elegant scenes of the court and big battle pictures for King Louis-Philippe, and moved easily between fashion and war. He died in Paris in 1890.

Q76829.bio: Alexander Ivanov was born in Saint Petersburg, Russia, and spent nearly 20 years in Rome working on one giant painting, 'The Appearance of Christ to the People'. He made hundreds of studies for it. He returned to Russia shortly before his death in 1858. His art deeply influenced Russian painters.

Q317920.bio: Simon Vouet was a French painter born in Paris in 1590. He spent years in Italy, where he learned the dramatic style, and then returned to France to become the king's painter. He died in Paris in 1649.

Q736379.bio: Jean Colombe was a French manuscript painter born in Bourges around 1430. He worked for the Duke of Savoy and finished the famous Très Riches Heures, and he painted beautiful illustrated histories for noble patrons. He lived in Bourges and died there around 1493.

Q2777444.bio: Marquard Wocher was born in Germany in 1760 and settled in Basel, Switzerland. He is remembered for his huge circular painting of Thun and the Alps, one of the oldest panoramas in the world. He died in 1830.

Q1347418.bio: Joseph Stella was an Italian-born American painter, born in Muro Lucano, Italy, in 1877. He moved to New York at 19, painted its bridges, factories and amusement parks in a bold Futurist style and is best known for his images of the Brooklyn Bridge. He died in New York in 1946.

Q528620.bio: Giuseppe Maria Crespi was an Italian painter, born in Bologna in 1665. He painted religious pictures and humble everyday scenes, in a shadowy, warm style. He died in 1747.

Q2335336.bio: Charles Édouard Armand-Dumaresq was a French painter born in Paris in 1826. He painted military subjects and the French army, including scenes of the Franco-Prussian War. He lived and worked in Paris and died there in 1895.

Q548205.bio: Hubert Robert was a French painter born in Paris in 1733. He spent years in Italy and became known as 'Robert of the Ruins' for his pictures of crumbling Roman monuments, and he later served as a keeper of the Louvre. He was imprisoned for a time during the French Revolution and died in Paris in 1808.

Q1441554.bio: Francis Hayman was an English painter born in Exeter in 1708. He worked in London, painting scenes for the pleasure gardens at Vauxhall and large history pictures, and was one of the founders of the Royal Academy. He died in London in 1776.

Q2327761.bio: Gianfrancesco Penni was an Italian painter born in Florence in about 1488. He was one of the main helpers in Raphael's workshop in Rome and helped finish Raphael's work after he died. He later worked in Naples.

Q6141349.bio: James Pollock was an American artist who served in the US Army's combat art program in Vietnam in 1967. His paintings of the war and the jungle are part of the Army's art collection.

Q351746.bio: Joaquín Sorolla was born in Valencia, Spain, and became known as the 'master of light' for his sparkling paintings of beaches and sunshine. He worked in Madrid and traveled to Paris and the United States, where he was very popular. His house in Madrid is now a museum. He died in Spain in 1923.

Q13099283.bio: Frédéric Théodore Lix was a French illustrator born in Strasbourg in 1830. He drew news pictures for magazines, such as L'Illustration, and recorded the war of 1870 and the Paris Commune. He lived in Paris and died there in 1897.

Q5597.bio: Raphael was an Italian painter born in Urbino in 1483. He moved to Rome as a young man and painted frescoes for the Pope, as well as many gentle Madonnas and portraits, and was admired for the grace and balance of his work. He died in 1520, at the age of 37.

Q9440.bio: Paolo Veronese was an Italian painter born in Verona in 1528. He moved to Venice, where he became famous for huge, colorful pictures of feasts and ceremonies full of costumes and architecture. He died in Venice in 1588.

Q310285.bio: Adam Elsheimer was a German painter born in Frankfurt in 1578. He worked in Rome painting tiny, jewel-like pictures with moonlight, firelight and stars, and he influenced Rembrandt and Rubens. He died in 1610.

Q5337451.bio: Edgar Samuel Paxson was an American painter born in 1852. He moved to Montana as a young man, worked as a scout and mailman, and painted detailed pictures of the Western frontier, especially of the Battle of the Little Bighorn. He died in Missoula in 1919.

Q4348982.bio: David Milne was born in Ontario and lived in New York, then returned to the Ontario woods in 1930. He painted with a delicate touch, using watercolors and thin oils to capture cities, flowers and woods. He is considered one of Canada's greatest modern painters. He died in 1953.

Q241732.bio: Rosa Bonheur was born in Bordeaux, France, and grew up in Paris, where she studied animals at farms and markets. She became one of the most famous women artists of the 1800s, painting horses, cattle and sheep. She even got official permission to wear trousers in public so she could work. She died at her château in Thomery, near Paris, in 1899.

Q736065.bio: Francesco Solimena was an Italian painter, born in 1657 near Naples. He painted grand, dramatic altarpieces and ceilings, and was the most famous painter in Naples. He died in 1747.

x-kurz-and-allison.bio: Kurz and Allison was an American printing firm in Chicago that made colorful lithographs of famous battles and historical scenes in the 1880s and 1890s. Their prints brought the Civil War into many homes.

Q598030.bio: George Caleb Bingham was born in Virginia and raised in Missouri. He painted the life of the Missouri and Mississippi rivers, from flatboatmen to election days. He also served in Missouri politics. He died in Kansas City in 1879.

Q324622.bio: Henri Félix Emmanuel Philippoteaux was a French painter born in Paris in 1815. He made large battle paintings and giant circular panoramas, including a famous one of Gettysburg. He died in Paris in 1884.

x-national-woman-suffrage-publishing-co.bio: The National Woman Suffrage Publishing Company printed posters, newspapers and flyers to win American women the vote. Its materials appeared around the country in the 1910s.

Q3155327.bio: Isidore Stanislas Helman was a French engraver born in Lille in 1743. He moved to Paris, where he engraved scenes of the French Revolution after the paintings of other artists, and his prints were widely sold.

Q212499.bio: Jean-Léon Gérôme was born in Vesoul, France, and became one of the most successful painters and teachers in Paris. He traveled to Egypt and the Middle East and painted lively scenes from ancient and modern life. He was also a sculptor. His students came from around the world.

x-joseph-gary-sheahan.bio: Joseph Gary Sheahan was an American combat artist who painted watercolors of the US Army during World War II, including a view of Utah Beach in Normandy in 1944.

Q191748.bio: Lucas Cranach the Elder was a German painter born in Kronach in 1472. He became court painter to the rulers of Saxony in Wittenberg, was a close friend of Martin Luther, and ran a busy workshop that made portraits, religious scenes and the first Protestant images. He died in Weimar in 1553.

Q205863.bio: Jan Steen was a Dutch painter born in Leiden in 1626. He painted lively, messy family scenes and parties full of jokes and lessons, so much that a messy home is called a Jan Steen household in Dutch. He died in 1679.

Q952938.bio: Ogata Kōrin was born in Kyoto into a rich family of fabric merchants and became one of Japan's greatest decorative painters. He founded the Rinpa style of bold shapes and gold leaf. His folding screens, such as 'Red and White Plum Blossoms', are national treasures. He died in Kyoto in 1716.

Q265398.bio: Clara Peeters was a Flemish painter, born in Antwerp in about 1587. She was one of the first women to paint still lifes, with beautiful shiny dishes, cheese, flowers and food, and she sometimes hid a tiny reflection of herself in them. She died in about 1657.

Q6394591.bio: Vasily Pukirev was born in the Tula region of Russia and became a painter and teacher in Moscow. His most famous painting, 'The Unequal Marriage,' criticized forced marriages. It was a sensation, and he later taught at the Moscow School of Painting. He died in 1890.

Q1374436.bio: Henry Ossawa Tanner was an African American painter born in Pittsburgh in 1859. He moved to Paris in 1891, became famous for his quiet religious paintings and was the first Black artist to win wide international fame. He died in Paris in 1937.

Q609959.bio: Paul Peel was born in London, Ontario, and studied in Philadelphia and in Paris, where he became a successful painter. His warm, sunny pictures of children won prizes at the Paris Salon. He died young, in Paris, at the age of 31.

Q468772.bio: Anne Vallayer-Coster was born in Paris and became famous for lifelike still-life paintings of flowers, fruit and musical instruments. She was admitted to the French Royal Academy at 26 and also painted portraits. She worked for Queen Marie Antoinette. She died in Paris in 1818.

Q367360.bio: Orazio Gentileschi was an Italian painter, born in Pisa in 1563. He worked in Rome, Genoa, Paris and England, and he was the father and teacher of Artemisia Gentileschi. He died in London in 1639.

Q34013.bio: Georges Seurat was born in Paris and studied at the École des Beaux-Arts. He invented pointillism, painting with tiny dots of pure color that blend in the viewer's eye. He worked slowly and carefully in his studio, making many sketches before big paintings. He died suddenly at only 31, leaving behind just a handful of masterpieces.

Q979534.bio: Isaac Israëls was born in Amsterdam, the son of the famous painter Jozef Israëls, in a Dutch Jewish family. He painted lively scenes of Amsterdam streets, fashion houses and beaches in a loose, fast Impressionist style. He lived in Amsterdam, Paris, and The Hague, and he traveled to Indonesia and elsewhere. He died in The Hague in 1934.

Q4768.bio: Karl Bryullov was born in Saint Petersburg, Russia, into a family of artists. He lived for many years in Italy, where he painted his huge masterpiece 'The Last Day of Pompeii.' He returned to Russia as a celebrity and was admired by writers like Pushkin. He died in Italy in 1852.

Q223725.bio: Francesco Hayez was born in Venice, Italy, and later became the leading painter in Milan. He painted history scenes that stirred Italian pride during the fight for unification of Italy. He also made fine portraits. He lived to be 91, long enough to see Italy become one country.

Q323144.bio: Ambroise Louis Garneray was a French painter born in Paris in 1783. He went to sea as a boy, was a prisoner of the British during the Napoleonic wars, and later became a famous painter of ships and sea battles. He died in Paris in 1857.

Q1269439.bio: Federico Benković was a painter born in about 1677 in Dalmatia, on the Adriatic coast of today's Croatia. He trained in Bologna and Venice and later worked in Croatia and Slovenia. He died in 1753.

Q313561.bio: Dieric Bouts was a Dutch painter born in Haarlem around 1410 who moved to Leuven, in modern Belgium. He painted quiet, sad figures in carefully drawn rooms and landscapes. He died in 1475.

Q156426.bio: Alexej von Jawlensky was a Russian painter born in Torzhok in 1864. He served as an army officer, moved to Munich to paint and became part of the Blue Rider circle, famous for faces painted in bold colors. He died in Wiesbaden, Germany, in 1941.

Q311398.bio: Jean Fouquet was a French painter born in Tours around 1420. He became the leading painter at the court of King Charles VII, painted portraits and illuminated manuscripts, and visited Italy, which influenced his style. He worked in Tours and died there around 1478.

Q7780.bio: Fra Bartolomeo was an Italian painter born in Prato in 1472 who lived in Florence. He became a Dominican friar after the death of his friend and hero Savonarola, and painted calm, majestic altarpieces. He died in Florence in 1517.

Q310973.bio: Lorenzo Lotto was a Venetian painter born in 1480, who traveled a lot and painted psychologically sharp portraits. His religious paintings have a quirky charm. He died in Loreto in 1556.

Q13583490.bio: Marcus Gheeraerts the Younger was a painter born in Bruges in 1561 who moved to England as a child. He became one of the leading portrait painters of the court of Queen Elizabeth I, painting rich clothes and jewels in fine detail. He lived in London and died there in 1636.

Q2460318.bio: Edmund Charles Tarbell was born in Massachusetts and was a leading Boston painter. He taught at the Museum School in Boston and painted graceful pictures of women in sunlit rooms. He later lived in New Hampshire. He died in 1938.

Q724508.bio: Stefano da Verona was an Italian painter born around 1374 in Verona. He painted in the courtly International Gothic style, with beautiful clothes, flowers and animals. He died in about 1451.

Q173223.bio: Mary Cassatt was born near Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and moved to Paris as a young woman. She was the only American to join the French Impressionists, and she specialized in tender pictures of mothers and children. She lived in France most of her life, and she also encouraged American collectors to buy Impressionist art. She died at her country home in France in 1926.

Q1356488.bio: Richard Bergh was born in Stockholm in 1858 and became one of Sweden's leading painters of the 'Nordic light'. He was also a director of the National Museum. He died in 1919.

Q206697.bio: Santi di Tito was an Italian painter born in Sansepolcro in 1536 who lived in Florence. He painted clear, natural religious scenes and portraits, including the best-known portrait of Niccolò Machiavelli. He died in Florence in 1603.

Q381248.bio: James Tissot was born in Nantes, France, and moved to London, where he painted fashionable scenes of Victorian life. Later he traveled to the Holy Land and made a famous series of illustrations of the Bible. He was a very successful artist. He died in France in 1902.

Q649390.bio: Carl Gustaf Pilo was born in Sweden in 1711 and worked for many years as a court painter in Denmark before moving to Stockholm. He painted portraits of royalty, and started a large painting of the coronation of King Gustav III. He died in 1793.

Q1988310.bio: Ivan Kliun was a Russian painter born in 1873 near Moscow. He was an early follower of Kazimir Malevich and a leader of the Suprematists, who painted with pure geometric shapes. He lived in Moscow and died there in 1943.

Q22583666.bio: Carl Kahler was born in Linz, Austria, and emigrated to the United States, where he worked in San Francisco. He painted landscapes, horses and animals. His giant painting of 42 cats made him famous, and he took three years to complete it. He died in 1906.

Q547055.bio: Carl Bloch was born in Copenhagen, Denmark, and became one of the country's most beloved painters of history and religious scenes. He spent years studying in Italy. His pictures of Bible stories are reproduced all over the world. He died in Copenhagen in 1890.

Q69651.bio: Eduard Bendemann was born in Berlin to a Jewish family and became one of Germany's leading painters. He studied in Berlin and then worked in Dresden and Düsseldorf, where he became the director of the art academy. His paintings of Bible stories and everyday life were admired all over Europe. He died in Düsseldorf in 1889.

Q1674765.bio: Issachar Ber Ryback was born in Ukraine, then part of the Russian Empire, to a Jewish family. He studied art in Kyiv and was part of a group that tried to create a modern Jewish art. In 1926 he moved to Paris, where he stayed until his death in 1935. He painted and drew Jewish village life.

x-arthur-rothstein.bio: Arthur Rothstein was an American photographer born in New York City in 1915. He was the first photographer hired by the government's Farm Security Administration, capturing the Dust Bowl, and later worked for Look magazine. He died in New Rochelle in 1985.

Q1969461.bio: Thomas Fearnley was born in Halden, Norway, in 1802 and studied in Copenhagen and Stockholm. He traveled widely in Europe and was a friend of J. C. Dahl and J. M. W. Turner. He painted landscapes in Italy, Switzerland and Norway. He died young in Munich in 1842.

Q41406.bio: Edvard Munch was born in Norway and grew up in Christiania (now Oslo), in a family troubled by illness and loss. He traveled in Europe, especially Germany and France, and used paint to express anxiety, love and loneliness. His most famous work, 'The Scream', is among the best-known images ever. He spent his last decades at his estate Ekely near Oslo and died in 1944.

Q2824028.bio: Adam Willaerts was a Dutch painter born in London in 1577, who settled in Utrecht. He painted busy seascapes, beaches and ships, and he died in 1664.

Q83155.bio: Jacques-Louis David was born in Paris and became the greatest painter of the Neoclassical style, inspired by ancient Greece and Rome. He supported the French Revolution and later became Napoleon's official painter. After Napoleon fell, he was forced into exile and spent his last years in Brussels, Belgium. He taught many famous students and shaped French art for generations.

Q5681.bio: Andrea Mantegna was an Italian painter born in 1431 and was the court painter to the Gonzaga family in Mantua. His sharply drawn, statue-like figures and bold use of perspective were studied by many painters, including his brother-in-law Giovanni Bellini. He died in 1506.

Q189117.bio: Jan Matejko was born in Kraków, Poland, and became the nation's great painter of history. He made huge canvases of Poland's glories and heartbreaks, at a time when Poland was no longer an independent country. He lived most of his life in Kraków, where he later directed the School of Fine Arts. He's a national hero for keeping Polish memory alive.

Q77324.bio: Anton von Werner was a German painter born in Frankfurt an der Oder in 1843. He lived in Berlin, where he became director of the art academy and the leading painter of the Prussian court, recording events such as the proclamation of the German Empire. He died in Berlin in 1915.

Q262771.bio: Michael Wolgemut was a German painter and printmaker born in Nuremberg in 1434. He ran a large workshop that illustrated the famous Nuremberg Chronicle in 1493, and the young Albrecht Dürer was his apprentice. He worked in Nuremberg and died there in 1519.

Q42207.bio: Caravaggio was an Italian painter born in 1571, whose real name was Michelangelo Merisi. He painted dramatic scenes lit by a strong beam of light with deep shadows and used ordinary people as models. He had a violent temper, had to flee Rome after a fight, and died in 1610.

Q2959390.bio: Charles Huot was born in Quebec City and studied painting in Paris. He became one of Quebec's most important history painters, creating large murals for the Quebec Legislature. He also taught drawing and illustrated books. He died in 1930.

Q260166.bio: Marc-Aurèle de Foy Suzor-Coté was born in Arthabaska, Quebec, and studied in Paris. He painted both traditional pictures and bright landscapes of the snowy Quebec countryside. He also made sculptures. He died in Florida in 1937.

Q4113103.bio: Ivan Vladimirov was a Russian painter born in Vilnius in 1869. He worked in Saint Petersburg and made large paintings and drawings of the revolutions of 1905 and 1917 as an eyewitness. He died in Leningrad in 1947.

x-stephen-h-randall.bio: Stephen H. Randall was an American artist who served as a combat artist with the US Army's Vietnam combat art team in 1968. His watercolors of helicopters, soldiers and daily life are in the US Army art collection.

Q601609.bio: Antonio Ciseri was born in Switzerland to Italian parents and worked in Florence. He painted religious subjects and portraits with great realism. His 'Ecce Homo' is his best-known work. He died in Florence in 1891.

Q724148.bio: Édouard Detaille was a French painter born in Paris in 1848. He studied with Meissonier and became the most celebrated painter of the French army, making huge, accurate pictures of the war of 1870 and of Napoleon's troops. He lived in Paris and died there in 1912.

Q271676.bio: Charles Le Brun was a French painter born in Paris in 1619. He became First Painter to King Louis XIV and directed the decoration of the palace of Versailles and the Gobelins tapestry works. He died in Paris in 1690.

Q187310.bio: Carl Larsson was born in Stockholm to a poor family and became one of Sweden's best-loved painters. He is famous for his watercolors of his own home and family in Sundborn, which show happy children, flowers and sunshine. He also painted large murals. He died in 1919.

Q931356.bio: Konishi Hirosada was a Japanese printmaker who lived in Osaka from about 1810 to 1864. He is known for woodblock prints of kabuki actors. His prints were collected by fans like trading cards. He lived in the city's theater district.

Q19034.bio: Arent de Gelder, also known as Aert, was born in Dordrecht, in the Netherlands, in 1645. He studied with Rembrandt and kept painting in Rembrandt's rich, thick style long after his teacher's death. He died in 1727.

Q354786.bio: Ernest Meissonier was a French painter born in Lyon in 1815. He became famous for tiny, extremely detailed pictures, and later for big scenes of Napoleon's armies and the siege of Paris, where he served as an officer. He lived in Paris and Poissy and died in Paris in 1891.

Q363308.bio: Walker Evans was an American photographer born in St. Louis in 1903. He photographed poor farm families for the government during the Depression, and his plain, honest style shaped documentary photography. He lived in New York and died in New Haven in 1975.

Q1239404.bio: José Salomé Pina was a Mexican painter born in Mexico City in 1830. He studied at the Academy of San Carlos, where he later taught, and painted historical and portrait scenes. He died in Tacubaya, near Mexico City, in 1909.

Q5669.bio: Sandro Botticelli was an Italian painter born in Florence in 1445. He worked for the Medici family and painted graceful, flowing pictures such as The Birth of Venus and Primavera. He lived in Florence all his life and died there in 1510.

Q153746.bio: Albrecht Altdorfer was a German painter born near Nuremberg in about 1480 who lived in Regensburg, where he also served as a city councilor and architect. He was one of the first European artists to make landscapes the main subject of his pictures. He died in Regensburg in 1538.

Q1293506.bio: Edward Savage was born in Massachusetts and was an American painter and engraver. He painted George Washington from life and made popular prints of his work. He lived in Philadelphia, New York and Boston. He died in 1817.

Q691796.bio: Abanindranath Tagore was born in Kolkata (Calcutta), India, into a famous family that included the poet Rabindranath Tagore. He founded the Bengal School of art, which revived Indian painting styles. His work inspired the movement for India's independence. He died in Kolkata in 1951.

Q75527.bio: Heinrich Leutemann was a German painter and illustrator born near Leipzig in 1824. He was known for lively book illustrations of animals, travel and history, and lived in Leipzig and nearby Saxony. He died in 1905.

Q310437.bio: Alexandre Cabanel was born in Montpellier, France, and became a star of the French Academy. He lived in Paris, where he taught at the École des Beaux-Arts. He painted classical and historical subjects, as well as portraits of the rich. Napoleon III admired him and bought his work.

Q163543.bio: François Gérard was a French painter born in Rome in 1770. He studied under Jacques-Louis David, became a favorite portrait painter of Napoleon's court, and was later made a baron. He lived in Paris and died there in 1837.
