x-anonymous-illuminator-st-albans-chroni.bio: This picture of the Battle of Agincourt comes from the St Albans Chronicle, an English history written by the monk Thomas Walsingham. The illustrator is not known, but the manuscript was made soon after the events it shows, in the early 1420s.

x-charles-alfred-stothard.bio: Charles Alfred Stothard was an English artist and antiquarian born in London in 1786. He made careful drawings of medieval tombs and of the Bayeux Tapestry, which he copied in the 1810s for the Society of Antiquaries. He died in 1821 after falling from a ladder while sketching a stained-glass window in a church in Devon.

Q2095810.bio: William Simpson was a Scottish war artist, born in Glasgow in 1823. He worked as a correspondent for the Illustrated London News and was sent to the Crimean War, drawing what he saw for newspapers at home, and later traveled to India, Abyssinia and elsewhere. He died in London in 1899.

Q1056862.bio: Cesare Maccari was an Italian painter born in Siena in 1840. He worked in Rome, where he painted large frescoes of ancient and national history, including one in the Italian Senate. He died in Rome in 1919.

Q436267.bio: Hilma af Klint was a Swedish artist born near Stockholm in 1862. She trained as a painter and in 1906 began making huge abstract paintings, years before the famous pioneers of abstract art, but she asked that they not be shown until 20 years after her death. She died in 1944, and her work became world famous in the 2000s.

Q48319.bio: Hans Holbein the Younger was a German painter born in Augsburg in about 1497. He worked in Basel and then in London, where he became court painter to King Henry VIII and painted portraits that made the Tudors famous. He died in London in 1543, probably of the plague.

Q134741.bio: Camille Pissarro was born on the island of St. Thomas in the Caribbean and moved to France as a teen. He was the oldest of the Impressionists and a father figure and teacher to many younger painters, including Cézanne. He painted farms, villages and city streets in France. He died in Paris in 1903. Pissarro came from a Sephardic Jewish family, and his background shaped his lifelong sympathy for ordinary working people.

Q365544.bio: Adolph Tidemand was born in Mandal, Norway, and trained in Copenhagen and Düsseldorf. He lived much of his life in Germany and Norway, painting scenes of Norwegian farmers and folk traditions. He helped create the image of Norwegian national identity in the 1800s. He died in Christiania in 1876.

Q334262.bio: Guercino was an Italian painter born in Cento in 1591. His nickname means the squinter, and his big, dramatic altarpieces are full of motion and strong light. He died in Bologna in 1666.

Q983949.bio: Józef Chełmoński was born in a village in Poland and became one of the country's most beloved painters. He studied in Warsaw and Munich and lived in Paris for some years. He painted the Polish countryside, wide skies, horses and birds. He died in 1914.

Q313183.bio: Konrad Witz was a German-Swiss painter born in about 1400 who worked in Basel. His pictures of solid, heavy figures in real landscapes were ahead of their time. He died in about 1445.

Q5588070.bio: William Blair Bruce was born in Hamilton, Ontario, and lived in Europe for most of his career, in France and Sweden. He painted landscapes and dramatic scenes. His paintings and sculptures are now in a museum he planned in his hometown. He died in Stockholm in 1906.

Q186748.bio: Dante Gabriel Rossetti was born in London to an Italian family of poets and scholars. He co-founded the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood and painted dreamy, romantic women. He was also a poet, and often paired paintings with verses. He lived in London and died in 1882.

Q4583808.bio: Carl Sundt-Hansen was born in Stavanger, Norway, in 1841, and spent much of his life in Denmark. He painted scenes of Norwegian and Danish peasant life. He died in Stavanger in 1907.

Q727643.bio: Paul Nash was an English painter born in London in 1889. He was an official war artist in both World Wars and painted haunting landscapes of broken trees and battlefields. He died in Boscombe, England, in 1946.

Q6503742.bio: Lawren P. Harris was a Canadian painter born in Toronto in 1910, the son of the Group of Seven painter Lawren Harris. He was an official Canadian war artist in World War II and later a teacher and painter. He died in Ottawa in 1994.

Q2065760.bio: Władysław Podkowiński was born in Warsaw, Poland, and was a leading Impressionist and Symbolist painter. He studied in Warsaw and Paris, and he is remembered for the shocking 'Frenzy of Exultations.' He died young, at 29, in 1895.

Q5660541.bio: Agustín Arrieta was born in Chiautempan and worked in Puebla, Mexico. He painted still lifes and kitchen scenes with great skill, as well as portraits. His paintings show details of everyday Mexican life. He died in 1874.

Q1513704.bio: Gerlach Flicke was a German painter born in Osnabrück around 1495. He moved to England, where he lived in London and painted portraits, including one of Archbishop Thomas Cranmer. He died in London in 1558.

Q3101368.bio: George Agnew Reid was born in Ontario and trained in Philadelphia and Paris. He was a leading Toronto painter, a teacher, and the president of the Ontario College of Art. During World War I he painted Canadian factory workers and street scenes. He died in 1947.

Q23380.bio: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was born in Montauban, in southern France, and trained under David in Paris. He spent many years in Italy and in the end died in Paris. He believed in the power of clean, elegant outlines and was a master of portraits. He was also a fine violin player, and the phrase 'Ingres's violin' came to mean a talented hobby.

Q215305.bio: Giulio Romano was an Italian painter and architect born in Rome in 1499. He was Raphael's best pupil and finished many of his works after Raphael's death, then moved to Mantua, where he designed the colorful Palazzo Te. He died in Mantua in 1546.

Q123757.bio: Jean-Étienne Liotard was born in Geneva, Switzerland, and traveled across Europe and to Constantinople. He is best known for pastel portraits with a precise, glowing look. He worked for royals and nobles in Vienna, Paris and England. He died in Geneva in 1789.

Q164696.bio: Hans Baldung Grien was a German painter and printmaker born around 1480. He worked with Albrecht Dürer in Nuremberg, and is known for strange pictures of witches, death and nudes. He died in Strasbourg in 1545.

Q41264.bio: Johannes Vermeer was a Dutch painter born in Delft in 1632. He painted calm scenes of women in sunlit rooms, with pearls, maps, letters and music, and made fewer than 40 paintings that we know of. He died in 1675, and he was almost forgotten until the 1800s.

Q159297.bio: John Constable was born in East Bergholt, in the English county of Suffolk, where his father owned mills. He painted the farms, rivers, and clouds of the countryside he grew up in, often outdoors, which was unusual at the time. He lived in London for much of his adult life. He was more admired in France than at home, and his work inspired the Barbizon painters and Impressionists.

Q576025.bio: Gerrit Berckheyde was a Dutch painter, born in 1638 in Haarlem. He painted detailed, peaceful views of the squares and canals of Haarlem and Amsterdam. He died in 1698.

Q356644.bio: Albert Edelfelt was born in Finland to a Swedish family and studied in Antwerp and Paris. He painted portraits, scenes of Finnish life, and historical subjects. He was one of the most famous Finnish painters. He died in Finland in 1905.

Q158062.bio: Max Liebermann was born in Berlin to a wealthy Jewish family and became the leading German Impressionist. He painted workers, beer gardens and gardens, and he served as president of the Prussian Academy of Arts. After the Nazis came to power in 1933, he was forced to give up his positions. He died in Berlin in 1935.

Q212754.bio: John William Waterhouse was born in Rome to English parents and later lived in London. He painted women from myths and legends — such as the Lady of Shalott and sirens — in lush, colorful detail. He admired the Pre-Raphaelites, who came before him. He died in London in 1917.

Q203768.bio: Abdülmecid II was born in Istanbul in 1868 and was the last caliph of the Ottoman family. He was also a talented painter and music lover. After Turkey became a republic, he was forced into exile. He died in Paris in 1944.

Q8457.bio: Antonio da Correggio was an Italian painter born around 1489 and named after the town of Correggio. He painted soft, glowing pictures with warm light and swirling clouds of angels, and he influenced the Baroque painters. He died in 1534.

Q275018.bio: Uemura Shōen was born in Kyoto, and became one of Japan's greatest women painters. She was best known for beautiful pictures of women in traditional style. She was the first woman to receive the Order of Culture, Japan's high honor, in 1948. She died in 1949.

Q214905.bio: Thomas Eakins was born in Philadelphia and lived there nearly all his life. He studied anatomy and photography so his paintings of people, rowers and surgeons would be true to life. His honest realism upset some people, but is now praised. He taught art in Philadelphia and died there in 1916.

Q5822.bio: Piero della Francesca was an Italian painter and mathematician, born in about 1415 in Sansepolcro. His calm, still pictures use geometry and clear light, with smooth, solid figures. He died in 1492.

Q473813.bio: Georg Bleibtreu was a German painter born in Xanten in 1828. He lived in Berlin and became a leading painter of the Prussian wars of the 1860s and 1870s, depicting them in huge canvases. He died in Charlottenburg in 1892.

Q282512.bio: Oscar Björck was born in Stockholm in 1860 and was a Swedish painter and teacher. He spent time in the Skagen artists' colony in Denmark. He painted portraits and landscapes. He died in 1929.

Q216406.bio: Edward Burne-Jones was born in Birmingham, England, and moved to London to become an artist. He was part of the second wave of Pre-Raphaelites and also designed stained glass and tapestries with William Morris. His dreamy paintings were inspired by medieval legends and myths. He was made a baronet and died in London in 1898.

Q41554.bio: Nicolas Poussin was a French painter born in Les Andelys in 1594. He moved to Rome as a young man and spent most of his life there, painting calm, well-planned scenes from ancient history and mythology that set the standard for classical painting. He died in Rome in 1665.

Q168659.bio: Franz Xaver Winterhalter was born in a small village in Germany's Black Forest and became one of the most famous painters of royalty in Europe. He worked for Queen Victoria, Napoleon III and many royal courts in Paris, London and Germany. His portraits show glittering silks and graceful poses. He died in Frankfurt in 1873.

Q8017377.bio: William Raphael was born in Poland, then part of Prussia, and moved to Montreal as a young man. He painted the streets, markets and views of Montreal and Quebec in the 1860s. His pictures record the city as it was. He died in Montreal in 1914.

Q981441.bio: Wilhelm Bendz was born in Odense, Denmark, and studied in Copenhagen. He painted lively portraits of his artist friends and finely detailed scenes of daily life. He died of an illness at only 28 in Vicenza, Italy, in 1832.

Q146691.bio: Alphonse Mucha was born in Ivančice, in what is now the Czech Republic. He moved to Paris and became world-famous for his elegant Art Nouveau posters. Later in his life he returned to Prague and painted a huge series of paintings called the Slav Epic. He died in 1939.

Q3136027.bio: Hippolyte Bellangé was a French painter and lithographer born in Paris in 1800. He painted soldiers and battle scenes, many from Napoleon's armies, and later served as curator of the museum in Rouen. He died in Paris in 1866.

Q46373.bio: Edgar Degas was born in Paris to a well-to-do family and lived there almost all his life. He's linked to the Impressionists, but preferred to work indoors, painting ballet dancers, racehorses, and women at their daily routines. He loved to catch unusual angles, as if a camera had snapped the scene. In old age his eyesight failed and he turned to sculpture.

Q352954.bio: Carel Fabritius was a Dutch painter born in 1622, who studied with Rembrandt. He painted only a few pictures, and he was killed at the age of 32 when a gunpowder store exploded in Delft in 1654, destroying much of his work. The Goldfinch is his best-known picture.

Q442484.bio: Cornelis van Haarlem was a Dutch painter born in Haarlem in 1562. He painted big pictures with twisting, muscular nudes, and helped start the Haarlem Mannerist style. He died in 1638.

Q15998924.bio: Nina Evans Allender was an American cartoonist born in Auburn, New York, in 1873. She was the official cartoonist of the National Woman's Party and drew hundreds of cartoons for the fight for women's right to vote. She lived in Washington, D.C., and died in Plainfield, New Jersey, in 1957.

Q1043318.bio: Carlos de Haes was born in Brussels and moved to Spain as a young man. He became the leading Spanish landscape painter, introducing a realistic, outdoor style. He taught at the Academy in Madrid. He died there in 1898.

Q3133062.bio: Henry Sandham was born in Montreal and became a leading Canadian painter, illustrator and a founding member of the Royal Canadian Academy. He later lived in Boston and London. His landscapes and harbor scenes were widely admired. He died in London in 1910.

Q28470603.bio: Zacharie Vincent was a Huron-Wendat painter from Wendake, near Quebec City. He is considered the first Indigenous painter in Quebec, and he often signed his portraits 'Zacharie Vincent Telariolin, the last of the Hurons'. He painted himself and his family in traditional dress. He died in 1886.

Q527191.bio: Laura Muntz Lyall was born in England and raised in Canada. She studied in Toronto and in Paris and became known for gentle, soft pictures of mothers and children. She was one of the leading women painters of her time. She died in Toronto in 1930.

Q379521.bio: Ercole de' Roberti was an Italian painter born in Ferrara around 1450. He worked for the ruling d'Este family and painted sharp, strangely charged scenes. He died in 1496.

Q539474.bio: Constantin Hansen was born in Rome to Danish parents and grew up in Copenhagen. He was a leading painter of the Danish Golden Age and painted portraits, historical scenes and murals. He also visited Italy. He died near Copenhagen in 1880.

Q673615.bio: Peter Snayers was a Flemish painter born in Antwerp in 1592. He became the court painter to the Archduke in Brussels and was famous for his panoramic battle scenes, often showing real battles of the Thirty Years' War. He died in Brussels in 1667.

x-elizabeth-thompson-lady-butler.bio: Elizabeth Thompson, later Lady Butler, was a British painter born in Lausanne, Switzerland, in 1846. She became one of the most popular battle painters of Victorian Britain, starting with her Roll Call in 1874. She married a general, lived in Ireland, and died in 1933.

Q167132.bio: George Bellows was born in Columbus, Ohio, and moved to New York City, where he became a leading painter of city life. He painted boxing matches, tenements and the construction of Penn Station. He died young, in 1925, at 42.

Q583015.bio: Jacques Amans was born in Maastricht, in the Netherlands, and worked as a portrait painter in France and the United States. He lived in New Orleans for several years in the 1830s and painted many local families. He returned to Paris, where he died in 1888.

Q4661858.bio: Aaron Bohrod was an American painter born in Chicago in 1907. He served as an official US Army war artist in World War II in the Pacific and Europe and later became the University of Wisconsin's first artist in residence. He died in Madison in 1992.

Q939197.bio: Rik Wouters was a Belgian painter and sculptor born in 1882 in Mechelen. He painted his wife Nel in bright, happy colors. He died young, in Amsterdam, at 33, in 1916, after fleeing the war.

Q2833597.bio: Alexandre Desgoffe was born in Paris and trained as a landscape painter under Ingres's circle. He spent his career in Paris, where he became known for classical landscapes in the Italian style. He exhibited for decades and received several honors. He died in Paris in 1882.

Q505758.bio: Karl von Piloty was a German painter born in Munich in 1826. He became director of the Munich art academy and was famous for huge, dramatic scenes from history, which he taught to dozens of students. He died near Munich in 1886.

Q937096.bio: John Martin was born in Northumberland, England, and made huge, dramatic paintings of disasters from the Bible and history. His work was hugely popular in London in the 1820s and 1830s, as thrilling as a movie. He also designed engineering schemes for his city. He died on the Isle of Man in 1854.

Q442491.bio: Joachim Patinir was a Flemish painter, born around 1475. He is often called the first landscape painter in European art, since in his pictures vast rocky landscapes take up more room than the religious figures. He died in Antwerp in 1524.

Q365891.bio: Adolphe Yvon was a French painter born in Eschviller in 1817. He painted large battles for the French army, including the Crimean and Italian campaigns, and spent his life in Paris, where he died in 1893.

x-bayeux-tapestry-embroiderers.bio: The Bayeux Tapestry was stitched in the 1070s, probably in England and perhaps ordered by Bishop Odo of Bayeux, William the Conqueror's half-brother. Its embroiderers are not known by name, though they were most likely skilled English needlewomen. It is about 70 meters long and now hangs in Bayeux, France.

Q323498.bio: Friedrich Georg Weitsch was a German painter born in Brunswick in 1758. He worked in Berlin as a painter for the Prussian court and painted many portraits, including one of the scientist Alexander von Humboldt. He died in Berlin in 1828.

Q453972.bio: John Collier was born in London and studied art in London, Paris and Munich. He painted portraits and scenes from history and legend, often with strong feelings. He also wrote about art and science. He died in London in 1934.

Q359421.bio: Salvator Rosa was a painter, poet and actor born in Naples in 1615. He painted wild, rocky landscapes with bandits and witches, and was well known as a wild character in Rome. He died there in 1673.

Q364226.bio: Kuzma Petrov-Vodkin was born in a small town on the Volga River in Russia, and trained in Moscow, Saint Petersburg, and Paris. He used Russian icon painting as inspiration for his bold, simple style. He later taught in Saint Petersburg (then Leningrad). He died there in 1939.

Q3114975.bio: Gustav Wentzel was born in Christiania in 1859 and became a Norwegian painter of everyday scenes and portraits. He studied in Paris and Munich and lived later in Lillehammer. His honest interiors were praised. He died in 1927.

Q928734.bio: Anicet Charles Gabriel Lemonnier was a French painter born in Rouen in 1743. He worked in Paris and was the director of the royal Gobelins tapestry works. He painted the Salon of Madame Geoffrin and died in Paris in 1824.

Q28867.bio: Juan Luna was born in the Philippines and studied art in Manila, Madrid and Rome. His enormous painting 'Spoliarium' won a gold medal in Madrid in 1884, and made him a hero to Filipinos. He lived in Spain and France and supported Philippine independence. He died in Hong Kong in 1899.

Q7793.bio: Donato Bramante was an Italian architect and painter born in 1444. He designed the plan for the new Saint Peter's Basilica in Rome, and he began as a painter in Milan. He died in Rome in 1514.

Q1190012.bio: Osman Hamdi Bey was born in Istanbul, in the Ottoman Empire, and studied painting in Paris. He was also an archaeologist and founded Istanbul's first modern art school and archaeological museum. His paintings show scenes of Ottoman life with great detail. He died in 1910 and is honored as a pioneer of Turkish art.

Q170068.bio: Akseli Gallen-Kallela was born in Pori, Finland, and became the country's most famous painter. He painted scenes from the Kalevala, Finland's national epic, and studied in Paris. He lived in Finland and traveled to Africa and the United States. He died in Stockholm in 1931.

Q20127345.bio: Joseph Kyle was an American portrait painter born in Ohio in 1815. He worked in New York City, painting many portraits of his time, including the Quaker minister Lucretia Mott. He died in 1863.

Q348024.bio: Carlo Crivelli was an Italian painter born in Venice in about 1430, who spent most of his life working in towns along the Adriatic coast. His altarpieces glitter with gold and jewels, and he liked to add painted fruit and flies. He died in about 1495.

Q1591928.bio: John Gilbert was an English painter and illustrator born in Blackheath in 1817. He became famous for drawings of Shakespeare's plays and for lively paintings of knights and battles, and he served as president of the Royal Watercolour Society. He died in London in 1897.

Q13434144.bio: Karl Uchermann was a Norwegian painter born in the Lofoten region in 1855. He painted scenes of Northern Norway and of animals, particularly dogs. He lived in Oslo. He died in 1940.

Q7779204.bio: Thure de Thulstrup was a Swedish-born American illustrator born in Stockholm in 1848. He served in the French army, moved to the United States and became famous for his illustrations of battles of the Civil War. He died in New York City in 1930.

Q11534323.bio: Ryūsai Shigeharu was a Japanese printmaker who worked in Osaka in the early 1800s. He made woodblock prints of kabuki actors and scenes of the theater. Fans bought these prints to remember their favorite performers.

Q49898.bio: Hyacinthe Rigaud was a French painter born in Perpignan in 1659. He painted portraits of kings, nobles and bishops, in grand poses with silk and velvet, and his portrait of Louis XIV is one of the best-known royal portraits. He died in Paris in 1743.

Q3588762.bio: Émile Signol was a French painter born in Paris in 1804. He won the Prix de Rome in 1830 and painted large religious and historical pictures, including some for the palace of Versailles. He died in Enghien-les-Bains in 1892.

Q1387579.bio: Otto Sinding was a Norwegian painter born in Kongsberg in 1842, who studied in Munich. He painted dramatic mountain landscapes and scenes of folk life. He lived in Munich and in Norway. He died in 1909.

Q718795.bio: Vincenzo Camuccini was born in Rome and became one of Italy's leading Neoclassical painters. He painted big history scenes and was in charge of the Vatican's paintings. He was also a collector. He died in Rome in 1844.

Q17790.bio: The Kangxi Emperor was the second Qing emperor of China, and he ruled for 61 years, from 1661 to 1722, longer than any other Chinese emperor. He was interested in science, art, poetry and calligraphy, and also painted himself. He lived in Beijing and the Imperial Summer Palace.

Q11977827.bio: Jacob Bratland was a Norwegian painter born in Bergen in 1859. He studied in Germany and painted landscapes of western Norway. He died in Christiania in 1906.

Q191423.bio: Domenico Ghirlandaio was a Florentine painter born in 1448. He painted busy, lively frescoes of Bible stories set in Florence with its real people, and he ran a big workshop that included the young Michelangelo. He died in 1494.

Q446631.bio: Master Theodoric was a Bohemian painter active in Prague between about 1348 and 1381. He was the court painter of Emperor Charles IV and painted the holy figures for the walls of Karlštejn Castle, which are among the best-known paintings of medieval central Europe.

Q1290058.bio: Eduard Steinbrück was a German painter born in Magdeburg in 1802. He worked in Berlin and Düsseldorf and painted historical and religious scenes and portraits. He died in Lądek-Zdrój, now in Poland, in 1882.

Q270460.bio: Olga Rozanova was a Russian painter born in Melenki in 1886. She was a leading woman of the Russian avant-garde who worked with Malevich on Suprematism and designed books and textiles. She died of diphtheria in Moscow in 1918 at the age of 32.

x-workshop-of-matthaus-merian.bio: Matthäus Merian was a Swiss-born engraver who lived in Frankfurt, Germany, and published famous books of city views and the news of the Thirty Years' War. This engraving is from his workshop, which kept making prints after he died in 1650.

Q312096.bio: Thomas Lawrence was an English painter born in Bristol in 1769. He became the most fashionable portrait painter of his time, painting kings, generals and beautiful ladies, and was president of the Royal Academy. He lived in London and died there in 1830.

Q1970087.bio: Philip James de Loutherbourg was an artist born in Strasbourg in 1740. He moved to London in 1771, where he designed spectacular theater scenery for the actor David Garrick and painted dramatic landscapes, battles and industrial scenes. He lived in Hammersmith and died in Chiswick in 1812.

Q7824.bio: Annibale Carracci was an Italian painter born in Bologna in 1560. He and his brother and cousin founded an art school that brought back the clear, natural style of the Renaissance, and he painted the ceiling of the Farnese Gallery in Rome. He died in 1609.

Q325835.bio: Frederick Arthur Verner was born in Ontario and became famous for paintings of the Canadian plains, with buffalo and Indigenous camps at sunset. He spent his later years in England, where he continued to paint Canadian scenes. He died in London in 1928.

Q1534936.bio: Josse Lieferinxe was a painter from the town of Enghien in what is now Belgium who worked in Marseille in southern France between about 1493 and 1508. He painted scenes of the life of Saint Sebastian, who was prayed to during the plague, and little else is known of his life.

Q1470796.bio: Frederick Sandys was born in Norwich, England, and became a painter and illustrator associated with the Pre-Raphaelites. He was famous for detailed portraits of beautiful women. He lived in London, and he died there in 1904.

Q2272816.bio: Peder Balke was born on an island in Norway and became a painter who started out as a house painter. He traveled to Norway's far north and painted bold, simple pictures of the sea and mountains. His work went unnoticed in his lifetime but is admired today. He died in Christiania (Oslo) in 1887.

Q505150.bio: Nicolaes Maes was a Dutch painter born in Dordrecht in 1634. He studied with Rembrandt, painted quiet home scenes of old women and children and later became a society portrait painter in Amsterdam. He died in 1693.

Q212657.bio: Artemisia Gentileschi was an Italian painter born in Rome in 1593, the daughter of the painter Orazio Gentileschi. She was one of the first women to become a successful professional painter in Europe, and her powerful pictures often show strong women from the Bible and myths. She died in Naples in about 1653.

Q353628.bio: Arkhip Kuindzhi was born in a poor family in the Mariupol area of Ukraine and trained in Saint Petersburg. He was famous for using light in his landscapes to create a nearly glowing effect, as in his moonlit nights. He lived in Saint Petersburg, where he taught and gave money to young artists. He died there in 1910.

Q1550144.bio: Thomas Jones Barker was an English painter born in Bath in 1815. He painted Crimean War scenes and popular pictures of the British army, and lived in London, where he died in 1882.

Q192720.bio: Thomas Gainsborough was born in Sudbury, a small town in England, and moved to London as a teenager to study art. He became one of Britain's most fashionable portrait painters, working in Bath and London. He secretly preferred painting landscapes, and he loved music. His elegant, feathery brushstrokes made his sitters seem alive.

Q192544.bio: Henryk Siemiradzki was born in what is now Ukraine to a Polish family and studied in Saint Petersburg, Munich and Rome. He lived mainly in Rome, where he painted giant, sunny pictures of ancient Greece and Rome. He was one of the most successful painters in Europe. He died in 1902.

Q127017.bio: Vasily Vereshchagin was born in Cherepovets, Russia, and traveled to Central Asia, India and the Balkans. He painted battlefields to show the true horror of war, sometimes as a war correspondent. His anti-war art shocked many viewers. He died in 1904 when a warship he was aboard struck a mine.

Q2965652.bio: Christian Skredsvig was a Norwegian painter and writer born in Modum in 1854, who studied in Paris and lived in Eggedal. His paintings show Norwegian farm life and rural people in soft light. He also wrote stories and novels. He died in 1924.

Q709461.bio: Arthur Dove was an American painter born in Canandaigua, New York, in 1880. He is considered one of the first American artists to paint abstractly, painting nature, music and feelings, often while living on a boat or in a farmhouse on Long Island. He died in Huntington, New York, in 1946.

Q1390711.bio: Kolë Idromeno was born in Shkodër, Albania, and became a painter, architect and sculptor. He studied in Italy and is regarded as a pioneer of modern Albanian art. He designed buildings in his hometown. He died in Shkodër in 1939.

Q786545.bio: Thomas Sully was an English-born American painter born in Horncastle in 1783. He moved to America as a boy, settled in Philadelphia and painted portraits of many leaders, including Queen Victoria. He died in Philadelphia in 1872.

Q464016.bio: Marianne von Werefkin was a Russian painter born in Tula in 1860. She studied with Ilya Repin, moved to Munich, and helped found the Blue Rider group, though she is less known than her partner Alexej von Jawlensky. She lived the last years of her life in Ascona, Switzerland, and died there in 1938.

x-robert-walker.bio: Robert Walker was an English portrait painter born around 1599 who worked in London. He painted many portraits of Oliver Cromwell and other leaders of the Parliamentary side in the English Civil War. He died in London around 1658.

Q534279.bio: Ogata Kenzan was born in Kyoto and was a famous potter and painter. He was the younger brother of the painter Ogata Kōrin, and together they made some of the most beautiful objects of their time. He decorated ceramics with simple, beautiful designs. He died in Edo (Tokyo) in 1743.

Q643303.bio: Jules Girardet was a French painter born in Paris in 1856, from a family of artists. He painted scenes of war and the French colonial empire, and illustrated books and magazines. He died in Boulogne-Billancourt in 1938.

Q434916.bio: Luigi Russolo was an Italian Futurist painter and composer, born in Portogruaro in 1885. He painted pictures of speed and light and invented the 'intonarumori', noise-making machines that played the sounds of the modern city. He died in Laveno-Mombello in 1947.

Q260135.bio: Édouard Castres was a Swiss painter born in Geneva in 1838. He volunteered as a Red Cross helper in the Franco-Prussian War and later painted the huge panorama of the Bourbaki army's retreat into Switzerland. He died in Annemasse, France, in 1902.

Q938442.bio: Giovanni Girolamo Savoldo was an Italian painter, born in Brescia around 1480. He painted quiet figures lit by soft glowing light, and worked in Venice. He died in about 1548.

Q9319.bio: Jacopo Tintoretto was an Italian painter born in Venice in 1519. He lived in Venice all his life and painted huge, fast, dramatic canvases for churches and palaces, including the Doge's Palace. He died in Venice in 1594.

Q29405091.bio: Francisco Maura y Montaner was a Spanish painter born in Palma de Mallorca in 1857. He studied in Madrid and Rome, painted history pictures that won prizes at national exhibitions, and spent his later years in the Basque Country. He died in Irun in 1931.

Q80442.bio: Robert Campin was a painter from Tournai, in today's Belgium, born around 1375. He painted solid figures in down-to-earth rooms full of everyday things, and the great Rogier van der Weyden was probably his pupil. He died in 1444.

Q41402.bio: Gilbert Stuart was born in Rhode Island and became America's best-known portrait painter. He painted George Washington and other leaders of the young United States. He lived for years in London and Dublin before returning to the U.S. He died in Boston in 1828.

Q295144.bio: Gustave Caillebotte was born into a wealthy Paris family and trained as a lawyer and engineer before painting. He was an Impressionist, but his pictures often show unusual high or low perspectives of the modern city. He generously used his money to support his friends, buying their paintings. He lived near Paris and died in Gennevilliers at 45.

Q156386.bio: Henri Rousseau was born in Laval, France, and worked as a tax-and-toll collector, earning the nickname 'Le Douanier' (the customs officer). He taught himself to paint and began exhibiting in his forties. His jungle scenes, painted from visits to the Paris botanical garden, were mocked at first but later admired by Picasso and others. He died in Paris in 1910.

Q2711324.bio: Alejo Fernández was a Spanish painter born in Córdoba around 1470 who worked mostly in Seville. He painted altarpieces in a style that mixed Gothic and Renaissance, including a famous picture of the Virgin of the Navigators. He died in Seville in 1545.

Q708498.bio: Gerolamo Induno was an Italian painter born in Milan in 1825. He fought for Italian independence in the 1840s and 1850s, joined Garibaldi and painted scenes of battles and ordinary people during the Risorgimento. He died in Milan in 1890.

Q251967.bio: Ángel Zárraga was born in Durango, Mexico, and lived in Paris for many years. He mixed Mexican themes with the modern styles of Europe, including Cubism. He painted large murals as well as portraits. He died in Mexico in 1946.

Q702700.bio: Joseph-Nicolas Robert-Fleury was a French painter born in Cologne in 1797. He worked in Paris, painted scenes from history and the Reformation, and served as director of the French Academy in Rome. He died in Paris in 1890.

Q93708.bio: Adolph Northen was a German painter born in Hann. Münden in 1828. He studied in Düsseldorf and became known for dramatic paintings of Napoleon's campaigns in Russia and of Prussian history. He died in Düsseldorf in 1876.

Q360679.bio: Joseph-Noël Sylvestre was a French painter born in Béziers in 1847. He studied in Paris and painted large history scenes, especially of the fall of ancient Rome, some of which hang in French museums. He died in Paris in 1926.

Q216873.bio: Pierre Puvis de Chavannes was a French painter born in Lyon in 1824. He painted calm, pale murals for the Panthéon in Paris and other public buildings, in a style that influenced many later artists. He died in Paris in 1898.

x-english-school-attributed-to-marcus-gh.n: English School (attributed to Marcus Gheeraerts the Younger)
x-english-school-attributed-to-marcus-gh.bio: The Rainbow Portrait of Elizabeth I was painted by an unknown English artist around 1602. It is sometimes attributed to Marcus Gheeraerts the Younger, a leading court portrait painter of the time, but experts are not sure.

Q11571471.bio: Kanō Eigaku was a Japanese painter of the Kanō school, a family of artists that painted for Japan's rulers for hundreds of years. He worked in the late Edo and Meiji periods. He was famous for traditional pictures of Japanese life. He died in 1867.

Q380494.bio: Charles Demuth was born in Lancaster, Pennsylvania, and studied art in Philadelphia and Paris. He was a leading American modernist known for crisp, precise paintings of buildings and factories. He lived with diabetes for most of his adult life. He died in Lancaster in 1935.

Q158840.bio: James Ensor was born in Ostend, Belgium, and lived there nearly his whole life. He painted bizarre carnival masks, skeletons, and crowds in bright, shocking colors. His strange work was ahead of its time, and he became a hero for modern artists. He died in Ostend in 1949.

Q360010.bio: Pierre Mignard was a French painter born in Troyes in 1612. He was a favorite of Louis XIV, painted many portraits of him and became the first painter to the king. He died in Paris in 1695.

Q5581.bio: Vittore Carpaccio was a Venetian painter born in about 1465. He painted large story pictures filled with details of Venetian life, such as boats, bridges, clothes and animals. He died in about 1520.

Q15433971.bio: Pierre-Charles Canot was a French engraver born around 1710 who moved to London. He engraved many sea scenes and battle pictures, and died in London in 1777.

Q7803.bio: Bronzino was a Florentine painter, born in 1503, who became the court painter of the Medici family. He is known for cool, elegant portraits with smooth skin, rich clothes and a proud look. He died in 1572.

Q727869.bio: Gustaaf Wappers was born in Antwerp and became the leading Belgian Romantic history painter. He painted scenes of the Belgian Revolution of 1830. He lived in Brussels and Paris. He died in Paris in 1874.

Q107308387.bio: Konstantinos Tzanes was a painter from the Greek island of Crete, born in 1633. Like many Cretan painters, he moved to Venice, where he mixed the Greek icon tradition with Italian art. He died there in 1685.

Q2339347.bio: Ivan Grohar was born in what is now Slovenia and became one of the country's best-known painters. He painted farmers and landscapes in bright, bold colors. He studied in Ljubljana and Munich. He died in Ljubljana in 1911.

Q44007.bio: Paul Klee was born near Bern, Switzerland, to a musical family and was also a talented violinist. He taught at the Bauhaus, a famous art school in Germany, and later fled the Nazis to Switzerland. His playful, imaginative paintings use lines, colors and symbols as if they were music. He died in Switzerland in 1940.

Q15104963.bio: Julian Russell Story was an American painter born in Walton-on-Thames, England, in 1857. He was the son of the sculptor William Wetmore Story, studied in Paris, and later lived in Philadelphia, where he died in 1919.

Q122382.bio: Henry Fuseli was born in Zurich, Switzerland, and moved to England as a young man. He became a professor at the Royal Academy in London. He loved stories of ghosts, witches, and nightmares and painted them with dramatic, wild imagination. His artwork influenced the Romantic movement and later the Surrealists.

Q20017223.bio: Merle De Vore Johnson was an American illustrator born in Oregon City in 1874. He drew posters and magazine covers and later became a well-known collector of rare books. He lived in New York and died there in 1935.

Q5589.bio: Henri Matisse was born in northern France and began painting after an illness at age 20. He lived in Paris and then in Nice in the south, where he painted in bold, free colors. He was the leader of Fauvism, whose name means 'wild beasts', and later made colorful paper cut-outs. He died in Nice in 1954.

Q65317.bio: Godfrey Kneller was a German-born painter, born in Lübeck in 1646. He moved to England and became the most successful portrait painter in London, painting eight kings and queens as well as Isaac Newton. He died in London in 1723.

Q5811.bio: Masaccio was an Italian painter, born in 1401, whose nickname means clumsy Tom. He was one of the first painters to paint people with real weight and shadow, which was a big step forward in Renaissance art, and he died young, in Rome in 1428.

Q18735046.bio: Thomas Falcon Marshall was an English painter born in Liverpool in 1818. He lived in London and painted historical and storytelling pictures, many of them about the English Civil War and Mary Queen of Scots. He died in Kensington in 1878.

Q18575166.bio: Martin Borgord was born in Gausdal, Norway, in 1869, and became a painter of history and portraits. He studied in Germany and spent time in the United States. He died in 1935.

Q3385390.bio: Pierre Gustave Staal was a French illustrator born in Vertus in 1817. He made lithographs and engravings of costumes and portraits, including a well-known portrait of Pocahontas, and lived in Paris, where he died in 1882.

Q318427.bio: Mikhail Nesterov was born in Ufa, Russia, and became a leading painter of religious and spiritual scenes. He painted frescoes in churches and created poetic pictures of saints in Russian landscapes. He lived through the Russian Revolution and continued painting in Moscow. He died there in 1942.

Q280851.bio: Piero di Cosimo was a Florentine painter born in 1461. He liked painting mythical stories with strange creatures and wild nature, and he had a reputation as an eccentric who lived on hard-boiled eggs. He died in 1522.

Q911575.bio: Paul Baudry was born in La Roche-sur-Yon, France, and trained in Paris and Rome. He painted elegant portraits and murals, including the ceiling of the Paris Opera foyer. His work was admired by the Emperor Napoleon III. He died in Paris in 1886.

Q381698.bio: John Michael Wright was a painter born in London in 1617, of Scottish descent. He lived in Rome as a young man and returned to England, where he painted portraits of King Charles II and his court. He died in London in 1694.

Q5599.bio: Peter Paul Rubens was born in Siegen, Germany, in 1577 and grew up in Antwerp, which became his home. He was the most famous Baroque painter of northern Europe, ran a huge workshop, and also worked as a diplomat for Spain. He died in Antwerp in 1640.

Q271484.bio: Marguerite Gérard was born in Grasse, France, and moved to Paris as a teenager to train with her brother-in-law, Fragonard. She became a successful painter of elegant home scenes, often showing women reading, writing or playing music. She exhibited at the Salon and sold to the wealthy collectors of Europe. She died in Paris in 1837.

Q156889.bio: Suzanne Valadon was born in a small town in France and moved to Paris as a girl. She worked as a circus performer and an artist's model for Renoir and Toulouse-Lautrec before teaching herself to paint. She became the first woman admitted to the French National Society of Fine Arts. She lived in Montmartre and died in Paris in 1938.

Q206820.bio: Anders Zorn was born in the Swedish region of Dalarna and became one of the most famous painters of his time. He was a master of watercolor and painted portraits of presidents, including Theodore Roosevelt. He made a home in Mora, Sweden, where his house is now a museum. He died in 1920.

Q468214.bio: Ludolf Bakhuizen was a Dutch painter born in Emden, Germany, in 1630. He lived in Amsterdam, where he painted ships and stormy seas, and was said to have gone out in small boats to watch the storms. He died in 1708.

Q270658.bio: Jacob Jordaens was a Flemish painter born in Antwerp in 1593 who lived there all his life. He worked alongside Rubens and became famous for lively scenes with big, rosy figures, including feasts and proverbs. He died in Antwerp in 1678.

Q734843.bio: Jean Le Tavernier was a painter and manuscript illuminator from Oudenaarde in Flanders, active between about 1434 and 1462. He worked in Brussels for the dukes of Burgundy, especially Philip the Good, painting richly detailed pictures in their chronicles and prayer books.

Q301.bio: El Greco, whose name means The Greek, was born on the island of Crete in 1541 and moved to Spain, where he lived in Toledo. He painted long, twisting figures with flickering light and brilliant colors, quite unlike anyone else of his time. He died in 1614.

Q662983.bio: Theodoros Vryzakis was a Greek painter born in Thebes in 1814. He studied in Munich and became known for large paintings of the Greek War of Independence, which helped shape Greek national memory. He died in Munich in 1878.

Q3319624.bio: Molly Bobak was a Canadian painter born in Vancouver in 1920. She was the first woman official war artist in the Canadian army in World War II, married the artist Bruno Bobak, and lived in Fredericton, New Brunswick, until she died in 2014.

x-nasa-photograph-by-neil-armstrong.bio: Neil Armstrong, born in 1930 in Ohio, was the commander of Apollo 11 and the first person to walk on the Moon in 1969. Because he carried the camera, most of the famous photographs from the Moon walk show Buzz Aldrin, not him. He died in 2012.

Q610971.bio: José María Velasco was born in a village in Mexico and became the country's most famous landscape painter. He was also a scientist who studied plants, animals and the sky. His paintings of the Valley of Mexico show its volcanoes and lakes. He died in Mexico City in 1912.

Q302062.bio: Antonio Bellucci was an Italian painter born in 1654, who worked in Venice, Vienna and England. He painted religious scenes and myths with warm color. He died in 1726.

Q184212.bio: Théodore Géricault was born in Rouen, France, and grew up in Paris, where he fell in love with horses and dramatic subjects. He studied wounded soldiers and even hospital patients so he could paint with truth. He rose to fame with 'The Raft of the Medusa' at 27. A passionate horse rider, he died in Paris at only 32, partly after riding accidents.

Q34618.bio: Gustave Courbet was born in Ornans, in eastern France, and moved to Paris to become an artist. He led the Realism movement, insisting on painting real people and real life instead of myths. He was outspoken and got into political trouble, and he fled to Switzerland in the end. He died there in 1877.

Q434006.bio: Pieter Coecke van Aelst was a Flemish painter, designer and writer born in Aalst in 1502. He designed tapestries and stained glass and was the teacher, and later the father-in-law, of Pieter Bruegel the Elder. He died in Brussels in 1550.

Q4568470.bio: Joachim Frich was a Norwegian landscape painter born in Bergen in 1810. He studied in Dresden with Johan Christian Dahl. He painted the fjords and mountains of Norway. He died in Christiania in 1858.

Q3130641.bio: Henri Beau was born in Montreal and studied in Paris, where he spent much of his life. He painted historical scenes of Canada and later official war paintings. He died in Paris in 1949.

Q2666703.bio: Halfdan Egedius was born in Drammen in 1877 and became one of the most promising Norwegian painters of his generation, especially for his landscapes and book illustrations. He died of illness at the age of 22, in 1899.

Q560548.bio: Joos de Momper the Younger was a Flemish painter born in Antwerp in 1564. He painted wild, rocky mountain landscapes and stormy seas, and he died in 1635.

Q1392667.bio: Patrick Henry Bruce was an American painter born in Campbell County, Virginia, in 1881. He lived in Paris for most of his career, studied with Matisse and painted bright, rhythmic pictures of shapes and objects. He returned to New York, where he died in 1936.

Q344838.bio: Winslow Homer was born in Boston and became one of America's greatest painters. He started as an illustrator and covered the Civil War for a magazine. Later, he lived on the rocky coast of Maine, where he painted the sea, fishermen and storms. He died at his home at Prouts Neck in 1910.

Q152797.bio: Umberto Boccioni was born in Reggio Calabria, Italy, and became the leader of Futurism, a movement that celebrated speed and machines. He worked in Milan and Rome, painting and making sculptures full of motion. He died at 33 after falling from a horse during military training in 1916.

Q68631.bio: Rogier van der Weyden was a Flemish painter born in Tournai in about 1399. He worked in Brussels and became one of the most admired painters of Northern Europe for pictures that show deep feeling and realistic tears. He died in 1464.

Q2199553.bio: Laurits Andersen Ring was born in a village in Denmark and became a leading Danish painter. He is known for quiet, thoughtful scenes of country life and portraits of his family. He lived and worked in the Danish countryside. He died in 1933.

Q391608.bio: Asher Brown Durand was born in New Jersey and began as an engraver before becoming a landscape painter. He was a leader of the Hudson River School and the second president of the National Academy of Design. His painting 'Kindred Spirits' is a famous American image. He died in 1886.

Q152233.bio: El Lissitzky was a Russian artist born in Pochinok in 1890. He worked as an architect, a painter and a designer, and made his famous poster of the Red Wedge in 1919. He lived in Vitebsk, Germany and Moscow, and died in Moscow in 1941.

x-ferdinand-pauwels-attributed.bio: Ferdinand Pauwels was a Belgian painter born in Eeklo in 1830. He became a professor at the art academy in Dresden, Germany, and painted large scenes from the history of the Reformation. This picture is attributed to him, which means experts think but cannot prove that he painted it. He died in Dresden in 1904.

Q186202.bio: Giovanni Battista Tiepolo was born in Venice and became the greatest Italian painter of the 1700s. He painted huge, airy ceilings full of angels, gods and clouds in churches and palaces in Italy, Germany and Spain. His light, bright colors defined the last great age of Venetian painting. He died in Madrid in 1770.

Q718474.bio: Panagiotis Zographos was a Greek painter from the Peloponnese who lived in the 1800s. He painted a famous series of scenes of the Greek War of Independence in a bright folk style, after the memories of the general Makriyannis, who hired him in the 1830s.

x-english-school.bio: This painting was made by an unknown English artist around 1590. Many paintings of the Armada were made soon after the battle, and the painters of these often did not sign their works.

Q1498652.bio: Solomon Alexander Hart was born in Plymouth, England, to a Jewish family and trained in London. In 1840 he became the first Jewish member of the Royal Academy. He painted history scenes, portraits and pictures of Jewish life. He died in London in 1881.

Q105320.bio: Berthe Morisot was born in Bourges, France, and studied painting with Corot. She exhibited in the first Impressionist show in 1874 and was one of the movement's leading figures. She married Eugène Manet, the brother of Édouard Manet, and lived in Paris. She painted women, children and gardens with a light, fresh touch.

Q1133777.bio: Cornelius Krieghoff was born in Amsterdam and moved to North America as a young man. He lived in Montreal and Quebec, where he painted lively scenes of French-Canadian farm life and winter. His humorous pictures made him one of Canada's most popular painters. He died in Chicago in 1872.

Q148458.bio: Jean-François Millet was born into a farming family in Gruchy, on the coast of Normandy, France. He moved to the village of Barbizon near Paris, where he painted peasants at work in the fields. He treated farm laborers with dignity at a time when few artists did. His paintings moved Van Gogh and many others.

Q671883.bio: Théo van Rysselberghe was born in Ghent, Belgium, and was a leading painter in the pointillist style, which uses tiny dots of color. He painted portraits and summer landscapes. He spent his last years on the French Riviera. He died in 1926.

Q658162.bio: Wilhelm Camphausen was a German painter born in Düsseldorf in 1818. He specialized in battle and military scenes, painted the wars of Prussia, and lived in Düsseldorf, where he died in 1885.

Q2576609.bio: Ludvig Karsten was a Norwegian painter born in Christiania in 1876. He lived a free, bohemian life, traveling in Europe and painting in bold, bright colors. He died in Paris in 1926.

Q5591.bio: Pinturicchio was an Italian painter born in Perugia in 1454. His nickname means little painter, and he painted rich, gold-covered frescoes in the Vatican for the Borgia pope and in many churches. He died in Siena in 1513.

Q359506.bio: Mark Gertler was born in London to Jewish immigrants from Poland and grew up in the poor neighborhood of Spitalfields. He studied at the Slade School of Art and became a friend of many writers and artists of his time. He is best known for his bold, rounded paintings, such as 'Merry-Go-Round'. He died in London in 1939.

Q5080054.bio: Charles Landseer was an English painter born in London in 1799, the older brother of the animal painter Edwin Landseer. He painted historical scenes, especially from the English Civil War, and was the Keeper of the Royal Academy. He died in London in 1879.

Q454945.bio: Charles Willson Peale was born in Maryland and became one of the best-known American painters of the Revolution. He painted George Washington many times, fought in the war, and also founded a museum in Philadelphia. He lived in Philadelphia and died there in 1827.

Q159758.bio: J. M. W. Turner was born in London, the son of a barber, and became a student at the Royal Academy at just 14. He traveled across Britain and Europe, painting storms, ships, and sunsets in swirling light and color. He called the sky his subject, and his late paintings are almost abstract. He left thousands of works to the British nation when he died in London in 1851.

Q310715.bio: Henri Fantin-Latour was born in Grenoble, France, and spent most of his life in Paris. He was a friend of Manet and the Impressionists, though his own style was more traditional. He painted lovely flowers and group portraits of artists and musicians. He died in 1904.

Q7129.bio: Cosimo Tura was an Italian painter born in Ferrara in about 1430. His pictures have sharp, strange, metallic-looking figures and rich colors, in a style all his own. He died in 1495.

Q332494.bio: Luca Giordano was a Neapolitan painter, born in 1632. He painted so fast that people called him Luca Fa Presto, Luca Work Fast. His huge, swirling ceilings and altarpieces decorated palaces and churches in Italy and Spain. He died in Naples in 1705.

Q3499926.bio: A. Y. Jackson was a Canadian painter born in Montreal in 1882. He was a founding member of the Group of Seven, an official war artist in World War I, and one of the painters who made rugged northern landscapes famous. He died in Kleinburg, Ontario, in 1974.

Q458671.bio: Giuseppe Castiglione was born in Milan, Italy, and became a Jesuit brother, traveling as a missionary to China. He took the name Lang Shining and served as a court painter for three Chinese emperors. He blended European realism with Chinese styles. He died in Beijing in 1766.

Q2834961.bio: Alfred Bastien was a Belgian painter born in 1873. He painted huge panoramas, then during World War I he was a war artist for the Canadian War Memorials, making large paintings of the front at Passchendaele. He lived in Brussels and died in Uccle in 1955.

Q556681.bio: Dmitry Levitzky was a Russian painter born in Kyiv in 1735. He became the leading portrait painter in Saint Petersburg during the reign of Catherine the Great, painting nobles and thinkers, including Diderot. He died in Saint Petersburg in 1822.

x-byzantine-mosaicists.bio: The mosaics of Hagia Sophia in Constantinople were made by Byzantine artists whose names are not known. They placed thousands of tiny pieces of colored glass and gold in the plaster, creating images that glitter in candlelight, over several centuries.

Q9348.bio: Parmigianino was an Italian painter, born in Parma in 1503. His pictures have long necks, elegant poses and smooth skin, and he painted one of the most famous self-portraits, in a convex mirror. He died in 1540.

Q304411.bio: Melchior d'Hondecoeter was a Dutch painter born in Utrecht in 1636. He specialized in painting birds, such as peacocks, roosters and ducks, in lively, feathery pictures. He died in Amsterdam in 1695.

Q208993.bio: Nicholas Roerich was a Russian painter born in Saint Petersburg in 1874. He painted scenes from ancient Russian history and legend, designed ballet sets, and after the revolution left Russia, traveling through Asia and finally settling in northern India. He died in Kullu, India, in 1947.

Q2112365.bio: Jean Duplessis-Bertaux was a French engraver and painter born in Paris in 1747. He is known for his lively prints of the events of the French Revolution and the Napoleonic wars. He lived in Paris and died there in 1818.

Q982011.bio: Giambattista Pittoni was a Venetian painter, born in 1687. He painted Bible scenes and myths in light, bright colors in the airy Venetian style, and became head of the Venetian art academy. He died in 1767.

Q432296.bio: Werner Holmberg was a Finnish landscape painter born in Helsinki in 1830. He studied in Düsseldorf in Germany, where he died of illness at only 30. His paintings of Finnish forests and fields were important for Finnish art.

Q154338.bio: Matthias Grünewald was a German painter born in about 1480. His religious paintings have strong colors and powerful emotions, and his Isenheim Altarpiece is one of the greatest works of German art. He died in Halle in 1528.

Q2938914.bio: Carl Frederik von Breda was a Swedish painter born in Stockholm in 1759. He spent nine years in England, where he painted portraits, including one of the antislavery campaigner Thomas Clarkson, and later became court painter in Sweden. He died in Stockholm in 1818.

Q33978.bio: Robert Delaunay was a French painter born in Paris in 1885. With his wife Sonia, he invented a colorful style called Orphism and painted the Eiffel Tower, windows and circles of color. He spent the war years in Spain and Portugal, and died in Montpellier in 1941.

Q5716922.bio: Henry Mayer, nicknamed Hy Mayer, was a cartoonist born in Worms, Germany, in 1868. He moved to the United States, where he became a popular cartoonist for Puck magazine and a pioneer of animated cartoons. He lived in New York and died in 1954.

Q360724.bio: Stanhope Forbes was an Irish-born English painter born in Dublin in 1857. He settled in Newlyn in Cornwall, where he painted fishermen and villagers in the open air, and founded an art school. He died in Newlyn in 1947.

Q2534502.bio: Thomas Hill was an English-born American painter born in Birmingham in 1829. He grew up in Massachusetts and moved to California, where he painted huge landscapes of Yosemite and the Sierra Nevada. He died in Raymond, California, in 1908.

Q289624.bio: Emily Carr was born in Victoria, British Columbia, and studied art in San Francisco, London and France. She became famous for her paintings of the forests, totem poles and Indigenous villages of the Pacific coast. She was also a writer and lived with many pets. She died in Victoria in 1945.

Q1383289.bio: John de Critz was a painter born in Antwerp around 1551 who moved to London as a boy. He became Serjeant-Painter to King James I, painting portraits and decorating royal buildings. He lived in London until he died in 1642.

Q269338.bio: Josefa de Óbidos was a painter born in Seville in 1630, who grew up and worked in Portugal. She painted religious pictures and still lifes and was one of the best-known Portuguese painters of her time. She died in 1684.

Q183458.bio: Andrea del Verrocchio was an Italian sculptor and painter born in Florence in about 1435. His busy workshop trained many famous artists, including Leonardo da Vinci. He died in Venice in 1488.

Q551695.bio: Domenico Fetti was an Italian painter born in Rome in 1589. He painted lively, loosely brushed pictures and worked in Mantua and Venice. He died young, in Venice, in 1623.

x-anonymous-illuminator-vigiles-de-charl.bio: This miniature was painted by an unknown artist who illustrated the Vigiles du roi Charles VII, a French poem by Martial d'Auvergne about the reign of King Charles VII, in about 1484.

Q207298.bio: Frédéric Bazille was born into a wealthy family in Montpellier, France, and moved to Paris to paint. He was a close friend of Monet and Renoir and shared a studio with them. He painted sunny outdoor scenes and portraits. He was killed in the Franco-Prussian War in 1870 when he was only 28.

Q27028228.bio: John Rose was a painter in the late 1700s who lived in the Colony of South Carolina. His watercolor 'The Old Plantation' is one of the earliest paintings to show the lives of enslaved African Americans. Little else is known about him.

Q5586.bio: Katsushika Hokusai was born in Edo (now Tokyo) and worked as an artist for over 70 years. He made thousands of drawings and woodblock prints, including The Great Wave and the Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji. He changed his name dozens of times and said he hoped to get better until he was 110. He died in 1849, at about age 89.

Q3469342.bio: Sakai Hōitsu was born in Edo (Tokyo) to a samurai family and became a leading painter of the Rinpa school. He admired Ogata Kōrin and worked to revive his style. He painted flowers, birds and the seasons. He died in 1828.

Q232423.bio: Judith Leyster was a Dutch painter born in Haarlem in 1609. She painted lively scenes of musicians and everyday people and was one of the few women admitted to the painters' guild. After she died in 1660 her work was mistaken for Frans Hals's until it was rediscovered in the 1890s.

Q167654.bio: Frans Hals was a Dutch painter who was born in Antwerp around 1582 and lived most of his life in Haarlem. He painted lively portraits with fast, loose brushstrokes, so his sitters seem to laugh, drink and talk right in front of you. He died in Haarlem in 1666.

Q297.bio: Diego Velázquez was a Spanish painter born in Seville in 1599. He moved to Madrid as a young man and became the court painter to King Philip IV, painting portraits such as Las Meninas that are among the greatest in the world. He died in Madrid in 1660.

Q363823.bio: Christoffer Wilhelm Eckersberg was born in southern Denmark and became the 'father of Danish painting.' He studied in Paris and Rome and taught many painters in Copenhagen. He painted portraits, ships, and clear, bright scenes of Rome. He died in Copenhagen in 1853.

Q229272.bio: Ernst Ludwig Kirchner was born in Aschaffenburg, Germany, and trained as an architect before he became a founder of the group Die Brücke ('The Bridge'). He lived in Dresden and Berlin and later in the Swiss Alps near Davos. His jagged, colorful paintings made him a star of German Expressionism. He died in Switzerland in 1938.

Q274909.bio: Émile Bayard was a French painter and illustrator born in La Ferté-sous-Jouarre in 1837. He is best known for illustrating books such as Les Misérables, including the famous drawing of the young Cosette with her broom. He died in Cairo, Egypt, in 1891.

Q365682.bio: Gordon Parks was an American photographer born in Fort Scott, Kansas, in 1912. He started as a government photographer, then worked for Life magazine, wrote books and directed the film Shaft. He lived in New York and died there in 2006.

Q552440.bio: Constantin Meunier was a Belgian sculptor and painter born in Etterbeek in 1831. He is famous for his dignified pictures and statues of coal miners, steelworkers and dockers, and he lived in Brussels, where he died in 1905.

Q2035136.bio: Tom Thomson was born in Ontario and worked as a commercial artist in Toronto before devoting himself to painting. He spent his summers in Algonquin Park, making small colorful oil sketches of lakes, trees and skies. His friends who later formed the Group of Seven were inspired by him. He drowned in Canoe Lake in 1917, and his death is still a famous mystery.

Q149571.bio: Carl Blechen was a German painter born in Cottbus in 1798. He lived in Berlin, traveled to Italy, and painted romantic landscapes and some of the earliest pictures of factories and industry in German art. He died in Berlin in 1840.

Q707046.bio: Piero del Pollaiuolo was a Florentine painter, born in 1443, who worked with his older brother Antonio. They shared a workshop and studied the human body in action. He died in Rome in 1496.

Q3325858.bio: Benedito Calixto was a Brazilian painter born in 1853 in Itanhaém, near São Paulo. He painted history, religious subjects and the coast. He was also an historian. He died in São Paulo in 1927.

Q381299.bio: Louis-Michel van Loo was born in Toulon, France, to a family of painters. He worked in Paris and also in Spain as the court painter to King Philip V. His portraits show silk, lace and royal splendor. He died in Paris in 1771.

Q758925.bio: Jan van Bijlert was a Dutch painter born in Utrecht in 1597. He went to Rome, followed Caravaggio's style, and painted Bible scenes, myths and musicians. He died in 1671.

Q120993.bio: Amedeo Modigliani was born in Livorno, Italy, and moved to Paris in 1906. He painted and sculpted people with long necks, almond-shaped eyes, and elegant simplified faces. He was poor and ill throughout his short life and died in Paris at 35. Only after his death did his fame explode. Modigliani was born into a Sephardic Jewish family in Italy and was proud of his heritage all his life.

Q184669.bio: Jean Ranc was a French portrait painter born in Montpellier in 1674. He worked at the court in Madrid, where he painted the Spanish royal family. He died there in 1735.

Q711903.bio: Albert Gleizes was a French painter born in Paris in 1881. He was one of the artists who invented Cubism and wrote an important book about it with Jean Metzinger. He lived in Paris and New York, and later in the south of France, where he died in 1953.

Q541976.bio: Jan Asselijn was a Dutch painter born in about 1600 in Dieppe, France. He traveled to Italy and painted sunny Italian landscapes, and later settled in Amsterdam. He died in 1652.

Q216999.bio: Antoine-Jean Gros was born in Paris and was a student of Jacques-Louis David. He became Napoleon's war painter, traveling with the army to capture battles and heroic scenes. His lively, dramatic art influenced the Romantic painters. He died in 1835 near Paris.

Q29447.bio: Cosimo Rosselli was a Florentine painter born in 1439. He was one of the artists invited to Rome to paint the walls of the Sistine Chapel in the 1480s. He died in 1507.

Q709280.bio: Arthur Streeton was born in Victoria, Australia, and became a leading painter of the Heidelberg School, a group of artists who painted outdoors. He is best known for golden, sunny landscapes. He later lived in London and returned to Australia. He died in 1943.

Q192062.bio: Bartolomé Esteban Murillo was a Spanish painter born in Seville in 1617. He painted soft, warm pictures of Mary and the saints and also lovely scenes of poor children in the street. He died in Seville in 1682.

Q5541159.bio: George Jones was an English painter born in London in 1786. He served in the army and then painted battle scenes and historical subjects, becoming a member and later the Keeper of the Royal Academy. He died in London in 1869.

Q33522534.bio: Alanson Fisher was an American portrait painter born in 1807. He lived mainly in New York, painting portraits of well-known people, including the author Harriet Beecher Stowe. He died in 1884.

Q346483.bio: Maurice Cullen was born in St. John's, Newfoundland, and grew up in Montreal. He studied in Paris, and became known for his glowing paintings of snowy Montreal and the St. Lawrence River. In World War I he served as an official Canadian war artist. He died in 1934.

Q187506.bio: Honoré Daumier was born in Marseille, France, and grew up in Paris. He was famous for his satirical cartoons that poked fun at politicians, and he created thousands of prints. He also painted sympathetic pictures of working people. He lost his sight late in life and died in 1879.

Q143595.bio: Stradanus, whose Flemish name was Jan van der Straet, was a painter and designer born in Bruges in 1523. He moved to Florence, where he designed tapestries for the Medici and many prints, including a famous series on the discovery of America. He died in Florence in 1605.

Q553258.bio: Francisco Pradilla y Ortiz was born in a small village in Aragón, Spain, and trained in Madrid and Rome. He became famous for large history paintings of kings and queens. He served as director of the Prado Museum. He died in Madrid in 1921.

Q7724.bio: August Strindberg was born in Stockholm, Sweden, and is best known as one of the world's greatest playwrights and novelists. He also painted dramatic, stormy landscapes in his later years, which were far ahead of their time. He lived in Sweden, Germany, France and Denmark. He died in Stockholm in 1912.

Q160252.bio: Frederic Leighton was born in Scarborough, England, and traveled across Europe as a child, speaking several languages. He became a leading Victorian painter of classical subjects and was President of the Royal Academy. He was the first British artist to be made a baron. His house in London is now a museum.

Q109061.bio: Guido Reni was an Italian painter born in Bologna in 1575. He became one of the most admired artists of the Baroque, known for graceful figures, soft light and pretty faces in his religious and mythological scenes. He died in Bologna in 1642.

Q9011444.bio: Jennie Augusta Brownscombe was an American painter born in Honesdale, Pennsylvania, in 1850. She became famous for her warm pictures of American history, especially the Pilgrims and Thanksgiving, and she lived and worked in New York. She died in Queens in 1936.

Q5854655.bio: Axel Ender was a Norwegian painter born in 1853 in Asker. He studied in Germany and painted landscapes and folk scenes. He lived in Christiania (Oslo). He died in 1920.

paintings.why: A woman with a calm face and a faint smile sits in front of a hazy landscape of winding paths and rivers. Leonardo da Vinci painted it in about 1503, and it is probably the most famous painting in the world, so visitors to the Louvre crowd around it.

A giant wave curls over like a claw above three small fishing boats, with Mount Fuji tiny and calm in the distance. Katsushika Hokusai made this woodblock print around 1831 when he was about 70, and it became the most famous image of Japanese art in the world. Thousands of copies were printed, and it inspired artists in Europe like Van Gogh and Monet. It's a perfect picture of nature's power.
paintings.k: Count the three boats, then spot tiny Mount Fuji hiding under the wave. What do the wave's foamy fingertips look like?

paintings.why: Van Gogh painted this from memory while staying in a hospital in southern France, and the swirling sky seems to be alive with energy. Instead of copying what he saw, he painted how the night felt: glowing stars, a rolling wind and a sleepy village below. The bold, curling brushstrokes were revolutionary, and they showed artists they could paint emotions, not just objects. Today it is one of the most recognized paintings on Earth.
paintings.k: Count the glowing stars in the sky, then find the tall church steeple in the village below.

paintings.why: A girl in a blue and yellow turban looks over her shoulder at us, with her lips slightly parted and a large pearl at her ear, against a dark background. Johannes Vermeer painted it in about 1665, and no one knows who she was. It is often called the Mona Lisa of the North.

A woman holding the French flag charges over a barricade, with people of every background following her. Delacroix painted it after the 1830 July Revolution in Paris, and it turned a real uprising into a symbol of freedom. The drama, color and movement made it a landmark of Romantic painting. Its image of Liberty has inspired posters, stamps, and even the Statue of Liberty's story.

A company of citizen soldiers in Amsterdam marches out with a flag and drum, with a little girl glowing in gold in the middle. Rembrandt painted it in 1642, and the name comes from a dark layer of varnish, but it is really a daytime scene.

The goddess Venus stands on a giant scallop shell, blown by the winds to the shore, where a woman waits to cover her with a cloak. Sandro Botticelli painted it in about 1485, and it is one of the most famous pictures in the world. Venus is shown without clothes, as a goddess of love.

A little princess stands among her ladies-in-waiting, dwarfs and a dog, while the painter, Velázquez, stands at a big canvas, and in a mirror at the back you can see the king and queen. He painted it in 1656, and people still ask who the painting is really about.

Mount Fuji glows red in the morning sun, with white clouds drifting and a deep blue sky. Hokusai made this woodblock print, called 'Red Fuji,' as part of his series Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji. The mountain looks big and calm, like a friendly giant. It's one of the most beloved prints from Japan.
paintings.k: Mount Fuji glows red in the morning. What color is the sky?

paintings.why: Van Gogh wanted to show how poor farmers really lived, so he painted a family sharing a humble meal of potatoes by lamplight. The dark, earthy colors and rough faces were deliberate: he wanted to honor honest work with hands that dug the food they ate. It was his first big masterpiece, painted long before his famous bright colors. It reminds us that great art can be about ordinary, hardworking people.

Monet painted the misty port of Le Havre at dawn, with a small orange sun and boats made of just a few quick strokes. When critics saw it in 1874, one mockingly said it was only an 'impression' — and the name Impressionism was born! The painting captures a fleeting moment of light instead of fine details. It launched a whole movement that changed how people think about painting.

The ancient Greek thinker Socrates was sentenced to drink poison, and David shows him calmly raising a finger to make one last point while friends weep around him. The clear, sculpture-like figures and calm lighting made it a model of Neoclassical painting. It is famous because it makes a big idea — standing up for your beliefs, even at great cost — feel real and powerful.

Two lovers are wrapped together in a golden robe, covered in glittering patterns, kneeling on a flower-dotted meadow. Klimt used real gold leaf, which makes the painting shimmer like a jewel. He mixed flat, decorative patterns with soft, realistic faces and hands. It became the most famous work of the Vienna Secession and is loved around the world as a picture of tenderness.

A young woman cradles a white, stoat-like animal called an ermine in her arm, and both of them turn to look at something off to the side. Leonardo da Vinci painted Cecilia Gallerani in about 1490, and the animal was a symbol of purity and also a pun on her name.

Christ holds a glass orb in one hand and raises the other in blessing, and his eyes meet yours. This painting is attributed to Leonardo da Vinci and sold in 2017 for 450 million dollars, the highest price ever paid for a painting.

The left panel shows paradise, the center a garden of naked people with giant fruit and birds, and the right panel a fiery hell full of monsters. Hieronymus Bosch painted this triptych in about 1490, and nobody is sure exactly what it means, which is part of why people love it.

paintings.t: Wanderer above the Sea of Fog
paintings.why: A lone traveler stands on a rocky peak with his back to us, gazing over a sea of mist and mountains. Friedrich wanted us to stand in his place and feel awe at nature's size and mystery. It has become the icon of Romanticism, the idea that nature and personal feelings matter deeply. We still know it because everyone has felt like that tiny wanderer at some big, quiet view.
paintings.k: He stands on a rock above the clouds. What would you see if you stood beside him?

paintings.why: In 1816 a French ship wrecked, and a handful of survivors drifted on a raft for almost two weeks. Géricault painted the moment they spot rescue far away, using huge, life-size figures and dramatic light. He even studied real survivors to get the details right. The painting was a sensation, turning a news story into a timeless picture of hope and survival against terrible odds.

According to legend, a band of Cossack warriors received an insulting demand from the Turkish sultan to surrender, and they responded with a joke-filled, rude letter. Repin shows them roaring with laughter as the scribe writes. It took him over a decade, and the laughing faces are so lively you can almost hear them. It's beloved in Ukraine and Russia for its humor and spirit.

paintings.t: The Anatomy Lesson of Dr. Nicolaes Tulp
paintings.why: A doctor with a hat demonstrates the muscles of an arm on a dead body, while seven men lean in to watch. Rembrandt painted it in 1632, when he was only 26, and it made him famous in Amsterdam.

Goya painted a woman reclining on a couch, looking directly at the viewer in a way that was bold and unusual for its time. The painting got him into trouble with the Spanish Inquisition, which only added to its fame. It is remembered for its honest, real-person feeling instead of the idealized goddesses artists usually painted. It's also famously paired with a clothed twin, La maja vestida.

A firing squad aims at a man in a white shirt who raises his arms, while others wait their turn in the dark. Goya painted this to remember Spanish citizens who were executed after standing up to Napoleon's army. He used a glowing lantern and a faceless line of soldiers to make the cruelty of war feel real. It's considered one of the first truly modern anti-war paintings.

Manet showed a picnic in the woods where two men in everyday suits sit with a woman who isn't dressed for the occasion — and the Paris art world was shocked. Everyone expected nudes to be goddesses from myths, not modern people at lunch. It was rejected from the official show in 1863, then displayed in the famous 'Salon of the Rejected.' It marks a turning point toward modern art.

A woman in a yellow bodice and blue apron pours milk very steadily from a jug into a bowl, in a plain room with light from the window. Johannes Vermeer painted it in about 1660, and every little thing, even the bread crumbs, shines.

paintings.t: Bal du moulin de la Galette
paintings.why: On a sunny Sunday in Montmartre, Parisians dance and chat under trees dappled with light. Renoir painted it on the spot with his friends as models, capturing the happiness of an ordinary afternoon. The flickering spots of sunlight on clothing are a hallmark of Impressionism. It's famous for making you feel as if you've joined the party, and it's one of the most valuable paintings ever sold.

A couple in a small bedroom holds hands, and a little dog stands at their feet. Look at the round mirror behind them: it shows the whole room, and two people standing in the door. Jan van Eyck painted this in 1434, and he even wrote on the wall that he was there.

A woman reclines on a bed, looking straight at us, with a maid bringing flowers and a black cat at her feet. Manet's frank, flat style and her confident gaze scandalized visitors in 1865; some even tried to attack it. Instead of a polite myth, he painted a real modern woman who isn't shy. Today it is seen as a brave starting point of modern art.

Van Gogh painted these irises in the garden of the hospital where he was staying. The purple blooms rise and bend across a sea of green, with one lonely white flower standing out. The bold outlines were inspired by Japanese woodblock prints, which he adored. It sold for a record-setting price in 1987 and remains one of the most beloved flower paintings ever.
paintings.k: Find the one white flower among all the purple irises.

paintings.why: A golden field under a stormy blue sky, with a path that seems to run out and crows swirling overhead. Van Gogh painted it in the final weeks of his life, and many people read deep feelings of loneliness in it. Whatever he meant, the wild brushwork and bold color are unforgettable. It's often shown as the ultimate example of how painting can carry strong emotion.

Venus, the Three Graces, Mercury, Zephyr and Flora stand in an orange grove where hundreds of flowers cover the ground. Sandro Botticelli painted it in about 1480, and botanists have counted over 500 plants in it. It's one of the most famous paintings of the Renaissance.
l: Bedroom of Lorenzo il Magnifico of Palazzo Medici
