paintings.t: The Hanging of the Sigismund bell at the Cathedral Tower in 1521 in Kraków
paintings.why: In 1521 in Kraków, workers raise a giant bell by ropes into the cathedral tower, as the crowd and the king watch. The Sigismund Bell is still in the cathedral and still rings. Matejko painted the pride of the city. It's a lively picture of a big community project.

A stylish young woman in a deep blue dress and a flowered hat looks out with a confident smile. Renoir painted it in 1874 in the first year of Impressionism. The blue fabric glimmers in the light. It's an elegant picture of the modern city.

A famous surgeon pauses in an operating theater to explain a procedure to a room of students, his hand bloody. Eakins's honest picture showed modern science. Many in 1875 found the realism hard to look at. Today it's seen as one of the greatest American paintings.

A woman in a bright red Japanese kimono stands with a fan against a background of fans. Monet's wife Camille posed for it. Japanese art was a craze in Paris in the 1870s. It's a colorful, playful piece.

A man and woman sit on a bench in a glass-roofed garden room, surrounded by lush plants. Manet used the real-life couple, the Guillemets, who ran a shop. The woman wears a ring while the man leans toward her, with a gap between them. It's a subtle picture of two people.

The Duke of Prussia kneels to swear loyalty to the king of Poland in Kraków's central square in 1525. Matejko packed it with portraits of nobles and knights in rich costumes. It's a picture of a time when Poland was strong. It's a national treasure.

Two sisters in pink and blue dresses stand side by side, smiling softly. Renoir painted the daughters of a Parisian banker, Alice and Elisabeth Cahen d'Anvers. The soft colors and curls give them a sweet charm. It's a very sweet double portrait.

paintings.t: View of the Sea at Scheveningen
paintings.why: Dark waves roll under a gray sky, with a few small figures and boats on the beach. Van Gogh painted this on the Dutch coast in 1882, in the wind and sand. Tiny grains of sand are still stuck in the paint. It's an early, wild seascape.

paintings.t: The Favourites of the Emperor Honorius
paintings.why: A Roman emperor feeds his pet chickens, which he called by the names of cities, while an official brings news. In the legend, he cared more for his hens than for the news that Rome was falling. Waterhouse painted a rich scene of the late Roman Empire. It's a funny and surprising story.

Cupids and woodland figures dance in a flowery glade as spring returns. Bouguereau often painted fairy-tale scenes full of soft color and joyful movement. Nature wakes up after winter. It's a cheerful celebration of the season.

A crab lies on its back, its claws and legs curled, in a few strokes of orange and green. Van Gogh was inspired by Japanese prints and painted it in Paris. It's a quick but lively study. It shows he could find wonder in simple things.

A group of painters, writers and friends raise their glasses in a sunny garden in Skagen, in northern Denmark. Krøyer painted his colony of artist friends, including himself. The light is warm and the mood is joyful. It's one of the best-loved Danish paintings.

A long avenue of poplars glows with yellow and orange autumn light, with strolling couples. It was an ancient Roman cemetery in Arles, France. Van Gogh painted it in autumn 1888. The golden trees seem to dance.

Blossoming orchards line the foreground, with the old town of Arles and its stone towers behind them. Van Gogh was captivated by the spring in Provence. The painting glows with white and pink flowers. It's a happy picture of a fresh season.

A bush of lilacs stands in the garden of an asylum in Saint-Rémy, with a blue sky. Van Gogh painted this in the spring of 1889. The soft purples and blues contrast with the green leaves. It's a quiet picture of beauty in a hard time.

paintings.t: The Boy in the Red Vest
paintings.why: A young man in a red vest leans on his arm, painted in sculpted blocks of color. Cézanne painted this model, an Italian youth, several times. Look at his unnaturally long arm — it's deliberate, for the balance of the composition. It's one of the most famous modern portraits.

Van Gogh looks out with a bandage over his ear, wearing a fur cap and a thick coat, with a Japanese print behind him. He painted it after he hurt his ear in December 1888. It's a direct, honest picture of a difficult time. It's among the most famous self-portraits.

The goddess Venus rises from the sea, wearing a seashell like a hat, while cherubs frolic nearby. Gérôme was a great admirer of the classical world. He painted it late in his life. It's a lively picture of mythology.

Three Russian knights on horseback, from folk tales, scan the horizon for danger. Vasnetsov painted Ilya Muromets, Dobrynya Nikitich and Alyosha Popovich, famous heroes. It took him nearly 20 years. Many Russian kids know this painting from school.
paintings.k: Three knights ride on horses. Can you tell what each one is carrying?

paintings.why: A woman stands in the shadows with a large snake draped over her shoulders, her eyes glowing. Franz von Stuck painted this as a symbol of temptation. It was a huge success, and he painted several versions. It is a dark and dramatic Symbolist painting.

According to legend, Lady Godiva rode a horse through the town in protest of a harsh tax, and the townspeople kindly stayed indoors. Collier painted her in a hush of dignity. The tale is a famous English legend. It's a picture of courage.

A couple's faces merge into one in a dim room, beside a window with a glimmer of light. Munch painted several versions of the scene. The way the two become one is touching and mysterious. It's one of his best-loved paintings.

Two women stand close together, one holding a bowl of flowers or fruit, in bright colors. Gauguin painted this in his later years in the Marquesas Islands. The flat, rich colors are a sign of his love of the Pacific. It's one of his best-known island paintings.

A path leads through arches of irises, daylilies and roses in Monet's colorful garden. He designed the garden himself and painted it for decades. The mass of flowers is painted in joyful strokes. It's a glimpse of the paradise he built.

A crowd of workers marches steadily out of the shadows toward us. Pellizza spent years on this painting. He called it 'The Fourth Estate' because it showed the working class as a new force in society. It became a symbol of workers' rights in Italy.

An open window frames a view of boats in a harbor, with window boxes of flowers and bursts of pure color. Matisse painted this in the summer of 1905 at Collioure on France's southern coast. It's a famous Fauvist painting. It invites us to look out at a bright new view.

A dark silhouette of a snake charmer plays a flute in a moonlit jungle, with glowing eyes and snakes coiled around. Rousseau said it was inspired by a friend's story of India. The painting is full of lush leaves painted in dozens of greens. It's a dreamlike masterpiece.

Horses, workers and a rising city explode in a blur of color and movement. Boccioni painted it as a celebration of the energetic new industrial city of Milan. He was a leader of Futurism, which loved speed and machines. It's one of the key paintings of the movement.

A fashionable woman in a pink, patterned dress looks out in front of a bright, richly colored background. Klimt painted her a second time, years after his gold portrait. This one is colorful instead of golden. It sold for $88 million in 2006.

A tangle of colored rectangles and lines tilts and floats on a white ground, like objects in space. Malevich created Suprematism to show pure feeling in shapes. The painting seems to drift in all directions. It's an exciting piece of early abstract art.

A woman sits upright on a divan, painted with Modigliani's simplified, elegant, elongated shapes. He painted many such portraits in Paris in 1917. The curved lines and warm colors create a feeling of calm. It's an example of his unique style.

A wide-eyed angel with wings seems to look back in surprise, drawn in a childlike style. Paul Klee made this in 1920, and philosopher Walter Benjamin later owned it and wrote about it as an angel of history. Benjamin saw the angel being blown backward into the future, looking at the pile of wreckage of the past. It's a famous image about time.

The three wise men bring gifts to the baby Jesus in this glowing little picture, which is round like a plate. Fra Angelico, a Dominican friar, began it in about 1430, and Filippo Lippi, who was a young friend, probably finished it.

A cardinal's face shows every wrinkle and bump, painted in great detail, and he looks tired and clever. Jan van Eyck met him in 1431 and probably drew him from life before painting this portrait in 1438.

Inside a huge church, scenes show the seven holy ceremonies of the Catholic Church, like baptism, marriage and last rites. Rogier van der Weyden painted this triptych in about 1440, and the crucifixion rises right through the middle.
l: Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp

paintings.why: Friends gather around Christ's body, and everyone's face is full of grief. Rogier van der Weyden and his workshop painted this about 1450, and the way the faces cry is just like real life.

Jesus kneels on a hill at night while his friends sleep nearby and soldiers gather in the distance. Andrea Mantegna painted this in about 1450, and the sharp rocks and golden sunrise make it unforgettable.

Three small panels show John the Baptist, Mary Magdalene and John the Evangelist, and a skull stands on the outside when it is closed. Rogier van der Weyden painted this in about 1452, and it is named for a family that owned it.
Three panels tell the story of John the Baptist, from his birth to his baptism of Jesus and his death. Rogier van der Weyden painted this triptych in about 1455.

Mary and the baby Jesus sit on a throne under a bower of fruit and flowers, surrounded by angels and saints. Andrea Mantegna painted this altarpiece in 1457 for a church in Verona, and the painted columns blend with the real ones.

Christ kneels on a rocky hill as the sun rises, while his friends sleep and Judas leads soldiers toward him. Giovanni Bellini painted this in about 1459, and the sky is one of the most beautiful in early Italian painting.

paintings.t: Madonna and Child with an Angel
paintings.why: Mary holds the baby Jesus, while an angel looks over their shoulders with a long, soft stare. Sandro Botticelli painted this about 1465, when he was a young artist learning from Filippo Lippi.

paintings.t: Scenes from the Passion of Christ
paintings.why: Dozens of tiny scenes tell the story of Jesus's last days, in a busy city with towers and gates. Hans Memling painted this in about 1470, and the artist put the whole story in a single picture, so you can follow it like a comic strip.
Dozens of tiny scenes of Jesus's life run through a wide landscape, with towns, roads and trees across the picture. Hans Memling painted this in about 1480, and it is like a big storybook page.
l: Alte Pinakothek, upper floor, gallery I

paintings.t: Madonna and Child enthroned with Saints and Angels
paintings.why: Mary sits on a throne with the baby Jesus, and saints stand beside her under a high arch while angels play music. Giovanni Bellini painted this altarpiece in 1487, and the music from the angels at her feet is lovely.
A hermit saint sits reading in a rocky place, surrounded by strange creatures. This is a panel from a triptych by Hieronymus Bosch, painted in about 1493.

A nymph lies dying beside the sea, while a faun kneels at her side and a dog watches sadly. Piero di Cosimo painted this tender, strange scene in about 1495, based on a story from Ovid's Metamorphoses.

Christ sits in the center of four men who press a crown of thorns on his head, and his eyes stare right at us. Hieronymus Bosch painted it in about 1495, and the men's faces are uglier than anything you would see in real life.
A woman is shown at the center of a busy scene in a Roman square, in a story that led to the end of the Roman kings. Sandro Botticelli painted it in about 1500.

A fat man's head peeps out of a hollow, and monsters, a big barrel and an owl crowd around in this bizarre scene. Hieronymus Bosch painted it in about 1500, and it is a funny warning against eating and drinking too much.
Christ bears the cross while a crowd presses around him, and the faces are painted as strange and ugly. Hieronymus Bosch painted it in about 1505.
l: Royal Monastery of San Lorenzo de El Escorial

paintings.why: A young Jesus sits among wise old teachers in the temple, and their hands and faces fill the picture. Albrecht Dürer painted it in 1506 in just five days, during a trip to Italy.

Crowds of saints, kings and ordinary people kneel in the clouds before the Trinity, in a picture ringed with figures. Albrecht Dürer painted it in 1511, and he included himself in the lower corner, standing near the ground with a tablet.
A man weighs coins on a scale while his wife, beside him, turns the pages of a prayer book and watches the gold. Quinten Metsys painted it in 1514, and a round mirror shows a man at a window.
An older man with wild, white hair looks sideways with a sharp look, in a fur collar. Albrecht Dürer painted him in 1526, and you can almost count the hairs.
A princess lies on a bed as a shower of gold falls on her lap, while little cupids test a gold arrow. Correggio painted it in about 1530, and the story comes from Greek myth.

A group of women enjoy a lake, with a big swan among them, and a princess and a swan are shown in tender poses. Correggio painted it in about 1532, and it is based on a Greek myth in which Zeus became a swan.

paintings.t: Portrait of the Artist's Sisters Playing Chess
paintings.why: Three sisters play chess, while a maid stands behind them, as one sister smiles at her own move. Sofonisba Anguissola painted her sisters in 1555, and it was one of the first group portraits that looked like a real family moment.

A man's face and body are made of books, with a bookmark for a nose and a curtain for a cloak. Giuseppe Arcimboldo painted it in about 1556, and it's a funny portrait of a scholar made out of the things he loves.

paintings.t: Finding of the body of St Mark
paintings.why: People find a saint's body in a dark crypt, and spirits fly out, in a deeply shadowed, deep perspective. Jacopo Tintoretto painted it in about 1562.

paintings.t: St Mark's Body Brought to Venice
paintings.why: Sailors carry the body of Saint Mark through a storm in a crowded square, with strong colors and diagonal lines. Jacopo Tintoretto painted it in 1564, about the legend of how Saint Mark's body came to Venice.

A farmer sits at a table with a bowl of beans, a loaf of bread and a glass of wine, and he looks up as if you've interrupted his meal. Annibale Carracci painted it in about 1583, and it is one of the first paintings of an ordinary working man.
A young man with a pointed beard and a black suit looks out, holding a plan of a building. El Greco painted his son, Jorge Manuel, who was also an artist and an architect, in about 1600.
l: Museo de Bellas Artes de Sevilla

paintings.why: A monk in black with glasses in his hand looks out with a stern, intellectual face. El Greco painted Paravicino, a priest and poet, in about 1609, and it is one of his best portraits.
Shepherds and angels crowd around the glowing newborn Jesus, in long, flame-like shapes under a dark sky. El Greco painted it in about 1612, and he planned it to be hung over his own tomb.

paintings.t: The Garden of Eden with the Fall of Man
paintings.why: Adam and Eve stand under a tree in a garden full of animals, with a snake wrapped around the tree. Rubens painted the people and Jan Brueghel the Elder painted the animals and plants, in about 1615.

paintings.t: Prince Balthasar Charles With a Dwarf
paintings.why: A small prince in a rich red suit stands next to a court dwarf who is holding an apple and a rattle. Diego Velázquez painted it in 1631, and the prince was the heir to the Spanish throne, but he died at 16.

paintings.t: The Cheat with the Ace of Diamonds
paintings.why: A young man at a card table is being cheated by a woman, a maid and a man with a card hidden behind his back, with everyone glancing at each other. Georges de La Tour painted it in about 1635, and the sly looks make it so funny.

paintings.t: The Origin of the Milky Way
paintings.why: The goddess Juno pushes baby Hercules away, and her milk sprays across the sky, making the Milky Way, while Jupiter looks on. Peter Paul Rubens painted it in about 1637.
A giant eagle carries the baby Ganymede up into the sky, with his arms outstretched. Peter Paul Rubens painted it in 1637, and the eagle is the god Zeus in disguise.

A smiling boy with a twisted foot holds a paper that says 'Give me alms for the love of God,' over his shoulder like a crutch. Jusepe de Ribera painted it in 1642, and he treated the poor boy with respect and warmth.

A huge white swan hisses, with its wings spread, to protect its nest from a dog, with a farmer in the back. Jan Asselijn painted it in about 1650, and it is said to be a symbol of a Dutch statesman standing up to enemies.
A young woman leans out of a window and smiles while an older woman hides behind a shutter, laughing. Bartolomé Esteban Murillo painted it in about 1657, and it is a sweet, playful moment.

paintings.t: The Immaculate Conception of Los Venerables
paintings.why: Mary floats up on a cloud with a crescent moon at her feet, surrounded by cherubs and clouds. Bartolomé Esteban Murillo painted it in about 1660, and it is one of his many versions of this subject.
Workers cut and carry stones beside a canal in Venice, near a church, under a pale sky. Canaletto painted it in about 1725, and it is one of his most appealing pictures of everyday life.

A British general dies on the battlefield after winning the Battle of Quebec in 1759, as officers gather around him like figures in a religious painting. Benjamin West dressed the scene in contemporary clothes, which was bold at the time. The painting was a sensation in London. It changed how history painting was done.

A man draws back in surprise as a captive starling, which can only say 'I can't get out,' flutters in a cage. The painting was inspired by a story by Laurence Sterne. Wright of Derby used lamplight to bring the moment to life. It makes you think about freedom and kindness.

A man in a green coat holds a violin as he glances out, with a bow in his hand. Anne Vallayer-Coster was a French painter, and one of the few women admitted to the French Royal Academy of Painting. She was famous for still lifes, and this is an unusual portrait. It's a lovely picture of music.

A man locks a door with one arm, as a woman tries to push him away and to reach a table with an apple in the background. Fragonard painted it in 1777. The sparkle of the fabrics is dazzling. The meaning is mysterious, so viewers still debate it.

A group of boys march and play with toy drums and swords. Goya painted this as a design for a tapestry, with bright colors and lively movement. It's a charming glimpse of children at play in 1700s Spain. It captures the joy of imagination.

The queen of France sits proudly with her children, and an empty cradle. Vigée Le Brun painted it to improve the queen's image, at a time when people were angry with her. The empty cradle represents a baby daughter who had recently died. It's a sad and important portrait.

paintings.t: Portrait of Antoine-Laurent Lavoisier and his wife
paintings.why: A famous chemist sits at a table of scientific instruments, as his wife leans on his shoulder. Lavoisier helped create modern chemistry, and his wife Marie-Anne was his partner in science. David painted them as a pair of modern, smart people. It's a landmark portrait of science.

Young people in fancy clothes play the game of blind man's bluff in a ring, outdoors. Goya painted it as a design for a tapestry for the Spanish palace. The light and fun scene is full of charm. It's a happy picture from his early career.
paintings.k: Everyone plays a game of tag with a blindfold. Which player is it?

paintings.why: The prince Paris sits beside Helen of Troy, with Cupid close by, in a graceful chamber. According to legend, their love began the Trojan War. David painted it in 1788 in the elegant style of ancient Greece. It's a beautiful scene with a sad ending to come.

A little girl sits in a landscape, her head tilted, with a sweet look of curiosity. Reynolds was the first president of the Royal Academy, and he often painted children. The soft light and fluffy dress capture childhood. It's one of the best-loved child portraits in English art.
paintings.k: The girl looks to the side. What do you think she is listening to?

paintings.t: The Ambassadors of Agamemnon in the tent of Achilles
paintings.why: Greek messengers come to the tent of the hero Achilles, who sulks over a quarrel with his commander, begging him to return to the war. Ingres painted it at 20, as a prize piece in Paris. It's based on Homer's Iliad. It shows how well he'd learned the lessons of ancient sculpture.

A young girl in a white dress and a soft yellow shawl looks gently out of the canvas. Ingres painted her when she was about 13, and the smooth, curving lines and delicate details show his skill. She died only a year later, which adds a sad note to the portrait. It's one of the most loved portraits of a child.

The god Jupiter sits on his throne, with an eagle by his side, while the sea-goddess Thetis begs a favor. Ingres painted it at age 31 in Rome. The great size and the strict calm made some critics unhappy. It's a bold act of artistic ambition.

Two men sink up to their knees in mud, striking each other with sticks, as a dark landscape stretches behind them. Goya painted this on the wall of his house in his Black Paintings series. It's often seen as a picture of conflict that goes nowhere. It's a serious, thoughtful painting.

Four racehorses are stretched out in mid-gallop, all their legs off the ground, with jockeys in bright colors. Géricault painted the 'flying gallop' at a time before cameras could show how horses really run. We now know that this is not how horses really move! It's a thrilling picture of speed that influenced later artists.
paintings.k: All four horses have their legs stretched out in the air. Is this really how horses gallop?

paintings.why: A huge old oak stands in a meadow under a gloomy sky, with a pale village and hills beyond. Friedrich painted the tree like a hero, strong but alone. It's a symbol of survival. It's one of his best-known landscapes.

Great wooden ships fire their guns in a smoky sea battle, as sailors battle on deck and in the water. Turner painted this scene from the Royal Navy's 1805 victory, in which Admiral Nelson died. It was commissioned for King George IV. It's a record of a famous naval battle.

A boy kneels to drink from a pond, as sheep and a dog wait on a path, bordered by a golden cornfield. Constable painted the place he knew from his childhood. The rich greens and the glowing sky are full of life. It's a classic of English landscape.

paintings.t: Entry of the Crusaders in Constantinople
paintings.why: Crusader knights ride through a city in 1204, with crowds of people begging for mercy. Delacroix painted the wildness of history in swirling colors. The painting hangs in the Louvre. It's a tough scene, painted with deep emotion.

A young woman, Mary, sits on a bed in a plain white room as the angel Gabriel appears. Rossetti used only white and blue, a bold choice. The title means 'Behold the handmaid of the Lord.' It was a fresh, modern view of a very old story.

A Highland soldier, freed from prison, gives the jailer the order to release him, while his wife, with a baby in her arms, rests her head on his shoulder. Millais used his future wife as the model. The picture earned him the greatest success of his career. It's an emotional tale of reunion.

Sheep graze on a bright green cliff above a blue sea, with sunlight on their wool. Hunt painted every blade of grass and animal in close detail. It was meant as a warning of an invasion — the sheep, he joked, were unprotected. It's a beautiful look at the English coast.

paintings.t: Joséphine-Éléonore-Marie-Pauline de Galard de Brassac de Béarn (1825–1860), Princesse de Broglie
paintings.why: A French princess sits in a blue satin dress with a pearl necklace and elegant poise. Ingres took a long time to paint her, and the dress is exquisitely detailed. The portrait is one of the most admired of the 1800s. It hangs in the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York.

A lone goat stands on the salt shore of the Dead Sea, with a red cloth on its horns. In an old tradition, a goat carried the sins of the people into the wilderness. Hunt traveled to the Dead Sea to paint it on the spot. It's famous for its harsh, shimmering landscape.

A young woman in a blue gown and a young man kneel together with a trailing rose bush, a shy and sad moment. Hughes painted it in a very fine detail with rich color. The painting is based on a poem by Tennyson. It's a dreamy scene of first love.

paintings.t: Empress Eugenie Surrounded by her Ladies in Waiting
paintings.why: The Empress of France sits on a flower-strewn lawn, with her ladies in pastel gowns gathered around, like in a garden party. Winterhalter was the favorite portrait painter of royalty across Europe. The picture has a dreamy, fairy-tale glow. It's a glimpse into royal life.

Dancing figures in a circle, in a lively swirl of ancient costume. Bouguereau's graceful figures seem to move to music. It's a classical celebration of dance as part of life. The smooth surface and gentle poses are signatures of his style.

At dawn in the snow, a man in a white Pierrot costume is held by his friend after losing a duel. The story's details are uncertain, but the picture was a hit with the public. The harsh cold and the colorful costumes make it unforgettable. It's a fine example of dramatic storytelling.

Two nuns in a convent graveyard at twilight, one digging a grave, the other sitting nearby. Millais painted it near London, with a sunset sky. The still, silent mood is unforgettable. It's a haunting view of quiet devotion.

After being stabbed by senators in Rome, Julius Caesar's body lies in a theater, while the conspirators scatter. Gérôme painted an empty hall instead of the actual fight. The still, quiet scene is more haunting than a battle. It's a clever painting of a famous event.

A soldier in a black uniform says a tender, hasty goodbye to his sweetheart before riding off to battle, just before Waterloo. She holds the door shut as if she could keep him back. Millais painted every fold of her satin dress. It was one of the most popular paintings of its day.

A priest preaches to the king and nobles of Poland about their duties, warning them of dangers ahead. Piotr Skarga was a real preacher in the 1500s who warned of a decline. Matejko painted it to inspire Poles in a time of foreign rule. It's famous for its message of patriotism.

Two polar bears prowl through the wreck of an Arctic expedition, gnawing at a torn flag and scattered supplies. Landseer painted this after the lost Franklin expedition. The title means we make plans but nature has the final say. It's a famous and very dramatic image.
paintings.k: Find the polar bears in the ice. What are they looking at?

paintings.why: A woman sits in front of a mirror, brushing her long golden hair, in a rich red-and-white room. In old legend, Lilith was Adam's first wife. Rossetti's painting is full of beautiful details, like flowers and a glowing mirror. It's a dreamy picture of beauty and mystery.

A young girl in a ragged dress stands in a field of tall grass, with a pair of large eyes and a sad, direct look. Bouguereau made many pictures of poor children for rich collectors. It's meant to inspire compassion. It's still a famous image of childhood.

The holy city shines golden in the late sun, seen from the Mount of Olives. Gérôme visited the Middle East and painted the scene with great fidelity. Its calm and glowing mood makes the city feel timeless. It's a majestic view.

A young man in a hat stands by a table, in a studio with a suit of armor and a mother-and-child nearby. Manet's son Léon posed. The scene doesn't tell a clear story, which keeps people curious. It's a modern, mysterious indoor scene.

Artists and friends gather in a bright studio full of paintings, including Manet, Monet and Renoir. Bazille painted the group that would form the Impressionists. The painting shows his friends before they became famous. It's like a family snapshot of art history.

A young Jesus, working in a carpenter's shop, stretches out his arms, and the shadow forms a cross on the wall behind. His mother looks on, feeling fear. Hunt painted it in the Holy Land. It's one of the most famous images of Jesus as a boy.

Two men sit by a chessboard in a quiet room, thinking deeply. Eakins painted his father and friends and was mindful of the light on the wood and on their faces. It was a gift to his father. It's a nice study of concentration.

A merchant, Sadko, is walking along the sea bottom in a magical underwater kingdom, as the Sea King's daughters parade past in dresses. It's based on a Russian folk tale, which inspired an opera, too. Repin painted the sea princesses with different faces from many nations. It's a fairy tale full of beauty.
paintings.k: Sadko walks along the seabed. Which creature would you ask for directions?

paintings.t: Madame Georges Charpentier and her Children
paintings.why: A wealthy publisher's wife sits with her young son and daughter, and a large dog on a couch, in a room with Japanese decor. Renoir's painting won him new patrons when it was well received at the Salon. It's fabulously cozy. It's a portrait of a stylish Paris family.

A view over Paris rooftops in the snow, with chimneys and gray skies. Caillebotte painted it from the window of his home. The cool colors and unusual view are quiet and modern. It's a favorite of city landscapes.

paintings.t: Miss La La at the Cirque Fernando
paintings.why: A circus performer hangs by her teeth from a rope high in the air, as the audience looks up from below. Degas made it after seeing her perform in Paris. The dizzying angle and the geometry of the dome are daring. It's an exciting picture.
paintings.k: She hangs by her teeth from a rope. Why do you think the artist painted it from below?

paintings.why: Two girls in black dresses stand with rosy cheeks and shining hair. Renoir painted them with warm light, with a touch of the outdoors in the colors. They are two of his favorite young models. It's a charming picture of youth.

A woman with dignity and calm looks out at us, wearing a white head covering and a draped shawl. Bilińska, a Polish painter who trained in Paris, painted this in 1884. It was a portrait that treated its sitter with respect, at a time when that was uncommon. It's a striking example of 19th-century portrait painting.

paintings.t: Cleopatra Testing Poisons on Condemned Prisoners
paintings.why: The Egyptian queen watches closely as a poison is tested on prisoners, while her servants stand by. Cabanel painted a gripping scene of the ancient world. The details of the room are exquisite. It's a dramatic image of ancient power.
l: Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp

paintings.why: Rooftops, chimneys and a cloudy sky stretch over Paris as seen from the apartment where Van Gogh lived with his brother Theo. Van Gogh painted the view in 1887 with fresh, quick strokes after learning from the Impressionists. It's one of the first signs of his bright palette. It's a city view with a feeling of home.

A woman with a snake wound around her body stands by a tree in a lush forest. John Collier painted Lilith, a character from old legends. The snake and soft light give it a dreamlike feel. It's an eye-catching Victorian painting.

A white farmhouse sits among golden fields and green trees under a bright blue sky. Van Gogh painted it in Arles in summer 1888. The bold color and clean lines show his Japanese influences. It's a sunny scene of country life.

People in bright clothes crowd the stands of a Roman arena for a bullfight, under a blue sky. Van Gogh was struck by the old structure and the festive crowd. The painting is made of bold dabs of color. It's a lively scene of Provençal life.

A sunny path curves through green fields lined with trees near the town of Arles. Van Gogh painted the bright scene in the summer light of southern France. The path draws the viewer into the picture. It's a peaceful stroll.

Dark, flame-shaped cypress trees twist up toward a swirling sky. Van Gogh said they were as beautiful as an Egyptian obelisk. He painted several versions during his stay in Saint-Rémy. They've become signature elements of his art.

A woman at a dressing table powders her face in front of a vase of flowers. Seurat painted his partner Madeleine Knobloch, and he later painted over a portrait of himself in the corner. It's made with fine dots, with a flat, decorative look. It's a quiet, witty picture.

Dancers kick up their legs in a lively Paris cabaret dance, with a musician and the audience. Seurat painted it with tiny dots of color, and the lines all lead upward for cheerfulness. The effect is a moving, energetic scene. It's one of the best examples of his method.

A young doctor sits in a swirling background of red, orange and green. Dr. Rey treated Van Gogh in the hospital in Arles. Van Gogh gave him the portrait, but the doctor wasn't a fan and used it to patch a chicken coop, the story goes. Today it's worth a fortune.

Two crabs, one on its back, scuttle on a pale green background. Van Gogh painted them in Arles in 1889, using bright orange and green. He loved Japanese prints, which have many pictures of sea life. It's a charming study.
paintings.k: One crab is upside down! Can you find its claws?

paintings.why: A man in a black coat and hat stands with a paintbrush and palette in front of a harbor and a ship decorated with flags. Rousseau painted himself as a proud artist in the world. The hot-air balloon and flags show his sense of fun. It's a charming self-portrait.
A smiling young woman in a colorful dress and headscarf leans her head on her hand. Bouguereau painted her with great care. It's a pleasant, charming portrait. It shows how popular his work was.

A girl in a white dress stands in a field of wheat in the sun, with her back slightly turned. Van Gogh painted it in Auvers-sur-Oise in 1890. The brushwork is lively and bright. It's a peaceful piece from his final weeks.

Moss-covered roofs of old cottages cluster together in a village, with trees and a cloudy sky. Van Gogh painted it in Auvers-sur-Oise, in northern France, in 1890. He loved these old thatched houses. It reminds you of simple country life.
A young girl with red hair looks out with soft, grave eyes, wearing a white dress. Bouguereau painted her in 1890. The soft realism is typical of his work. It's a sensitive portrait of a child.

A woman in a long white dress holds a flower to her ear, in warm tropical light. Gauguin painted it soon after arriving in Tahiti. The simple, strong figure and bold colors show his new direction. It's a famous image of his first stay on the island.

A crowd of 42 cats, each with a different personality, poses on and around a luxurious cushion. Carl Kahler painted the cats of a rich woman in San Francisco, and the painting took three years. The cats' names are known, and the painting is a world record in cat portraits. It's a delight for cat lovers.
paintings.k: There are 42 cats in this painting. Can you count ten of them? Which cat looks the grumpiest?

paintings.why: Two figures, one wading and one on the beach, are near the sea in Tahiti, with a pink tree arching overhead. The title means 'near the sea.' Gauguin built the picture out of flat, bold areas of color, like a Japanese print. It's a dreamy view of paradise.

A basket of apples sits tilted on a table with a bottle, a plate of biscuits and a cloth, painted from several angles at once. Cézanne wanted to show how we actually see, with our eyes moving around. The table looks tilted and the bottle too. It's a great example of his groundbreaking approach.

A crowd of people with ghostly faces walk toward us under a blood-red sky on a bridge. Munch made this just after his most famous painting, The Scream, with similar colors. The mood is one of unease. It's a picture of worry that many people recognize.

A pale man stares out in the foreground of a garden as a couple stands behind him. Munch painted jealousy as a green-faced mood. The painting is more about feeling than action. It's a revealing look at a strong emotion.

A skeleton gardener in a black cloak waters flowers as a boy and girl in white watch. Simberg's strange, gentle painting turns death into a friendly gardener. He was a Finnish Symbolist painter. It's both spooky and sweet.

A woman reclines on a bed in a Tahitian room, as a raven sits by the window and two people whisper in the background. Gauguin named it after a poem by Edgar Allan Poe. The mood is mysterious and moody. It's a rich picture of colors and symbols.

The boy Icarus, who flew too close to the sun, lies on the shore as sea nymphs mourn. In the Greek myth, his wax wings melted. Draper painted the beautiful, glowing scene in 1898. It's one of the most beloved paintings of Greek myth.

A knight leans down from his horse as his lady ties a scarf around his arm and wishes him luck before battle. Edmund Blair Leighton painted such romantic scenes from the Middle Ages with great detail. This one is among the most popular. It's a picture of love and courage.

Five red figures stand on a green hill under a deep blue sky, singing and playing. Matisse used just three colors: blue, green and red. The simplicity and boldness were revolutionary. It's a masterpiece of modern color.

A whirlwind of colors, shapes and lines swirls across the whole canvas. Kandinsky made dozens of studies for it and painted it in just four days. He believed that color and shape could move us like music. It's often called his masterpiece and one of the first great abstract paintings.

A young woman in a white dress stands before a background of Chinese-style patterns and figures. Klimt painted Elisabeth when she was around 17. The decorations are inspired by East Asian art. It's a stunning portrait filled with ornament.

A woman looks over her shoulder with a bold stare, wearing a patterned robe, set against a pale background. Klimt painted it at the end of his career. It was stolen from a museum in Italy in 1997 and mysteriously reappeared in 2019. It's one of the strangest art stories.
Mary sits holding the baby Jesus in front of a red cloth, with a book in her hand. Rogier van der Weyden painted this small panel in about 1435, and it is named after a Spanish man who once owned it.
A goldsmith weighs a ring while a young couple chooses jewelry. Petrus Christus painted it in 1449, and a round mirror on the counter shows the street outside, with two men and a falcon.
Mary holds the baby Jesus in front of a window with a view of a landscape, and angels help hold him up. Filippo Lippi painted this about 1460, and it is among his most loved pictures.
The three kings kneel in a ruined stable to honor the baby Jesus, in a large, crowded panel. Hugo van der Goes painted it in about 1470, and the faces look like real people from the town.
Mary holds the baby Jesus in front of a green cloth, with a landscape of hills and clouds behind them. Giovanni Bellini painted it around 1475, and he was the best painter in Venice.

A young man in a red cap holds up a small round painting of a saint, as if showing it to us. Sandro Botticelli painted him in about 1480, and the little round picture was probably painted by an older artist.

Angels sing and play lutes beside the baby Jesus, who lies on the ground on a corner of Mary's cloak. Piero della Francesca painted it in about 1480, and an ox and a donkey look on, and the donkey brays at the top of his voice.

A friar in a brown robe stands outside his cave, looking up into the light with his arms open. Giovanni Bellini painted it in about 1480, and the landscape, with its rocky hills, donkey and tiny town, is as important as the saint.
A young man kneels on one panel, and on the other Mary holds the baby Jesus, offering him an apple. Hans Memling painted it in 1487, and in the round mirror behind Mary you can see the whole room.

paintings.t: Miracle of the Holy Cross at the Rialto Bridge
paintings.why: A crowd of people in Venice stands on balconies and gondolas around the old wooden Rialto Bridge, where a miracle is happening. Vittore Carpaccio painted it in about 1494, and it shows what the city looked like at the time.
Saint Jerome kneels beside a rock, holding a stone to beat his chest, with a lion nearby. Albrecht Dürer painted it in about 1496, and the sky and rocks show how much he was studying nature.

A king sits in judgment while a cruel punishment happens in the background, in a painting meant to warn judges in the city of Bruges. Gerard David painted it in 1498, and it is one of the grimmest paintings of the Renaissance.
Mary sits in a garden with the baby Jesus and two saints, with palm trees and cypresses behind them. Sandro Botticelli painted it in about 1500, and the plants are painted with a lot of care.
Mary rises toward heaven on a cloud of angels, with a gold light all around her. Peter Paul Rubens painted it in 1626 for the cathedral in Antwerp, where it still hangs over the altar.

Joseph slides a ring onto Mary's finger in front of a priest, while a group of suitors snap their staffs in disappointment. Pietro Perugino painted it in 1501, and Raphael later copied the composition.
A saint reads quietly while weird demons and animals swarm around him in a strange landscape. This is a painting by Hieronymus Bosch or a follower, from about 1510.

paintings.t: Naked Young Woman in Front of the Mirror
paintings.why: A woman sits in front of two mirrors, so we see her face from a few angles. Giovanni Bellini painted it in 1515, when he was about 85, and it is a bold experiment.
Mary uncovers the sleeping baby Jesus while the young John the Baptist kneels and prays. Gianfrancesco Penni or Raphael's workshop painted it in about 1515.

The little god Cupid has been stung by bees while stealing honey, and he cries to his mother Venus, who smiles. Lucas Cranach the Elder painted it in about 1526, and the lesson is that love is sweet but can hurt.
A woman in a rich dress sits with her hands in her lap and looks out with an open, friendly face. Lorenzo Lotto painted it in about 1530.
Venus lies on a couch while Cupid, wearing a wreath, stands over her and pees on her, a funny, joking wedding picture. Lorenzo Lotto painted it in about 1530.
A huge crowd of people gather around Christ on the cross in a huge, dramatic scene with the sky growing dark. Jacopo Tintoretto painted it in 1565 for the Scuola Grande di San Rocco in Venice.
The apostles gather around Mary on her deathbed, while Christ stands above her holding her soul. El Greco painted it in about 1565 when he was still a young painter on the Greek island of Crete.
Christ's dead body lies stretched out on a slab, painted in a shocking, foreshortened view. Annibale Carracci painted it in about 1582, and Mantegna's Lamentation had inspired the shocking angle.
Two saints stand together in a bold, tall picture, one with the keys of heaven and the other with a sword. El Greco painted it in about 1595.
A young Hercules sits between two women, one offering him the easy path of pleasure and the other offering the hard path of duty. Annibale Carracci painted it in about 1596.
Christ rises from his tomb in a twisting swirl, while soldiers tumble around him. El Greco painted it in about 1598, and the long, stretched bodies are typical of his style.
Angels with lutes, violins and other instruments make a swirling heavenly concert in the clouds. El Greco painted it in about 1600, and the long, flame-like figures are typical of his style.
Mary kneels in the clouds as Christ and God the Father place a crown on her head, with angels all around. El Greco painted it in about 1600, and it is a blaze of bright color.
l: Hospital de la Caridad de Illescas

paintings.why: Mary, Joseph and the baby Jesus walk through a dark forest at night, with a torch, a campfire, the Milky Way and the moon reflected in a pond. Adam Elsheimer painted it in 1609, and it was one of the first pictures to show the stars as they really look.

Soldiers on a stage-like street try to take away babies from their mothers, in a very tense moment. Guido Reni painted it in 1611, and it is one of the best examples of a graceful and balanced Italian Baroque painting.
Warrior women on horses fight Greek soldiers on a wooden bridge in a whirl of swords, horses and bodies. Peter Paul Rubens painted it in about 1618.

A mother tries to save her child in a terrible scene, as soldiers fight the mothers in a courtyard. Nicolas Poussin painted it in about 1625, and the mother's scream is one of the most famous faces in painting.

paintings.t: Portrait of a Couple probably Isaac Massa and Beatrix van der Laen
paintings.why: A young couple sit in a garden, and she rests her hand on his shoulder, as they smile at us. Frans Hals painted it in about 1622, and it is one of the first portraits of a happy, relaxed married couple.
A woman in a big black hat looks out with a warm, steady gaze. Peter Paul Rubens painted it in about 1622, and it is known as Le Chapeau de Paille, the straw hat, because of a mistaken name.

paintings.t: Willem van Heythuysen posing with a sword
paintings.why: A young man in a black outfit sits in a chair, leaning over the back, with a sword resting on his knee. Frans Hals painted it in about 1625, and the pose is relaxed and confident.

Queen Esther, in a rich blue gown, faints in front of the king when she asks him to save her people, and the king rushes to hold her. Artemisia Gentileschi painted it in about 1629, and the golden clothes and curtains are painted with care.
A young man is being charmed by a fortune teller while the women around him quietly steal his purse and cut his coin pouch. Georges de La Tour painted it in about 1630.

A king stands relaxed with a walking stick, with his horse and groom behind him, in front of an open landscape. Anthony van Dyck painted Charles I in 1635, in a pose that was meant to look easy and royal.

paintings.t: Charles I (1600-1649) with M. de St Antoine
paintings.why: A king rides a large white horse under an arch, with his master of horse beside him. Anthony van Dyck painted Charles I in 1636, and the arch makes him look like an ancient emperor.

paintings.t: The Gallant Conversation, known as Paternal Admonition
paintings.why: A man in a dark coat speaks to a young woman in a fine satin dress, who looks down while drinking, as a woman behind them looks at us. Gerard ter Borch painted it in about 1654, and his beautiful silk has been admired for centuries.

Children in a family find gifts, and one little girl clutches a doll, while a boy who has been bad cries over a shoe filled with a switch. Jan Steen painted it in about 1665, and the festival of Saint Nicholas is the Dutch ancestor of Santa Claus.

A tall, sad clown in a loose white suit stands in front of a group of other actors, with his arms hanging down. Jean-Antoine Watteau painted it in about 1718, and it is one of the best-loved pictures of the 1700s.

A magnificent chestnut horse rears up against a plain background, the size of life. Stubbs painted it for the Marquess of Rockingham, and it is thought that there was no background by design. His knowledge of horse anatomy is astonishing. It is the most famous horse painting in Britain.
paintings.k: This horse is life-size. Can you stand up as tall as his shoulder?

paintings.t: General Johnson Saving a Wounded French Officer from the Tomahawk of a North American Indian
paintings.why: In a scene from the French and Indian War, a British officer protects a wounded French soldier. Benjamin West, an American in London, painted it with dramatic action in the forest. It shows kindness in a time of war. It's an early work of American-born art.

Mary floats in a pale blue gown, standing on a crescent moon and surrounded by angels, in a cloud of golden light. Tiepolo painted it for a church in Madrid. The airy colors make the whole scene look like it's floating. It's one of the most graceful paintings of the Baroque era.

An old philosopher in a red hat sits reading by the light of a single lamp, which makes his face glow in the dark. Wright of Derby was a master of dramatic candlelight. The picture makes you think about the quiet joy of studying. It's a model of strong light and shadow.

A young woman sits on a grassy bank with a little dog on her lap, as a young man holds a bright green parasol over her. Goya designed this as a pattern for a tapestry for a royal palace. The colors are cheerful and bright. It's a delightful picture of leisure.
l: Museo Nacional Centro de Arte Reina Sofía

paintings.why: An old, blind general, once a great hero, begs on the street as a soldier recognizes him in astonishment. In the story, Belisarius was Rome's top commander who was treated unfairly. David painted it with clear and strong emotions. It's a lesson that glory can vanish.

A group of figures, with pointed hats, fly through the sky as they hold up a man, in a swirl of eerie blue and gray. Goya painted a world of superstition and fear. It's meant to make people think about the foolish things people believe. It's a spooky picture.

A young noblewoman in a pale dress with a feathery hairdo sits with her hands folded, wearing a soft, thoughtful look. Goya painted her when she was about 20, a few years after she'd been forced into a marriage. He saw the sadness in her eyes, and the portrait is full of feeling. It's one of his greatest portraits.

paintings.t: Portrait of the Marchioness of Santa Cruz
paintings.why: A Spanish noblewoman lies on a couch, in a classical white dress, with a lyre, as if she were a Muse. Goya painted it with loose brushstrokes and with a cool and gentle mood. It's an original and fresh view of portraits. It's a favorite in Madrid's Prado Museum.

paintings.t: The Death of Leonardo da Vinci
paintings.why: The great artist Leonardo da Vinci lies on his deathbed in France, in the arms of the king, as friends look on. It's a legend, not a proven fact, but Ingres loved the story. The painting is a tribute to a genius. It reflects the great respect for artists in 1800s France.

The hero Achilles is furious as Agamemnon takes back a prize, in a scene from Homer's Iliad. David painted it late in his life, in exile, in a rich, sculpted style. The rage is felt in every face. It's a dramatic moment from the Trojan War.

A dark, ghostly crowd of people sing, stagger and stare out in a wild procession. Goya painted it on a wall of his house as part of the Black Paintings. It's a contrast with his earlier cheerful version of the same festival. It shows how his view of the world had darkened.
The elderly Goya, ill and pale, is held by his doctor, who offers him a drink. Goya painted it as thanks to Dr. Arrieta for saving his life. Dark shadows loom behind them. It's a touching tribute.

The Egyptian queen sails in a golden barge, dressed as the goddess Venus, to meet Mark Antony in Tarsus. Etty painted the shimmering scene with rich color and flowing movement. The sails, flowers and attendants are dazzling. It's a lush picture of ancient glamour.

The cathedral's slim spire rises beyond a stream and meadow beneath a stormy sky, with a bright rainbow. Constable painted it in 1831, when he was sad about the death of his wife. The dramatic clouds show his feelings. It's one of his grandest landscapes.

A curving river winds through a green valley as a storm clears. A tiny painter at an easel stands on the hillside in the corner. Thomas Cole showed that nature was big and beautiful, and humans were small. It's one of the most famous American landscape paintings.

A calm sunset glows red and gold behind a quiet landscape, with black trees on the horizon. Friedrich painted this late in life. The quiet colors remind us of the end of a day. It's a gentle painting.

A woman in a theatrical pose leans on a stone, holding a cup, in a wild forest. In ancient times, a bacchante was a follower of the wine god. Courbet painted it early in his career, in a Romantic manner. It's an experiment before he turned to Realism.

A French countess leans on her hand with a thoughtful look, in a satin blue dress. Ingres painted her over three years, and the textures of the flowers and silk are exquisite. A mirror shows the back of her head. It's a famous painting in the Frick Collection in New York.

A group of men sit relaxed around a table in a warm room after dinner, one of them playing a violin. Courbet painted his friends and his father in a dark, calm space. The painting won him a medal and was bought by the state. It's the start of his fame.

A shepherd flirts with a girl in a sunlit field as the sheep stray into the wheat. Hunt painted each leaf, each tuft of wool, in vivid color. He meant it as a lesson about neglecting duty. It's a joyous, detailed picture.

paintings.t: The Destruction of Sodom And Gomorrah
paintings.why: Fire rains from a stormy sky over a city of towers while tiny figures flee across a bridge. John Martin painted spectacular disasters from the Bible that thrilled huge crowds in Victorian England. His giant scenes were like the movies of their day. It's a famous piece of apocalyptic art.

A boy in a white shirt and a big hat carries a sword that's too big for him, with a bright sash and pale background. Manet painted it as a young artist, inspired by the Spanish masters. It's both charming and bold. It's an early favorite.

paintings.t: Mademoiselle V. . . in the Costume of an Espada
paintings.why: A woman dressed as a bullfighter holds a pink cape in a studio, with a little fight scene behind her. Manet's model, Victorine Meurent, is the same woman from 'Olympia'. It's a playful picture of costume and performance. It shows his love of Spanish art.

Two boys sit together in a room, drawing at a table, absorbed in their work. Sofie Ribbing, a Swedish painter, painted a quiet scene of children learning. The soft lighting and calm mood make it feel real. It's a gentle moment of creativity.

A woman in a white dress sits by a window, reading, as a man looks away from a book at her. Manet's wife, Suzanne, posed for it. The painting is calm and gentle. It's a pleasant moment of a quiet day.

Bazille's family are posed on a terrace under the trees at their home in southern France. He painted them in strong sunlight, looking out in rows. The picture was accepted at the Salon of 1868. It's an early step in Impressionism.

A couple stands arm in arm and smiles, the man holding his wife's arm. Renoir painted his friend, the Impressionist Alfred Sisley, and his future wife, Eugénie. It's a tender portrait of friendship and love. It's a fond record of an artist and his companion.

At dawn, a firing squad has just shot a French marshal, who lies on the ground by a wall, while the soldiers walk away. Gérôme left out the actual moment, showing only the aftermath. It's a quiet, strong picture about the end of an era. It's a haunting painting of history.

paintings.t: Jeune Fille au piano (Girl at the Piano - The Overture to Tannhauser)
paintings.why: A young woman sits at a piano, playing, as an older woman sews in a rocking chair. Cézanne painted his sister and mother in a bold, flat way. The famous music of Wagner's Tannhäuser was the inspiration. It's a quiet moment in a family.

A man in a straw hat and a woman in a blue dress sit in a sailboat on a sparkling river, painted in a very bold crop. Manet painted it in the summer of 1874 at Argenteuil with Monet nearby. The blue water fills most of the canvas. It's a refreshing scene.

Two winged brothers from Greek myth, Sleep and Death, lie side by side on a bed of poppies, in a quiet, dreamy pose. Waterhouse painted them in a haze of purple and gold. Sleep is the one who clutches a poppy. It's a peaceful picture of a serious subject.

A tall iron bridge crosses a train station, with a man in a top hat looking over the rail. Caillebotte painted the new Paris of steel and steam. The perspective lines pull you into the picture. It's one of the first paintings about industry and the city.

paintings.t: A Girl with a Watering Can
paintings.why: A little girl in a blue dress holds a watering can on a path with flowers and dappled light. Renoir captured a child's quiet game in a garden. It's very peaceful and sweet. The painting is in the National Gallery of Art in Washington.
paintings.k: What do you think is she going to water?

paintings.why: A queen in black stands by the coffin of her husband, refusing to let it be buried, in a bleak landscape. Joanna of Castile was the Queen of Spain and was said to be overwhelmed with grief. Pradilla painted the scene in a vast, wild setting. It's a famous work from Spain.

paintings.t: Little Girl in a Blue Armchair
paintings.why: A girl slouches in a big blue armchair in a living room, looking bored, with a sleeping dog in another chair. Cassatt painted a child's real attitude instead of making her look perfect. Degas helped with the painting, they say. It's one of the most famous paintings of childhood.
paintings.k: The little girl looks bored. What would you do in this room?

paintings.t: Woman with a Pearl Necklace in a Loge
paintings.why: A woman in a pale dress with a pearl necklace sits in a theater box, leaning forward and holding a fan. Cassatt painted this for the 1879 Impressionist show, with the glow of the theater lamps. She looks across at the audience while being observed herself. It's a picture of a woman who is clever and independent.

A girl in a dark dress stands among tall beech trees with brown leaves. Van Gogh painted it in the Netherlands when he was starting out. The mix of light and shadow is lively. It's a rustic look at an early painting.

Two girls in a forest rest after gathering nuts, one of them sitting with a basket and the other reclining. Bouguereau was a master of smooth, careful finish. The fresh-faced girls seem to glow in the green woods. It's a sweet, natural scene.

In the dark cellar of a Roman arena, slaves drag the bodies of fallen gladiators away, as crowds look on. Juan Luna from the Philippines won the top prize at an art show in Madrid in 1884 with this huge painting, among the biggest in the world. Filipinos were proud that one of their own beat the best European artists. It's a national treasure of the Philippines.

paintings.t: King Cophetua and the Beggar Maid
paintings.why: A king sits on the steps of his throne, wearing golden armor, gazing up at a barefoot beggar girl who holds a flower. According to a legend, he fell in love with her and made her his queen. Burne-Jones painted a glittering, richly decorated scene. It's a fairy tale in paint.

A big black ox pulls a farm cart across a field, under a stormy sky. Van Gogh painted the dark, heavy earth colors in the Netherlands when he lived with his parents. The ox seems strong and patient. It's an early look at rural labor.

A barefoot young girl in a rural dress stands in a green field, with a gentle, direct look. Bouguereau painted idealized peasant girls that were very popular. This one is shown with soft, smooth finish. It's a typical beloved image.

A straw hat lies on a wall in dark shadows, painted with little dashes. Van Gogh worked on it in the Netherlands. The hat is a cheerful sign of summer. It's a small, humble object painted with affection.

A boy gazes at a soap bubble he has just blown, with a dreamy look. Millais painted it as a picture of his grandson, 'A Child's World.' It was later used in a soap advertisement, which made it one of the most famous paintings ever. It's a well-known image of childhood wonder.
paintings.k: What do you think the boy is thinking as he watches his bubble? Try to imagine the bubble's whole life.

paintings.why: A bird rises above a golden field of waving wheat under a wide sky. Van Gogh painted it in Paris in 1887, and the field swirls in lively brushstrokes. He loved the open countryside. It's a happy, breezy landscape.

A young woman in a white dress sits by the shore, looking out, with her hair in the breeze. Munch painted his sister Inger at the seaside in Norway. The peaceful mood is a contrast with his later, anxious paintings. It's a tender early portrait.

Van Gogh stands in a heavy coat and hat, with a bandage on his ear, and a pipe, looking calm. The painting shows him in a moment of recovery after a hard time. A bold orange background and strong lines make it memorable. It's a direct, honest self-portrait.

paintings.t: Landscape with a Carriage and a Train
paintings.why: A horse-drawn carriage races across a golden field, as a train steams by in the distance, under a cloudy sky. Van Gogh painted it in 1890 in his last weeks. The old and new world are side by side. It's a lively, energetic view of the countryside.

Thatched farmhouses sit beside a golden wheat field and a path, under a bright blue sky with a swirl of clouds. Van Gogh painted it near Paris in the last weeks of his life. The roofs are in warm greens and reds. It's a happy look at rural life.

Pink roses burst from a vase against a pale green background. Van Gogh painted it in Auvers-sur-Oise in his final months. The roses were originally a bright pink, though the color has faded. It's a lovely flower painting.

A farming couple takes a nap in the shade of a haystack, with their tools beside them. Van Gogh copied the design of a Millet print and put it into his own bold colors. He said it was like translating into another language. It shows his love for the painter Millet.

The hero Ulysses is lashed to the mast of his ship as bird-women, the sirens, swoop and sing to lure him. His crew, ears plugged, row on. Waterhouse painted the sirens with a wild energy. It's a famous scene from the Odyssey.
Women in the Tahitian countryside play music under a red dog's gaze, with a spirit figure in the background. 'Arearea' means 'joyousness.' Gauguin's colors are bold and flat. It's a dreamy scene.

A pitcher, a fruit bowl and a patterned curtain are arranged on a table, with apples and peaches that seem to tilt. Cézanne changed the viewpoint on purpose, as if he moved while painting. It's like a puzzle made of color. It helped lead the way to Cubism.

A wild-eyed man rides a rearing black horse that tramples a woman, in a vivid painting of passion. Podkowiński made this in 1894 and showed it in Warsaw, where it caused a huge uproar. He eventually slashed it with a knife. It's a famous Polish Symbolist painting.

Winged spirits carry the maiden Psyche up into the sky in a swirl of silks. In the story, she's taken to a palace where she meets Cupid. Bouguereau painted a beautiful, soft scene. It's an enchanting picture of ancient myth.

A shy girl wearing a blue-and-white headscarf looks out with a sweet, solemn face. The girl, Angelina, was a street kid in Venice who sold flowers. The painting won a top prize at an exhibition in 1897. It became one of the most-copied pictures in Italy.

A crowd in masks and costumes dance and shout in a wild carnival procession. Goya painted it in the 1810s, a festival at the end of Carnival in Madrid. The faces are strange and frightening. It's an energetic piece.
l: Royal Academy of Fine Arts of San Fernando

paintings.why: A bird-woman with a swan's wings looks back over her shoulder against a darkening sky, wearing a jeweled crown. Vrubel painted the Swan Princess from a Russian opera, and his wife sang the role. The shimmering colors look like mosaic. It's one of the most captivating Russian fairy-tale paintings.
paintings.k: This princess has wings. What does she have on her head?

paintings.why: A young woman in a flowing robe struggles against the cold north wind, represented by Boreas. In Greek myth, Boreas was the god of the north wind. Waterhouse painted him coming from the cloud with a mighty gust. It's a magical picture of weather.

paintings.t: Ceremonial Sitting of the State Council on 7 May 1901 Marking the Centenary of its Foundation
paintings.why: Dozens of officials in uniform sit and stand in a vast hall, in a massive group portrait for the 100th anniversary of Russia's State Council. Repin painted 81 individual portraits with the help of his students. It's a record-setting giant canvas, over 4 meters tall. It's a window into a world that was about to vanish.

Figures relax on a beach in dots of purple, orange and blue, around a table with a picnic, beneath the bright sun. Matisse got the title from a poem by Baudelaire. He used the dots of Seurat but made them bigger and wilder. It was an important step toward Fauvism.

A woman in a blue dress, her hands in her lap, sits with a steady look. Cézanne painted her in a patchwork of blue and tan strokes. His later portraits are made of blocks of color. It's an example of his simple but powerful way of painting.

The hero Jason watches as the sorceress Medea mixes a magic potion to help him win the Golden Fleece. Waterhouse painted her in a rich turquoise gown, with a cauldron and flames. The picture is filled with mystery. It's a favorite of fans of Greek legends.

A church on a small island in Venice glows pink and gold, and the water shimmers in purple and blue. Monet painted it in 1908 on a trip with his wife, and he finished some of the pictures at home. The colors melt like a dream. It's a lovely view of an unforgettable city.

Four bright blue horses stand huddled together in a landscape of red, yellow and purple. Franz Marc believed animals were pure and innocent, and he used colors to show feelings, not to match real life. The painting disappeared during World War II and has never been found. It is one of the most famous lost paintings.
paintings.k: How many blue horses can you count? Can you spot where they are touching each other?

paintings.why: A single big black circle sits on a white square. Malevich painted it as a partner to his Black Square, and it might be a symbol of a wheel or of a whole world. It was among the boldest artworks of the 1920s. It's a minimal abstraction.

Mary kneels beside her newborn baby in a Flemish winter landscape, and the whole scene is painted in warm, lifelike detail. Robert Campin, the master of Tournai, painted it around 1430, and it is a fine early example of oil painting in the Netherlands.

A young woman sits quietly with a huge tower behind her and a book in her hand. Jan van Eyck made this drawing in 1437, and it is not a painting but a drawing made with a brush and ink. The tower is Barbara's symbol, because the story says she was locked in one.
l: Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp

paintings.why: Saint Barbara reads by the fireplace in a cozy room, with a little towel, a candle and a window onto the street. Robert Campin painted this in 1438, and it is full of ordinary things from a house in Flanders.

A woman in a red headdress looks out calmly, with careful, tiny wrinkles painted around her eyes. Jan van Eyck painted his wife, Margareta, in 1439, and wrote on the frame that he finished it on June 17.
Mary and the angel are painted in shades of gray, as if they were statues, in this narrow panel. Jan van Eyck painted it in about 1440 as one half of a diptych, which is a picture made of two panels.

paintings.t: Portrait of a Young woman with a Winged Bonnet
paintings.why: A young woman wears a bonnet that looks like it has wings, and she looks down with her hands pressed together. Rogier van der Weyden painted this portrait in about 1440, and she remains a mystery.
Mary holds the baby Jesus in front of a rich, red cloth. This is a small panel painted in the workshop of Jan van Eyck in about 1441, showing how popular his style had become.
The shepherds kneel in a rocky landscape to see the baby Jesus, in a picture with sharp, strong lines. Andrea Mantegna painted it in about 1450, and it looks almost like a carved relief.
The baby Jesus lies on the ground in a ruined stable, and Mary and Joseph kneel beside him. Petrus Christus painted this in about 1450, and it was probably part of a bigger altarpiece.

Mary spreads her wide cloak to shelter a group of people kneeling under it, in a many-paneled altarpiece. Piero della Francesca painted it in about 1460, and the people under her cloak are the townspeople who paid for it.
Mary holds the baby Jesus in a stone niche, and two little angels stand by her. Rogier van der Weyden painted it in about 1460, and it was possibly made for the Medici family in Florence.
A young knight in shining armor stands holding a lance, with a dead dragon at his feet. Andrea Mantegna painted this in about 1460, and the dragon is no bigger than a lizard under the saint's foot.
Mary holds the baby Jesus on a balcony with a view out to the sky. Sandro Botticelli painted it in 1467, and the baby seems to reach up for his mother's face.

paintings.t: Madonna and Child and Two Angels
paintings.why: Mary and the baby Jesus sit with two angels in a soft, rounded picture. Sandro Botticelli painted it about 1468, and the angels' long curling hair shows his love of flowing lines.
The apostles gather around Mary as she lies on her deathbed, and they are shocked and sad. Hugo van der Goes painted it about 1470, and every face shows a different feeling.

Mary and the baby Jesus sit in the center, with saints and angels beside them and scenes from John the Baptist and John the Evangelist on the side panels. Hans Memling painted it in about 1470 for a hospital in Bruges.

A young woman in a tall black hat and a red gown with a gold necklace looks calmly out at you. Hans Memling painted Maria Portinari in about 1470, and she was the wife of a rich banker from Florence living in Bruges.

Mary sits in a garden full of roses with the baby Jesus, while angels hold a crown above her head. Martin Schongauer painted it in 1473 for a church in Colmar, and the golden background makes it glow.

Saint Sebastian is tied to a tree and shot with arrows by six archers, each in a different, active pose. Antonio and Piero del Pollaiuolo painted this in 1475, and they studied how muscles work to get the poses right.

paintings.t: Madonna and Child with a Pomegranate
paintings.why: Mary holds the baby Jesus, who has a pomegranate in his little hand, in front of a window with a landscape. Lorenzo di Credi painted it in about 1477, and he was a friend of Leonardo da Vinci.
Moses comes down from the mountain with the Ten Commandments, while the people below worship a golden calf. Cosimo Rosselli and his workshop painted this fresco in the Sistine Chapel in 1481.

Christ hangs on the cross against a dark sky, with a small man kneeling at the foot. Hieronymus Bosch painted it in about 1485, and the donor kneeling at the cross is shown much smaller than Mary and the saints.

A woman bathes in a quiet pool beside a palace, while a servant helps her dress, and a king looks on from far above. Hans Memling painted it in about 1485, and it shows the Bible story of King David and Bathsheba.
Mary holds the baby Jesus, in front of a stone wall and a hanging cloth, with a sweet, serious face. Giovanni Bellini painted it in about 1486.
The goddess Minerva chases vices out of a garden, a bunch of strange creatures, half man and half animal, who are fleeing. Andrea Mantegna painted it in 1487 for the study of a princess.
A half-length Christ stands with a rope around his neck, beside a column in a dark room. Donato Bramante painted it in 1487, and he later became the architect of Saint Peter's Basilica.
Christ sits on the edge of his tomb with angels around him, showing his wounds and looking at us. Andrea Mantegna painted this in 1488, and it is a quiet, sorrowful image for people to meditate on.

Saint John sits on a rocky island, writing his book of visions, while an angel shows him a scene of Mary in the sky. Hieronymus Bosch painted it in 1489, and on the back is a picture of the life of Christ.

Judith, in a long gown, holds a sack with a severed head, and a servant stands nearby. Andrea Mantegna or a follower made this picture in gray tones in about 1495, and it shows the Bible hero who saved her city.

Mary holds the baby Jesus, offers him a small piece of fruit and a crown, and looks down at her son. Albrecht Dürer painted it in about 1495, and he was a young artist who had just come back from Italy.

King Solomon sits on a throne and orders a baby to be cut in two, to find the real mother. Giorgione is credited with this panel, in about 1500, and the baby is saved when the true mother begs him not to.

paintings.t: Saint Christopher Carrying the Christ Child
paintings.why: A giant saint wades through a river carrying a small boy on his shoulders, in a weird landscape with a strange tree and a tiny creature. Hieronymus Bosch painted it in about 1500.
Two young people sit at a chessboard, and a crowd of onlookers lean in to watch, in a quiet, hushed moment. Lucas van Leyden painted it in about 1510, and the gaze of each person is full of life.

paintings.t: The Creation of the Sun, Moon and Planets
paintings.why: God flies through the sky and points at the sun, then flies the other way to make the moon, in a powerful, whirling picture. Michelangelo painted it on the Sistine Chapel ceiling in about 1511.
Mary looks gently at the baby Jesus in her arms, and she wears a fine, jeweled crown. Albrecht Dürer painted this small picture in 1512.
Mary sits in a sunlit garden with the baby Jesus, with a rainbow and bright flowers behind her. Matthias Grünewald painted it in about 1514, and it has some of the brightest colors of its time.
l: Church of the Coronation of Mary, Stuppach

paintings.t: Landscape with Charon Crossing the Styx
paintings.why: The boatman Charon rows a lost soul across the River Styx, with heaven on one side and hell on the other. Joachim Patinir painted it in about 1515, and the dark and light sides of the landscape split the picture.

An emperor in a fur coat and big hat looks sideways, and a pomegranate, a symbol of power, is in his hand. Albrecht Dürer painted it in 1519, shortly after Maximilian died, working from a drawing he'd made earlier.

Mary Magdalene kneels at Christ's feet in a garden after the resurrection, and he holds a hoe, because she thought he was a gardener. Correggio painted it in about 1525, and the story is told in the Gospel of John.
Saint Jerome lies asleep at the bottom in a long, thin painting, while Mary and the baby Jesus appear in the sky above, with the Baptist pointing. Parmigianino painted it in 1526.
The goddess Venus stands holding her son Cupid, who is holding a honeycomb. Hans Holbein the Younger painted it in about 1526, after studying painting in Italy.
Mary spreads her cloak over sailors and explorers, including Columbus, who kneel before her. Alejo Fernández painted it in about 1533 for the house in Seville that organized voyages to the New World.
A woman in a golden-sleeved dress and a fur piece with a little head looks out with a proud, steady gaze. Parmigianino painted it in about 1535, and her name, Antea, is a mystery.

paintings.t: Christina of Denmark, Duchess of Milan
paintings.why: A tall young woman in black stands in a full-length portrait, with a gold ring on her finger. Hans Holbein the Younger painted her in 1538 for King Henry VIII, who was thinking of marrying her. She was only 16 and a widow.
A baby, a young woman and an old woman stand together, while a skeleton Death holds an hourglass above them. Hans Baldung Grien painted it in about 1541 to remind us that life passes quickly.

paintings.t: Portrait of Cosimo I de' Medici
paintings.why: A young duke in armor stands with his hand on his helmet and looks at us with a firm gaze. Bronzino painted Cosimo I de' Medici in about 1544, and he ruled Florence.
A young knight with a lance fights a dragon while a princess flees in the dark, in a wild, stormy scene. Jacopo Tintoretto painted it in about 1555.
A young man stands between two women, one telling him to follow the path of duty and the other tempting him with pleasures. Paolo Veronese painted it in about 1565.
A man's face is made out of a chicken, a fish and a pile of legal papers and books. Giuseppe Arcimboldo painted it in 1566, and it makes fun of lawyers.
A princess lies on a bed as a shower of gold falls on her, while a maid holds a cloth to catch the coins. Jacopo Tintoretto painted it in about 1570, and the story is a Greek myth.
l: Museum of Fine Arts of Lyon

paintings.why: Mary Magdalene looks up to heaven with wet eyes, with her hands clasped and her hair spilling over her shoulder. El Greco painted it in about 1570, and he painted many versions.
Mars, the god of war, sits quietly while Venus presses milk from her breast, and a cupid ties them together. Paolo Veronese painted it in about 1570, and it is about how love can bring peace.

paintings.t: Allegory of the Battle of Lepanto
paintings.why: Venice's ruler kneels in the clouds before Mary while a huge naval battle rages below. Paolo Veronese painted this in 1571 to celebrate the victory over the Ottoman fleet.
An old man in black holds a book of tiny paintings, looking out gently, with a shadowed face. El Greco painted Giulio Clovio in 1571, a master of miniature painting who was his friend.

paintings.t: The Mystic Marriage of St. Catherine
paintings.why: Mary and the baby Jesus sit in a glorious cloud of light with Saint Catherine, in a rich Venetian scene. Paolo Veronese painted it in about 1575.
Huge muscular giants tumble in the air, falling from heaven in a twisting heap. Cornelis van Haarlem painted it in 1588, and he showed off his skill at painting the human body.
Misty pine trees appear and fade into the fog on a pair of folding screens, painted in black ink. Hasegawa Tōhaku painted it in the late 1500s, and it is one of the best-known paintings in Japan.
Two saints stand together, one with the keys and the other with a book, in a stormy scene with strong colors. El Greco painted this in about 1587.

Hundreds of saints, angels and ordinary people swirl around in the clouds in this giant painting, which fills the whole end wall of a council hall. Jacopo Tintoretto painted it in 1588, and it is one of the biggest oil paintings in the world.

Mary, Joseph and the baby Jesus travel over a river in a calm, golden landscape, led by a donkey and a guide. Annibale Carracci painted it in 1604, and this tranquil idea of landscape influenced later painters.
Christ stands in a dark room lit by a single candle in front of a high priest, who tears his robe. Gerard van Honthorst painted it in about 1617, and the candle's glow is the star.

A woman in a rich yellow dress turns away from a mirror and raises her hand, as her sister speaks to her. Artemisia Gentileschi painted it in about 1620, and the story is about Mary Magdalene giving up her old life.
A woman holds a mallet and a tent peg over a sleeping soldier, to save her people. Artemisia Gentileschi painted it in about 1620, from a Bible story.
