Christ hangs on a cross against a dark background, with the body painted as if it were a statue, lit by a single light. Francisco de Zurbarán painted it in 1627 for monks to pray in front of.
A young shepherdess in a beautiful dress holds a palm and a small dragon on a leash. Francisco de Zurbarán painted Saint Margaret in about 1630, and she looks like a real girl of the time.
A man offers coins to a woman who is sewing by candlelight, and she ignores him. Judith Leyster painted it in 1631, and it is a picture that says that a good woman will not be tempted by money.

paintings.t: Hercules Separates Mounts Calpe and Abylla
paintings.why: The hero Hercules pushes apart two mountains at the entrance of the Mediterranean, making the Strait of Gibraltar. Francisco de Zurbarán painted it in 1634, and the story is from legend.

paintings.t: The Defense of Cadiz Against the English
paintings.why: Spanish officers stand in a large, grand council room, talking about how to defend the port against the English fleet. Francisco de Zurbarán painted it in 1634.
The hero Hercules fights the many-headed hydra monster with his club, while it winds around his arm. Francisco de Zurbarán painted it in 1634 for a king's palace.

paintings.t: A Dance to the Music of Time
paintings.why: Four figures, the Seasons, hold hands and dance in a circle to music played by an old man, Time, while a baby blows bubbles, and the sun god rides by in the sky. Nicolas Poussin painted it in about 1635.
Saint Philip is lifted onto a cross with a rope while a crowd of men look on, in a dark, dramatic scene. Jusepe de Ribera painted it in 1639.

Two ragged boys eat fruit and enjoy it, a boy with a bunch of grapes and another with a slice of melon, while a little dog looks on. Bartolomé Esteban Murillo painted it in about 1650, and his street boys are cheerful and warm.

paintings.t: The Holy Family with a Bird
paintings.why: Mary, Joseph and the baby Jesus play with a pet bird and a little dog in a warm, homey scene. Bartolomé Esteban Murillo painted it in about 1650, and the family looks like a real Spanish family.

paintings.t: The Man with the Golden Helmet
paintings.why: A man in a shining helmet looks out of the dark with a shadowed face. The painting was once credited to Rembrandt, but experts now think it was painted by someone in his circle, in about 1650.

paintings.t: The Courtyard of a House in Delft
paintings.why: A woman and a child stand in a corridor next to a sunny courtyard, with a bucket and a broom. Pieter de Hooch painted it in 1658, and the light and the brick make it very peaceful.
Women prepare the newborn Mary for her bath, while angels float above in a golden light. Bartolomé Esteban Murillo painted it in about 1660, in a warm, family scene.

A young woman in a red hat and a blue and yellow coat holds a flute, in a close-up portrait. This was painted in the studio of Johannes Vermeer, in about 1669, and it is not thought to be by Vermeer himself.

A folding screen is painted with scenes of ladies and men at play in Kyoto, with music, games and gorgeous kimonos. An unknown artist painted it in about 1624, and it gives a lively view of life in Japan in the early Edo period.

The king of France stands in a huge, flowing blue cloak with fleur-de-lis, in white stockings with red heels, with his crown, scepter and sword beside him. Hyacinthe Rigaud painted it in 1701, when Louis was 63, and he looks grand and proud.

Four children in fancy clothes stand and play in a bright room: a girl does a curtsy, a boy winds up a bird organ, and a baby in a walker reaches for a cherry. Hogarth painted it for their father. A cat eyes the caged bird, and a clock has a Cupid on it. It's full of fun details.
paintings.k: Find the cat. What do you think it is watching in the cage?

paintings.why: The King of Spain and his queen sit with their children, in a splendid hall, in rich satins. Van Loo painted a large group portrait to display the royal family in 1743. Each member is carefully painted in elegant clothes. It's a glimpse of Spanish royalty.

A blindfolded girl reaches out as her friends laugh and dart away, in a woodland scene. Fragonard's picture is full of the lighthearted spirit of the Rococo. The leaves and silks swirl with color. It's a delightful picture of a game.

The king's favorite stands in a silky gown covered in bows and flowers, in a garden room with books and a mirror. Boucher painted her as a patron of the arts, with books beside her. She was one of the most powerful women in France. It's a stylish picture.

paintings.t: Miravan Breaking Open the Tomb of his Ancestors
paintings.why: A man breaks into a tomb, with his torch, in search of treasure, but finds an inscription that warns him to leave. Wright of Derby painted dramatic lighting inside a gloomy vault. It's based on a story from a popular book. It's a haunting scene.

paintings.t: Earthstopper on the Banks of the Derwent
paintings.why: A man with a lantern and a shovel works by moonlight, blocking fox dens before a hunt. Wright painted a moonlit scene on the Derwent river in England, with a glowing moon behind the clouds. The light is magic. It's an unusual picture of rural work.

A man in prison sits with his head in his hands, in a dark cell lit by a single lamp. This is an illustration from a story by Laurence Sterne about a man who is imprisoned. Wright used the light to create a sad, quiet drama. It's a thoughtful work about freedom.

A calm figure of Jesus on the cross, against a dark background, with a soft light. Goya painted it as a young man to win admission to the Academy. The body is shown in a sculptural, classical style. It's a quiet, thoughtful painting.

paintings.t: The Family of the Infante Don Luis
paintings.why: A prince and his family are gathered around a card table in a candlelit room, with servants and a painter in the corner. Goya painted himself on the left, almost at the prince's feet. It's a daring and informal royal portrait. It's one of his earliest great family paintings.

In June 1789, members of the French National Assembly, locked out of their meeting hall, gathered in an indoor tennis court and swore to write a new constitution. David's sketch shows people with their arms raised, as curtains billow in the wind. It's a moment that started the French Revolution. It's a drawing of an idea in action.

A young general in a dashing uniform charges forward with a flag, determined to lead his soldiers across a bridge in Italy. Gros painted the romantic, hero's portrait of Napoleon. It was the first of many pictures that made him a legend. It's an energetic image.

George Washington looks out calmly, with a pale background left unfinished. Gilbert Stuart painted this in 1796, and it's the image of Washington on the U.S. one-dollar bill. Stuart never finished it, so he kept it and made copies. It's perhaps the most reproduced portrait in American history.
A woman representing Truth is held up by Time, as History writes in a book. Goya painted the allegory in 1797. It means that, in time, the truth will be known. It's a hopeful idea.

paintings.t: Napoleon on the Battlefield of Eylau
paintings.why: Napoleon surveys the snowy field after a bloody battle in 1807, surrounded by wounded soldiers. Gros painted the horror of war along with the general's calm. It was a controversial picture that showed the cost of victory. It's a landmark of Romanticism.

paintings.t: The Distribution of the Eagle Standards
paintings.why: Napoleon, standing on a platform, gives his soldiers their eagle standards, with troops pledging loyalty. David painted the grand ceremony from 1804. The colors and flags are dazzling. It's a picture of power and pageantry.

A man in a pointed hat is being judged before a court of stern officials, in a dark, gloomy hall. Goya was critical of the Spanish Inquisition, a harsh religious court. He painted it with powerful light and dark. It's a bold statement against injustice.
l: Royal Academy of Fine Arts of San Fernando

paintings.why: Judith, in a long gown, holds a sack with a severed head, and a servant stands nearby. Andrea Mantegna or a follower made this picture in gray tones in about 1495, and it shows the Bible hero who saved her city.

In 1781, after the Battle of Yorktown, British officers lay down their arms as the American and French soldiers watch. Trumbull painted many portraits of real officers, and he worked from life. The surrender was a decisive moment in the American Revolution. It hangs in the U.S. Capitol.

A huge jagged mountain towers over a valley, as clouds swirl and a tiny house sits far below. Friedrich painted the Alps as a huge symbol of nature's power. The peaks look like they glow. It's one of his most dramatic mountain scenes.

A gnarled, leafless oak stands in a field with a flock of black crows above it, under a pale sky. Friedrich painted bare trees that stood for strength and loneliness. The twisting branches are drawn with great care. It's a dramatic look at the bleakness of winter.

A woman looks out of an open window in a studio, seen from behind, toward the river and ships. Friedrich painted his wife Caroline. The picture is a metaphor for longing. It's one of the most famous images of looking out.

Through an open window, you can see the rooftops and the harbor of Copenhagen, on a sunny day. Martinus Rørbye painted it in a clear and precise way. It's an unusual 'window picture,' which fits inside and outside in one. It's a charming early Danish painting.

A frozen fjord lies below snowy mountains, under a cold, blue-gray sky. J. C. Dahl, a Norwegian painter, painted nature with great accuracy. He was among the first to paint Norway's wild scenery. It's a famous landscape.
l: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

paintings.why: Three white children sit with a young Black boy named Bélizaire, an enslaved child who was part of their household in New Orleans. Jacques Amans painted this in 1837. Today the painting is studied for what it shows about slavery in America, because Bélizaire is one of few enslaved children painted by name. It reminds us that art can record difficult parts of history.

A prince lies sick in bed, but a doctor discovers the cause: he's in love with his father's young wife, and his father, the king, looks on. In the story, the king gave her up for his son's sake. Ingres painted it with a lot of detail. It's a story about kindness and sacrifice.

A young Mary sits embroidering a lily as her mother, Anne, watches in a quiet room, with a vine outside. Rossetti painted this when he was 20, one of the first Pre-Raphaelite pictures. Every object has a symbolic meaning. It's an early, important work.

A woman in armor stands before the flag of a united Germany, wearing a crown, and holding a sword. Veit painted this in 1848 during a revolution when Germans hoped for a unified country. It hung in Frankfurt's parliament. It's a symbol of national hope.

Three women in fine dresses walk down a country lane, as a cow and a girl stand by. Courbet painted his sisters as the village ladies, giving alms to a peasant girl. The picture was criticized for showing ordinary folks as large as life. It's a landmark of Realism.

A young woman tries to tie a white scarf around her sweetheart's arm to save him from danger, but he gently pulls it off to stay true to his faith. Millais painted it in 1852, based on a historical story of religious conflict in France. The emotions are visible on both faces. It was a hit with the public.

paintings.t: Frederick the Great Playing the Flute at Sanssouci
paintings.why: King Frederick the Great plays the flute in a glittering hall lit by candles as musicians and courtiers listen. Menzel painted the king as a music-lover, which he truly was. The chandeliers and mirrors shimmer. It's a famous German painting of the 1700s.

paintings.t: Symphony in White, No. 2: The Little White Girl
paintings.why: A young woman in a white dress leans at a mantelpiece, looking into a mirror, with a Japanese fan and a flower pot. Whistler painted Joanna Hiffernan, as a study in white. He named the picture like music. It's a famous work of the Aesthetic Movement.

paintings.t: The Battle of the Kearsarge and the Alabama
paintings.why: Two warships fire at each other in the English Channel off Cherbourg in 1864, during the American Civil War. Manet, a Paris artist, painted a big wide sea with a tiny ship, and the Alabama sinking. The sea is a green-gray ocean with a high horizon. It's his first major seascape.

A bride, surrounded by attendants, lifts her veil, as a young Black child offers a bouquet of flowers. Rossetti painted this scene inspired by a Bible poem. It's rich with colors and details. It's one of his finest.

A tall young man works at his easel, painting a still life of a bird, in a studio. Renoir painted his friend Frédéric Bazille, a fellow painter who shared his studio. It's a picture of friendship. It's a sweet look at two painters at work.

paintings.t: Isabella and the Pot of Basil
paintings.why: A woman cradles a pot of basil, which holds a sad secret, in a rich red room. The story, from a poem by Keats, is about love and loss. Hunt painted it as a symbol of devotion. It's a famous Pre-Raphaelite painting.
A woman holds a fan, with a pink rose behind her ear, her dark eyes distant. Rossetti painted the portrait with deep, rich colors. The title is Italian for 'Lady Rose.' It's an elegant picture.

Manet sits at his easel, painting a model, while a group of his friends, including Monet and Renoir, gather to watch. Fantin-Latour painted this tribute to Manet, who was a leader of a new type of art. It's a group portrait of artists. It documents a key moment in art history.

The poet Dante dreams of the death of his beloved Beatrice, who lies in a room full of flowers and angels. Rossetti painted this huge picture over several years. The colors are rich and the mood is dreamy. It's a moving image of love and loss.

A hazy blue river scene at dusk shows the Thames in London, with a barge and a dark shoreline. Whistler titled his misty twilight pictures 'Nocturnes' after music. He simplified the view to just a few soft tones. It's a masterpiece of mood and atmosphere.

A mother gazes tenderly at her sleeping baby in a cradle under a gauzy, see-through veil. Berthe Morisot painted her sister Edma and her niece. Morisot was a leading Impressionist and the only woman in their first exhibition in 1874. It's one of the most beloved pictures of motherhood.

A woman in a green dress plays the violin, in a bright room with a window. Rossetti painted the model Alexa Wilding with a flowing golden hair, as a musician. It's a feast of color. It's a rich portrait of music and beauty.

A woman reads in the dappled shade of a lilac tree in bloom, as the spring light falls. Monet painted it in 1872 at Argenteuil with his wife as the model. The pink blossoms and green leaves glow. It's a lovely picture of spring.

A woman with a parasol and a child walk along a path in a field of red poppies, and another pair walks across the hill above. Monet painted the scene in early summer, with bright red dots of flowers. It's one of the most beloved Impressionist landscapes. It's a happy image of a sunny day.

A crowd of people in black suits and costumes, with masks and hats, are packed into a hall at the Paris Opera. Manet painted friends among the crowd. The black suits and colored costumes make a fascinating pattern. It's a picture of modern Paris at night.

A small stone house with a red roof sits at a bend in a country road in Auvers, France. The gloomy title was just a local name for the building. Cézanne painted it with thick, solid strokes. It was shown at the first Impressionist exhibition in 1874.

A young bride looks sadly away as an old official stands at her side during a wedding in a church. Pukirev's painting was a protest at forced marriages. It made a stir in Russia in 1862 and was widely discussed. It's famous as a social message in paint.

A young man in a suit stands with his hands in his pockets, looking down at a Paris boulevard from his balcony, seen from behind. Caillebotte painted his brother René. We can't see what he is looking at, which makes us curious. It's a famous picture of city life.

A man and woman sit in a garden at a table, near orange trees in big green tubs. Caillebotte painted the sunlit garden of his family's home. The fresh sunlight and cool shade are lovely. It's a peaceful moment.

A road winds through tall fields of golden rye, with towering pine trees against a bright sky. Shishkin loved the Russian countryside and painted it in great detail. The rye seems to ripple in the wind. It's a classic Russian landscape.

paintings.t: The Millinery Shop by Edgar Degas
paintings.why: A woman at a table in a hat shop tries a hat on a stand, with a tray of colorful hats in front. Degas shows a typical shop with unusual angles. The pale tones are soft and quiet. It's a modern view of work.

A young man leans toward a woman at a restaurant table, in the sunny garden, as a waiter looks on. Manet painted the lively scene outdoors, in bright daylight. The flirting is charming. It's a picture of Paris café life.

paintings.t: Congregation Leaving the Reformed Church in Nuenen
paintings.why: Villagers in black walk out of a small church after a service, among bare trees. Van Gogh painted it in 1884–85, when his father was the pastor there. The sad dark colors reflect the winter mood. It's a painting of his early life.

A young woman in a fur-trimmed coat and a hat stands in the autumn sunshine, looking at us with a calm expression. Manet painted this near the end of his life. The model was Méry Laurent, a friend. It's a delightful portrait.
l: Museum of Fine Arts of Nancy

paintings.why: A woman with a parasol walks along a sunny beach, as the waves and sails sparkle. Monet painted the Normandy coast with fresh and feathery strokes. The sea is a blaze of blue. It's a breezy summer day.

Dante in a red robe stands on a bridge in Florence, as Beatrice walks by with her friends, not seeing him. Holiday painted a famous moment from Dante's life. It's a story of love at a distance. It's a Pre-Raphaelite-style painting.

A young man wakes in a forest and sees a sleeping girl, and he is changed forever by love. Leighton painted a scene from a story by Boccaccio. The golden light and rich colors are beautiful. It's a lush picture of a magical moment.
l: Art Gallery of New South Wales

paintings.why: A sorceress draws a circle on the ground with a wand, while a raven and a cauldron wait nearby, on a wild, stormy moor. Waterhouse painted a witch casting a spell. The rich colors give it a magical feeling. It's a famous painting of witchcraft.
paintings.k: Look at the witch and the circle on the ground. What do you think she is brewing?

paintings.why: A noblewoman is dragged through the snowy streets of Moscow on a sled, her chained hand raised with two fingers in a defiant sign. Surikov painted Feodosia Morozova, who was jailed in the 1600s for her faith. The crowd reacts with sorrow, mockery and awe. It's one of the greatest Russian history paintings.
A bright blue kingfisher sits on a branch beside the water, painted with strokes of color. Van Gogh loved the glowing colors of birds. It's a small, quick study. It's a charming animal portrait.
paintings.k: The kingfisher is bright blue. What is the bird looking at?

paintings.why: A huge, wild crowd of masked, grinning people fills the street in a parade, with a tiny Jesus on a donkey. Ensor painted a carnival that mocked modern society. The colors are neon bright. It was shocking in 1888, and today it's regarded as a Belgian masterpiece.

paintings.t: Peasant Woman Against a Background of Wheat
paintings.why: A woman in a straw hat stands in front of a golden field of wheat, painted with bold, swirling lines. Van Gogh painted the portrait in 1890 in Auvers-sur-Oise. The yellow and blue colors seem to vibrate. It's a happy tribute to the working people he admired.

paintings.t: At the Moulin Rouge, The Dance
paintings.why: Dancers kick and twirl in the Moulin Rouge nightclub while onlookers in top hats watch. Toulouse-Lautrec painted the stars of Paris nightlife, here the dancer Valentin the Boneless. He used a quick sketchy style. It's a bright picture of Parisian entertainment.

A white monastery sits on a green hill by a river, in a golden, quiet light. Levitan loved to paint the Russian landscape with a mood of calm. It's a place that seems out of time. It's a peaceful, spiritual scene.

A rocky mountain rises over a patchwork of fields and a viaduct, painted in blocks of blue, green and orange. Cézanne painted this mountain more than 60 times. He broke the scene into patches of color. It's one of the paintings that led to modern art.

A river sparkles in the pink twilight, with a monastery and wooded banks, as the sound of bells seems to echo. Levitan painted a quiet scene on the Volga in a dreamy light. The soft sky is magical. It's one of the best-loved Russian landscapes.

A lonely, wide road stretches across a gloomy plain under a gray sky. The Vladimirka was the road along which prisoners were marched to Siberia. Levitan painted a quiet, sorrowful landscape. It's a landscape with a story of suffering.

A woman in a shimmering, silky gown leans back in a chair, with a calm and slightly amused look. Sargent painted Gertrude Agnew, and the picture made him a sensation in London. The fresh and daring style was new. It's one of the most famous portraits of the 1890s.

A calm, blue night with a glowing, shimmering sea and a few stars, and a pair of faint figures on the shore. Munch painted this in 1893, before Van Gogh's version was famous. The swirling blue sky is full of mood. It's a lesser-known night scene.

paintings.t: Summer Evening on Skagen's Southern Beach
paintings.why: Women in white dresses walk together along the beach in the dusk, with the soft blue sea and sky. Krøyer's friends are the models. The calm, glowing colors are magical. It's a favorite Danish painting.

A young girl in a white dress stands in a room, in front of a vase of large flowers, looking out. Olga Boznańska was a Polish painter who worked in Paris. Her soft, gray tones are very special. It's one of the best-known Polish portraits.

paintings.t: Pont Boieldieu in Rouen, Rainy Weather
paintings.why: A busy city bridge crosses a river in the rain, with umbrellas, wagons and gray sky. Pissarro painted it from a hotel window in Rouen, France. The wet gray colors reflect the weather. It's a lively picture of everyday life in the rain.

A woman in a red robe hugs a golden box as mist and shadowy figures rise from it. In Greek myth, Pandora opens a box and lets out all the troubles of the world, but hope remains inside. Waterhouse painted the moment just before. It's a gripping image of curiosity.

paintings.t: At the French Windows. The Artist's Wife
paintings.why: A woman stands by a window, in a quiet room with a calm light, seen from behind. Ring, a Danish painter, painted his wife Sigrid. The picture feels peaceful and still. It's a famous Danish interior.

paintings.t: Summer Evening at Skagen Beach – The Artist and his Wife
paintings.why: A couple walks along the beach at dusk, as the sea and the sky glow in tones of blue. Krøyer painted himself and his wife Marie in the soft evening light of northern Denmark. The 'blue hour' of Scandinavia is a magical time. It's a lovely, gentle scene.

Farm workers pitch hay and rake in the fields under the sunny sky. Pissarro, one of the Impressionists, lived in the village of Éragny and painted its people. The colors are fresh and bright. It's a happy picture of country work.

A rider on a galloping horse dashes through a bright meadow, in blue cloak and dots of color. Kandinsky's painting inspired the name of the art group 'Der Blaue Reiter' (The Blue Rider). The figure is almost abstract. It's a landmark of modern art.
paintings.k: A rider gallops through bright patches of color. What color is the horse?

paintings.why: A twilight scene of a silent fjord, with dark trees and a pale pink sky, as the night sun stays low. Slott-Møller painted the magical light of a northern summer night. The picture is hushed and dreamy. It's a favorite Danish landscape.

A twisted tree branches across the canvas in a net of black lines on a gray background. Mondrian painted it in 1911 as he moved from realism toward abstraction. The branches almost become a pattern. It's a key step toward his famous grids.

A woman in a blue-green dress stands in a rich room, mixing a potion in a pot with a black cat and a bubbling cauldron. Waterhouse painted her intent look. It's a picture of magic at work. It's among his finest.

A bright blue horse stands in a landscape of red and yellow hills, with its head bent. Franz Marc used blue to represent strength and spirit. He believed animals were closer to nature than humans. It's one of the most famous expressionist paintings.
paintings.k: Horses are never really blue. Why do you think the artist chose that color?

paintings.why: A sculptor and his wife stand together, with calm, long faces, in a simple background. Modigliani painted his friend Jacques Lipchitz, a sculptor, and his bride, Berthe. They paid for the portrait, and Modigliani later added more work. It's a famous double portrait.

Christ hangs on the cross while Mary and John grieve below, and Mary Magdalene kneels with her arms thrown wide. Masaccio painted it around 1426, and the figures have real weight and shadow, a new way of painting that changed art in Florence. He died at only 26.
Mary sits on the ground, which was a way of showing she was humble, holding the baby Jesus in her lap. Fra Angelico painted this sweet scene in about 1433 with soft colors and gold.
Christ crowns Mary Queen of Heaven in the middle of a crowd of cheering saints and angels. Fra Angelico painted this sparkling scene in about 1434, with gold and bright blue and pink.

The angel Gabriel arrives to tell Mary she will have a baby, in a cozy Flemish room with a bed and a bright window. Rogier van der Weyden painted this triptych, a picture with three panels, in about 1434.

Mary stands holding the baby Jesus in front of a rich red cloth held up by two angels, beside a small fountain. Jan van Eyck painted this tiny picture in 1439, and it is just about as wide as a sheet of paper.
l: Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp

paintings.why: Mary sits in a garden of roses with the baby Jesus while angels play music and hold up a green cloth behind her. Stefan Lochner painted it in Cologne in about 1440, in a sweet, storybook style.
The cross stands at the center with Mary and Saint John grieving, and on the side panels more saints. Rogier van der Weyden painted this triptych in about 1440, and the faces express deep sadness.

Mary holds her dead son's body and weeps, with Mary Magdalene beside her. Rogier van der Weyden painted this sad, quiet scene in about 1441, and many people say it is one of the most moving pictures of the 1400s.
A prince in a red hat looks to one side, in profile, with a heavy nose and a stern face. Piero della Francesca painted it in 1450, and Sigismondo was a warlord who ruled the Italian city of Rimini.
Mary holds her baby close while he sleeps, and her cheek rests near his. Andrea Mantegna painted this in about 1457, and the sleeping baby is a sign of how the story would end.
Mary holds the baby Jesus tenderly, with her face lowered and a soft, sad look in her eyes. Giovanni Bellini painted it around 1460, and he painted many such Madonnas.

Jesus and his friends sit at a table in a modern-looking room, as he breaks the bread. Dieric Bouts painted this big altarpiece in 1464 for a church in Leuven, and it has side panels from the Old Testament.

A knight on a white horse stabs a dragon, while a princess leads the monster away on a string like a pet. Paolo Uccello painted it in the 1470s, and the sky, with a swirly storm cloud, adds to the drama.
The nymph Daphne turns into a tree as the god Apollo chases her, and her fingers sprout leaves. Piero del Pollaiuolo painted this in about 1470, and the story comes from Greek myth.

A man in black holds up a coin from ancient Rome, with a palm tree and a landscape behind him. Hans Memling painted him in about 1473, and the coin shows the emperor Nero. It is thought to be Bernardo Bembo, a Venetian diplomat.
l: Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp

paintings.why: Christ glows with white light on a mountain while Moses and Elijah stand beside him, and his friends cower below. Giovanni Bellini painted it in about 1478, and the green hills and quiet sky in the back are as beautiful as anything in his career.
Mary holds Christ's body in her lap while John and other friends mourn around him. Pietro Perugino painted it in about 1483, and the soft light and gentle faces give it a quiet peace.
Mary holds the baby Jesus against a red background of angels' heads. Andrea Mantegna painted it in about 1485, and the red, blue and gold are rich and dark.

The kings arrive with a large crowd of followers, kneeling to the baby Jesus in front of a ruined arch. Domenico Ghirlandaio painted it in 1485, and he included lots of things from daily life in Florence.
Mary holds her baby with a tender expression, and the heads of red cherubs float around them. Giovanni Bellini painted it in about 1485, and the red color makes the whole picture glow.
Mary appears to a monk at his desk, and angels hold the rocks of a cave around her. Filippino Lippi painted it in 1486, and the little donor portrait hides in a corner.

paintings.t: Christ with singing and music-making Angels
paintings.why: Angels sing and play the harp, the lute, the organ and the trumpet, and some are shown reading music. Hans Memling painted these panels in 1489, and the details of the instruments are exactly right.
l: Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp

paintings.why: Mary sits on a platform in a garden while saints stand around her, and a lake with distant hills shines beyond. Giovanni Bellini painted this puzzling picture in about 1490, and no one is sure exactly what the story is.

The baby Jesus glows with light on the ground in a night scene, and angels stand around him. Geertgen tot Sint Jans painted it in about 1490, and it is one of the first pictures to show a scene lit mainly by firelight.
Mary and Elizabeth meet and embrace under an arch, in a view of a calm Italian town. Domenico Ghirlandaio painted it in 1491, and it is full of grace and quiet joy.

A huge crowd walks through Saint Mark's Square in Venice, carrying a relic of the True Cross under a canopy. Gentile Bellini painted it in 1496, and it shows the great church of St. Mark's with its gold mosaics as they were.
A crowd of people in rich clothes fills the foreground while the kings kneel before the baby Jesus, and the mood is lively. Filippino Lippi painted it in 1496, and it is packed with details.
The god Apollo and the satyr Marsyas compete in music, and the god sits on a rock holding a violin-like instrument. Pietro Perugino painted it in 1497, and the story is told in Greek myth.

Christ stands with his hands tied, looking gaunt, while men crowd in from either side. Andrea Mantegna painted it in about 1500, and it is drawn so close up that it feels as though you were in the crowd.
The god Mars and the goddess Venus stand on top of a stone arch while the Muses dance below, and the god Apollo plays his lyre. Andrea Mantegna painted it in about 1500 for a princess in Mantua.
Friends crowd around Christ's body at the foot of the cross, weeping, as dark clouds fill the sky. Albrecht Dürer painted it in about 1500, and the faces show deep sadness.
Mary and the baby Jesus sit between saints in a golden altarpiece, with a long row of small scenes below. Fra Angelico painted it, and Lorenzo di Credi later changed it.

paintings.t: Madonna and Child with the Young St John the Baptist and St Peter Martyr
paintings.why: Mary and the baby Jesus sit with the young John and Saint Peter Martyr in a landscape. Lorenzo Lotto painted it in about 1503, and it is an early work of his.

paintings.t: Still-Life with Partridge and Iron Gloves
paintings.why: A dead partridge hangs next to a pair of iron gloves and a crossbow bolt on a plain wall. Jacopo de' Barbari painted it in 1504, and it is one of the first still lifes in Europe.

Mary holds the lifeless Christ, with a calm sky and a glowing landscape behind them. Giovanni Bellini painted it in about 1505, and the stone-gray tones and soft light make the sorrow feel still and quiet.
l: Gallerie dell'Accademia - room V Giovanni Bellini

paintings.why: A wrinkled old woman holds a bag of gold in her hand, with a sad, sour face. Albrecht Dürer painted this in 1507 as a warning about greed.
Mary sits behind a hedge of roses and holds the baby Jesus, while he plays with a small child. Bernardino Luini painted it in about 1510, and he was a follower of Leonardo da Vinci.
Noah lies passed out after drinking wine, while one son covers him up and the others laugh. Giovanni Bellini painted this in about 1515, when he was about 85, and it is one of his last paintings.
l: Musée des Beaux-Arts et d'Archéologie de Besançon

paintings.t: Meeting of St Erasm and St Maurice
paintings.why: Two saints meet, one in a bishop's robe and the other in shining golden armor. Matthias Grünewald painted it in about 1520, and the glittering armor is amazing.

paintings.t: Moses Defending the Daughters of Jethro
paintings.why: Moses leaps into a fight to help two women at a well, in a twisting, packed scene. Rosso Fiorentino painted it in 1523, and it is full of energy and bright, strange colors.
Four saints are about to be killed in a dramatic scene, with soldiers bending low to do the deed. Correggio painted it in 1524.
A young soldier looks out at you in a rich suit of armor, with a landscape behind him. Parmigianino painted Lorenzo Cybo in 1524.

paintings.t: Portrait of a Halberdier, Francesco Guardi?
paintings.why: A young soldier in a bright pink and white suit stands with his hand on his hip, holding a spear. Pontormo painted him in 1529, and this is the only painting by him in the United States west of Texas.

Three slim, pale women stand side by side, wearing only jewelry and hats, against a dark background. Lucas Cranach the Elder painted it in 1531, and they are the Three Graces, who stand for beauty and charm.
A man in black with a gold chain and ring looks out calmly in front of a green background. Bronzino painted Bartolomeo Panciatichi in about 1540, and the cool, smooth finish is typical of him.
Friends carry Christ's body down from the cross, in a bright, smooth painting. Bronzino painted it in about 1543.
l: Musée des Beaux-Arts et d'Archéologie de Besançon

paintings.why: Mary Magdalene sits in her fine gown while her sister Martha speaks to her, as she turns away from the pleasures of the world. Paolo Veronese painted it in about 1548, with rich colors.
An older man in a red robe looks out sharply from the picture, in a thick and quick brush style. Jacopo Tintoretto painted this portrait of a Venetian official in about 1550.
Eve offers a fruit to Adam, who reaches for it, with the tree of knowledge between them. Jacopo Tintoretto painted it in about 1550, and the muscled bodies show how he was influenced by Michelangelo.

paintings.t: A Meat Stall with the Holy Family Giving Alms
paintings.why: A big butcher's stall full of sausages, a pig's head and cuts of meat takes up the front, while in the back Mary, Joseph and the baby Jesus give a coin to a beggar. Pieter Aertsen painted it in 1551, and the food is the star.

paintings.t: Portrait Group with the Artist’s Father, Brother and Sister
paintings.why: A father, a son and a daughter stand close together, with the little boy pushing a big dog. Sofonisba Anguissola painted her family in 1559, when she was in her twenties.

paintings.t: The Family of Darius Before Alexander
paintings.why: The family of a defeated king kneels before Alexander the Great, and the queen mistakenly bows to the wrong man. Paolo Veronese painted it in about 1565, with sumptuous clothes and a grand palace.

A Roman woman raises a dagger to her chest in a gloomy room, as she is determined to end her life to save her honor. Paolo Veronese painted it in about 1580, and the story is about the start of the Roman Republic.

Mary holds the baby Jesus in her arms, dressed in a simple dress with a soft, tender look. Artemisia Gentileschi painted it in about 1612, when she was a young painter, and the mother is warmly painted.
A woman in a golden dress plays the lute, tuning a string, in a warm, gentle scene. Orazio Gentileschi painted this in about 1612 and it is soft and quiet.
A woman looks up with a palm branch in her hand, a sign of a martyr, in a close, dramatic picture. Artemisia Gentileschi painted herself in about 1615.
A woman in a rich golden dress looks out from the picture, holding a lute, and she looks up as if she is thinking about a tune. Artemisia Gentileschi painted herself in about 1616.
Christ, tied up, bows his head while soldiers press a crown of thorns onto it. Anthony van Dyck painted it in about 1620, and the faces are sharp and emotional.
The Egyptian queen Cleopatra lies on a bed, about to end her life, in a solemn, quiet scene. Artemisia Gentileschi painted it in about 1620.
A woman sits at a table in the dark with a candle, a mirror and a skull, thinking quietly. Georges de La Tour painted it in about 1625, and the soft candlelight makes it feel calm and still.

A young woman in a blue and yellow dress holds a plate with her own breasts, which is the sign of Saint Agatha, with a calm look on her face. Francisco de Zurbarán painted it in about 1630, and she looks out as if nothing is wrong.

paintings.t: Militia Company of District XI under the Command of Captain Reynier Reael
paintings.why: A company of Amsterdam's citizen soldiers pose around a table in dark clothes and colored sashes, some standing, some sitting. Frans Hals and Pieter Codde painted it between 1633 and 1637, and each man has a different expression.
A queen in a rich gown stands with her arm raised and flowers in her lap, in a story about a miracle in which bread turned to roses. Francisco de Zurbarán painted it in about 1635.

A big black and white bull stands in a field in front of a farmer, a ram and a few cows. Paulus Potter painted it in 1647 when he was only 22, and it is life-size, so large that it was once thought to be too big to hang.

A ragged boy sits in a doorway, picking fleas from his shirt, in a patch of sunlight. Bartolomé Esteban Murillo painted it in about 1650, and the boy's bare feet and dirty clothes are shown with sympathy.
A boy with a dog shows a bright, friendly look as he holds the dog's collar, and the dog jumps up. Bartolomé Esteban Murillo painted it in about 1655.
A young mother with a baby on her lap sits by a window, and a servant leans in from behind. Gerrit Dou painted it in 1658, with tiny, precise brushstrokes.
A young boy with long hair holds a lamb and a staff, looking out of a green landscape. Bartolomé Esteban Murillo painted it in about 1664, and the Good Shepherd is Christ as a child.
A man in a red coat stops writing a letter at a desk, a woman reads one nearby, in a matching painting. Gabriel Metsu painted it in about 1665, and the two paintings are hung side by side.

A skate fish hangs open on a hook, a cat arches its back at the sight, and oysters lie on a kitchen table. Chardin painted this at 28, and it won him membership in the French Academy. The colors, textures and shapes are magical. It's one of the greatest still lifes ever painted.

A young woman stands in a farmhouse, with her broken basket of eggs, as an old woman scolds her. Greuze painted this story in a soft, delicate way. It's a fine example of a 'moral' picture. It was very popular in the 1700s.

paintings.t: The Fight Between Mars and Minerva
paintings.why: The god of war, Mars, battles the goddess of wisdom, Minerva, as Venus tries to help. David painted this as a student and won a prize in Paris. It's a lesson that wisdom defeats brute force. It's an early peek at his talent.
A Polish nobleman rides a rearing white horse in a fine uniform, in a heroic pose. David painted the portrait in Rome. The dramatic composition shows his skill. It's a spirited portrait.

The queen of France holds a rose in her hand in a simple dress and a straw hat, in a garden. Vigée Le Brun painted her as a lovely woman instead of a queen. The first version was shocking because it was so informal. It's a very charming portrait.

The great German writer Goethe reclines in a traveler's cloak and a wide hat, by a ruin in the Italian countryside. Tischbein painted his friend during their trip to Italy. The pose looks like an ancient hero. It's the most famous portrait of Goethe.

A nervous man in a theater looks out as a lamp holds a ghostly light, while a monster-like figure watches. Goya painted a comic scene to poke fun at superstitions. It's a spooky painting with a silly side. It's one of his best-known works.

George Washington, his wife Martha, and her grandchildren sit around a table with a map of the new capital city, with an enslaved servant at the side. Savage painted it in 1796 and it was widely copied as a print. The picture shows the nation's first family in their elegant home. It also reminds us that the Washingtons enslaved people.

A beautiful woman in a black dress points to her ring, which bears Goya's name, as a wry reminder of the artist's skill. The Duchess of Alba was one of Spain's grandest ladies. Goya's portrait of her is powerful and playful. It's a famous mystery of art history.

The pope sits wearing a red cape, looking weary, and he rests his hands on a chair. David painted it in Paris before Napoleon's coronation. The face is full of character. It's among the best portraits of its day.

A young woman carries a heavy water jar on her shoulder, with a strong, calm face. Goya painted this around 1808–12 with a loose, quick brush. He admired ordinary people who held up society. It's a fine portrait of dignity.

A woman in a dark red velvet dress with a gold shawl sits in an elegant pose, her cheeks flushed, in front of a mirror. Ingres painted the fine details of fabrics, hair and jewelry. The critics found the picture odd at the time, but it's now admired. It's one of his greatest portraits.

paintings.t: A View through Three of the North-Western Arches of the Third Storey of the Coliseum
paintings.why: The huge stone arches of the Colosseum in Rome frame a sunlit view of the city. Eckersberg, a Danish painter, painted it on a visit to Italy. The light and the shadow on the stone are exact. It's a classic Danish painting.

Two old men in a dark room, one gaunt and one hunched over a bowl, with strange, shadowy faces. Goya painted this on a wall in his house. It is one of the 'Black Paintings' that he made for himself. It's a strange and powerful image.

Ships rest at the harbor of Friedrich's hometown, with the town's church spires against a glowing sky. He painted his birthplace from memory. The sky is a soft, golden blue. It's a calm and lovely harbor view.
A woman in a dark dress leans on a tomb at a cemetery, looking back at us. Goya's painting hangs on the wall of his house. Leocadia Weiss was his housekeeper. It's a striking portrait.

paintings.t: Bella and Hanna. The Eldest Daughters of M. L. Nathanson
paintings.why: Two teenage sisters in plain dresses sit close together, holding each other. Eckersberg painted them in 1820 for their father, a banker in Copenhagen. The soft light and quiet closeness make it very touching. It's one of the most-loved Danish portraits.

An ancient Roman bridge with a broken arch crosses a gorge, in clean sunlight with a hill town above. Corot painted it on the spot in Italy, as a young artist. The solid shapes and gentle light are remarkable. It's one of the most admired landscape sketches of the 1800s.

A group of people gather in a rich, dreamlike garden before the great Flood of Noah's time. Etty painted a lush, paradise-like world about to be washed away. The colors are warm and glowing. It's an imaginative Bible scene.

A huge stone cup stands on the shore of a tiny island, with a miniature world inside it, in a mysterious seascape. Cole painted a giant's goblet, which may be a symbol of the rise and fall of civilization. It's one of his most mysterious paintings. People still wonder what it means.

A wedding party fills a courtyard in Morocco, with musicians, guests and the bride in a rich costume. Delacroix visited Morocco in 1832 and was struck by the color. He painted this from sketches. It's a window into a different culture.

paintings.t: The Return of the Dove to the Ark
paintings.why: Two of Noah's sons gently hold a dove that has returned with an olive branch, a sign that the Flood is ending. Millais used a vivid red and green. The picture is bright with hope. It's a famous Pre-Raphaelite painting of a Bible story.

A woman in a silky dark gown leans against a wall, her hands in her lap, with a steady and serious look. Courbet painted the portrait of Mathilde Desportes, a friend. The texture of the fabric shines. It's an elegant portrait by a painter who is better known for his rugged scenes.

A man in a black coat and hat stands on a vast, empty beach with the Mediterranean in front of him, waving. Courbet painted himself, greeting the sea. The enormous sky and sea fill the whole picture. It's a bold, sun-filled seascape.

A fireman carries three small children out of a burning house, as the mother kneels in thankfulness. Millais painted the glowing flames. The painting was a favorite for its drama. It's a thrilling image of bravery.

A British officer sits in a chair, his wife leaning on him, while their children hold a toy and look at a newspaper announcing the end of the Crimean War. Millais painted a family's joy at the end of a war. The details of uniforms and toys are lovingly done. It's a heartfelt homecoming.

An old woodcutter, bent under a heavy load, is startled by Death, who comes to take him. Millet based it on a fable by La Fontaine, in which the man changes his mind about wanting to die. The painting shows the hard life of a working man. It's a famous story told in paint.

A young man in a clergyman's coat leans toward a woman, in a woodland, with ivy carved with their initials. Hughes painted a couple who must wait years to marry. The meticulous details of leaves and bark are amazing. It's a touching story.

paintings.t: Portrait of Monsieur and Madame Auguste Manet
paintings.why: The artist's parents sit stiffly in a dark room, his father in a chair and his mother at a table with her sewing. Manet painted them early in his career, with deep care. The calm, serious faces reveal their characters. It's a quiet and moving family portrait.

paintings.t: The Finding of the Saviour in the Temple
paintings.why: The young Jesus is surrounded by teachers in a temple, as his parents arrive to find him. Hunt spent years in the Holy Land to paint authentic costumes and architecture. It sold for an enormous sum at the time. It's a famous Pre-Raphaelite painting.

A massive iceberg rises from a cold, calm sea, with a ship's broken mast lying in the foreground. Church sailed to the Arctic to sketch the real ice. When shown in New York, people paid to see this panorama. It's one of the most spectacular polar landscapes.
paintings.k: The icebergs are huge. Can you find the broken mast?

paintings.why: A woman in a light-colored dress steps out of a cheap Paris café, holding a guitar and eating cherries, with a thoughtful look. Manet saw a real street singer and asked her to pose in his studio. He treated her with the same dignity as a society lady. It's a famous picture of everyday life in Paris.

A Spanish dancer in a glittering, spangled skirt strikes a proud pose. Manet painted Lola Melea when she came to Paris with a Spanish troupe in 1862. The sparkling outfit and bold stance are eye-catching. The poet Baudelaire wrote a verse for the frame.

Jesus sits in shadow, in the dim light of a lamp, after dinner, as Judas leaves the room with a huge shadow. Nikolai Ge painted the emotional moment before the betrayal. The dramatic lighting was new for religious art. It caused a sensation in Russia in 1863.
A bullfighter lies in the sand, in a black suit, shot in the ring. Manet cut a figure from a larger picture. The soft grays and blacks are painted with great skill. It's a quiet and striking picture.

A group of artists and writers, including Manet and Whistler, gather around a portrait of the painter Delacroix. Fantin-Latour painted it to honor Delacroix, who had recently died. It's like a family photo. It shows who the leading artists of the day were.

A philosopher sits with a book, as his two little daughters play beside him. Courbet painted his friend Pierre-Joseph Proudhon, who had recently died, and the children. The scene is quiet and affectionate. It's a deeply human portrait.

Fairies dance in a circle on a misty meadow, in the pale light of a summer night, according to Swedish folk tales. Malmström painted the scene in a soft, glowing way. It's a magical picture. It's one of the most beloved Swedish paintings.
paintings.k: The fairies dance in a circle. Can you count them?

paintings.why: A boy leans on a table, watching a bubble he's made, with a skull nearby that reminds us that life is short. Manet painted it as a 'vanitas,' a type of picture about how things are fragile. The boy is Léon Leenhoff, his stepson. It's a thoughtful picture about time.

Near the end of the American Civil War, President Lincoln and three leaders meet on a steamship to discuss peace. Healy painted the scene a few years after, in a quiet cabin with a view of the sea. The painting honors the hope for peace. It hangs in the White House.

A man reads a newspaper in a chair as a woman sits at the piano, smiling gently. Degas painted his friend Manet and his wife Suzanne. Manet later cut a piece off the canvas because he didn't like how Suzanne looked, which upset Degas. It's a famous story.

A man in a hat strolls through Paris with two little girls and a dog, in a quick, candid scene. Degas painted Viscount Lepic, who was a friend and a fellow artist. It looks like a snapshot. It's a lively view of the city.

paintings.t: Max Schmitt in a Single Scull
paintings.why: A rower glides across the Schuylkill River in Philadelphia in the early morning, as a tiny figure of the artist rows in the distance. Eakins painted his friend, who was a champion. The sunlight on the water is gorgeous. It's among the first great American sports paintings.

A woman leans down from heaven over a golden bar, her arms folded, as lovers below on Earth remember each other. Rossetti painted it from his own poem. The picture is full of golden hair, lilies and angels. It's a rich, dreamy Victorian picture.

Rows of worshippers kneel on carpets in a grand mosque, with lamps hanging and walls covered in patterns. Gérôme visited Cairo and filled the picture with real architecture. The painting is amazingly precise about its details. It's a window into a world that many Europeans had never seen.

paintings.t: Nocturne: Blue and Gold – Old Battersea Bridge
paintings.why: A long wooden bridge rises as a shadowy silhouette in the dusk, with fireworks and a tiny boat below. Whistler was inspired by Japanese prints and used simple shapes and subtle tones. He painted the London night like a piece of music. It's a famous atmospheric painting.

People hurry in all directions across the oldest bridge in Paris, under a cloud-filled sky. Renoir painted a crowd of cabs, walkers and umbrellas in tiny dabs of color. It's a lively snapshot. It's a fresh, early Impressionist city scene.

Three women in colorful costume relax in a room, with an elaborate pattern of cushions. Renoir was inspired by Delacroix's painting of Algiers. It's a fantasy of an exotic setting. It shows how artists dreamed of other places.

paintings.t: A Cotton Office in New Orleans
paintings.why: Men in a busy office examine samples of cotton, read newspapers and talk business. Degas painted the office of his uncle during a trip to New Orleans. It's an unusual picture of work. It's also a reminder that cotton was a huge industry that depended on enslaved labor before the Civil War.

A busy Paris boulevard is seen from above, with crowds and carriages that are painted as tiny dabs. Monet painted this from the studio of the photographer Nadar. A critic mocked it as 'black licks of tongue'. It's an important and vibrant Impressionist picture.

A couple sits at the edge of a river in the sun, with sailboats and the town of Argenteuil in the background, in bright blue. Manet painted it outdoors in 1874, following the Impressionists. The colors are fresh and the mood is cheerful. It's one of his boldest paintings.

paintings.t: Claude Monet painting in his studio boat
paintings.why: Monet sits on his floating studio, painting while his wife Camille sits in the cabin. Manet painted his friend at work on the river Seine at Argenteuil. They painted together in the open air. It's a picture of one great painter looking at another.

A woman in a long, dark dress with a hooded cloak, with a sad, strong look, in a Roman setting. Rossetti painted Alexa Wilding as a classic widow. The colors and shapes are bold. It's a statuesque portrait.
A mother in a flowered hat with her two children, dressed up for a walk, in light and shade. Renoir painted a loving family in a soft, glowing style. It's a charming and tender picture.

White huts glow in the moonlight by a stream, in a deep blue night under a starry sky. Kuindzhi painted the glowing moon so brightly that people thought there was a lamp behind it. The silvery light is magical. It's a favorite Ukrainian landscape.

Eighteen young women in flowing gowns, each with a musical instrument, glide down a spiral staircase. Burne-Jones painted this with a quiet, dreamy rhythm. The softly colored dresses make it feel like music in a picture. It's one of the most beloved Victorian paintings.

Whitewashed cottages glow with the last red rays of the setting sun, as the dusk covers the fields. Kuindzhi painted the village in warm and cool light. The shining color made visitors gasp. It's a famous glowing landscape.

Manet stands with his palette and brushes in a pale suit and a hat, looking out calmly. This is his only full-length self-portrait, and the style is elegant and cool. He painted it near the end of his life. It's a very stylish portrait.
A woman and a young girl are in a rowboat on a lake in a park, in soft daylight. Berthe Morisot painted it with light, quick strokes. It's one of her best-known paintings. It's a peaceful moment.

A single stalk of asparagus lies on a table, painted with just a few strokes. Manet made this after a collector paid more than he asked for another painting of a bunch of asparagus. It's a joke, a little 'thank you' note. It's a tiny gem.

A woman in a white and blue hat sits with a teacup in her hand, in a room with patterned wallpaper. Cassatt painted her mother, Lydia, relaxing at home. The quiet, everyday scene is full of charm. It's a lovely picture.
A woman in a green gown sits in the branches of a tree, a book in her lap, looking away. Rossetti used his muse, Jane Morris. A honeysuckle flower grows in her hand. It's a dreamy, romantic image.

Two ancient Greek poets, Sappho and Alcaeus, perform and listen on a marble terrace beside the blue sea. Alma-Tadema painted a sunny, perfect, imaginary Greece. Each person is shown in elegant detail. It's a lovely vision of a poet's world.

A young woman in a straw hat and a blue dress sits on a rocky coast, her hands in her lap, with a soft smile. Renoir painted her at the beach in Guernsey, in a gentle, feathery style. The warm tones glow. It's one of his best portraits.

A woman in an elegant Albanian costume with a gold-embroidered jacket looks calmly out, in front of a pale background. Kolë Idromeno, an Albanian painter, painted it in the 1880s. The textiles are beautiful. It's a treasured portrait in the art of Albania.

Priestesses and visitors gather around a bronze bowl to hear a prophecy in an ancient Greek temple. Waterhouse studied ancient art to get the details right. The women lean in with awe. It's an atmospheric picture of ancient belief.

paintings.t: Maison devant la Sainte-Victoire près de Gardanne (House in Provence)
paintings.why: A group of orange-roofed houses sits in front of the mountain in the south of France, in blocks of color. Cézanne painted the village of Gardanne, simplifying the buildings into cubes. Some people say this led to Cubism. It's a pioneering piece.

A pair of worn leather boots with muddy laces sits on the floor. Van Gogh painted several pictures of old boots, finding beauty in them. The philosopher Heidegger wrote about them. It's an ordinary thing that tells a story about a hard-working life.

paintings.t: Still Life with Profile of Laval
paintings.why: A pot, fruits and flowers on a table, and the profile of a young man's face seems to float in the background. Gauguin painted it as a tribute to his friend Charles Laval. The mix of a portrait and a still life is playful. It's a clever picture.

A band of musicians plays on a platform in front of a circus, under the glowing yellow gas lights. Seurat painted tiny dots of color to capture the glimmer of the evening. The figures look as stiff as statues. It's a magical, strange picture.
paintings.k: The musicians are playing on a stage. What instruments can you spot?

paintings.why: A woman in a black jacket and an orange-yellow hat sits at a table, with a thoughtful expression, against a mustard-yellow wall. Van Gogh painted Agostina Segatori in Paris in 1887, using strong complementary colors. The yellow and blue-black seem to hum. It's a vivid early portrait in his new colorful style.

A surgeon performs an operation in a medical amphitheater, as students lean in to watch. Eakins painted Dr. Hayes Agnew, who has just finished teaching his last class. The picture is clean and well-lit, in contrast with his earlier, darker Gross Clinic. It shows how medicine had changed.

paintings.t: The Vision to the Youth Bartholomew
paintings.why: A young boy named Bartholomew kneels, as a monk in black appears in the meadow, in a calm, golden evening. Nesterov painted the vision of the future St. Sergius of Radonezh. The landscape is shimmering. It's a quiet and holy picture.

paintings.t: A Meadow in the Mountains: Le Mas de Saint-Paul
paintings.why: A meadow of wildflowers stretches below craggy mountains, with big pine trees and a fresh blue sky. Van Gogh painted it near the asylum where he stayed. The brushwork is lively. It's a happy, free landscape.

A Breton woman in a traditional dress sits in front of a colorful, round background with a Japanese-style design. Gauguin painted the portrait of Marie-Angélique Satre. She didn't like it, though, and refused to take it. It's a fascinating mix of old and new.

A little boy, Cupid, whispers to a girl, in a meadow of wildflowers and soft light. Bouguereau painted many scenes like this. The smooth, delicate look was very popular. It's a sweet and charming picture.

Two girls in white dresses drift in a rowboat on a calm green river. Monet painted them near his home in Giverny, in the glow of the water. The reflections are rippling and beautiful. It's a beautiful scene of summer.

paintings.t: Portrait of the Artist with the Yellow Christ
paintings.why: Gauguin sits in front of two of his paintings, a yellow Christ and a strange ceramic pot, with a cool gaze. He painted himself among his own work. The bold flat colors and shapes were new. It's a confident self-portrait.

A young country girl with a stick stands barefoot with a flock of geese in a field. Bouguereau painted peasant girls in soft light. The smooth skin and bright colors are typical of his charm. It's a delightful and sweet picture.
l: Herbert F. Johnson Museum of Art

paintings.why: A young woman in a country dress sits by a stone wall, her work in her lap, looking up as if she's been interrupted. Bouguereau painted a calm and pretty scene. The lighting and polished skin are typical of him. It was a favorite of American collectors.

Sunlight falls on a floor and a woman sits by a window in a bright, blue-painted room in Skagen. Anna Ancher painted her own home. She was one of Denmark's best painters, known for her use of light. It's a calm and glowing picture.

The hero Perseus rides his winged horse Pegasus to rescue Andromeda from a sea dragon. Leighton painted a thrilling battle, with a swirl of wings and coils. It's a big and exciting myth. It's an action-packed Victorian painting.
paintings.k: Find the winged horse. What is it carrying?

paintings.why: A crowd of people in dark clothes, with pale, mask-like faces, walks toward us along a main street in Oslo, with a single man going the other way. Munch painted the feeling of being alone in a crowd. The strange lights make it eerie. It's an early step toward his famous anxiety paintings.

paintings.t: Summer Evening at Skagen. The Artist's Wife and Dog by the Shore
paintings.why: The artist's wife walks on the beach with her dog, under a pink and blue twilight. Krøyer painted the tender glow of a northern evening. The sea is a soft, glassy color. It's a peaceful scene.

A procession of women in colorful robes, with flowers, move along a marble street in an ancient festival, with the blue sea in the distance. Alma-Tadema loved to paint the warm Mediterranean world. The scene is rich in details. It's a bright vision of spring in the ancient world.

Sunlight on melting snow around a cottage, with a tree and a horse, in early spring. Levitan painted the first days of spring in Russia with a clear, bright eye. The blue shadows on the snow are lovely. It's a fresh landscape.

paintings.t: The Wyndham Sisters: Lady Elcho, Mrs. Adeane, and Mrs. Tennant
paintings.why: Three sisters in pale gowns pose in an elegant drawing room, sitting and leaning together as if they were in conversation. Sargent painted them in 1899, and critics said it looked like a spirited dance of satin and silk. The painting showed Sargent at his best. It's one of the most graceful group portraits.

A woman in a red robe looks into a crystal ball in a dim, magical room full of strange instruments. Waterhouse painted a fortune-teller. The glowing orb is the center of the picture. It's a picture of mystery.

A dark city of tall, gabled buildings sits under a stormy blue-black sky. August Strindberg, the famous Swedish playwright, also painted wild, moody landscapes. The thick paint and dramatic mood are unlike anything else of his time. It's a picture from a writer's imagination.

paintings.t: The Hungry Lion Throws Itself on the Antelope
paintings.why: A lion leaps onto an antelope amid giant, lush jungle plants with huge blossoms. Rousseau never saw a jungle but visited Paris zoos and botanical gardens for ideas. The brightly colored leaves and flat shapes give it a dreamy, storybook feel. It's one of his wildest jungle scenes.
paintings.k: This jungle was made up from plants in a garden. How many different leaf shapes can you find?

paintings.why: A woman in a saffron robe stands with four arms, holding a book, rice, cloth and a rosary, in an Indian landscape. Abanindranath Tagore, an Indian artist, painted her as 'Mother India' in 1905. It was a symbol for the independence movement. It's a landmark of Indian modern art.

paintings.t: Gather Ye Rosebuds While Ye May
paintings.why: Young women in soft, flowing dresses gather pink roses in a sunlit garden. The title is taken from a famous poem that tells us to enjoy life while we're young. Waterhouse painted the faces and the flowers with great skill. It's a gentle and lovely picture.

Two strong, bare-skinned figures prepare to cast a net, in a natural landscape. Suzanne Valadon was a painter who started out as an artist's model and became a famous painter herself. She painted people with strength and honesty. It's a lively, vigorous picture.
l: Museum of Fine Arts of Nancy

paintings.why: A simple black cross shape floats on a white background. Malevich made it as part of his Suprematist series, along with the Black Square. The shapes are like symbols. It's an art of pure shapes.

Mary holds the Christ Child while saints stand nearby in this fresco by Fra Angelico. He was a friar who painted gentle figures in clear, bright colors, and people later called him Beato, meaning blessed.

Angels, saints and blessed souls dance toward heaven on one side, while on the other side sinners are driven toward hell. Fra Angelico painted this scene of Judgment Day in the 1430s for a church in Florence.
Mary holds the baby Jesus on a throne with a beautiful carved marble frame around them. Filippo Lippi painted this in about 1437, with the tender faces that made him famous.
A baby lies on the ground, wonderfully lit, while a donor kneels in a cold winter scene with a long road running into the distance. Rogier van der Weyden painted this triptych in about 1440.
A gleaming fountain stands at the center, with a white lamb on top and a crowd of people gathered around it. This is a workshop copy of a Jan van Eyck painting, and the water means the gift of life.

Mary and the baby Jesus sit on a throne with angels while a group of city councillors from Barcelona kneel beside her. Lluís Dalmau painted it in 1445, and the councillors are painted like real people.

Mary sits under a pink and white arch with the baby Jesus while four saints stand nearby, all bathed in pale daylight. Domenico Veneziano painted it in about 1445, and it is known for its fresh, sunny colors.
A cardinal with a big nose and a strong jaw looks calmly at you. Andrea Mantegna painted it in about 1457, and he made the old man's skin look as real as stone.
Mary and the baby Jesus stand in front of a dry tree with a small fountain, and angels nearby. Petrus Christus painted it in about 1462, and the dead tree is a sign that Christ will bring new life.
Christ hangs on the cross between two other crosses under a calm blue sky, with Mary and John grieving. Antonello da Messina painted it in about 1475, with a view of the peaceful countryside.
l: Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp

paintings.why: A young man in a dark cap looks at you with a faint smile and bright eyes. Antonello da Messina painted it in about 1475, and the smile makes it feel as if he is about to speak.

Mary and the baby Jesus stand in a plain, bright room, and two angels hold up small, calm faces beside them. Piero della Francesca painted it in about 1476, and the light pours in from the window in the wall.

Saint Sebastian, pierced with arrows, is tied to a column in a town square, and the street behind him goes on and on. Antonello da Messina painted it in about 1478, and the perspective of the street is wonderfully exact.
Mary sits on a throne with the baby Jesus while saints stand to both sides of her. Ercole de' Roberti painted this altarpiece in 1479 for a church in Ravenna.

The shepherds hurry in to see the baby Jesus, and a curtain is pulled back to reveal the scene. Hugo van der Goes painted it in about 1480, and the shepherds' faces are painted with a great deal of feeling.
Moses, an old man, gives his last speech to the people on one side, and on the other he is buried on a mountain. Luca Signorelli painted this fresco in the Sistine Chapel in about 1482.

Two women sit on a balcony in Venice, looking bored, with a pigeon, a dog and a peacock. Vittore Carpaccio painted it in about 1490, and it is a rare glimpse into the daily life of Venetian women, though the painting has been cut down.

A man with long hair and a slight smile stands in front of a window that looks out on a calm landscape. Pietro Perugino painted Francesco delle Opere in 1494, and he was a Florentine craftsman who made fine jewelry.
Mary, John and Mary Magdalene mourn over Christ's body, set in a landscape with a calm sky. Pietro Perugino painted it in about 1495, and the quiet feeling is typical of him.
Mary sits holding the baby Jesus in a circle of angels and saints, in a huge altarpiece. Andrea Mantegna painted it in 1497, and the richly dressed saints surround them.

A monk draws shapes on a slate while a handsome young man stands beside him, and a glass shape hangs in the air. Jacopo de' Barbari painted it in 1497, and the monk, Luca Pacioli, was a famous mathematician who taught Leonardo da Vinci.

Christ crowns Mary in heaven, with dozens of saints and angels in glowing colors standing in rows beside them. Fra Angelico painted this altarpiece, and a row of small scenes below shows stories of Saint Dominic.

A saint sits in his study, with a rich room of books, a globe and musical instruments, as he stares up in wonder. Vittore Carpaccio painted it in about 1502, and the details of the room make it a fascinating glimpse of a scholar's life.
l: Scuola di San Giorgio degli Schiavoni

paintings.why: A young man with long hair and a hat looks softly out of the picture, with his hand on a ledge. Giorgione painted it in about 1503, and nobody knows who the young man was.

A woman with flowing hair held by a thin cord looks out to the side, wearing a fur-trimmed dress. Albrecht Dürer painted it in about 1505 on his second trip to Venice, and she may be a Venetian friend.
Venus and Mars lie asleep side by side in a meadow, while little cupids play with his armor. Piero di Cosimo painted it in about 1505, and Mars's helmet and lance are in the grass.

paintings.t: Portrait of a Young Man with a Lamp
paintings.why: A young man holds up a lamp as he looks out from the dark, with a twist in his shoulders. Lorenzo Lotto painted it in about 1508, and the light and shadow are painted in a daring way.
After the flood, Noah's family makes an offering to God, with a fire and animals. Michelangelo painted this scene on the Sistine Chapel ceiling in 1508 to 1509.
A man with long dark hair looks to the side, with a heavy, serious face. This is believed to be a self-portrait by Giorgione, about 1509.
People struggle in a rising flood, climbing onto a rock and boats while a big ark floats in the distance. Michelangelo painted this fresco on the Sistine Chapel ceiling in about 1509.

The hero Perseus fights a sea monster, rescuing the princess Andromeda who is chained to a rock. Piero di Cosimo painted it in about 1510, and the monster looks more like a funny dragon than a scary creature.
A knight in black armor stands in a leafy landscape with animals, his hand on his hip. Vittore Carpaccio painted it in about 1510, and he is surrounded by symbols like an ermine and a peacock.
God twists in the dark sky, in the first scene on Michelangelo's Sistine Chapel ceiling, as the light is separated from the dark. He painted it in 1512.
Mary and the baby Jesus sit in the center with saints and a curtain, in a quiet, light-filled scene. Correggio painted it in about 1514.
Mary holds the baby Jesus with cherubs gathered around, in a picture painted with strong colors. Rosso Fiorentino painted it in about 1517.
Men on ladders lower Christ's body, with sharp, twisting poses and bright colors. Rosso Fiorentino painted it in 1521, and the strange, jagged figures are typical of Mannerism.
l: Pinacoteca e Museo Civico di Volterra

paintings.why: Christ's face looks gently down in a small panel with deep shadows. Correggio painted it in about 1521, and the soft shading makes it glow.

paintings.t: Marsilio Cassotti and His Bride Faustina
paintings.why: A bride and groom sit side by side while a little Cupid puts a yoke of marriage over them. Lorenzo Lotto painted them in 1523, and the dog, the ring and the wreath are all wedding symbols.
Women weep over Christ's body in a quiet, soft-lit scene. Correggio painted it in 1524, and his gentle shading makes it feel full of feeling.
Mary sits on a throne in the clouds, with angels around her and saints at her feet. Correggio painted it in 1524, and the sweet, soft faces are typical of him.

Two huge armies clash on a river, with dozens of tiny soldiers, horses and cannons stretched over a big landscape. A painter close to Lucas Cranach made this in about 1525, and it shows a battle in 1514 where the Poles and Lithuanians beat the Russians.

paintings.t: Venus and Cupid with a Satyr
paintings.why: A woman sleeps in a landscape, while a satyr pulls back her cloth, and a baby Cupid and Venus look on. Correggio painted it in about 1526, and it is also called Antiope.

paintings.t: Mystic Marriage of Saint Catherine of Alexandria with Saint Sebastian
paintings.why: Mary and the baby Jesus sit with saints in a soft glow, while Jesus gives a ring to Catherine. Correggio painted it in 1526.
The princess Danaë sits in a fine marble room while a rain of gold falls onto her lap. Jan Gossaert painted it in 1527, and the story is the Greek myth of how the god Zeus visited her.

paintings.t: Portrait of a gentleman in his studio
paintings.why: A man sits at his desk, turning to look at the viewer, with a ring, a letter and a view of the room around him. Lorenzo Lotto painted it in about 1530, and the details of the table are meant to tell about his life.
A woman and a man play and sing music in an outdoor scene, with a rich, dreamy light. Dosso Dossi painted it in about 1530.
Dark, twisted figures wrestle in a gloomy scene, painted to show the evil of vices. Correggio painted it in about 1531 for a duchess's study.

A winged woman sits on a step, sharpening a stick, while children play with a hoop and a group of riders gallops through the sky. Lucas Cranach the Elder painted it in 1532, and the dark mood is called melancholy.
The little god Cupid carves a bow from a piece of wood, looking over his shoulder with a wicked smile, while two small children try to grab him. Parmigianino painted it in 1536.
A woman in a rich red dress looks out with a calm expression, as part of a pair of portraits. Lorenzo Lotto painted her in 1543, as the pair of her husband, Febo.

A young woman in a dark dress holds a medallion with a monogram and looks out with a clear, direct gaze. Sofonisba Anguissola painted it in 1554, and she was one of the first women to become a famous painter in Europe.
A small round painting shows a woman looking calmly out with a hint of a smile. Sofonisba Anguissola painted this tiny self-portrait in 1556, and it is only a few inches wide.

A tailor stands with big shears in his hand, looking up from a piece of cloth with a quiet, serious face. Giovanni Battista Moroni painted it in about 1567, and it is one of the first portraits of a working man in Italian art.
Mary and Joseph kneel before the baby Jesus in a rundown stable, while shepherds watch from a hillside. A painter in the style of Hieronymus Bosch made this in the 1500s.
The apostles look up in wonder at the empty tomb while Mary rises into the sky on a cloud of angels. Annibale Carracci painted it in about 1587.
An old man with a white beard and a gaunt face looks out of a dark background. Jacopo Tintoretto painted this self-portrait in about 1587, near the end of his life.
Mary, Joseph and shepherds gather around the glowing baby Jesus, while angels watch from above. Federico Barocci painted it in about 1597, and the soft pink and blue colors give it a sweet quiet.
Christ hangs on a cross between mourners in a calm, sharply drawn, cold-colored scene. Bramantino painted it in about 1500, in a style of smooth shapes and clear light.
Saint Peter, running away from Rome, meets Christ on the road, and falls back in surprise. Annibale Carracci painted it in about 1601, and the legend says Peter turned back to Rome after the meeting.
Ships toss in a stormy sea, with waves crashing on rocks and the dark sky ripped by lightning. A Flemish painter, thought to be Joos de Momper, painted it in about 1610.

paintings.t: Allegory of the Dutch victory over the Spanish fleet at Gibraltar, 25 April 1607
paintings.why: Dutch ships set fire to Spanish ones in a crowded sea battle, with fire, smoke and splashes. Adam Willaerts painted it in about 1615 to celebrate a Dutch victory at Gibraltar in 1607.

paintings.t: Still Life with Cheeses, Almonds and Pretzels
paintings.why: Big wheels of cheese, a pile of almonds and a pretzel sit on a table, and in the shiny pewter jug you can see a tiny reflection of the artist. Clara Peeters painted it in about 1615, and she was one of the few women painting in the Netherlands.
A young woman in a red robe leans on the spiked wheel, which was the tool used to torture her, and looks up to heaven. Artemisia Gentileschi painted it in about 1619.

paintings.t: Self-Portrait as Saint Catherine of Alexandria
paintings.why: A woman with dark hair rests her arm on the wheel with spikes, looking out at us. Artemisia Gentileschi painted herself as Saint Catherine in about 1616.
A fat, tipsy old man, a friend of the wine god Bacchus, is held up by satyrs while holding a cup, with grapes and a flushed face. Anthony van Dyck painted it in about 1620.
Susanna sits in a garden as two men spy on her and whisper to her. Artemisia Gentileschi painted it in 1622.
A man in a big hat and a ruffled coat strums a lute, laughing, with his mouth open. Frans Hals painted it in about 1624 in a bold, loose style.

The handsome Narcissus lies by a pool, in love with his own reflection, while the nymph Echo fades away behind him. Nicolas Poussin painted it in about 1629, and in the myth Narcissus is turned into a flower.
A man sits with a cup in his hand as two women look at him, in a story from the Bible. Artemisia Gentileschi painted it in about 1630.
The strong man Samson lies asleep as soldiers creep in to capture him, while Delilah looks on. Anthony van Dyck painted it in about 1630.
A man in a black coat and a gold chain points to a big sunflower, as if showing off his talent. Anthony van Dyck painted himself in about 1632, soon after he became court painter to Charles I.

paintings.t: Still Life with Lemons, Oranges and a Rose
paintings.why: A plate of lemons, a basket of oranges and a cup of water with a rose are lined up on a table against a black background. Francisco de Zurbarán painted it in 1633, and each object glows.
The god Apollo punishes a satyr, Marsyas, who dared to challenge him to a music contest, while others gather round. Jusepe de Ribera painted it in 1637, and the Greek myth is dark and gruesome.
l: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium

paintings.t: Lord John Stuart and His Brother, Lord Bernard Stuart
paintings.why: Two young brothers stand in elegant silver and gold clothes, one with a hand on his hip. Anthony van Dyck painted them in about 1638, and both were killed in the English Civil War.

paintings.t: Seaport with the Embarkation of Saint Ursula
paintings.why: A harbor with tall buildings is lit by a low, glowing sun, while Saint Ursula and her friends board ships. Claude Lorrain painted it in 1641, and the sun's light on the water is amazing.

paintings.t: The Embarkation of the Queen of Sheba
paintings.why: A queen goes down a grand flight of steps to board a ship in a sunny harbor with huge buildings. Claude Lorrain painted it in 1648, and the glow of the low sun lights the whole port.
