The furnaces of the ironworks at Coalbrookdale in England glow red against the night sky, in a picture of the place where the Industrial Revolution is said to have begun. Philip James de Loutherbourg painted it in 1801.
George Washington, the leader of the American army in the Revolution and first president, in a portrait by Gilbert Stuart painted in 1803. Stuart painted Washington from life and made many copies.

paintings.t: Cincinnatus Leaves the Plow to Dictate Laws to Rome
paintings.why: The Roman farmer Cincinnatus is called from his field in 458 BC and made dictator to save the city, then gives up power after only a few days and goes back to his farm. People later compared George Washington to him. Juan Antonio de Ribera painted it around 1806.

Alexander von Humboldt, the scientist who explored South America and described the planet as an interconnected whole, sits with his notebooks after a five-year journey. Friedrich Georg Weitsch painted him in 1806.

paintings.t: Caius Marius Amid the Ruins of Carthage
paintings.why: The exiled Roman general Marius sits alone among the ruins of Carthage, a symbol of how quickly fortune changes. John Vanderlyn painted it in Paris in 1807, and it won a gold medal from Napoleon.

paintings.t: Richard the Lionheart at the Battle of Acre
paintings.why: Richard the Lionheart of England fights in the siege of Acre during the Third Crusade, in 1191. Philip James de Loutherbourg painted this wild battle around 1807.

Napoleon on horseback directs his army at Austerlitz on December 2, 1805, where he won his greatest victory against the Russians and Austrians. François Gérard painted it in 1810 for Napoleon's palace.

paintings.t: A Reading of Voltaire's Tragedy at Madame Geoffrin's Salon
paintings.why: A crowd of writers and thinkers listens to a reading in the salon of Madame Geoffrin, one of the places where Enlightenment ideas were discussed, while a bust of Voltaire looks on. Anicet Charles Gabriel Lemonnier painted it in 1812 to show the famous salons of the 1750s.

Christoffer Wilhelm Eckersberg paints the wise old Socrates and the handsome young Alcibiades in the Athens of the 400s BC. The Danish painter made this in the 1810s, when artists were studying ancient Greece closely for new ideas.
Arthur Wellesley, the Duke of Wellington, the British general who defeated Napoleon at Waterloo, in a portrait by Thomas Lawrence of 1815 in his scarlet uniform.

paintings.t: Benjamin Franklin Drawing Electricity from the Sky
paintings.why: Benjamin Franklin raises a hand to catch lightning from the sky, while cherubs bring electricity into the room. Benjamin West painted it around 1816 to show Franklin's famous experiment of 1752, which proved lightning is electricity.
General George Washington on his horse watches his soldiers cross the icy Delaware River on Christmas night, 1776, before their surprise attack on Trenton. Thomas Sully painted this moment in 1819.

Three men hammer a glowing piece of iron in a dark smithy in one of Goya's late paintings, a celebration of strength and hard work. He painted it around 1819, when workshops and forges were being replaced by factories.

paintings.t: The Destruction of Pompeii and Herculaneum
paintings.why: John Martin's glowing sky and lightning show the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in AD 79 that buried Pompeii and Herculaneum. Painted in 1822, it turns the ancient disaster into a Romantic spectacle.

In the early 1800s the English antiquarian Charles Alfred Stothard made careful copies of the Bayeux Tapestry for the Society of Antiquaries. His engraved plates, like this one with the Norman fleet, made the tapestry famous in Britain.

The Marquis de Lafayette, a young French nobleman, joined Washington's army at the age of 19 and became a hero of the American Revolution. Ary Scheffer painted this portrait in 1823, when Lafayette toured the United States.

A saint kneels in a vision with a dog at his side as angels appear in the sky. Joseph Légaré was one of the first Canadian-born painters, from Quebec City. He copied European paintings and painted religious works for churches. It's an example of early Quebec art.
l: Musée national des beaux-arts du Québec

paintings.t: Forum Romanum, for Mr Soane's Museum
paintings.why: J. M. W. Turner paints the ruins of the Roman Forum in 1826, a place where emperors and senators once walked, now crumbling in a golden haze. It was made for the collector Sir John Soane.
On September 20, 1792, the French revolutionary army, mostly new volunteers, stopped the experienced Prussian army at Valmy and saved the Revolution. Horace Vernet painted the cannonade in 1826.

In October 1827 a British, French and Russian fleet destroyed the Ottoman and Egyptian ships at Navarino, a sea battle that turned the Greek War of Independence in favor of the Greeks. Ambroise Louis Garneray painted it soon afterward.

paintings.t: The Death of Queen Elizabeth I
paintings.why: The old queen sits on cushions on the floor of her room, refusing to go to bed, while her courtiers watch anxiously. Paul Delaroche painted this sad scene of Elizabeth I's last days in 1828.
At Poitiers in 1356 the English army led by the Black Prince defeated the French and captured their king, John II. Eugène Delacroix painted the confused clash in 1830.
Smoking chimneys and a factory stand beside a quiet canal in this early German picture of industry, painted by Carl Blechen in 1830. It is one of the first landscapes to show a factory as a subject.

Thomas Cole paints the half-ruined Colosseum glowing in the Roman sun in 1832, the great arena of the emperors now open to the sky. Cole, a founder of American landscape painting, saw it on his trip to Italy and later painted a series about the rise and fall of empires.

paintings.t: Godiva Preparing to Ride through Coventry
paintings.why: The legend says Lady Godiva of Coventry agreed to ride through the town to persuade her husband to cut the taxes, while the people promised to stay inside. George Jones painted her preparing to ride in 1833.

A man in formal dress sits for a portrait in a calm pose. Paul Kane was a portrait painter before he made his famous journey across Canada. This early work shows his training. It's part of the story of how Kane became an artist.

A woman in a bonnet and a plain dress sits for her portrait. Paul Kane painted portraits in Ontario before his great journey to the west. The carefully painted face shows his skill. It's an early Canadian portrait.
The English explorer Henry Hudson sails up what is now the Hudson River in 1609 and meets the Lenape people on the shore. Robert Walter Weir painted this meeting in 1835.

People who have been enslaved are held for sale at a market in Brazil, which received more enslaved Africans than any other country in the Americas. Johann Moritz Rugendas, a German artist who traveled there, made this picture in 1835.

paintings.t: Julie Papineau (née Bruneau) and her Daughter Ezilda
paintings.why: A mother and her young daughter pose in their best clothes. Antoine Plamondon was one of Quebec's most important early portrait painters, and he painted leaders and their families. Julie Papineau was the wife of a famous political leader, Louis-Joseph Papineau. It's an elegant picture of a family from French Canada.

In 455 AD the Vandal king Genseric captured Rome and looted it for two weeks, one of the blows that weakened the Western Empire. The Russian painter Karl Bryullov painted this chaos in 1836, soon after his famous Last Day of Pompeii.
Clovis, king of the Franks, vows to become a Christian if he wins at Tolbiac against the Alemanni, and then he does. Ary Scheffer painted this founding moment of France in 1836.

paintings.t: Henry VIII's First Interview with Anne Boleyn
paintings.why: King Henry VIII meets Anne Boleyn in a palace hall, the beginning of the romance that led him to break with the Catholic Church. Daniel Maclise painted this imagined meeting in 1836.

In 732 the Frankish leader Charles Martel stopped a Muslim army from advancing farther into France at the Battle of Tours and Poitiers, and his grandson was Charlemagne. Charles de Steuben painted this clash in 1837.

paintings.t: Charles I Insulted by Cromwell's Soldiers
paintings.why: King Charles I sits quietly while his Puritan guards mock him before his trial in 1649. Paul Delaroche painted the king's calm dignity in 1837, and it made viewers sympathize with him.

paintings.t: The Fountain of the Gate of the Old Seraglio, Constantinople
paintings.why: A domed fountain stands at the gate of the old palace of the Ottoman sultans in Constantinople, in a drawing by the English artist John Frederick Lewis, who traveled through the Ottoman capital in the 1830s and 1840s.
Peter the Great and his companions look over the swamp on the Neva River where he will found Saint Petersburg in 1703, a new capital that was meant to be Russia's window to Europe.

A Greek folk-style painting shows the Ottoman conquest of Constantinople in 1453 like a map, with soldiers and ships all around the city. Panagiotis Zographos made it in the 1830s as part of a series for a Greek general who had fought for independence.

A girl in a ruffled dress and cap sits calmly for her portrait. Antoine Plamondon, an early Canadian painter from Quebec, trained in Paris and returned to paint portraits of the middle class and religious figures. His faces are simple and honest. It's a portrait from early Canadian art.

paintings.t: Baldwin of Boulogne Entering Edessa in February 1098
paintings.why: Baldwin of Boulogne, a leader of the First Crusade, is welcomed into the city of Edessa in 1098, where he became its ruler and founded the first Crusader state. Joseph-Nicolas Robert-Fleury painted it in 1840.

Delegates from many countries pack a London hall at the World Anti-Slavery Convention of 1840, where women were not allowed to take part, an event that helped start the women's rights movement. Benjamin Robert Haydon painted the meeting in 1841.

Lucretia Mott, a Quaker minister and abolitionist, was one of the organizers of the Seneca Falls Convention in 1848, which launched the American women's rights movement. Joseph Kyle painted her portrait in 1842.

paintings.t: Attila and His Hordes Overrun Italy and the Arts
paintings.why: Attila the Hun, whose army terrified Rome in the 450s, rides over Italy, trampling art and learning under his horses' hooves. Eugène Delacroix painted this as part of a huge ceiling decoration in Paris in the 1840s.
The Pilgrims pray on the deck of the Speedwell in the Dutch port of Delfshaven in 1620 before sailing to America. Robert Walter Weir painted this in 1843 for the US Capitol.

paintings.t: A View of Murton Colliery near Seaham
paintings.why: A coal mine with its winding towers stands in the flat landscape of County Durham in northern England. James Wilson Carmichael painted it in 1843, when coal fed the engines of the new industrial age.

paintings.t: The Last Words of Marcus Aurelius
paintings.why: The Roman emperor and philosopher Marcus Aurelius, dying, presents his young son Commodus to his friends and asks them to guide him, though Commodus turned out to be a bad emperor. Eugène Delacroix painted this sad scene in 1844.

King Louis IX of France, called Saint Louis, rides on a rearing horse. He led two crusades, was captured on the first, and died on the second in 1270. Émile Signol painted him in 1844 for the French royal museum at Versailles.
In November 1812, Napoleon's army fights to cross the freezing Berezina River in Russia as it retreats. Peter von Hess painted the desperate crossing in 1844.

A quiet landscape with a monument that honors General Wolfe, who died at the Battle of the Plains of Abraham in 1759. Joseph Légaré painted this in Quebec City, near the site. It is a calm picture with a big history behind it. It's an early Canadian landscape.
l: Musée national des beaux-arts du Québec

paintings.t: L'Incendie du quartier Saint-Jean à Québec, vu vers l'ouest
paintings.why: A huge fire lights up the night sky over Quebec City, with people rushing through the street. Joseph Légaré witnessed the great fire of 1845 in Saint-Jean neighborhood and painted it with powerful color. It's one of Canada's earliest paintings of a disaster. It's a vivid record of the event.
l: Musée national des beaux-arts du Québec

paintings.t: The Eve of the Battle of Edge Hill, 1642
paintings.why: Cavaliers and soldiers share a quiet meal and some rest before the first big battle of the English Civil War in 1642. Charles Landseer painted this calm before the storm in 1845.
American and British cavalry fight in a sword duel at the Battle of Cowpens in South Carolina in 1781, one of the clearest American victories of the Revolution. William Ranney painted it in 1845.

paintings.t: The Louth–London Royal Mail Travelling by Train
paintings.why: A Royal Mail coach is loaded onto a railway truck so that it can travel by train, a sign that railways were replacing horses. James Pollard painted this scene of the new age in 1845.

A dignified man in dark formal clothes sits for his portrait. René-Édouard Caron was a mayor of Quebec City and later a lieutenant-governor. Théophile Hamel was one of Quebec's most important portrait painters, trained in Europe in the 1840s. It's a typical example of the serious portraits that recorded the leaders of early Canada.
l: Musée national des beaux-arts du Québec

paintings.why: A portrait of an Indigenous woman in traditional dress. Cornelius Krieghoff, a Dutch-born painter who lived in Quebec, painted many scenes of First Nations people. His pictures are an important record of life in the 1800s, though they show how a settler artist saw Indigenous people. It's a picture to study with care.

A cozy room with an officer's belongings, bed and gear, in the glow of lamplight. Cornelius Krieghoff painted this in his early years in Montreal, when many British officers lived there. It gives a close look at daily life in Canada in the 1840s. It's a charming interior.

An Indigenous hunter stands in a forest with his rifle, in a quiet pose. Cornelius Krieghoff painted First Nations people he met near Montreal and Quebec. The scene shows him in the setting of his daily life. It's part of a body of work that is important for Canadian history.

paintings.t: Pizarro Seizing the Inca of Peru
paintings.why: In 1532 the Spanish conquistador Francisco Pizarro captured the Inca emperor Atahualpa, beginning the Spanish conquest of the Inca empire. John Everett Millais painted this violent scene in 1846, when he was only 17.

Catherine of Aragon kneels before her husband Henry VIII at a church court in 1529, begging him not to end their marriage. Henry's 'Great Matter' was getting this annulled, which led England to leave the Catholic Church. Emanuel Leutze painted it in 1846.

A priest in a black robe and white collar looks out with a calm, thoughtful face. Théophile Hamel painted many portraits of religious and political leaders in Quebec. His portraits are known for their lifelike faces and clear lines. It's a good example of Canadian portraiture in the 1840s.
l: Musée national des beaux-arts du Québec

paintings.why: An Indigenous mother holds her baby in a cradleboard. Paul Kane painted this on the Pacific coast, recording how the baby's head was shaped as part of a custom. His paintings are valuable records of the customs of many peoples. It's a gentle family portrait.

paintings.t: The Siege (Defense of a Church Courtyard during the Thirty Years' War)
paintings.why: Defenders hold out in a churchyard during the Thirty Years' War, with a stormy sky overhead. Carl Friedrich Lessing painted this dramatic scene in 1848.

Frederick the Great of Prussia is badly defeated by the Russians and Austrians at the Battle of Kunersdorf on August 1, 1759, in the Seven Years' War, which was fought in Europe, India and North America. Alexander von Kotzebue painted it in 1848.

paintings.t: Barricade in the Rue Soufflot, June 1848
paintings.why: Revolutionaries fight behind a barricade in a Paris street during the June Days of 1848, in one of the revolutions that swept through Europe that year. Horace Vernet painted the fight in 1848.

paintings.t: During the March Unrest in Stockholm, 1848
paintings.why: Crowds and soldiers clash in the streets of Stockholm during the March Unrest of 1848, a Swedish echo of the revolutions across Europe. Fritz von Dardel sketched what he saw that year.

paintings.t: No Sheet of Paper Shall Come between Me and My People
paintings.why: A cartoon from 1848 mocks the Prussian King Frederick William IV, who said he would not allow a written constitution to come between him and his people. It is one of the satirical prints of the revolutions of 1848 in Germany.
Hungarian cavalry fight Austrian troops at Komárom in 1849, during the Hungarian Revolution against the Habsburg Empire. The Hungarian painter Mór Than painted the battle that same year.
Goffredo Mameli, the young poet who wrote the words of Italy's national anthem, died at the age of 21 defending the Roman Republic in 1849. Domenico Induno painted his portrait.

paintings.t: The Abolition of Slavery in the French Colonies, 27 April 1848
paintings.why: Crowds cheer in the French colonies as slavery is abolished on April 27, 1848, with a flag raised and people embracing. François-Auguste Biard painted the celebration in 1849.
Daniel Boone and his friends look out over the green land of Kentucky for the first time in 1769, in a painting that made the frontier look wide open. William Ranney painted it in 1849.
A young Dutch couple meets in the days when New York was still the Dutch town of New Amsterdam. Francis William Edmonds painted this gentle scene of colonial life in 1850.

Assiniboine hunters on horseback race across the plains, chasing a herd of buffalo. Paul Kane painted this on his trip across the prairies in the 1840s. The galloping horses and flying dust are full of excitement. It's one of the most famous Canadian paintings of the plains.

paintings.t: Cromwell at the Battle of Naseby, 1645
paintings.why: Oliver Cromwell leads the cavalry charge at Naseby in 1645, the battle where Parliament's New Model Army won the English Civil War. Charles Landseer painted it in 1851.
Napoleon walks through the snow with his frozen, starving army in the winter of 1812, after taking Moscow but being unable to win the war. Adolph Northen painted the great army's retreat in 1851.

paintings.t: The Opening of the Great Exhibition by Queen Victoria
paintings.why: Queen Victoria and Prince Albert open the Great Exhibition in the Crystal Palace in 1851, with thousands of guests looking on. Henry Courtney Selous painted this scene of a world fair celebrating industry.

paintings.t: The Inauguration of the Great Exhibition: 1 May 1851
paintings.why: Queen Victoria opens the Great Exhibition in the giant glass Crystal Palace in London on May 1, 1851, a world fair full of machines and inventions. David Roberts painted the opening in 1852.

paintings.t: Daniel Boone Escorting Settlers through the Cumberland Gap
paintings.why: The frontiersman Daniel Boone leads a group of pioneers through the Cumberland Gap into Kentucky, with a woman riding a white horse. George Caleb Bingham painted this hopeful image of westward settling in 1852.

paintings.t: Chinook Indians in Front of Mount Hood
paintings.why: Chinook people stand in front of a huge snowy volcano, Mount Hood, on the Columbia River. Paul Kane painted this on his journey to the Pacific Northwest. The mountain towers over the scene. It's a grand landscape of a faraway place.

A hiding Royalist soldier in a hollow tree is brought food and secret messages by the girl he loves, who is on the other side of the war. John Everett Millais painted this romantic scene from the English Civil War in 1853.

On December 14, 1825, Russian officers led their soldiers into Senate Square in Saint Petersburg to demand reforms after the death of the tsar, but the revolt was crushed. Vasily Timm painted the scene in 1853.

The Russian navy sets the Ottoman fleet ablaze at Sinop in November 1853, a night battle that helped bring about the Crimean War. Ivan Aivazovsky, Russia's famous painter of the sea, painted it with glowing flames.
Harriet Beecher Stowe, whose novel Uncle Tom's Cabin of 1852 sold millions of copies and made many Northerners see the cruelty of slavery, in a portrait painted in 1853 by Alanson Fisher.

paintings.t: The Arrest of Louis XVI and His Family at Varennes
paintings.why: In June 1791 the royal family, trying to escape France in disguise, was recognized and stopped by villagers in the town of Varennes. Thomas Falcon Marshall painted the moment of the arrest in 1854.

Jean-Léon Gérôme shows peoples from across the Roman Empire bowing before Augustus in Rome, at the moment of peace in which, according to Christian tradition, Jesus was born. He painted it in 1855 and it shows how huge the empire had become.
Pocahontas, the daughter of the Powhatan chief, marries the English settler John Rolfe in 1614, a wedding that brought a few years of peace to Virginia. Henry Brueckner painted it in 1855.
Count Camillo Benso di Cavour, the prime minister of Piedmont, was the clever politician who helped unite Italy in the 1860s. Michele Gordigiani painted his portrait in the 1850s.
French and British soldiers climb the hills above the Alma River on September 20, 1854, the first big battle of the Crimean War. Hippolyte Bellangé painted the assault in 1855.

paintings.t: The Battle of the Alma, 20 September 1854
paintings.why: Eugène Lami paints the Battle of the Alma in 1855 with a wide, pale view of the hills where the French and British armies attacked Russian positions.

paintings.t: Charge of the Light Cavalry Brigade, 25th Oct. 1854
paintings.why: On October 25, 1854, British light cavalry rode straight down a valley into Russian cannons in the Charge of the Light Brigade, immortalized in Tennyson's poem. William Simpson, a war artist, drew this view the next year.

A wide view of the cavalry battle at Balaklava in October 1854, drawn by William Simpson, who traveled with the army to the Crimea as a war artist. His images were printed to show the war to people at home.
Columbus sits alone beside the sea, lost in dreams of the voyage west that will change the world. José María Obregón, one of Mexico's leading painters, painted it in 1856.

paintings.t: Fighting in the Gorge of the Malakoff, 8 September 1855
paintings.why: French troops fight hand-to-hand in the trenches of the Malakoff fortress in September 1855 in the final attack on Sevastopol. Adolphe Yvon painted this huge battle scene in 1856.
The Russian painter Grigory Shukaev shows the defense of Sevastopol during the long siege of 1854 and 1855, one of the longest sieges of the Crimean War.

Two small children dig and plant in a garden, with their gardening tools. Antoine Plamondon, a Quebec painter, made this charming scene of childhood. It's one of his less formal pictures. It shows how Canadian painters also painted scenes of everyday life.
l: Musée national des beaux-arts du Québec

paintings.t: The Landing of Roger Williams in 1636
paintings.why: After being banished from the Massachusetts colony for his beliefs, Roger Williams is welcomed by Narragansett people in 1636 and founds Providence, Rhode Island, as a place of religious freedom. Alonzo Chappel painted it in 1857.

A forest is ablaze with red, orange and gold leaves beside a calm stream. Cornelius Krieghoff painted the glorious color of Canadian autumn, which became a favorite subject. The warm colors make the picture glow. It's a good example of his love of the Canadian landscape.

paintings.t: Christopher Columbus at the Gates of the Monastery of Santa María de la Rábida
paintings.why: Christopher Columbus, poor and worn out, stops with his young son at a monastery in Spain, where a friendly prior helps him get a hearing at the court of Queen Isabella. Benet Mercadé painted this story in 1858.

A portrait of Pocahontas, the young Powhatan woman who became known to the English settlers at Jamestown and later traveled to England, where she died in 1617. This engraving was made in 1858 from an older portrait.
French soldiers plant the tricolor flag on the Malakoff tower on September 8, 1855, the attack that finally brought down Sevastopol. Horace Vernet painted the victory in 1858.

Tipis stand by a trading fort in Wyoming, where trappers and Native American traders met and where the Oregon Trail passed. Alfred Jacob Miller, who first visited the Rockies in 1837, painted this view around the 1850s.

Gladiators salute the emperor with the words 'we who are about to die salute you' before a fight in the Roman arena. Jean-Léon Gérôme painted this in 1859 and helped create how everyone imagines the Colosseum.

paintings.t: The Fall of King Olav at the Battle of Stiklestad
paintings.why: King Olav II falls at the Battle of Stiklestad in 1030. He was later made Saint Olaf, the patron saint of Norway. Peter Nicolai Arbo painted it in the 1850s.
The Battle of Solferino in 1859 was so bloody that a Swiss businessman who witnessed it, Henry Dunant, started the Red Cross. Carlo Bossoli painted it the same year.

A sleigh speeds away from a tollgate as the toll keeper shouts after it, in a snowy scene full of fun. Cornelius Krieghoff's lively scenes of French-Canadian country life made him one of Canada's most popular painters. It's a funny story told in a picture. It shows his eye for humor.
Olav Tryggvason sails back to Norway in 995 to take the throne, and the sagas say he then pushed his people to become Christian. Peter Nicolai Arbo made this black-and-white scene in 1860.
A British trading fort stands on the shore of Lake Ontario at Oswego, New York, which the French captured in 1756 early in the Seven Years' War. This view is a 19th-century picture of the fort.

Charlotte Corday, a young woman from Caen, stabbed the revolutionary journalist Jean-Paul Marat in his bath in July 1793 because she believed he was leading France into terror. Paul Baudry painted her in 1860, after the deed.

paintings.t: An Episode from the Five Days of Milan
paintings.why: A fighter holds a barricade in Milan during the Five Days of March 1848, when the people rose up and drove the Austrian army out of the city for a time. Baldassare Verazzi painted the rebellion in 1860.
Garibaldi's volunteers, the Thousand, storm a hill at Calatafimi in Sicily in May 1860 and beat a larger Neapolitan army, a key victory on the way to uniting Italy. Remigio Legat painted it in 1860.
After a long siege, the Ottoman fortress of Kars surrendered to the Russians in November 1855 after its defenders ran out of food. Thomas Jones Barker painted the surrender around 1860.
Alexey Bogolyubov paints the burning ships of the Battle of Sinop in 1860, a few years after the Russian navy destroyed the Ottoman fleet there in 1853.

Mathew Brady took this photograph of Abraham Lincoln in New York on the day he made his famous Cooper Union speech in February 1860. Lincoln later said that the speech and the photo helped him become president.

Anishinaabe (Chippewa) hunters track caribou through the woods and along a stream. Cornelius Krieghoff painted this to show life he'd seen in the northern wilderness. The trees and small figures show how large the land was. It's an important image of Indigenous hunting.

paintings.t: The Reception of Lord Byron at Missolonghi
paintings.why: The famous English poet Lord Byron is welcomed at Missolonghi in Greece in January 1824, when he came to help the Greek war for independence. He died there of fever a few months later. Theodoros Vryzakis painted the welcome in 1861.
French and Italian troops defeat the Austrian army at Magenta in 1859, one of the first big victories in the war that began Italy's unification. Adolphe Yvon painted it in 1861.

paintings.t: The Opening of the First Parliament of the Kingdom of Italy
paintings.why: Italy's first national parliament is opened in 1861 under a canopy of flags and cheering crowds, when the Kingdom of Italy was officially born. Carlo Bossoli painted the festive scene.

paintings.t: Bombardment of Fort Sumter, Charleston Harbor
paintings.why: Cannon fire lights up Fort Sumter in Charleston Harbor on April 12, 1861, the first shots of the American Civil War. This lithograph was published by Currier and Ives soon after.
In 1709 Peter the Great's army defeated the Swedes under Charles XII at Poltava, a victory that made Russia a great power. Alexander von Kotzebue painted the battle in 1862.

paintings.t: The Injured Garibaldi in the Aspromonte Mountains
paintings.why: The Italian hero Giuseppe Garibaldi is wounded in 1862 at Aspromonte while trying to march on Rome, and his red-shirted followers gather around him. Gerolamo Induno painted the scene.

paintings.t: A Ride for Liberty: The Fugitive Slaves
paintings.why: A family of enslaved people flee on horseback in the early light of the Civil War. Eastman Johnson painted it in 1862 after seeing such an escape, and it is one of the first great American paintings to show the bravery of people escaping slavery.

paintings.t: Emancipation: The Past and the Future
paintings.why: A circular scene in the center shows a Black family at home in freedom, surrounded by scenes of slavery on one side and a hopeful future on the other. Thomas Nast made this print in 1863, after the Emancipation Proclamation.
Timothy O'Sullivan photographed the battlefield at Gettysburg in July 1863, showing the true cost of the war. It is one of the most powerful early war photographs.

paintings.t: The First Reading of the Emancipation Proclamation by President Lincoln
paintings.why: President Lincoln reads the first draft of the Emancipation Proclamation to his cabinet in July 1862. Francis Bicknell Carpenter painted this meeting in 1864, and it hung in the US Capitol.

Two young Indigenous girls from Wendake (then called Lorette), a Huron-Wendat village near Quebec City, pose in their dresses. Théophile Hamel painted them with great sympathy and care. Many Quebec artists visited Wendake to paint portraits. It's a gentle record of the people who lived there.
l: Musée national des beaux-arts du Québec

paintings.why: A small round painting shows a quiet river framed by trees in glowing autumn colors. Cornelius Krieghoff painted the glorious color of the Canadian fall, which became a favorite subject. The round shape makes it feel like looking through a window. It's a peaceful picture of autumn.

On the Ides of March in 44 BC, Roman senators, including Caesar's friend Brutus, stabbed Julius Caesar in the Senate. Karl von Piloty painted the moment just after in 1865 with Caesar lying beneath his statue.

A bright moon shines over a rocky coast and calm sea, painting a silver path on the water. Cornelius Krieghoff painted many moonlit scenes that were popular with buyers. The mood is dreamy. It's a quiet night view.

A busy market square beside the harbor of Montreal is filled with shoppers, carts and sailing ships. William Raphael, born in Prussia, settled in Montreal and painted its streets and markets. His pictures record what the city looked like in the 1860s. It's a historic snapshot of Montreal.
Hannibal's elephants and soldiers struggle over a steep snowy pass in the Alps in 218 BC on their way to attack Rome. Heinrich Leutemann made this dramatic picture in 1866.
In the legend of the siege of Magdeburg in 1631, young women of the city are in desperate danger as the city falls. Eduard Steinbrück painted this sad scene of the Thirty Years' War in 1866.

People gather around a campfire in the woods at night, with the flames lighting the trees. Cornelius Krieghoff painted the glow of firelight with great skill. The picture feels warm and cozy against the dark forest. It's a favorite style of his.

paintings.t: Mary, Queen of Scots: The Farewell to France
paintings.why: Eighteen-year-old Mary, Queen of Scots, stands on a ship leaving the shores of France in 1561, where she grew up, to return to Scotland. Robert Herdman painted this farewell in 1867.
Pilgrims walk through the snow to church, with muskets over their shoulders in case of danger. George Henry Boughton painted the scene in 1867 as an image of the settlers' faith and courage.

People and boats gather on a harbor wharf at dusk, with the glow of sunset. Henry Sandham, a Canadian painter from Montreal, was a master of landscapes and harbor scenes. He later moved to Boston and London. It's a quiet seaside moment.

Wilhelm von Kaulbach shows the sea battle of 480 BC in which the Greek ships crushed the Persian fleet of King Xerxes in the narrow waters near Athens. It is a giant painting full of tangled ships, flying spears and a sky glowing over the water, made to celebrate the victory that kept Greece free.

paintings.t: Phidias Showing the Frieze of the Parthenon to His Friends
paintings.why: The sculptor Phidias shows Pericles and a circle of Athenian friends the carved marble frieze made for the Parthenon, the great temple on the Acropolis. Lawrence Alma-Tadema, famous for his research, painted this Athens of the 400 BC golden age in 1868, long before the real frieze was properly understood.

paintings.t: Olav Tryggvason and Sigrid the Haughty
paintings.why: According to a saga, King Olav Tryggvason asks the proud Swedish queen Sigrid to marry him and become Christian, she refuses, and he strikes her with his glove. Mårten Eskil Winge painted this tense meeting in 1868.
General William Tecumseh Sherman's Union army marches across Georgia in 1864, destroying railroads and supplies to break the Confederacy. This engraving was made by Felix Darley in 1868.

paintings.t: Pheidippides Announcing the Victory at Marathon
paintings.why: According to legend, a runner named Pheidippides raced from the battlefield of Marathon to Athens to announce that the Greeks had beaten the Persians, then collapsed and died. Luc-Olivier Merson painted the moment he reaches the city in 1869, and the legend is why a long-distance race is called a marathon.
Prussian infantry advance across the fields at Königgrätz in 1866, the battle where Prussia defeated Austria and took the lead in uniting Germany. Georg Bleibtreu painted it in 1869.
President Abraham Lincoln, who led the Union during the Civil War and issued the Emancipation Proclamation, sits deep in thought in this 1869 portrait by George P. A. Healy.

Wagons wind through a glowing landscape under a red sky on the Oregon Trail, the long route that tens of thousands of settlers took west. Albert Bierstadt, famous for his big Western landscapes, painted it in 1869.

Two huge buffalo lock horns in a fierce battle on the open prairie. Frederick Arthur Verner was a Canadian painter who traveled across the Canadian west and painted the buffalo and the plains. He is known for sunset scenes of the buffalo, which he painted often. The picture captures the wild strength of the animals before their herds disappeared.

A shady forest path in dim light, painted with tall trees and soft moss. Aaron Allan Edson was a Canadian landscape painter from Quebec who loved the woods and mountains. His paintings celebrate the wilderness of eastern Canada and New England. It's a calm view of the forest.

Attila the Hun feasts with his warriors and advisors in a great hall. The Hungarian painter Mór Than painted this in 1870, when many Hungarians looked at Attila as a figure from their own early history.

In 1066 King Harald Hardrada of Norway, the last great Viking king, is killed in a battle against the English at Stamford Bridge. Peter Nicolai Arbo painted this clash in 1870, only days before the Norman invasion.

paintings.t: Harald Fairhair in the Battle of Hafrsfjord
paintings.why: Harald Fairhair wins the sea battle of Hafrsfjord around the year 872, a victory the sagas say united Norway under one king. The Norwegian-American painter Ole Peter Hansen Balling painted it in 1870.

paintings.t: Party for New Year's Day in New Amsterdam, 1636
paintings.why: Dutch settlers in the colony of New Amsterdam on Manhattan, the future New York, celebrate New Year's Day in the snow. George Henry Boughton painted this cozy imagined scene in 1870.

A train crosses a bridge over the Seine at Argenteuil, a village near Paris where the railway brought city people for weekends. Claude Monet painted the modern age into the peaceful countryside in 1870.

paintings.t: The Battle of Gettysburg: Pickett's Charge
paintings.why: Confederate soldiers cross a wide field in Pickett's Charge, the last big attack at Gettysburg on July 3, 1863, which failed. Peter Frederick Rothermel painted this huge picture in 1870.

paintings.t: Chinese Railroad Workers in the Sierra Nevada
paintings.why: Thousands of Chinese workers built the Central Pacific Railroad through the Sierra Nevada, digging tunnels and clearing rock by hand, in very dangerous conditions. This print from the 1870s shows the railroad climbing through the mountains.

Paris, personified as a woman holding a flag, rises among dead soldiers during the German siege of the French capital in the winter of 1870 and 1871. Ernest Meissonier, who served in the siege, painted it in 1870.

After the emperor Caligula was killed in AD 41, soldiers found his uncle Claudius hiding behind a curtain and made him emperor. Lawrence Alma-Tadema, who loved Roman history, painted the moment in 1871.
A steam train rolls into a little suburban station in south London while the painter Camille Pissarro, who was staying in England to escape the Franco-Prussian War, looked on. He painted it in 1871.
Louise Michel, a teacher who fought for the Paris Commune, is arrested by soldiers in 1871 and later sent to a prison colony in the Pacific. Jules Girardet painted her capture in 1871.

paintings.t: Execution of Communards at the Lobau Barracks
paintings.why: Soldiers shoot captured members of the Paris Commune at the Lobau Barracks in May 1871, during the 'Bloody Week' that ended the Commune. Frédéric Théodore Lix drew it in 1871 for a French newspaper.

According to tradition, on October 31, 1517, Martin Luther nailed his 95 Theses, complaints against the Church's sale of pardons, to the church door in Wittenberg, which launched the Reformation. Historians debate how it happened, but this scene from 1872 is the famous image.
A young woman in white sits among ruins, holding a green branch, as a symbol of hope after France's defeat in the war of 1870 and 1871. Pierre Puvis de Chavannes painted it in 1872.

paintings.t: A Scene in the White Mountains
paintings.why: Mountains rise above a quiet valley, with the soft light of dawn or dusk. Aaron Allan Edson painted landscapes in Quebec and the White Mountains of New Hampshire. He was part of a generation of Canadian painters who showed the beauty of the land. It's a peaceful wilderness view.

paintings.t: Ojibwa Camp, Northern Shore of Lake Huron
paintings.why: An Ojibwe camp sits on the shore of Lake Huron, with tents and canoes under a wide sky. Frederick Arthur Verner painted Indigenous people and the northern landscape. The scene records a way of life by the Great Lakes. It's an important image of 19th-century Canada.

paintings.t: The Charge of the 9th Cuirassiers at Morsbronn
paintings.why: French armored cavalry charge through the narrow streets of the village of Morsbronn on August 6, 1870, in a brave but hopeless attack against Prussian infantry. Édouard Detaille painted this charge in 1873.

paintings.t: The Burning of the Hôtel de Ville, 24 May 1871
paintings.why: The great Paris city hall, the Hôtel de Ville, burns on May 24, 1871, during the last week of the Paris Commune, the radical government of Paris. Léon Sabatier painted the fires in 1873.

Guests recline at a dinner party in ancient Athens, taking turns to give speeches about love, in a scene from Plato's dialogue The Symposium. Anselm Feuerbach, who loved ancient Greece, made two versions of it and painted this second one in the early 1870s.

paintings.t: Charge of the French Cuirassiers at Waterloo
paintings.why: Armored French cavalry charge up the slope at the Battle of Waterloo on June 18, 1815, the battle where Napoleon was finally defeated. Henri Félix Emmanuel Philippoteaux painted this charge in 1874.
Eugène Thirion shows Joan of Arc, in a simple red dress, listening to the angels and saints whose voices, she said, told her to save France. He painted it in 1876.

paintings.t: A Visit from the Old Mistress
paintings.why: A white woman visits former slaves on a plantation in Virginia after the Civil War, and the women's faces show different feelings. Winslow Homer painted this quiet scene about freedom and its limits in 1876.

In 1212 thousands of European children, many in poor families, set off on a march to the Holy Land, and most never got there. Gustave Doré drew this scene for a famous illustrated history of the Crusades in 1877.

paintings.t: Bohemond Alone Mounts the Rampart of Antioch
paintings.why: The Norman leader Bohemond climbs the walls of Antioch in 1098 in one of the crusaders' most daring moments. Gustave Doré drew it in dark, dramatic black and white.
The aged and blind Doge of Venice, Enrico Dandolo, speaks in front of the cathedral to stir up the Fourth Crusade. Gustave Doré illustrated it in 1877.

paintings.t: Luther at the Diet of Worms
paintings.why: In 1521 Martin Luther stands in front of the Emperor Charles V in Worms and refuses to take back his writings, saying 'Here I stand.' Anton von Werner painted this scene in 1877 as a founding moment of the Reformation.
The Pilgrims row ashore at Plymouth in December 1620, in a famous painting by Henry Bacon of 1877. The idea of the Pilgrims stepping onto Plymouth Rock is a later tradition.
In 1714 Peter the Great's new navy won its first big victory over the Swedish fleet at Gangut in the Baltic Sea. Alexey Bogolyubov painted the battle in 1877.

paintings.t: Arrival of the Normandy Train, Gare Saint-Lazare
paintings.why: Steam from a train fills the glass-roofed Gare Saint-Lazare in Paris in this painting by Claude Monet. He painted a series of the station in 1877 and fell in love with how smoke and light swirled around the engines of the new age.
Monet turns a busy train station into a cloud of blue and gray steam and sunlight. He painted this view of the Gare Saint-Lazare in 1877 and saw the railway as a modern wonder.

Tired, silent Grenadier Guards trudge back after the Battle of Inkerman in 1854. Elizabeth Thompson, later Lady Butler, painted this sad picture of the cost of war in 1877, when she was becoming one of Britain's best-known battle painters.

paintings.t: The Remorse of the Emperor Nero after the Murder of his Mother
paintings.why: The emperor Nero, who has just had his own mother Agrippina killed, lies on a couch filled with guilt while his attendants look away. John William Waterhouse painted this dark moment in 1878.

paintings.t: And When Did You Last See Your Father?
paintings.why: A small boy, the son of a Royalist, is questioned by Parliament's officers about where his father is hiding. William Frederick Yeames painted this tense scene from the English Civil War in 1878, and it became one of the most famous pictures in Victorian Britain.

paintings.t: Bismarck and Napoleon III after Sedan
paintings.why: The captured French emperor Napoleon III sits with the Prussian chancellor Otto von Bismarck after the Battle of Sedan in September 1870, the defeat that ended the French Empire. Wilhelm Camphausen painted it in 1878.

paintings.t: A Coming Storm in the Adirondacks
paintings.why: Dark storm clouds roll over a mountain valley, with trees swaying in the wind. Homer Watson was a self-taught painter from Ontario, whom Oscar Wilde admired. He painted dramatic skies and landscapes. The painting shows nature's power.

A sailing ship glows in dim, hazy light near the harbor of Saint John, New Brunswick. Henry Sandham painted Atlantic Canada's ports and coasts in a clear, careful way. The soft light on the water gives the scene a quiet mood. It's a calm harbor view.
The Visigoth king Alaric enters Athens in 396 AD, and the city's people stand before him in fear. Ludwig Thiersch painted this scene of the later fall of the classical world in 1879.

The poet Dante, in exile from Florence, passes some women in Verona while they whisper that he has been to hell, a joke on his great poem the Inferno. Antonio Cotti painted this famous scene in 1879, long after the Renaissance he helped start.

Hernán Cortés, the Spanish conqueror who led the fall of the Aztec empire in 1519 to 1521, in a 19th-century portrait by the Mexican painter José Salomé Pina. His conquest is still a deeply debated chapter of Mexican history.

paintings.t: Grand Duchess Sofia at the Novodevichy Convent
paintings.why: Peter the Great's half-sister Sofia, who ruled Russia in his place before he took over, was locked in a convent in 1689. Ilya Repin painted her in 1879 looking angry and trapped.

French troops attack in the snow at Champigny in December 1870, trying to break out of besieged Paris. Édouard Detaille painted this battle in 1879, as part of a wave of paintings in France remembering the war of 1870.

paintings.t: Muslim Troops Leaving Narbonne to Pepin the Short, 759
paintings.why: Pepin the Short, Charlemagne's father, finally takes the city of Narbonne in 759, driving out the Muslim garrison. This black-and-white illustration by Émile Bayard was made in 1880 for a history of France.

The famous Viking hero Ragnar Lodbrok sits beside his clever wife Kráka in this scene from the Norse sagas. The Swedish painter August Malmström made it around 1880, when Scandinavians were falling in love with their Viking past.

paintings.t: The Last Voyage of Henry Hudson
paintings.why: Henry Hudson, his son and a few others sit in a small boat in the icy northern sea after the crew turned against him in 1611 and cast them adrift. They were never seen again. John Collier painted it in 1881.

The 93rd Highlanders stand in a thin line against the Russian cavalry at Balaclava on October 25, 1854, refusing to retreat, and a newspaper called it the 'thin red line'. Robert Gibb painted the famous moment in 1881.

paintings.t: The Driving of the Last Spike
paintings.why: On May 10, 1869, the last spike joined the Union Pacific and Central Pacific railroads at Promontory, Utah, creating the first railroad across America. Thomas Hill painted the crowd at the ceremony in 1881.

French soldiers defend a village cemetery at Saint-Privat against German attackers during the Franco-Prussian War in August 1870. Alphonse de Neuville painted it in 1881 in a lifelike style meant to show how fiercely they fought.

The worn-out French army of General Bourbaki, starved and half frozen, crosses into Switzerland in February 1871 to escape the Germans, and Swiss people took the soldiers in. Édouard Castres, a Swiss painter who was there as a Red Cross volunteer, painted it in 1881.

Woods and hills spread out in the Laurentian Mountains of Quebec, painted in rich greens and browns. Homer Watson was called Canada's greatest landscape painter of his day. He painted what he saw around him in Ontario and Quebec. It's a calm, natural scene.
The Mayflower, the ship that carried about 100 Pilgrims to America in 1620, rests in the harbor at sunset while a boat heads to shore. William Halsall painted it in 1882.

paintings.t: The Favorites of the Emperor Honorius
paintings.why: The weak emperor Honorius was told that Rome had fallen and said it couldn't be, he had just fed her. He meant his pet chicken, which he had named Roma. John William Waterhouse shows the emperor with his birds in 1883.

At the sea battle of Svolder in the year 1000, King Olav Tryggvason's famous ship the Long Serpent was surrounded by enemy ships. According to the sagas he leapt overboard rather than be captured. Otto Sinding painted it in 1883.

Alexander Menshikov, once Peter the Great's best friend and the second most powerful man in Russia, sits in a hut in Siberia with his family after his fall from power. Vasily Surikov painted this sad scene in 1883.
French General Louis Faidherbe rides on a white horse at the Battle of Bapaume in January 1871, one of the few French successes in the late war. Charles Édouard Armand-Dumaresq painted it in 1883.

A group of men stand and sit in a conference room in Quebec City in 1864, planning a new country: Canada. The painter Robert Harris created it long after the meeting, and it shows 33 delegates gathered at the Quebec Conference. It became a symbol of the birth of Canada. The original burned in a fire in 1916, and this is a copy of the lost painting.

paintings.t: Morning of the Battle of Agincourt, 25th October 1415
paintings.why: King Henry V of England, with a small tired army, waits for the French on the morning of the Battle of Agincourt in 1415. John Gilbert painted the muddy scene in 1884.

paintings.t: The Meeting of Antony and Cleopatra
paintings.why: In 41 BC Cleopatra of Egypt arrives to meet the Roman general Mark Antony and wins him over with a spectacular show. Alma-Tadema paints her waiting under a golden canopy on her barge as Antony approaches, a meeting that changed Rome's history.
Titus's soldiers parade through Rome in AD 71 with treasure from the conquest of Jerusalem. Lawrence Alma-Tadema painted the great procession passing on a staircase of the city in 1885.
Steelworkers pour white-hot metal in a Belgian steelworks in a glowing picture by Constantin Meunier of about 1885. Meunier painted workers in factories and mines with great respect.

paintings.t: The Proclamation of the German Empire
paintings.why: On January 18, 1871, in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles, the German princes proclaim King Wilhelm I of Prussia Emperor of Germany, with Bismarck in white at the center. Anton von Werner painted this third version in 1885.
Union ships under Admiral Farragut steam into Mobile Bay in August 1864, where he is said to have shouted 'Damn the torpedoes!' Julian Davidson made this color print in 1886.

Ulpiano Checa, who loved painting wild horses and chariots, shows hordes of mounted warriors charging across a snowy plain. The picture imagines the peoples who pushed into the Roman Empire at the end of antiquity.

paintings.t: Joan of Arc, Victorious over the English, Enters Orléans
paintings.why: On May 8, 1429 Joan of Arc rides into Orléans as a hero after the English siege is broken, and the crowd cheers her. Jean-Jacques Scherrer painted the triumph in 1887.

Smoking factory chimneys rise over green fields in Clichy, on the edge of Paris, in a painting by Vincent van Gogh of 1887. It shows how the city and its factories were spreading into the countryside.
Union and Confederate soldiers clash at Antietam on September 17, 1862, the bloodiest single day in American history. Thure de Thulstrup made this scene for a famous set of Civil War prints in 1887.
The Union army holds a long ridge while the Confederates attack across the fields at Gettysburg in July 1863, the turning point of the Civil War. Thure de Thulstrup made this view in 1887.

A mother cuddles her baby in a loving embrace, with a warm and tender mood. Paul Peel was a Canadian painter from London, Ontario, who became a star in Paris. He is known for tender pictures of mothers and children. It's a sweet, gentle family picture.

paintings.t: Fulvia and Mark Antony, or Fulvia's Revenge
paintings.why: Fulvia, the fierce wife of Mark Antony, takes revenge on the dead Cicero, the great speaker who had attacked her husband, in this gruesome scene from the civil wars after Caesar's death. The Spanish painter Francisco Maura y Montaner made it in 1888.
The sixteen-year-old Edward, called the Black Prince, stands among the dead after the Battle of Crécy in 1346, where English archers beat the French. Julian Russell Story painted it in 1888.

paintings.t: A Lost Cause: Flight of King James II
paintings.why: King James II, who had lost his throne in the Glorious Revolution of 1688, waits on the shore for a boat to take him into exile in France. Andrew Carrick Gow painted the sad moment in 1888, 200 years later.
Soldiers fight through smoke and trees at the Battle of Shiloh in Tennessee in April 1862, an early and very bloody battle of the Civil War. Thure de Thulstrup painted it in 1888.

A farm sits at the edge of a ravine, with trees and rolling land. Homer Watson, from Doon, Ontario, painted the farms and woods near his home. His quiet, thoughtful pictures became symbols of Canadian landscape. It's a gentle country view.

Colorful Japanese dolls and a fan are laid out together, with a bright patterned cloth. Paul Peel loved to paint beautiful objects, and Japanese goods were popular in Paris. The bright colors and rich textures are charming. It's a lovely still life.

paintings.t: Cicero Denounces Catiline in the Roman Senate
paintings.why: In 63 BC the great speaker Cicero stands and accuses Catiline of plotting against Rome, and the other senators move away from him. Cesare Maccari painted this fresco in the 1880s for the Italian Senate.
In March 1862 the ironclad warships Monitor and Virginia fought the first battle between armored ships, changing sea warfare forever. This color print was made in 1889.

A mother in a dark dress holds her small daughter on her lap in a quiet, tender moment at the end of the day. Paul Peel, a Canadian painter who became a star in Paris, was famous for warm pictures of home and childhood. The soft light and gentle pose make it feel cozy. It's a sweet picture of love at bedtime.
paintings.k: A mother holds her little girl. What bedtime story would you tell?

paintings.t: The Sack of Rome by the Visigoths on 24 August 410
paintings.why: In 410 the Visigoths under Alaric broke into Rome, the first time in about 800 years that an enemy had taken the city. Joseph-Noël Sylvestre's big painting of 1890 shows the invaders pulling down the statues of the old gods.

paintings.t: Joan of Arc at the Siege of Orléans
paintings.why: Joan of Arc, a teenage peasant girl who said saints told her to save France, rides into battle with her banner to lift the siege of Orléans in 1429. Jules Eugène Lenepveu painted this scene around 1890 for the Panthéon in Paris.

paintings.t: Cortés and Montezuma at Mexico City
paintings.why: The Spanish conqueror Hernán Cortés and the Aztec ruler Montezuma meet in the great city of Tenochtitlan in 1519, followed by war. This colorful print was made in the 1890s by the American lithographers Kurz and Allison.

In 1618 angry Protestant nobles threw two Catholic officials out of a window of Prague Castle. They survived by landing in a pile of rubbish, but it started the Thirty Years' War. The Czech painter Václav Brožík painted the dramatic scene in 1890.
Otto von Bismarck, the Prussian chancellor who united Germany under Prussia in 1871, in a portrait of 1890 by Franz von Lenbach. Bismarck was nicknamed the Iron Chancellor.

Confederate and Union soldiers fight in the woods at Chickamauga, Georgia, in September 1863, one of the largest and bloodiest battles of the Civil War in the West. This color print was made around 1890.

John Singer Sargent paints the soaring inside of the great church of Hagia Sophia, built by Justinian in 537 and turned into a mosque after the Ottoman conquest of 1453. He painted it on a trip to Istanbul in 1891.
A Union line holds against waves of Confederate attackers at the Battle of Franklin in Tennessee in 1864, one of the last big Confederate attacks of the war. This color print was made in 1891.

Edmund Blair Leighton shows Lady Godiva before her famous ride through Coventry, which in the legend she made to persuade her husband to lower the town's taxes. She lived in the years before the Norman Conquest.

A sunny, dry riverbed in the oasis town of Biskra in Algeria, with a faraway ridge and a few small figures. Maurice Cullen, a Montreal painter, traveled to North Africa and painted its vivid colors. He is best known for his snowy Canadian winter scenes. It's an unusual desert view by a painter of snow.
German officers rest in a smart French parlor during the siege of Paris, one with his boots on the table beside a piano. Anton von Werner, a German painter who was at the siege, painted it in 1894.

paintings.t: John, 7th Earl of Aberdeen, Later 1st Marquess, Montreal
paintings.why: A distinguished gentleman in formal dress sits in a stately pose. Robert Harris, who was born in Wales and grew up in Prince Edward Island, was one of Canada's top portrait painters. The Earl of Aberdeen was a governor general of Canada. It's a formal portrait of a public figure.

paintings.t: The Trial of Joan of Arc
paintings.why: Joan of Arc stands before her judges at her trial in 1431, after she was captured by the English allies. The French artist Louis-Maurice Boutet de Monvel painted her in a wide scene in the 1890s for a children's book.

Napoleon watches the huge Battle of Borodino in 1812 from a hill, looking small and uncertain among his generals. The Russian painter Vasily Vereshchagin painted him in 1897 as a worn, anxious commander.
Two cowboys race on horses to catch a runaway steer, in a scene full of speed and dust. Charles M. Russell painted it in 1897, drawing on his years working as a cowboy in Montana.

Two girls snuggle together on a sofa over a big book, absorbed in an exciting story. Laura Muntz Lyall was a Canadian painter from Toronto who became well known for her gentle pictures of children. She painted in a soft, delicate style and exhibited in Paris and London. It's a cozy picture of reading together.

Death, a skeleton on a winged creature, swoops over a plague-stricken city in this chilling painting. Arnold Böcklin made two versions in 1898, in the years after great epidemics had struck cities across Europe.

paintings.t: Vercingetorix Throws Down His Arms at the Feet of Julius Caesar
paintings.why: The Gaulish chief Vercingetorix surrenders to Julius Caesar in 52 BC after the siege of Alesia, ending a big revolt against Rome. Lionel Royer painted it in 1899, when French people thought of Vercingetorix as their first national hero.

paintings.t: The Captured King Gryting Is Brought Before King Harald
paintings.why: The conquered king Gryting is brought before Harald Fairhair in a scene from the Viking sagas. Erik Werenskiold drew it in 1899 for an illustrated edition of Snorri Sturluson's Heimskringla, the saga of the Norwegian kings.

The men of the Mayflower sign an agreement to make fair laws and govern themselves in the new colony. The Mayflower Compact of 1620 is one of the earliest steps toward self-government in America. Jean Leon Gerome Ferris painted it in 1899.

In June 1876 the Lakota and Cheyenne warriors defeated General Custer's soldiers at the Battle of the Little Bighorn, one of the greatest victories for Native Americans in the Plains Wars. Edgar Samuel Paxson painted this version in 1899.

paintings.t: Millicent Fawcett and Louisa Garrett Anderson
paintings.why: Millicent Fawcett, the leader of Britain's peaceful suffrage societies, sits with her niece Louisa Garrett Anderson. Fawcett believed in persuading Parliament by law-abiding campaigns, and she led the movement for decades.

paintings.t: Labour aux premières lueurs du jour
paintings.why: A farmer with oxen plows a field at dawn, in a misty light that shines on the earth. Horatio Walker, a Canadian painter from Ontario who lived on Île d'Orléans near Quebec City, painted the farmers and animals of rural Quebec. He admired the French painter Millet. It's a noble picture of work on the land.
l: Musée national des beaux-arts du Québec

paintings.why: Children and a woman gather nuts in a forest in autumn, in warm light. Homer Watson was known for his landscapes but occasionally included people. The picture feels peaceful and golden. It's a cozy autumn day.

paintings.t: The Wounded Montcalm Is Brought Back to Quebec
paintings.why: The French commander Montcalm, mortally wounded on the Plains of Abraham, is carried back into Quebec City on horseback in 1759. Louis Bombled painted the sad moment in 1900.
Viking-age traders, called Varangians, sail a dragon-headed ship into a Slavic harbor in this glowing scene. The Russian painter Nicholas Roerich, who loved ancient history, painted it in 1901.
Cowboys, also called buckaroos, ride in the open West in this lively painting by Charles M. Russell, who worked as a cowboy himself before he became an artist. He painted it in 1902.

paintings.t: In the shade of the apple tree
paintings.why: A young woman sits quietly in the dappled shade of an apple tree on a sunny day. Horatio Walker painted the countryside of Quebec, where he lived much of the year. The soft light and calm mood are typical of his peaceful style. It's a restful country scene.
l: Musée national des beaux-arts du Québec

paintings.why: Sultan Mehmed II rides in triumph through the gates of Constantinople after its fall in 1453, with red banners overhead. The Italian painter Fausto Zonaro, who worked for the Ottoman court, painted it in 1903.

The Ottoman army marches toward Constantinople in 1453 in a painting by Fausto Zonaro, an Italian artist who worked for the Ottoman sultans. The city fell after a siege of 53 days, ending the Byzantine Empire.

Swedish soldiers charge in a snowstorm at the Battle of Narva in 1700, where young King Charles XII beat the larger Russian army of Peter the Great. Peter lost the battle but learned from it and built a better army. Gustaf Cederström painted it in 1905.

On January 22, 1905, soldiers fired on peaceful workers marching to the Winter Palace to ask the tsar for help, killing and wounding many, an event that started the Revolution of 1905. Wojciech Kossak painted this scene of Bloody Sunday.

A portrait of a Huron-Wendat man, painted by Eugène Hamel, a Quebec artist. The Huron-Wendat have lived in the Quebec area for centuries. Painters of the time often recorded the faces of Indigenous people they knew. It's a quiet, dignified portrait.
l: Musée national des beaux-arts du Québec

paintings.why: A stone church stands in a village in Brittany, France, painted in warm, soft colors. Emily Carr, a Canadian painter from British Columbia, studied in France in the early 1900s. She was inspired by the strong colors and shapes of French painting. It's from the years before she became known for her Pacific Coast paintings.

A dancer in a bright red dress stands with her arm raised in a flamenco pose, while a guitarist plays beside her. Clarence Gagnon, a Quebec painter, traveled widely in Europe and painted scenes from Spain. The title is the Spanish shout of praise, 'Olé!' It shows that Canadian artists also painted the world.
l: Musée national des beaux-arts du Québec

paintings.why: Ilya Repin's lively early study for his painting of the crowds celebrating Tsar Nicholas II's October Manifesto of 1905, with swirls of red flags.

paintings.t: Leaders of the Women's Social and Political Union, about 1906
paintings.why: Women's Social and Political Union leaders meet around 1906. Founded by Emmeline Pankhurst in 1903 with the motto 'Deeds, not words,' the WSPU used marches and protests to demand votes for women in Britain.

People stroll and rest on a sunny beach with colorful parasols and striped beach tents at the seaside resort of Dinard in France. Clarence Gagnon painted this in his early career, when he was studying in Paris. The bright sand and sea are lively. It's a happy summer day at the beach.
l: Musée national des beaux-arts du Québec

paintings.t: Pocahontas at the Court of King James
paintings.why: Pocahontas, dressed as an English lady, is presented to King James I in London in 1616. Richard Rummell made this colorful picture in 1907, three hundred years after the founding of Jamestown.
Tsar Peter the Great strides ahead so fast that his courtiers struggle to keep up in this lively painting, which shows his energy and force of will. Valentin Serov painted it in 1907.

paintings.t: Washington and Lafayette at Valley Forge
paintings.why: George Washington and the young French marquis de Lafayette ride through the snow at Valley Forge in the winter of 1777–1778, when the American army nearly starved but became a stronger force. John Ward Dunsmore painted it in 1907.

Hilma af Klint, a Swedish artist, painted this in 1907 as part of a series of ten giant paintings, each about three meters tall, showing the stages of a human life. This first painting, Childhood, is full of rings, flowers and bubbles, and she painted abstractly before most famous artists.

Big circles in blue and orange, with a pink flower, flow across the canvas in the second of Hilma af Klint's Ten Largest, which show the ages of a person from childhood to old age. They were painted in 1907 and are bigger than most doors.
Swirls of orange and bright colored flowers fill the third of Hilma af Klint's ten giant paintings of the ages of life, called Youth. Painted in 1907, it feels full of energy and growth.

The fourth giant painting of the Ten Largest series shows spirals and petals in orange and pink, full of the bursting energy of youth. Hilma af Klint painted it in 1907, working in a studio in Stockholm.

Soft pink and lilac colors with writing and flower shapes mark the fifth of Hilma af Klint's ten giant paintings, Adulthood, painted in 1907. She said she painted these as if guided by a higher power.

Tall shapes like an hourglass or a plant stand out in the sixth painting of Hilma af Klint's Ten Largest series of 1907. She painted abstract pictures years before Kandinsky, though almost no one saw them until long after she died.
A big yellow shape like a flower or a lantern glows in the middle of the seventh of Hilma af Klint's Ten Largest paintings, Adulthood, painted in 1907.

Circles in pink, white and gray float in the eighth painting of Hilma af Klint's Ten Largest, painted in 1907. Hilma af Klint asked that her paintings be kept secret until 20 years after she died, and they were first shown to the public in 1986.

paintings.t: The Ten Largest, No. 9, Old Age
paintings.why: Pale pink and white discs, like dandelion clocks, fill the ninth painting in the Ten Largest series, which shows old age. Hilma af Klint painted it in 1907 in soft, fading colors.

paintings.t: The Ten Largest, No. 10, Old Age
paintings.why: Squares of red, blue and yellow and little flowers stand on a pale ground in the last of Hilma af Klint's Ten Largest paintings, about old age. It ends the series of 1907 with a calm, balanced picture.

A church leader in rich robes sits in a dignified pose. Charles Huot was a well-known Quebec painter who made historical paintings and large decorations for the Quebec legislature. This portrait shows his skill with serious, formal subjects. It's an example of French-Canadian portraiture.
l: Musée national des beaux-arts du Québec

paintings.why: A cow stands beside a fence in a soft, misty farmyard in the early morning. Horatio Walker was known as the painter of Quebec farm life, and he sold many paintings in the United States. The gentle light and quiet mood are typical of his style. It's a peaceful rural scene.
l: Musée national des beaux-arts du Québec

paintings.why: Nellie McClung, the Canadian writer and activist who led the campaign that made Manitoba the first province to give women the vote in 1916. This portrait is from about 1910.

A farmyard in Brittany, with old buildings and the glow of sunlight. Emily Carr painted this during her time in France. The bright colors show she was learning from the modern painters there. She would later bring these lessons home to Canada.

Trees in fall colors line a country lane in France. Emily Carr studied in Paris and Brittany, and learned about the bright colors of Post-Impressionism. She painted this with a bold, free brush. It shows her artistic growth before returning to Canada.

A woman in a stylish dress sits in a gentle, modern style. James Wilson Morrice was a Canadian painter who lived mostly in Paris and was friends with Matisse. He painted with soft, bright colors and simplified shapes. He's now seen as Canada's first great modern painter.

Crowds joyfully wave flags and red banners in the streets after Tsar Nicholas II promised civil rights and a parliament in October 1905. Ilya Repin painted this big crowd scene, which captures the hope, and the tension, of Russia's first revolution.

paintings.t: First Nations War Canoes in Alert Bay
paintings.why: Large carved canoes sit on the beach of Alert Bay, a First Nations village on the coast of British Columbia. Emily Carr traveled to Indigenous villages along the Pacific Coast to paint and to record carvings and village life. She wanted to preserve what she saw. It's an important record of the West Coast in the early 1900s.

A city street scene of tall buildings and giant signs, in a bold, simple style. David Milne was a Canadian painter who lived in New York and later in Ontario. He made pictures of cities, signs, and nature with clean shapes and a light touch. It's an early work from his time in New York.

A big carved canoe from the Pacific Northwest Coast, with bold shapes and strong colors. Emily Carr, a painter from Victoria, British Columbia, visited Indigenous villages to record their carvings and canoes. She was one of the first non-Indigenous artists in Canada to take this art seriously. The picture shows her respect for the beauty of what she saw.

A big wooden community house stands in the village of Ucluelet on the west coast of Vancouver Island. Emily Carr visited the village in 1912 and painted the building with bold, simple shapes. She wanted to record the Indigenous villages that were changing quickly. It's an important historical record as well as a painting.

paintings.t: Lewis and Clark Meeting Indians at Ross' Hole
paintings.why: The explorers Meriwether Lewis and William Clark, who crossed the continent in 1804 to 1806, meet the Salish people at Ross' Hole in what is now Montana. Charles M. Russell painted it in 1912 for the Montana Capitol.

paintings.t: Official Program, Woman Suffrage Procession, March 3, 1913
paintings.why: A colorful program for the great Woman Suffrage Procession held in Washington on March 3, 1913, the day before Woodrow Wilson became president. About 5,000 women marched down Pennsylvania Avenue demanding the vote.

A Life magazine cover from the suffrage-themed issue of February 1913, in black and gold, by Rea Irvin, who later designed the New Yorker's first cover. Magazines like Life helped bring the vote debate to every living room.
Eyes, petals, stripes and shields are packed together in a swirl in this 1913 painting by Marsden Hartley, one of the first American artists to paint without recognizable subjects.

paintings.t: Battle of Lights, Coney Island, Mardi Gras
paintings.why: Fireworks, towers and fairground lights explode in a sparkling night in Joseph Stella's Battle of Lights, painted in 1913 and 1914. Stella, who had moved to New York from Italy, loved the modern city.

A quiet, simple painting in dark tones, with bold shapes. David Milne painted both in New York and in the Canadian woods, always using a thin, delicate touch. He is now considered one of Canada's most important modern painters. It's an early example of his inventive style.
The Pilgrims and the Wampanoag people share a harvest meal in the autumn of 1621, the event we remember as the first Thanksgiving. Jennie Augusta Brownscombe painted this friendly gathering in 1914.

paintings.t: Emmeline Pankhurst Arrested outside Buckingham Palace
paintings.why: Police carry the British suffragette leader Emmeline Pankhurst away on May 21, 1914, after she tried to bring a petition to King George V at Buckingham Palace. She was arrested many times for the cause of women's votes.

Bright stripes, rings and zigzags tumble together in a painting by Marsden Hartley from 1914. Hartley, an American, spent time in Berlin before World War I, where he met artists of the Blue Rider group.
Flags, stars and a tiny red horseman make a puzzle of bright patterns in Marsden Hartley's painting called Himmel, which means sky or heaven in German. It was painted in Berlin in 1914.

Bright colors and circles seem to spin around like the rides at the Coney Island amusement park in New York. Joseph Stella, an Italian-American artist, painted this in 1914 and loved the lights of the park.

White houses with red roofs reflect in a still canal framed by dark green trees, in a painting by Oscar Bluemner from 1914. Bluemner treated color like music, and this picture shows a very quiet harmony.

A small bouquet of wildflowers bursts with orange, yellow and blue against a dark background. Tom Thomson is best known for landscapes, but he also painted flowers as small sketches. The glowing colors have a joyful energy. It's a rare and cheerful still life.

A white house with a red roof stands in the sunny Caribbean, painted in a few clean, bright colors. James Wilson Morrice traveled to Cuba and the Caribbean in the winter. His light, simple style was ahead of its time. It's a sun-filled picture.

A camp in the woods is lit by the first rays of sunrise, with smoke rising from a campfire. Homer Watson painted this late in his career, with softer colors. The warm light is magic. It's a quiet and calm early morning.

Bright red and orange autumn leaves stand out against the dark woods, painted on a small panel. Tom Thomson loved the Ontario fall, when the maples blaze with color. His small sketches captured the feeling of the season. It's a vivid example of Canadian autumn.

Charred tree trunks stand on a hill after a forest fire, with new green growth rising beneath them. Tom Thomson saw the burnt land in Algonquin Park and made it the subject of a powerful sketch. Despite the damage, the spring colors show hope. It's a famous image of nature recovering.

paintings.t: Blue Lake: Sketch for "In the Northland"
paintings.why: A deep blue lake is surrounded by bright trees in a quick, colorful study. Tom Thomson made it as a first idea for his painting 'In the Northland.' The sketch is full of fresh, direct feeling. It shows how he worked outdoors, painting fast.

A woman in a golden gown, a symbol of Liberty, strides across a map of the United States in which the states where women could vote glow in gold. Henry Mayer's cartoon, published in 1915 in Puck magazine, shows the suffrage movement spreading from the West.

paintings.t: Vote for the Woman Suffrage Amendment
paintings.why: A map shows in yellow the states where women already had equal suffrage in 1915, and the poster urges voters to approve the woman suffrage amendment in November. New York's vote failed that year but passed two years later.

paintings.t: I Didn't Raise My Girl to Be a Voter
paintings.why: An anti-suffrage poster from 1915, made by opponents of women voting, borrows the title of a famous song. It shows what the suffragists were up against.
A tree of shapes grows like a pale and glowing seedpod in this painting from Hilma af Klint's Tree of Knowledge series of 1915. She was interested in plants and science as well as spiritual ideas.
A swirl of branches and roots grows out of an oval shape in this painting by Hilma af Klint, from 1915. It is one of a series that she painted about how things grow and connect.

Boats rest by the shore of a lake in dappled light. Tom Thomson often painted on Canoe Lake in Algonquin Park, where he lived and worked as a guide. The little sketch is relaxed and bright. It's a happy picture of life on the water.
Pieces of blue, black and orange tumble through a white space like falling shapes in a game. Olga Rozanova made this in 1916 and was one of the first artists to join Malevich in painting pure shapes.
Triangles and diamonds in many colors fit together like a puzzle in a painting by the American Patrick Henry Bruce, who lived in Paris. He painted this in 1916.

paintings.t: President Wilson Says Votes for Women
paintings.why: A cartoon by Nina Allender, the cartoonist of Alice Paul's National Woman's Party, shows suffragists behind bars after being arrested for picketing outside the White House in 1917. They had held signs asking President Wilson 'How long must women wait for liberty?'

A map of North America, with the states and provinces where women could vote marked, on a suffrage poster from 1917. By then women could vote in many western states, and the poster urges the rest to follow.

Canadian gunners push and pull an artillery piece through deep mud at Passchendaele in late 1917, one of the worst battles of the war. Alfred Bastien, a Belgian painter working for the Canadian War Memorials, painted this.
A print of a cemetery on Vimy Ridge, the French hill where Canadian soldiers won a famous victory in April 1917. It was made as a record of the war as soon as it ended.

paintings.t: A Grave and a Mine Crater at La Boisselle, August 1917
paintings.why: A huge crater from a mine explosion and a lonely grave mark the old battlefield at La Boisselle, on the Somme. William Orpen, a British official war artist, painted it in 1917.

paintings.t: The Pogrom of the Winter Palace
paintings.why: Soldiers and workers rush into the Winter Palace, the home of the Russian government, on the night of October 25, 1917, when the Bolsheviks seized power. Ivan Vladimirov painted it in 1917 as an eyewitness.

Big shapes in red, pink and gray overlap like pieces of colored glass or sails. Lyubov Popova made her Architectonics in 1917 and said she wanted her paintings to be like buildings made of color and light.
Slabs of blue, orange and cream seem to slide over each other like layers of a building. Lyubov Popova, one of the leading women artists of the Russian avant-garde, painted this in 1917.
Angular shapes in black, blue and rose twist and cross like a tangle of wires. Olga Rozanova, a Russian avant-garde artist, painted this in 1917, in the middle of the revolution.
An orange oval and a black rectangle float on a white ground as if in space. Ivan Kliun painted this in 1917 as a Russian experiment in pure shape and color.

Bright red houses and trees are cut into sharp shapes beside a bend in the river at Little Falls, New Jersey. Oscar Bluemner, a German-born American painter, painted this in 1917 and loved to use bold colors, especially red.

Rows of simple huts painted in camouflage patterns stand in a muddy World War I camp. Maurice Cullen was a Canadian official war artist who went to France in 1918. His paintings record what soldiers' daily lives were like. It's a quiet record of wartime.

A gray dawn light shines over a battlefield, with trenches and bare ground. Maurice Cullen painted this as an official Canadian war artist. The quiet colors seem to show both beauty and sadness. It's a thoughtful war landscape.

The ruined village of Ablain-Saint-Nazaire in France sits in rubble after the fighting of World War I. Maurice Cullen painted the ruins after Canadian troops fought near here at Vimy Ridge. The broken buildings show the cost of war. It's a record of a village changed by history.

A scene of a French town damaged by war, with broken walls and a quiet sky. Maurice Cullen painted the places where Canadian soldiers served in 1918. The painting is quiet and respectful. It's part of a series that preserves the memory of the war.

paintings.t: We Are Making a New World
